en: “I hope no one minds if we dispense with this for now?” Orso tossed his circlet down, gold twinkling in a dusty shaft of spring sunlight as it spun around and around. “Damn thing chafes rather.” He rubbed at the sore spots it had left above his temples. There was a metaphor there somewhere. The burden of power, the weight of a crown. But his Closed Council had no doubt heard all that before.
bs: — Nadam se da nitko nema ništa protiv da ovo za sada odložimo? Orso ležerno baci svoj vijenac, dok mu je zlato svjetlucalo u prašnjavoj gredi proljetnog sunca vrteći se u Round. — Prokleta stvar prilično žulja. Protrlja bolna mjesta koja su mu ostala iznad sljepoočnica. Tu se negdje krila metafora. Teret moći, težina krunjenja. No njegovo ga je Tajno vijeće nesumnjivo već sve to slušalo.

en: “It would be folly,” said Bayaz, his attention already back on the gardens, “to obstruct the free operation of the market.”
bs: — Bila bi ludost — odbrusi Bajaz, a pažnja mu se već vratila na vrtove — ometati slobodno djelovanje tržišta.

en: “The job of your Closed Council,” said Glokta, “is to anticipate threats to Your Majesty before they become threats.”
bs: — Zadaća je vašeg Zatvorenog vijeća — reče Glokta — predvidjeti prijetnje Vašem Veličanstvu prije nego što doista to postanu.

en: Superior Lorsen lowered the letter, frowning at Vick over the rims of his eye-lenses. He looked like a man who had not smiled in some time. Perhaps ever.
bs: Viši inspektor Lorsen spusti pismo namrštivši se na Vik preko rubova svojih naočala. Izgledao je poput čovjeka koji se već dugo nije nasmiješio. Možda i nikada.

en: She got the sense that Lorsen had heard the same rumours she had, delivered in breathless whispers with a great deal of lurid detail. That Shenkt’s skills went beyond the mortal and touched the magical. That he was a sorcerer who had damned himself by eating the flesh of men. Here in Westport, where calls to prayer echoed hourly over the city and cut-price prophets declaimed on every corner, such ideas were somehow harder to dismiss.
bs: Stekla je dojam da je Lorsen načuo iste glasine koje i ona, izgovorene zadihanim šapatom i praćene mnoštvom morbidnih pojedinosti. Da Šenktove vještine nadilaze smrtničke i dotiču se čarobnjaštva. Da je on mračnjak koji se prokleo blagujući ljudsko meso. Ovdje u Vestportu, gdje su pozivi na molitvu odzvanjali gradom svakoga sata, a jeftini proroci propovijedali na svakom uglu, takve su se zamisli činile nekako teže odbacitljivima.

en: “With thanks to our distinguished patrons—the Lady Ardee and her daughter Lady Savine dan Glokta.” Curnsbick gave his usual showman’s flourish towards the box where Savine sat, but the clapping now was yet more subdued. Did she even hear a few tattletale whispers below? She’s not all she was, you know. Not one half of what she was…
bs: — Uz zahvalnost našim uglednim pokroviteljima — gospođi Ardi i njezinoj kćeri, gospođi Savin dan Glokta. Kurnsbik izvede svoju uobičajenu zabavljačku gestu prema loži u kojoj je Savin sjedila, ali pljesak je sada bio još suzdržaniji. Je li dolje doista čula nekoliko izdajničkih šaputanja? Nije ona više ono što je bila, znate. Ni upola ono što je nekad bila…

en: She squeezed her face into a smile, snapped out her fan and forced herself into the midst of the press with Zuri at her shoulder. Eyes turned in her direction, expressions harder than she was used to. Assessing, rather than admiring. Scornful, rather than envious. They used to crowd around her like pigs around the one trough in the farmyard. Now the most tempting morsels went elsewhere. Savine could scarcely see Selest dan Heugen through the swarm of gentlemen competing for her attention. Only a
bs: Gomila ju je podsjećala na mnoštvo u Valbeku kada su Razbijači dijelili hranu po sirotinjskoj četvrti. Nosili su svilu umjesto krpa, zaudarali su na parfem umjesto na ustajali znoj, stalna prijetnja bila je propast radije nego nasilje, no guranje i glad ostali su posve isti. Bilo je vrijeme kada se Savin u tom gmizavom metežu osjećala ugodno poput matice u košnici. Sada joj je cijelo tijelo trnulo od prohladne panike. Morala je ugušiti nagon da počne mlatiti laktovima i vrišteći pobjeći prema iz

en: But when she glanced up, Curnsbick was not even looking at her. He was staring across the busy foyer towards the door.
bs: No kad je podignula pogled, Kurnsbik je nije ni gledao. Ziljio je preko živahnog predvorja prema vratima.

en: Broad nudged his food around the plate with it. Just holding the damn thing made his hand hurt. Felt too delicate for his aching fingers. “You reach an age it’s hard to learn new ways, I reckon.”
bs: Brod je njome gurao hranu po tanjuru. Sama pomisao da drži tu prokletu stvar boljela ga je u ruci. Činila se nekako preosjetljivom za njegove napaćene prste. — Dođeš u godine kada je teško usvojiti nove navike, reklo bi se.

en: “Boast of?” Broad stared back, over the rims of his lenses, so Gaunt was just a sparkly blur in the lamplight. “Fuck, no. I wake up with the sweats. I cry, sometimes. In the quiet times. Don’t mind admitting it.”
bs: — Hvaliti? Brod ga pogleda ispod okvira svojih naočala, tako da mu je Gaunt u svjetlosti svjetiljke bio tek svjetlucava mrlja. — U pičku materinu, ne. Budim se obliven znojem. Zaplačem, ponekad. U trenucima tišine. Nije me sram to priznati.

en: “Your problem, Master Broad, is you confuse your best with your worst. I need work to continue on the canal first thing tomorrow. First thing. I need it open and making me money.” She snarled the last word, teeth bared, her fury setting his heart thumping. She was a head shorter than him. He’d have been shocked if she was half his weight. But she still scared him. Not because of what she might do. Because of what she might get him to do. “Now make it happen, there’s a darling.”
bs: — Vaš je problem, majstore Brod, što svoje najbolje miješate s najgorim. Zahtijevam da radovi na kanalu počnu sutra ujutro, odmah u zoru. Odmah. Želim da bude Otvoreno i da mi donosi novac. Iskezila je tu posljednju riječ, ogolivši zube, a njezin mu je bijes natjerao srce da poskoči. Bila je niža od njega za glavu. Iznenadilo bi ga da je imala i upola manje kilograma od njega. Pa ipak, i dalje ga je plašila. Ne zbog onoga što bi ona mogla učiniti. Nego zbog onoga na što bi ga mogla nagovoriti. —

en: “A man can take a lot, when he thinks he’s fighting the good fight. I know that.” Broad rubbed gently at his knuckles. “But seeing it done to your child? That’s something else.”
bs: — Čovjek može podnijeti mnogo toga kada misli da se bori za pravu stvar. Znam ja to. — Brod je nježno protrljao zglobove prstiju. — Ali kad vidiš da to rade tvom djetetu? To je već nešto posve drugo.

en: It had been a bad idea to bring him. Vick knew she was better off alone. A lesson learned fresh in the camps with every family member gone in the frozen ground. Her father, shivering, lips turned blue, shortened fingers turned black. Her mother, always asking what she’d done to deserve this, as though deserve had anything to do with it. All the sweat and pain it had taken to get that medicine for her sister. Turning up with the bottle gripped tight to find her stiff and cold under the threadbare
bs: „Tako uvjerljiv. Tako zarazan. Tako silno… koja je ono riječ… karizmatičan. Voljen onako kako mogu biti samo političari oslobođeni vlasti — a samim time i razočaranja. Pridobio je mnoge za svoj način gledanja na stvari. Strana Unije nema nikoga u njegovoj klasi. Sve je to nekako ukočeno. Ali onda, teško je, zar ne, strastveno zagovarati ono što već imaš? Tako dosadno. Dok je divna alternativa? Buket obećanja! Vreća puna snova! Veličanstven brod fantazija, netaknut sudarima sa stvarnim obavljanje

en: Glaward pushed out his bottom lip. “If it’s a weak enemy you’re after, I hear the Gurkish are obliging. The Empire’s broken into splinters. No Prophet. Priests and princes and chiefs and governors all fighting each other for control.”
bs: — A ljudi mrze Stirijce više nego ikad — reče Antaup. — Čujem da je Vestport pravi bure baruta. Jedna iskra i… puf. — Nasmiješi se od uha do uha glumeći eksploziju. — A tamošnje žene… — Još se šire osmjehnu oponašajući još veću.

en: “The Great Wolf only respects the boot across his neck! To disarm us? How can they be so blind? It’s not half a year since we were fighting for our lives, without a shred of help from those bastards!”
bs: — Jesam je odmorio, i boljelo je još više. Pa sam trenirao, i postalo je gore. Pa sam je opet odmorio, i to nije pomoglo. Ništa krvavo ne pomaže! Zatočen sam u toj jebenoj stvari!

en: “Axes!” he bellowed, and the spearmen split apart, pretty neat. Not too far from what they’d practised, which was quite the wonder under the circumstances. The best fighters Stour had given him came pouring through the gap, mail and shields and good axes smashing into the flatheads from uphill with a sound like hail on a tin roof.
bs: Klover ga uhvati za rame i čvrsto stisne. — Mirno. U takvom trenutku svatko pomišlja na bijeg, barem nakratko, a dovoljan je samo jedan da sve uvjeri kako je to najbolja ideja. Prije nego što se snađeš, love te po šumi umjesto da slaviš pobjedu. A Kloverova su koljena postala previše ukočena za lovljenje, a kamoli za to da bude lovina.

en: Platforms were scattered in front. Stages where men and women stood in robes, in rags, festooned with talismans and beads or brandishing books and staffs. Wailing in broken voices to little crescents of curious onlookers, tearing at the air with their hands, pointing skywards with clawing fingers, eyes popping with passion and certainty, promising salvation and threatening damnation. Each insisting all the rest were frauds, and they alone were the one with all the answers.
bs: — Vjerojatno. Trgnula je ruku i probila se kroz krcati prolaz za Shudrom i njegovim stražarima, uzevši pravac prema tržnici začina koja je u svojoj suludoj mjeri bila zasljepljujuća, zaglušujuća i zagušljiva poput valbečke tkaonice. Košare i bačve stajale su u klimavim kulama, police bijahu krcate blistavim staklenkama ulja. Boje su bile iznimno žive na sunčevu svjetlu, puderi jarko crvene, narančaste i žute boje, lišće u svakoj nijansi zelene i smeđe. Utezi i novčići zveckali su i zvrčali, mušk

en: Lady Wetterlant turned a glare on the high justice that might have frozen milk. “Mine is an old family, Your Majesty. We have many friends.”
bs: — Sedamnaest prokletih seljaka! Wetterlant u iznenadnom gnjevu zgrabi rešetke. — Uzeo bi njihovu riječ ispred moje?

en: “It is not an easy role to fill.” Bayaz reached out to touch that flower with his fingertip, ever so gently brushing a few specks of glittering dew from its petals. “Living kings are always objects of derision. But people cannot wait to worship the dead ones. Someone must lead. Someone must make the hard choices. For everyone’s benefit.”
bs: — Nije lako ispuniti tu ulogu. Bajaz posegnu kako bi vrhom prsta dotaknuo taj cvijet, sasvim nježno otresajući nekoliko iskričavih kapi rose s njegovih latica. „Živi su kraljevi uvijek predmet podsmijeha. No ljudi jedva čekaju obožavati mrtve. Netko mora voditi. Netko mora donijeti teške odluke. Za svačiju korist.”

en: “It has not been the happiest of marriages in recent years, then,” observed Orso, thinking of his father’s grinding teeth during their fencing sessions.
bs: — Onda to posljednjih godina i nije bio najsretniji brak, primijeti Orso, prisjećajući se kako su mu ocu škripali zubi tijekom njihovih mačevalačkih treninga.

en: “Most of them are every bit as disgusted at his behaviour as we are, Your Majesty. They are keen to see justice done.”
bs: — Većina njih zgrožena je njegovim ponašanjem baš kao i mi, Vaše Visočanstvo. Žarko žele vidjeti da je pravda zadovoljena.

en: “Very little worth anything is ever given away. I am sure you know that, too.” Bayaz smiled at Savine’s father. The one in the chair, not the one immortalised in stone. “I have no doubt your father will stand here one day. Who has sacrificed more for the Union, after all? Except perhaps your uncle.” Bayaz turned to look up at the statue of Lord Marshal West. “Who gave his life defending it.”
bs: — Vrlo se malo toga vrijednog ikada poklanja. Siguran sam da i vi to znate. — Flik se osmjehnu Savininom ocu. Onome u stolici, ne onome ovjekovječenom u kamenu. — Nemam nimalo sumnje da će vaš otac jednog dana stajati ovdje. tko je, uostalom, žrtvovao više za Uniju? Osim možda vašeg ujaka. — Flik se okrenu kako bi pogled usmjerio prema kipu lorda maršala Westa. — Koji je dao život braneći je.

en: “I’ve been made some outrageous proposals,” Savine threw over her shoulder to Zuri as she pulled off her gloves, “but that must be the first time a statue on the Kingsway has been put on the table…”
bs: — Dobivala sam već prilično nečuvene prijedloge, dobaci Savin preko ramena Zuri dok je skidala rukavice, ali ovo je zasigurno prvi put da je kip na Kingswayju stavljen na stol…

en: “It’ll be the event of the season,” said Savine’s mother, “though if you’re asking me, the man’s a bloody viper. Wine, Savine?”
bs: — Bit će to događaj sezone, dometnu Savinina majka, mada je, ako mene pitate, taj čovjek obična krvava guja. Vina, Savin?

en: “Don’t be cross and don’t be coy. Neither suits you. Zuri is worried for you, as a good servant should be. As a good friend should be. She is thinking of your best interests. We all are, believe it or not.” Her mother leaned forward, holding her eye, and put a reassuring hand on Savine’s knee. “She told us about your… situation.”
bs: „Nemoj se srditi i nemoj se pretvarati. Nijedno ti ne priliči. Zuri brine za tebe, kao što dobra služavka treba brinuti. Kao što dobar prijatelj treba brinuti. Ona misli na tvoje najbolje interese. Sve mi mislimo, vjerovala tomu ili ne.” Njezina majka se nagne naprijed, zadržavajući njezin pogled, te položi umirujuću ruku na Savinino koljeno. „Rekla nam je za tvoju… situaciju.”

en: “Congratulations on your forthcoming marriage.” Leo winced at a twinge in his leg as he broke free. “Haven’t seen my mother this excited in years.” He turned slowly around, looking up towards the gilded dome high, high above. “Doubt you could find a grander venue.”
bs: Krunski princ Orso činio mu se sasvim u redu, ali prijestolje samo pojačava čovjekove loše osobine, a njegovo Zatvoreno vijeće činili su isti oni korumpirani crvi koji su vladavinu kralja Džezal otjerali u jarak. Ono što je Uniji trebalo bili su ljudi od hrabrosti, ljudi od strasti, ljudi od akcije.

en: “Let me be your shepherdess. I can help you get your way.” By the dead, she was close now. “With the Closed Council. With my father. With the great men of the realm.” He could smell her. That sweetness, that heady sharpness. “I know everyone worth knowing. And how to use them.” Her scent brought all the excitement of that night rushing back.
bs: Na njegovo iznenađenje, ali nipošto razočaranje, njezina ruka nađe se među njegovim nogama. Već polukrut, i nije trebalo dugo da ga dovede do kraja. Činjenica da su bili na vidiku pola Agrionta, a majke im nisu bile ni deset koraka daleko, činila je sve to još uzbudljivijim.

en: A hand lifted her head, the rim of a cup pressed to her mouth. She coughed on something bitter, shuddered as she swallowed.
bs: Ruka joj podiže glavu, rub čašice prisloni se uz usta. Zakašlja se na nešto gorko, prestrašeno se strese dok je gutala.

en: “That they are,” said Scenn. The hillman stood grinning next to one of the Shanka and it narrowed its already narrow eyes at him while it used a splinter of bone to pick at one huge tooth. “They guard the witch. She can speak to ’em. Sings to ’em, some say. They’re tame. Long as we behave.”
bs: — Jesu, odvrati Skenn. Brđanin je stajao cerkajući se pored jednog Shanka, koji je suzio svoje ionako uske oči prema njemu dok je komadićem kosti čačkao ogroman zub. — Oni čuvaju vješticu. Ona može razgovarati s njima. Neki kažu da im pjeva. Pitomi su. Dok god se pristojno ponašamo.

en: “She has to go up there and that’s all there is to it,” snapped Isern, harshly. “This girl matters, Scenn. She’s beloved of the moon. I’ve always known it.”
bs: — Ona se mora popeti gore i to je sve — odbrusi Izern oštro. — Ova djevojka je važna, Skenne. Mjesec ju obožava. Oduvijek sam to znala.

en: Shivers gave Rikke a glance, but she was too out of breath to do much more than shrug. “How… do we get there… then?” she asked between her wheezes.
bs: Šivers uputi Rike pogled, ali ona je bila odviše zadihana da bi učinila išta više od slijeganja ramenima. — Kako… da se domognemo… toga onda? — upita kroz hropac.

en: “The cold has a wonderful way of clearing the mind.” Not the witchy croak Rikke had expected. A young voice, smooth and full of music. “It fixes you on what counts. Draws your attention inwards.”
bs: — Hladnoća ima čudesan način bistrenja uma. — Nije to bio vještičji hropac koji je Rike očekivala. Mladi glas, gladak i ispunjen glazbom. — Usmjerava te na ono što je važno. Privlači tvoju pozornost prema unutra.

en: The witch gave a hiss of disappointment. “It is the potter’s task to impose her will upon the clay. To shape the clay into something useful. Or something beautiful.”
bs: Vještica otpuhnu razočarano. „Zadatak je lončara nametnuti svoju volju glini. Oblikovati glinu u nešto korisno. Ili nešto lijepo.”

en: It was far from his first visit to the Lords’ Round, of course. He remembered being mildly bored when his father had shown it to him as a building site, rather impressed when his father had shown it to him largely completed, then exceedingly bored when his father had presided over the first meeting of the Open Council there.
bs: Ipak, to mu ni izdaleka nije bio prvi posjet Okrugloj vijećnici. Sjećao se da mu je bila donekle dosadna kad mu ju je otac pokazao dok je još bila gradilište, prilično impresivna kad mu ju je otac pokazao uglavnom dovršenu, a zatim iznimno dosadna kad je otac ondje predsjedavao prvom sjednicom Otvorenog vijeća.

en: A side door was flung open with an echoing bang. There was a rustling as lords and proxies twisted to see, people in both public galleries leaning out dangerously far in their eagerness to glimpse the prisoner. The hall fell quiet. There was a scraping, tapping, clinking sound, and Fedor dan Wetterlant emerged from the darkness.
bs: Bio je to trijumf, a nakon svih nedaća, preokreta, da i ne spominjemo užase opasne po život iz prethodnih nekoliko mjeseci, bio joj je prijeko potreban da si malo olakša dušu. Trebala se topiti u pažnji. Uživati u ljubomori svojih mnogobrojnih neprijatelja. Pustiti svijet da iza lepeze nazre barem nagovještaj njezina samodopadnog osmijeha.

en: Orso frowned up towards the public gallery, looking angrier than Savine had ever seen him. She shrank back from the rail, wondering whether her own history with the two men might be aggravating things. But the Young Lion was aggravating enough without her help.
bs: — Gubimo vrijeme?, prošaptao je Leo. Išer je podigao obrve i nemoćno raširio dlanove kao da želi reći: Što sam ti ja govorio? Iza njega, na jednom od velikih vitraja, Otvoreno vijeće ustalo je ujedinjeno protiv tiranije Luđaka Morlica, i to samo zato što je Arnault smogao hrabrosti stati prvi, sasvim sam.

en: They walked in silence, one of the wheels of Glokta’s chair catching on every turn with a regular squeak, squeak, squeak which might as well have been a saw applied directly to Orso’s nerves.
bs: — Ali… — Wetterlant odvrati pogled prema Išeru, kao da uopće nije očekivao takav ishod, no Išer prekriži ruke na prsima i ne pogleda nikoga u oči. — Ja sam član Otvorenog vijeća…

en: “And my heart.” Rikke wasn’t sure whether she’d meant to let go the string or not, but her arrow stuck into the lad’s back, just under his shoulder blade.
bs: — I moje srce. — Rike nije bila sigurna je li namjeravala pustiti tetivu ili ne, ali njezina strijela zabode se mladiću u leđa, neposredno ispod lopatice.

en: The bench had ropes around it. And on the polished-smooth cave floor salt had been scattered. Circles and lines and symbols in salt. Candles burning in the darkness. A joke of a witch’s cave.
bs: Klupa je bila opasana konopcima. A po uglađenom podu pećine bila je posuta sol. Krugovi i crte i simboli u soli. Svijeće su gorjele u tami. Izgledalo je kao sprdnja od vražje pećine.

en: By the Fates, her eyes were already brimming again, making her powder run. It can be pleasant to have someone weak leaning on you. It can make you feel strong. But there comes a point when they become a dead weight to carry. Savine was happy to play big sister but she drew the line at motherhood. She would have her own child to worry about soon enough.
bs: Savin nije bila ni približno sigurna je li čvrst karakter osobina koju mladoženje najviše cijene kod mladenke. Prihvatila je Isoldine mlohave ruke. — Ponašaj se kao da sve ide točno po tvom planu. Kao da si najsamouvjerenija osoba na svijetu. Kao da nikad u životu nisi imala ni trunku sumnje. — Savin je zabacila ramena, podigla bradu i okrenula se prema vratima. — Kod mene to pali.

en: And Orso snatched two glasses from a passing waiter’s tray and pressed one into Isher’s hand. “There’s as much need for cooperation between the Crown and Open Council as ever. More! I hope we can work together again to bring it about. This time… with a happier outcome?” Such as Isher’s neck in the noose rather than Wetterlant’s, for example. “To your happiness, my friend, and that of your charming bride, of course!”
bs: Orso bi radije bio bilo gdje drugdje. Tamnice gurkulskog cara u tom su mu trenutku zvučale privlačnije. Uostalom, teško je bilo zamisliti veću torturu od veličanstvenog vjenčanja žene koju je volio s mužem kojega definitivno nije podnosio, a među gostima se našla čitava lepeza podrugljivih neprijatelja koji su mu se u lice klanjali i ulagivali, a čim bi zamaknuo izvan dometa sluha, sipali prezir na njega.

en: “Dinner will be served shortly, Your Majesty.” A powdered footman gestured towards his chair—the largest chair, of course—in the very centre of the great polished horseshoe of table. He wondered how many trees had died to make it possible. “If it please Your Majesty, you are to be seated between the two brides, the grooms just without, to either side.” And he managed to back away and bow simultaneously.
bs: Leo bi joj se rado pridružio i uživao u svom dijelu divljenja. No nikada nije bio neki plesač, čak ni prije povrede noge. Malo koji vojnik jeste. Antaup, možda. Zapitao se što bi njegovi prijatelji rekli kad im predstavi svoju mladu. Ostali bi bez teksta, najvjerojatnije. Kako bi uopće mogli ostati ravnodušni? Kako bi to bilo tko mogao?

en: There was a long, expectant silence. The hairs on Leo’s neck prickled. A clock on the marble mantel tick, tock, ticked. He looked the three lords in the eye, one after another. Isher spoke far from plainly but, at the same time, left no doubt what they were discussing.
bs: Heugen ispusti uzdah negodovanja. Barezinovi podbratci zatreseše se u nijemom otporu. Išer odlučno odriješši bijelom glavom. „Mi bismo postupili u kraljevu najboljem interesu. U najboljem interesu zemlje.“

en: “They have been frustrated for years,” said Isher. “Chafing at the taxes, the infringements, the insults. Wetterlant’s treatment, and yours—a genuine hero of the Union, mark you, in our own Lords’ Round—was the final straw.”
bs: Leovo je srce zatreperilo na pomisao o stezanju oklopa. Mjesto mu je bilo na čelu redova raspjevanih vojnika, a ne izmučenom i pod papučom iza nekakvog prašnjavog, starog stola. Nasmiješio se pomislivši na marševske čizme, vjetar koji nosi zastave, zveket isukanog čelika, tutnjavu konjskih kopita u jurišu…

en: She shoved him. He didn’t even try to stay standing. Caught his head on an occasional table as he fell, bit his tongue and sprawled on his back, surrounded by scattered ornaments. Marshal Kroy stared down at him from the heavy frame. His feelings on the business were hard to judge.
bs: Gurnula ga je. Nije se ni pokušao održati na nogama. Udario je glavom o stolicu dok je padao, ugrizao se za jezik i srušio se na leđa, okružen razbacanim ukrasima. Maršal Kroy promatrao ga je s visine iz teškog okvira. Njegove dojmove o cijelom poslu bilo je teško procijeniti.

en: Gorst shook his head, eyes eternally roving around the dim room as though a Styrian assassin might spring from the dresser at any moment. If one had, Orso never doubted Gorst would have been ready with the utmost extremes of lethal force.
bs: Gorst odvrgnu glavu, očiju koje su neprekidno lutale po zagušljivoj prostoriji kao da bi štirski ubojica svakoga trena mogao skočiti iz ormara. Da jest, Orso ni na trenutak ne bi posumnjao da bi Gorst bio spreman uporabiti krajnje mjere smrtonosne sile.

en: “Reckless,” piped Gorst. Orso turned to him, surprised. It might have been the first time he’d ever heard the man volunteer a word of conversation. He shrugged, armour faintly rattling. “Kings needs cool tempers.” And he went back to frowning about the room.
bs: — Lakomislen, oglasi se Gorst. Orso se okrenu prema njemu, iznenađen. Možda je to bio prvi put da je čuo tog čovjeka kako dobrovoljno izusti riječ razgovora. On slegnu ramenima, a oklop mu slabašno zveknu. — Kraljevima treba hladna glava. I vrati se mrštenju po sobi.

en: “Morning, Your Grace,” said Savine as he sat opposite her at the breakfast table and gingerly stretched out his leg.
bs: „Jutro, Vaša Visosti”, odvrati Savin sjedajući nasuprot njemu za doručkovni stol te oprezno ispruži nogu.

en: “Bride is youthful,” said Carmee Groom, plucking out one of the pencils shoved through her shambolic bun and causing half of it to collapse across her face. “Bride bursts with potential.”
bs: — ! odbrusi ona, s bijelim zglobovima dok je stiskala rub stola. — Mjesto iskrenosti. Ako Svorbrik od govana može ispresti dijamante, samo naprijed. Kamo je, do đavola, stavila svoj prah od bisera?

en: But things had changed since she went to the forbidden lake, and not just ’cause she kept getting surprised on her right-hand side. The left was full of sad shocks, too. Folk she’d have called friends stared as she passed like they saw the dead walk, slunk off and wouldn’t meet her one good eye. Folk who used to smile looked scared, shocked, disgusted even. One woman Rikke had never been able to shut up about the weather herded her three children inside at the sight of her and slammed the door.
bs: No stvari su se promijenile otkad je posjetila zabranjeno jezero, i to ne samo zato što su je stalno s desne strane dočekivala iznenađenja. I s lijeve su je čekali tužni šokovi. Ljudi koje bi nekad nazivala prijateljima zurili bi u nju dok je prolazila kao da vide mrtvaca koji hoda, izmicali bi se i odbijali susresti se s njenim jedinim zdravim okom. Oni koji su se nekad smiješili djelovali su uplašeno, šokirano, štoviše zgroženo. Jedna žena s kojom Rike nikako nije uspjela prestati razglabati o

en: Lots of weapons in that hall, lots of sorrow and lots of anger, and Clover made sure he knew where all the doors were. When a great man dies, those left over always take a moment working out where their loyalties are most fruitfully laid, and there’s a high risk of bloodshed in the meantime. He’d seen one funeral turn into several often enough.
bs: Bilo je mnogo oružja u toj dvorani, mnogo tuge i mnogo gnjeva, a Klover se pobrinuo da dobro upamti gdje su svi izlazi. Kada velik čovjek umre, oni koji preostanu uvijek uzmu malo vremena da razmisle gdje će im lojalnost biti najplodonosnija, a u međuvremenu postoji velika opasnost od prolivanja krvi. Vidio je on to prečesto, kako se jedan sprovod pretvori u nekoliko njih.

en: Bit by bit, with shuffling feet and hanging heads, folk started to drift back to their lives. Bit by bit, the garden emptied. Rikke stood looking at the ground, wishing she could see through it. Wishing she could force the Long Eye open and see her father’s face again. But her eye stayed cold as the rain, and the sea, and the cold ground.
bs: — Jesam, zar ne? Caurib je bila u pravu. Moć Dugog Oka nije bila toliko u onome što vidiš, koliko u onome u što natjeraš ljude da povjeruju. Rike se nikada u životu nije osjećala moćno sve dok nije natjerala Staura i njegove ljude da pobjegnu glavom bez obzira samo svojim okom i svojim riječima. — Ali vratit će se, reče. — Kao vukovi što vrebaju tik iza vatre.

en: Alas, not everyone was so easily pleased. Mustred and Clensher advanced with weighty frowns the moment the gangplank clattered across from ship to quay. Short of diving into the brine, there was no escape.
bs: — Kakve li sretne slučajnosti! Kao da je išta što je Savin učinila bilo slučajno. Ona se još slađe osmjehne, pružajući obje ruke. — A vi morate biti Džurand, Leov stari prijatelj i suborac.

en: “… since savings must be made in order to satisfy the Closed Council,” gurgled out Clensher, sounding as if he had a sockful of gravel in his throat, “I move that we reduce Angland’s standing armies by two regiments, and—”
bs: — … budući da se uštede moraju ostvariti kako bi se zadovoljilo Zatvoreno vijeće, zagrgolja Clensher zvučeći kao da u grlu ima čarapu punu šljunka, predlažem da smanjimo anglandsku stajaću vojsku za dvije pukovnije, i —

en: Orso slumped further yet. “I never doubted I’d be a terrible king, but I never thought I’d be my father’s son so— ah!”
bs: Orso se još više pogrbio. — Nikad nisam sumnjao da ću biti užasan kralj, ali nikad nisam mislio da ću biti očev sin na ta — ah!

en: One of the nobles from the Open Council—Barezin, maybe—was on his feet and roaring his outrage but was entirely inaudible over the screeching commoners, who were pelting the scaffold with rotten food. There was a shriek, followed by another surge through the crowd but wilder, arms flailing. A fight breaking out and quickly spreading.
bs: Jedan od plemića iz Otvorenog vijeća — možda Barezin — ustao je i urlao od bijesa, ali se njegov glas uopće nije čuo od vike pučana koji su gnjusnom hranom zasipali vješala. Zaorio se prodoran krik, a potom je uslijedio još jedan nalet kroz gomilu, još divlji, s mlatarajućim rukama. Izbila je tuča i ubrzo se proširila.

en: She pulled the old sheepskin tight around her shoulders. Still smelled like him, somehow. She wished for a moment he could be woken, and thought of him striding in to see what all the fuss was about. Thought of him smiling at her the way he used to, like she was the most precious thing he had. The most precious thing there was. Then she wondered if he would smile, when he saw her blinded eye and the runes on her face. Wondered if he’d have stared, fearful and queasy like everyone else. The thoug
bs: Uz određenu dozu nevoljkosti, dvojica starih ratnih poglavica stadoše krugom obilaziti jedan drugoga; Crvenkapica s uzdignutim vrhom mača, a Oksel s mačem ispruženim u stranu. Kružili su sve bliže, Oksel ogoljenih zubi, a Crvenkapica vrškom jezika prelazeći preko donje usne. Kružili su još bliže, a onda Crvenkapica izbode, dok Oksel odbi udarac, uzvrati silovitim zamahom, a Crvenkapica izmače saginjanjem. Držači štitova zadihano uzdahnuše, a štitovi zaškripaše dok se Round napinjao i pomicao, a

en: “We can hope.” Though since Savine had been with child several months before her wedding it did not seem terribly likely. She kept the smile clamped to her face until Isold was gone, then she stood, pushed the heels of her hands into her aching back, and went straight to the connecting door. She had planned to sweep through and take her share of the conversation by force, but there was something secretive to Leo and Isher’s hushed tones that made her hold back. She ever so gently eased the door
bs: — Jesi. To se naprosto više nije moglo sakriti, a Savin je prilično uživala u tome što se vidi. Očekivala je da će je silno živcirati to što joj sebični mali parazit svakim danom sve više krade tijelo. No, u njezinu ispupčenom trbuhu bilo je nečeg neobično utješnog. Čak se povremeno zatekla kako mu pjeva. Onomad je osjetila kako se pomaknuo. Savin podiže obrve nježno ga milujući. „Tko bi rekao da je ključ sreće u široj odjeći? Kakve su prilike u Miderlandu?“ upita nastojeći zvučati ravnodušno. —

en: “I… was,” he said, frowning. He didn’t know where she was taking him but didn’t much like the direction of travel. “Thought I was doing right. I guess.” Hard to remember what he’d thought. Seemed like a different man who’d thought it.
bs: — Ja… jesam — reče namrštivši se. Nije znao kamo ga vodi, ali mu se smjer puta nije odviše sviđao. — Mislio sam da postupam ispravno. Valjda. — Teško se bilo prisjetiti što je točno mislio. Činilo se kao da je te misli imao netko sasvim drugi.

en: Rikke stuck her fingertip in her milky right eye. “This eye fought the other, so it had to go. My visions come much cleaner now.” She leaned close and muttered it out of the corner of her mouth, “Don’t shit myself no more neither. And I’m still me!” She punched him on the arm. Good-natured, but hard. “More or less.”
bs: Potjera konja naprijed, kroz skupinu novih koliba i kuća, ostavljajući Antaupa, Jina i ostale iza sebe s kočijom i zapregama. Savin je držala korak s njime, prošavši kroz vrata i truckajući se popločanim putem, dok su ih prljava lica u bezbojnoj odjeći u čudu promatrala dok su prolazili. Mnogo se toga promijenilo. Možda nove građevine ondje gdje je Staur Najtfol spalio stare. Veličanstvenije građevine, od kamena i škriljevca umjesto od drva i pletera.

en: “I tend somewhat to agree. No reason you and I can’t be good neighbours, though. Why don’t you come inside? I’ll toss a fresh log on the firepit and crack a keg of my father’s ale.”
bs: — Isto mislim i ja, dometnu Rike namještajući iza uha pramen kose koji joj je slani povjetarac otpuhao s lica. — Što te dovodi ovamo, Nokte?

en: We all are carried into the future, always. What greets us when we arrive, that is the pressing question. When the Prophet vanished, Muslan and those of his mind—the thinkers, philosophers, engineers—had hoped for a new age of reason. Instead had come an age of madness. The priests had said his work was against the laws of God. Ignorant cowards. Who made the minds of men, if not God? What was the desire to create, if not a humble imitation of His example? What was the grand idea, the great visio
bs: Svi smo mi uvijek nošeni u budućnost. Što nas dočekuje kad stignemo, to je goruće pitanje. Kad je Poslanik iščeznuo, Muslan i oni slična uma — mislioci, filozofi, inženjeri — nadali su se novom dobu razuma. Umjesto toga stiglo je doba ludila. Svećenici su govorili da je njegov rad protivan Božjim zakonima. Neuki kukavice. Tko je stvorio ljudske umove, ako ne Bog? Što je bila žudnja za stvaranjem, ako ne ponizno oponašanje Njegova primjera? Što je bila uzvišena ideja, velika vizija, duboko otkrov

en: Orso stood staring for what felt like a very long time, one hand weakly holding his mother’s limp arm, his sword dangling uselessly from the other. He would have dropped it had his fingers not been stuck in the elaborate basketwork. The first of the attackers lay on his side at their feet, the cloth twisted from his stubbly face, a steadily widening pool of blood bubbling from his nose and mouth.
bs: Gdje su bili vitezovi Tjelesne straže? Zar nisu trebali rješavati takve stvari? Ta to je bila jedina svrha tih kopiladi, zar ne? Ugledao je jednoga mrtvog, s komadom metala probodenim kroz oklop na prsima. Stoga mu se nije moglo previše prigovoriti. Gdje je bio Bremer dan Gorst? Dao mu je slobodan dan. Inzistirao je na tome. Grozna odluka. Je li Orso donio ijednu dobru? Nije se mogao sjetiti se nijedne. Vjerojatno je krivica bila njegova. Obično i jest bila. Kralj je bio tek svojevrsna kanta u k

en: “The Young Lion!” Stour rose from Skarling’s Chair. “Not as young as you were, but no worse for that.” He caught Brock’s hand, and pulled him up onto the dais, and flung his other arm around his shoulders, and slapped him on the back with an echoing clap. Then the two of ’em had one of those hugs which is halfway to a wrestling match, making out they were best of friends while each tried to drag the other off his feet.
bs: Brok to prevede na jezik Unije svojoj ženi, a ona se nasmija jednako blistavo kao što joj je haljina sjajila. Klover se zapita koliko je vježbala da bi taj smijeh zvučao savršeno, ali se istodobno silno obradova saznanju da je on bio uzrok tomu, a onda se silno razočara kad ona produži dalje. Daunsajd je blenuo za njom poput lisice u otvoreni kokošinjac.

en: She could usually slit a man right open with one compliment, but Black Calder was better armoured than most. “My own father always said it serves a man well to learn the ways of his enemies,” he grunted.
bs: Obično je mogla rasparati čovjeka jednim jedinim komplimentom, no Blek Kalder bio je bolje oklopljen od većine. — Moj mi je otac uvijek govorio da čovjeku koristi upoznati običaje svojih neprijatelja, odbrusio je on.

en: Sad to say, Stour didn’t slit his hand and swear a blood oath to their alliance on the spot. Instead, he sat back, toying with his ale cup.
bs: Nažalost, Staur ne rasiječe dlan i ne zakle se na krvni Unija za njihovo savezništvo na licu mjesta. Umjesto toga se zavalio, poigravajući se vrčem aleja.

en: But all Stour gave Leo was another dose of the side-eye. “Once you’ve heard one song of victory you’ve heard ’em all. Swap the names out and it’s the same spears shaken and horns blown and bodies carpeting the glen and all that shit. You see my friend Clover down there?” And he pointed out that balding bastard, the one who’d had the girl beside him with all the belts. “That fat fool used to be Jonas Steepfield.”
bs: No sve što je Staur udijelio Leu bila je još jedan prijeki pogled ispod oka. — Kad čuješ jednu pjesmu o pobjedi, čuo si ih sve. Samo zamijeni imena i to je to — ista priča o zveckanju koplja, puhanju u rogove, tijelima koja prekrivaju dolinu i sva ta sranja. Vidiš li mog prijatelja Klovera tamo dolje? Pokazao je na onog ćelavog kopilana, onog s djevojkom do sebe koja je bila okićena remenjem. — Taj debeli idiot nekada je bio Jonas Strmograd.

en: “It might.” To her, at least. For him, there was no help. His Majesty’s Inquisition tended away from leniency when it came to attempted regicide. “Who planned it?”
bs: — Svi to govore. No možda su nešto propustili. Možda si ti nešto propustio. Nešto čega nisi bio ni svjestan da je važno.

en: She pulled the door shut and clipped his voice back to a muffled burble. A Practical stood outside, arms folded.
bs: Privukla je vrata i prigušila mu glas u prigušeno mumljanje. Inkvizitorov čovjek stajao je vani, prekrštenih ruku.

en: “Besides, we have no evidence. The one thing I’m sure Leo dan Brock is guilty of is finding me contemptible. If that’s a crime, I’ll have to hang three-quarters of the country. Have you seen the latest pamphlets? About me? About my mother? About the debt?”
bs: — Osim toga, nemamo dokaza. Jedina stvar za koju sam siguran da je Leo dan Brok kriv jest to što me prezire. Ako je to zločin, morat ću objesiti tri četvrtine zemlje. Jeste li vidjeli najnovije pamflete? O meni? O mojoj majci? O dugu?

en: “At last!” The barman’s accent was a strange cocktail—a slosh of Styrian and a dash of the Union with a few more ingredients which were harder to place. Tall and pale, with spiky red hair and a spiky red beard. He had a white cloth over one shoulder and a little monkey squatting on the other and he smiled a wide smile full of good teeth. “Victarine dan Teufel graces my humble establishment.”
bs: — Napokon! Barmenov naglasak bio je čudan koktel — mješavina štirijskog i primjese Unije s još nekoliko sastojaka koje je bilo teže odrediti. Visok i blijed, s usiljenom crvenom kosom i usiljenom crvenom bradom. Preko jednog ramena nosio je bijelu krpu, a na drugome mu je čučao mali majmun te se široko nasmiješio otkrivši niz zdravih zuba. — Viktarin dan Tojfel, počasti moju skromnu ustanovu.

en: He trudged down a slum street not far from where he’d once lived, the way just rutted dirt and ashes and rubbish flung out from the houses, dark from the buildings leaning together and the washing flapping in the gritty breeze. There were no drains, only pools of flyblown filth, fenced off in places to make pens for the squealing hogs, their run-off leaking through the slit windows into the cellars where the poorest eked out some kind of a living.
bs: Teško je koračao ulicom u sirotinjskoj četvrti, nedaleko od mjesta gdje je nekada živio; put je bio tek izlokana zemlja pomiješana s pepelom i smećem izbačenim iz kuća, zamračen zgradama koje su se naginjale jedna prema drugoj i rubljem što je lepršalo na prašnjavom vjetru. Odvoda nije bilo, samo lokve prljavštine pune muha, mjestimično ograđene kako bi se napravili torovi za cvileće svinje, čiji se otpad cijedio kroz uske prozore u podrume gdje su najsiromašniji jedva sastavljali kraj s krajem.

en: “I can take you to ’em.” Sarlby slowly chewed, slowly swallowed, slowly sat back. “But what happens after ain’t up to me.”
bs: — Pokušao sam na tvoj način — reče Brod. Namjestio je naočale na znojni nos i prisilio se disati polako. — Gledaj kamo nas je to dovelo.

en: Now the violinist had seen them, prancing over to the bridge just below their balcony, grinning up and hacking out a jauntier, more marshal theme. Beside the winery, two fellows started up a noisy argument. Typical Styrians, all swagger and no action.
bs: Sada ih je ugledao violinist, poskakujući prema mostu točno ispod njihova balkona, cereći se gore i izvodeći življu, ratoborniju melodiju. Pokraj vinarije dvojica su započela bučnu svađu. Tipični Štajerci, sve od hvalisanja, a nigdje djela.

en: He noticed there were grey streaks in her hair. Wrinkles around her eyes, at the corners of her mouth. When had she started to look old? It made him feel deeply uneasy. He had always supposed she was indestructible.
bs: Primijetio je sive pramenove u njezinoj kosi. Bore oko očiju, u uglovima usta. Kada li je to počela stariti? Zbog toga ga obuze duboka nelagoda. Uvijek je mislio da je ona neuništiva.

en: “Don’t worry.” Jurand, slipping up close to speak softly. Knowing Leo’s feelings without a word said, like always. He guided Leo over to the dice table. It was the right height to lean on, at least, and take the weight off his throbbing leg without showing any weakness. “You’re the Young Lion! You convinced Rikke and Stour to join you. United two bitter enemies under your banner! Just be honest, and strong, and generous. Just be you.” Jurand leaned closer, grinning. “Only a bit more ruthless. Th
bs: „Sve.“ Domaćin ih uvede u dvoranu tamnih drvenih obloga u kojoj su se igrale igre vještine, sreće i propasti. Skupine muškaraca sjedile su razgovarajući, smijući se, pušeći i pijući. Djevojke su gugutale, pjevušile i mahale lepezama. Šareno svjetlo blistalo je na finom staklu i mekoj koži, probijajući se kroz jantarna pića i kovitlac dima. Rijetko kad, ako ikad, tako je probran prizor visokoklasnog razvrata bio okupljen na jednom mjestu, a Orso ih je i sam priredio podosta u svojoj promašenoj ml

en: His meeting with Jappo had gone badly, he knew. Worse the more he thought about it. He wondered whether he might’ve made a serious mistake by not offering more. Then he felt disgusted with himself for offering as much as he had, annoyed with Savine for making him try, irritated at the world and everything in it. He’d made a grubby compromise too far by even talking to that greasy bastard and hadn’t gained a thing. What use could a man like that be in a battle anyway? If you could even call him a
bs: Orso duboko uzdahne. — Ako sam bio spreman zabiti vlastitoj sestri nož u leđa, kako bi mi uopće mogao vjerovati? Kako bi bilo tko mogao? Mogao bih slagati i reći da hoću, a onda kasnije prekršiti riječ, ali mislim da nam je svima dosta takvog ponašanja. Radije ću biti pošten i reći da je najbolje što od mene možeš dobiti to da stvari ostanu ugodno poznate. Odreći ću se svojih prava na Talini. Taj sam grad vidio samo na slikama. Uzmi ga s mojim blagoslovom. Možda s vremenom uspijemo čak pružiti j

en: Glokta gave a little snort of laughter. “Only promise me one thing. Should you think me worthy of a statue on the Kingsway… have it stand up.” He waved a finger towards the Practical lurking behind him, and the man turned his wheeled chair towards the door.
bs: — Ne vidim razloga da to imenovanje ne učinimo trajnim, reče Orso. Možda će Bajaz imati drugačije ideje kad sljedeći put navrati, ali za sada će mali ljudi morati sami praviti svoje pogreške.

en: “Your Majesty.” Forest made to put his hat on, then stopped. “Bloody thing does look like a quim.” And he strode away.
bs: — Vaše Visočanstvo. Forest se spremi staviti kapu, pa zastane. — Prokleta stvar stvarno sliči na pičku. I odmaršira dalje.

en: “You…” Matstringer looked like he might swallow his tongue. “This is an unprecedented breach of protocol—”
bs: — Ti… — Matstringer je izgledao kao da će progutati vlastiti jezik. — Ovo je kršenje protokola bez presedana…

en: “Go to your departments,” said Orso, “and make preparations. I want our defences shored up. I want forces on high alert. I want anything disloyal rooted out.” He stood, planting his hands on the table. “You are the only ones I can trust. My father’s faithful advisors. My loyal Closed Council. If we stay together, we will yet weather this storm.”
bs: — Idite u svoje urede, zapovjedi Orso, i pripremite se. Želim da nam se obrana učvrsti. Želim snage u visokom stupnju pripravnosti. Želim da se svaka neposlušnost iščupa iz korijena. On ustane oslonivši se dlanovima o stol. — Vi ste jedini kojima mogu vjerovati. Vjerni savjetnici moga oca. Moje odano Zatvoreno vijeće. Ako ostanemo zajedno, prebrodit ćemo ovu oluju.

en: Maybe that thought put a bit more venom in her next slap, hard enough to get his mouth bleeding. “You’ve given me no time to be subtle,” she hissed at him, “so this is going to get very painful very fast.” She slapped him again, even harder, her fingers stinging and blood speckling the wall beside his face. “Give me names.”
bs: Možda joj je ta pomisao unijela još malo otrova u sljedeći šamar, dovoljno snažan da mu natjera krv na usta. — Nisi mi ostavio vremena za suptilnost, prosikta mu u lice, tako da će ovo postati jako bolno i jako brzo. Opet ga ošamari, još jače, dok su je prsti pekli, a krv prskala po zidu pokraj njegova lica. — Daj mi imena.

en: “Why do you think I did it? We’re supposed to be a Union!” He roared the last word with sudden anger, clenching his one fist, and Vick stepped back, watchful. She reckoned him far more dangerous than Heugen, however many limbs he was missing.
bs: — Zašto misliš da sam to učinio? Trebali bismo biti Unija! Urliknuo je posljednju riječ s iznenadnim gnjevom, stisnuvši svoju jedinu šaku, a Vik odskoči natrag, na oprezu. Smatrala ga je daleko opasnijim od Heugena, bez obzira na to koliko mu je udova nedostajalo.

en: “I am leaving Adua today,” said Glokta. “My wife thinks the country air may be good for my health. That is… what she tells me she thinks, anyway. I suspect she does not want us to become sad ghosts haunting the halls where we were once powerful. I suspect she is wise in this, as in so much else.” He cleared his throat. “Before I left, I wanted to thank you.”
bs: — Danas napuštam Aduu, reče Glokta. — Moja žena smatra kako bi seoski zrak mogao dobro djelovati na moje zdravlje. Barem… tako mi govori da misli. Sumnjam da želi bismo postali tužni duhovi koji opsjedaju dvorane u kojima smo nekad bili moćni. Sumnjam da je mudra u tome, kao i u toliko toga drugog. On pročisti grlo. — Prije nego što odem, htio sam ti zahvaliti.

en: “It would have been easy to give in to sentimentality,” said Glokta. “But you did the brave thing. The right thing. Turning him in. Buying your freedom.”
bs: — Bilo bi lako prepustiti se osjećajima, reče Glokta. — Ali ti si učinila hrabru stvar. Ispravnu stvar. Prijavila si ga. Kupila svoju slobodu.

en: The fear sharpened, and the excitement underneath it, creeping up his throat as lamplight glimmered on the rotten tree stumps, gleamed on the puddles in the road, caught the sharpened logs of the collapsing fence and the long shed with its fallen-in roof.
bs: Strah se izoštrio, a s njime i potmulo uzbuđenje koje mu se penjalo uz grlo dok je svjetlost svjetiljki titrala po trulim panjevima, blistala na lokvama na cesti i obasjavala zašiljene trupce srušene ograde te dugačku šupu urušenog krova.

en: Broad was already running. Towards the lamplight, the plunging horses, the swelling cloud of smoke. Pounding across the clearing for the road and the sawmill, the black world bouncing, the quick breath hissing through his gritted teeth, the eagerness boiling up his throat, setting him on fire.
bs: Brod je već trčao. Prema svjetlosti fenjera, propinjućim konjima, nabujalom oblaku dima. Lupajući preko čistine prema cesti i pilani, dok mu se Black svijet tresao pred očima, ubrzani dah sukljao je kroz stisnute zube, a žudnja mu se penjala grlom i palila ga iznutra.

en: Had a feeling two writhing shadows was one man stabbing another but he’d no idea who was who. There were no sides. Only those doing the killing and those getting killed.
bs: Imao je osjećaj da su dvije isprepletene sjene jedan čovjek koji bode drugoga, ali pojma nije imao tko je tko. Nije bilo strana. Bilo je samo onih koji ubijaju i onih koji ginu.

en: “Thought it was prisoners,” grunted Broad, frowning at him. “Off to Valbeck to be hanged, you said.”
bs: — Mislio sam da su zarobljenici, prosiktao je Brod mršteći se na nj. — Rekao si, pravac Valbek i vješala.

en: “For what?” said Judge, laughter in her voice. “The House o’ the Maker to open and great Euz to spring forth wreathed in fire? ’Cause that’s what it’ll take to stop this.” Sarlby finally tore the case free, braced his feet against the stump and dragged the manager’s arm across it by the chain while two other Burners held him, the bracelet cutting white into his wrist. A third raised a lamp high so no one missed anything, his eager grin lit from above.
bs: — Zašto? upita Džadž, s podsmijehom u glasu. — Da se Stvoriteljeva kuća otvori i veliki Euz pomoli u plamenu? Jer jedino bi to moglo ovo zaustaviti. Sarlbi naposljetku istrgne kovčežić, upre nogama o panj i prevuče upraviteljevu ruku preko njega držeći je za lanac, dok su je dvojica drugih Spaljivača držala, a narukvica se urezivala u bijelu kožu na zglobu. Treći visoko podigne svjetiljku da nitko ništa ne propusti, a željno mu se lice odozgo žarilo u osmijehu.

en: Sarlby tossed the hand away and shook the contents of the case onto the muddy ground. “Just papers,” he grunted, holding up a sheaf of documents. Judge started leafing through them by the flickering light of one of the fires.
bs: Sarlbi baci šaku i istrese sadržaj kovčežića na blatnjavo tlo. — Samo papiri, prozbori promuklo podižući snop dokumenata. Džadž ih je počela listati na treperavoj svjetlosti jedne od vatri.

en: As dawn broke, the army of Angland filed through Ostenhorm towards the quay, where just about every vessel in the province had been pressed into service as a transport, the harbour made a shifting thicket by their masts. Drums thumped, pipes tooted, sergeants bellowed, boots tramp, tramp, tramped. The salt breeze caught flags stitched with old victories, the rising sun gleamed on gear newly forged in Savine’s own armouries.
bs: Kako je zora svitala, anglandska je vojska koračajući prolazila kroz Ostenhorm prema pristaništu, kamo je gotovo svako plovilo u provinciji bilo rekvirirano kao transportno, a njihovi su jarboli od luke činili gustu, pomičnu šumu. Bubnjevi su tutnjali, svirale su piskutale, narednici urlički izdavali zapovijedi, a čizme su marširale u monotonom ritmu. Slani je povjetarac nosio zastave izvezene starim pobjedama, dok je izlazeće sunce sjalo na opremi tek iskovanoj u Savinim vlastitim oružarnicama.

en: “Leo, I’ve heard a rumour…” She said the words in a horrified whisper. “That you mean to move against the Closed Council.” She gave a desperate, quivery smile. “Tell me it’s not true!”
bs: — Leo, čula sam glasine… Izgovorila je te riječi užasnutim šapatom. „Da namjeravaš krenuti protiv Zatvorenog vijeća.” Uputila mu je očajan, drhtav osmijeh. — Reci mi da to nije istina!

en: Finree stared from him to Savine. She looked so utterly distraught that it was hard to meet her eye. “Have you thought about what you’re risking? Have you thought about what happens if you lose?”
bs: Finri ga je pogledala pa prešla pogledom na Savin. Izgledala je toliko potreseno da ju je bilo teško pogledati u oči. „Jesi li pomislila na ono što riskiraš? Jesi li pomislila što će biti ako izgubiš?”

en: Isern propped her hands on her own hips, such as they were. “I’m the way the moon wants me and naught wrong about it from where I stand.”
bs: Izern stavi ruke na vlastite bokove, kakvi već bijahu. — Ja sam onakva kakva me mjesec stvorio i nema ništa loše u tome s moje točke gledišta.

en: “Fought all his life so we could choose our own way. But here we are, still stuck ’twixt the Union and the North. It’s like we’ve a foot on either boat, but now the two are going different ways on the current, and if we don’t jump to one or the other we’re apt to get torn in two.” She grimaced and grabbed her crotch. “And in the most sensitive spot!” More laughter at that. Make ’em laugh, you’re halfway there, her father always told her.
bs: — Borio se cijelog života da bismo sami mogli birati svoj put. Ali evo nas, još uvijek zaglavljenih između Unije i Sjevera. Kao da stojimo jednom nogom na jednome, a drugom na drugome čamcu, ali sad ta dva čamca plove u različitim smjerovima na struji, i ako ne skočimo na jedan ili drugi, lako bismo se mogli raspoloviti. Siktavo se nasmiješila i uhvatila se za međunožje. — I to na najosjetljivijem mjestu! Još smijeha na to. Nasmjasi ih, pa si obavio pola posla, govorio joj je otac uvijek.

en: “No.” Clover didn’t bother to say that men usually fight harder on their own ground. He doubted Stour wanted to hear that, either.
bs: — Ne. Klover se nije trudio reći da se ljudi obično bore žešće na vlastitom tlu. Sumnjao je da i to Staur želi čuti.

en: “I said don’t land yourself in his debt. I didn’t say spit in his eye.” Calder shook his head grimly. “You don’t understand what he is.”
bs: — Rekao sam da mu ne ostaješ dužan. Nisam rekao da mu pljuneš u lice. Kalder odbrusi smrknuto. „Ti ne shvaćaš što on jest.”

en: Clover had his doubts on that score. He’d seen victories enough, and they were like the false summits of a great fell. You struggle towards ’em, sure you’ve made the top, then the moment you get there you see another just beyond. No fight was ever the last. No victory was ever for good. But Black Calder was getting old. He wanted to see his great legacy secured before he went back to the mud. Then he could trick himself into believing it wouldn’t crumble a few moments after.
bs: Klover je imao sumnji u tom smislu. Vidio je dovoljno pobjeda, a one su bile nalik lažnim vrhovima golemih planina. Mučiš se penjući se prema njima, uvjeren da si stigao na vrh, a onda u trenutku kad dospiješ ondje ugledaš novi, odmah iza njega. Nijedna borba nije bila posljednja. Nijedna pobjeda nije bila zauvijek. Ali Blek Kalder je stario. Želio je da mu velika ostavština bude osigurana prije nego što se vrati u blato. Tada bi mogao zavarati samoga sebe povjerovavši kako se sve neće srušiti n

en: “That is enough!” shouted Orso. “Forest, Pike, Tunny, Teufel and Hoff, stay. The rest of you out.” He would not have minded ejecting a couple of those named, but he supposed he needed all the help he could get. “Gorst, make sure we are not disturbed.”
bs: — To je dosta! — uzviknu Orso. — Forest, Pajk, Tani, Tojfel i Hof, ostanite. Ostali, vani. — Ne bi mu smetalo izbaciti i nekolicinu s tog popisa, ali pretpostavljao je da mu treba sva moguća pomoć. — Gorst, pobrini se da nas nitko ne ometa.

en: It wasn’t the most glorious stretch of shore, he had to admit, as his flooded boots finally crunched up onto the beach and he stood to rest his aching leg. A great grey curve of cold shingle, then a great yellow curve of wind-torn grass, then brown dunes and scrubby trees swept sideways, a few lonely birds hovering on the breeze the only sign of life. No cheering crowds waiting to celebrate their liberation from the tyranny of the Closed Council.
bs: Morao je priznati da to nije bio najslavniji komad obale, dok su mu promočene čizme naposljetku zašuštale po plaži i dok je zastao da odmori bolnu nogu. Veliki sivi Arch hladnog šljunka, zatim veliki žuti Arch vjetrom iščupane trave, pa smeđe dine i zakržljalo drveće pometeno u stranu, uz nekoliko usamljenih ptica koje su lebdjele na povjetarcu kao jedini znak života. Nikakve navijačke gomile nisu čekale da proslave oslobođenje od tiranije Zatvorenog vijeća.

en: Leo’s standard was unfurled above him, the crossed hammers and the lion, holed and torn from victories in the North but never taken by an enemy. He smiled up as the sea wind made it flap and flutter, setting his doubts to rest and his heart leaping.
bs: Leova se zastava vijorila iznad njega — ukriženi čekići i lav, izrešetani i poderani u sjevernim pobjedama, ali nikada pokoreni od neprijatelja. Podignuo je pogled s osmijehom dok ju je morski vjetar razvijao i tresao, rasteretivši mu sumnje i natjeravši srce da poskoči.

en: They picked their way around the boggy margins of a vast puddle in the road. One could have described it as a lake without fear of contradiction, men squatting on an upended cart at one side like shipwrecked mariners, all manner of gear floating on the rain-pricked water while others waded past, weapons over their heads, or tried to force their way through the hedges to either side.
bs: Zaobišli su močvarne rubove golemih lokvi na cesti. Netko ju je mogao opisati i kao jezero bez straha da će ga tko opovrgnuti, a ljudi suučesnički čučali na preokrenutim kolima s one strane poput brodolomaca, dok je najrazličitija oprema plutala po vodom našaranom kišnim kapima, a drugi gacali uokolo držeći oružje iznad glava ili pokušavali pronaći prolaz kroz živicu s jedne ili druge strane.

en: Isher’s unhappy horse kept trying to turn around. Savine sympathised. He bad-temperedly jerked it back. “You haven’t heard from him?”
bs: Išerov se uznemireni konj neprestano pokušavao okrenuti. Savin ga je savršeno razumjela. Išer ga je živčano trgnuo natrag. — Zar niste čuli ništa od njega?

en: “Hardbread!” said Leo, grabbing the old warrior by the hand and giving it a shake fit to tear his arm off. “At last! Where’s Rikke?”
bs: — Hardbred! reče Leo, zgrabivši starog ratnika za ruku i protrestavši je tako snažno da mu je umalo otkinuo ruku. — Napokon! Gdje je Rike?

en: The door rattled at a thudding knock, and she gritted her teeth and worked her way into a slightly more presentable position, bladder aching again already. “Yes?”
bs: Vrata zatreperiše pod tucajućim udarcem, a ona stisnu zube i namjesti se u nešto pristojniji položaj, dok ju je mjehur već ponovno mučio. — Molim?

en: The corporal barely looked up from his sizzling pan, just waved her on. One of the soldiers gave her a weak smile, then went back to scraping mud from a boot. None of them challenged her as she nudged her horse past, but that was no surprise.
bs: Desetar jedva da je podigao pogled s tave koja je cvrčala, tek joj mahnuo da prođe. Jedan joj se vojnik blago osmjehnuo, a zatim se vratio struganju blata s čizme. Nitko je nije zaustavio dok je poticala konja naprijed, ali to joj nije bilo iznenađenje.

en: “On your side.” She leaned down, glancing left and right, using an urgent whisper, as if she’d picked him and only him to trust with a secret. “And I have a message from Lord Marshal Brint that could change everything.”
bs: — Na vašoj strani. Nagnula se niže, osvrnuvši se lijevo i desno, i progovorila žurnim šapatom, kao da je izabrala upravo njega i nikoga drugog da mu povjeri tajnu. „A imam i poruku od lorda maršala Brinta koja bi mogla promijeniti sve.”

en: “Everyone’s loyalties are a touch tangled these days.” She hooked out the chair at the head of the table with her foot and dropped into it, meeting Savine’s eye. “I like to think I never let your father down. He got me out of the camps. I owed him. But he’s gone now.”
bs: — Svačija su odanost današnja vremena malo zamrsila. Nogom je privukla stolac s čela stola i sručila se na nj, susrevši Savinin pogled. — Volim misliti da nikada nisam iznevjerila tvog oca. Izvukao me iz logora. Bila sam mu dužna. No njega više nema.

en: Worse than she’d feared. The rebels might outnumber the loyalists two to one. She smiled as though it was better than she’d hoped. “You might outnumber him four to one.”
bs: Gore nego što se pribojavala. Pobunjenici bi mogli nadjačati lojaliste dva naprema jedan. Nasmiješila se kao da je to bolje nego što se nadala. — Možda ih nadjačavate četiri naprema jedan.

en: Prettyboy must’ve been named by a real wag since he was, by any standard, a thoroughly ugly man. “Just pointed the bow,” he said, shifting awkwardly on his knees. Everything’s awkward when your hands are tied to your ankles, to be fair. The bow in question lay in the mud not far away, and he gave it a filthy look like it was to blame for the whole business. “But I fumbled the string, you know, and shot him.”
bs: Prettyboya je morao nazvati neki golemi šaljivdžija budući da je bio, po svim mjerilima, temeljito ružan čovjek. — Samo sam usmjerio Arch, reče vrpoljeći se nespretno na koljenima. Sve je nespretno kad su ti ruke svezane za gležnjeve, ruku na srce. Predmetni Arch ležao je u blatu nedaleko od njega, a on ga je prostrijelio mrkim pogledom kao da je on kriv za cijelu tu gungulu. — Ali omakla mi se tetiva, znaš, i upucao sam ga.

en: And who should burst from the trees but the Young Lion and a crowd of his bastards. They reined in so Stour and his lot were sneering bitter scorn from one side of the yard, Brock and his lot scowling righteous outrage on the other. Seemed the Young Lion hadn’t reached the point where tragedies became chores. If anything, he tended towards too much feeling.
bs: I tko bi drugi izbio iz šume nego Mladi Lav i gomila njegove kopiladi. Zaustavili su konje tako da su Staur i njegova družina podrugljivo širili gorki prezir s jedne strane dvorišta, dok su Brok i njegovi namrgođeno iskazivali pravednički gnjev s druge. Činilo se kako Mladi Lav još nije dosegnuo točku u kojoj tragedije postaju obveze. Štoviše, naginjao je tomu da previše osjeća.

en: His turn to wrench his horse around and ride off, showering everyone with dirt. Dancer stared at the ground. Prettyboy frowned bitterly at his bow. The fat one set to sobbing again. The corpses, naturally, were unmoved.
bs: Dođe red na njega da okrene svoga konja i odjaše prskajući sve oko sebe zemljom. Danser je zurio u tlo. Lijepi se gorko namrštio gledajući u svoj Arch. Debeljko ponovo navali jecati. Leševi, posve prirodno, ostadoše nepomični.

en: “Your August Majesty!” gushed the mayor as Orso’s party approached, collapsing in a bow so low his chain of office feathered the cobbles. “I cannot find the words to describe the privilege of hosting you! The honour for me and the entire town of Stoffenbeck is quite indescribable.”
bs: — Vaše Uzvišeno Visočanstvo! prosu gradonačelnik dok se Orsova pratnja približavala, spuštajući se u naklon toliko dubok da mu je službeni lanac dotaknuo kaldrmu. „Ne nalazim riječi kojima bih opisao privilegij da vas ugošćujemo! Čast za mene i cijeli grad Stoffenbeck naprosto je neopisiva.“

en: “Their first scouts.” Forest rubbed at his grizzled jaw. “Even with the roads in the state they are, their main body should be with us before sunset.”
bs: — Njihove prve prethodnice. Forest protrlja svoju prosijedu čeljust. — Čak i s obzirom na stanje puteva, njihova glavnina trebala bi stići do nas prije zalaska sunca.

en: “I told them a tale,” said Vick. “That you’re disorganised and short on men. That Brint has prevented any chance of reinforcements. The Lioness had her doubts, but her husband swallowed it whole, I think.”
bs: — Ispričala sam im priču, reče Vik. — Da ste neorganizirani i u manjku s ljudima. Da je Brint spriječio svaku mogućnost pojačanja. Lavica je imala sumnji, ali njezin je muž to progutao s udicom i plovkom, čini mi se.

en: “You’d want a ruthless commander,” said Tunny, considering the hills. “Someone who scares our men more than the enemy.”
bs: — Trebao bi ti bezobziran zapovjednik, reče Tani zagledan u brda. — Netko tko plaši naše vojnike više nego neprijatelj.

en: “I would like you to conduct Corporal Tunny and his Steadfast Standard across those fields. Seek out the intrepid Lord Governor of Angland! Seek him out with the most pomp, ceremony and military bluster possible. Tunny, I want your bloody salute to take an hour minimum.”
bs: — Htio bih da dopratiš despornika Tanija i njegovu Čvrstu zastavu preko tih polja. Potraži neustrašivog lorda namjesnika Englenda! Potraži ga s najviše pompe, ceremonije i vojne buke što je moguće. Tani, želim da tvoj krvavi pozdrav traje minimalno sat vremena.

en: “Your Grace! My lords of the Open Council! Representatives of the North! I’m Corporal Tunny, standard-bearer to the High King of the Union, His August Majesty King Orso the First. Colonel Gorst, Commander of the Knights of the Body, I believe you all know.”
bs: — Vaša Milosti! Moji Lords iz Otvorenog vijeća! Predstavnici Sjevera! Ja sam desetnik Tani, stjegonoša Velikog kralja Unije, Njegova Uzvišenog Veličanstva kralja Orsa Prvog. Vjerujem da svi znate pukovnika Gorsta, zapovjednika Tjelohranitelja.

en: Tunny drew himself up in the saddle to deliver that exhibition of a salute again, then whisked his horse masterfully about and bore the king’s radiant standard back towards Stoffenbeck. You couldn’t deny it was a hell of a flag. Perhaps when this was over it would have to go back to Angland, where it belonged.
bs: Tani se uspravi u sedlu kako bi ponovno izvio onu paradnu počast, a zatim majstorski okrenu konja i odjaha kraljevski blistavi barjak natrag prema Stoffenbecku. Nisi mogao poreći da je to bila paklena zastava. Možda će se, kad ovo završi, morati vratiti u Englend, kamo je i pripadala.

en: He found himself wishing that Rikke was there. He loved Savine, but she’d a habit of forcing her opinions on people. A subtle, velvety kind of forcing, but her opinions still. Rikke had a way of cutting through the tangle to the simple heart of things. She’d helped him see what he wanted.
bs: Uhvati se kako priželjkuje da je Rike tu. Volio je Savin, ali ona je imala naviku nametati svoje mišljenje drugima. Suprotno, baršunasto nametanje, ali ipak njezino mišljenje. Rike je imala dar probiti se kroz zamršeno klupko do same srži stvari. Pomogla mu je sagledati što on zapravo želi.

en: She winced at the clattering footfalls as Shivers and the rest ran out onto the wooden bridge. A moment she’d seen before, she was almost sure. Seen with the Long Eye. The cloaked man in the gateway fumbled for his sword.
bs: Trznula se na bat koraka dok su Šivers i ostali istrčavali na drveni most. Prizor koji je već vidjela, u to je bila gotovo sigurna. Vidjela Dugim okom. Muškarac u ogrtaču na ulazu u prolaz spetljano je tražio mač.

en: He blew a little dust from the top of his egg and his pale eyes rolled up to hers. “I’m saying don’t give me one.”
bs: On otpuhne malo prašine s vrha jajeta i prebaci svijetle oči prema njoj. — Govorim ti da mi ga ne stvaraš.

en: “I heard him,” said Rikke. “Guess there might be time for that later. Just a celebratory finger or two. But right now, I’m a little busy stealing your city. Where’s Black Calder?”
bs: — Čula sam ga, rekla je Rike. — Pretpostavljam da će možda biti vremena za to kasnije. Samo par slavljenih prstiju. Ali sada sam malo zauzeta krađom vašeg grada. Gdje je Blek Kalder?

en: Rikke nodded towards the gates of the inner wall. The gates with Skarling’s Hall beyond, still tight shut. “So who’s in charge in there?”
bs: Rike kimnu glavom prema vratima unutarnjega zida. Vratima iza kojih se nalazila Skarlingova dvorana, a koja su i dalje bila čvrsto zatvorena. — Pa tko je onda tamo glavni?

en: “For the Fates’ sakes, you know I’m good for it.” Orso gave a weary sigh as he dropped into his chair. “But that’s being king. Everyone wants a little piece of you. You’ll find out. If you win.”
bs: — Bogamu miloga, znaš da sam čovjek od riječi. Orso umorno udahnu i sruši se u stolac. — Ali to ti je to kad si kralj. Svatko bi htio komadić tebe. Saznat ćeš i sam. Ako pobijediš.

en: “Perhaps,” said Brock coldly, “if you were to dismiss your entire Closed Council and replace them with men of our choosing.”
bs: — Možda, odvrati hladno Brok, kada bi raspustio cijelo svoje Zatvoreno vijeće i zamijenio ih ljudima po našem izboru.

en: “Patriots, yes, of course,” said Orso, “but I’m not sure you’ve thought this all the way through. Once the troops go home… what’s to stop me changing my mind?”
bs: — Patrioti, da, , reče Orso, ali nisam siguran da ste ovo promislili do kraja. Jednom kad vojska ode kući… što me sprečava da se predomislim?

en: “A bolt of lightning could have struck me no more forcefully than when she said no,” mused Orso, chopping at his fish with the side of his fork. “But… perhaps she found another way to make herself queen? I hear she is with you on campaign. She always did like to keep a close eye on her investments.”
bs: — Munja me nije mogla snažnije udariti nego kad je rekla ne, razmišljao je Orso, režući ribu rubom vilice. — Ali… možda je pronašla drugi način da postane kraljica? Čujem da je s tobom u pohodu. Uvijek je voljela imati na oku svoja ulaganja.

en: He was half-hard by the time she got his nightshirt up. She kept kissing him, one hand between her legs, one hand between his. Someone has to do the work, after all.
bs: Bila je polutvrda kad je skidala njegovu košulju za spavanje. Nastavila ga je ljubiti, jedna ruka između njezinih nogu, druga između njegovih. Netko mora obaviti posao, na kraju.

en: “This one a little to the left, I think,” said Pike, then walked up to the summit of the hill to stand beside Vick, staring out at the valley. “We have been experimenting in the Far Country for several years now.” He watched the crews drag brush around the maws of the great iron tubes to hide them from sight. “And have found that cannons are like birthday presents. Best kept as a surprise.”
bs: — Ovaj malo ulijevo, rekao bih, odvrati Pajk, a zatim se popeo na vrh brijega kako bi stao pored Vik, zagledan u dolinu. — Već nekoliko godina eksperimentiramo u Dalekoj Zemlji. Promatrao je posade kako vuku grane oko otvora velikih željeznih cijevi kako bi ih sakrili od pogleda. — I otkrili smo da su topovi poput rođendanskih poklona. Najbolje ih je držati u tajnosti.

en: “I find reputations rarely fit people all that well. What are they, after all, but costumes we put on to disguise ourselves?” The mottled skin above his hairless brows twitched as he gave her uniform a glance. “Costumes we are forced to put on. If men are to be productive, they must have something to fear. That is why we have an Inquisition. I like to tell myself that every life I have taken has saved five more. Fifty more, perhaps. Not everyone has the stomach for that kind of arithmetic.” His
bs: — Smatram da ugled rijetko doista odgovara ljudima. Što su oni, naposljetku, nego kostimi koje odijevamo da bismo se skrili? Prošarana koža iznad njegovih obrvâ bez dlaka zatreperila je dok je bacio pogled na njezinu odoru. — Kostimi koje smo primorani nositi. Ako ljudi žele biti produktivni, moraju se nečega bojati. Zato i imamo Inkviziciju. Volim si utuviti u glavu da je svaki život koji sam oduzeo spasio još pet. Možda pedeset. Nema svatko želudac za takvu matematiku. Oči su mu zasjale na svj

en: “Well, we’ve got no walls to climb,” said Bannerman, “so I’ll take a sword, thanks all the same.” And he drew a few inches of his own blade, then slapped it back into its sheath.
bs: — Pa, mi nemamo zidine koje treba penjati, dometnu Banerman, tako da ću ja uzeti mač, hvala lijepo u svakom slučaju. I izvukao je nekoliko centimetara vlastite oštrice, a zatim je ponovno gurnuo natrag u korice.

en: He twitched a curtain back to watch those men marching past. Probably he should have been moved by their loyalty. His father would have flapped a half-clenched fist around and trotted out some patriotic platitude. But Orso found himself wondering what strange combination of doubts and desires compelled each individual to subsume themselves into this metal mass, plodding towards their own destruction rather than making the eminently sensible choice to run like hell the other way.
bs: Zastor pomaknu u stranu kako bi promatrao one vojnike što su marširali mimo. Vjerojatno su ga trebala dirnuti njihova odanost. Njegov otac mahao bi polustisnutom šakom i izbacivao kakve domoljubne općepoznate istine. No Orso se zapita koja čudna mješavina sumnji i želja nagoni svakog pojedinca da se utopi u toj čeličnoj masi i klipsa ususret vlastitom uništenju umjesto da donese krajnje razumnu odluku i pobjegne glavom bez obzira na drugu stranu.

en: Mostly that he was bored and he wanted to fight someone, Clover imagined, and there’d been no one big enough within arm’s reach.
bs: Uglavnom to da mu je dosadno i da se želi s nekim potući, pomislio je Klover, a na dohvat ruke nije bilo nikoga dovoljno krupnog.

en: Barezin gave a cavalier salute, caught hold of his saddle horn, bounced a couple of times and then, with some subtle shoving from one of his aides, hauled himself up and turned his mount towards the west.
bs: Barezin mu domahne s viteškim prezirom, uhvati se za sedlenu kvrgu, poskoči nekoliko puta i zatim se, uz prikriveno guranje jednog od svojih pobočnika, nekako ispetlja gore i okrene konja prema zapadu.

en: The forces of the Open Council were gathered on the far left. Yellow blocks, red blobs, blue wedges, bright flags streaming overhead. Their wondrous variety suggested a lack of coordination, but also spoke strongly to the breadth of the coalition against him.
bs: Snage Otvorenog Vijeća bile su okupljene posve na lijevoj strani. Žuti blokovi, crvene mrlje, plavi klinovi, jarke zastave što su lepršale visoko iznad njih. Ta je šarolika raznolikost ukazivala na manjak koordinacije, ali i glasno svjedočila o širini koalicije uperene protiv njega.

en: “Alas, the younger generation refuses to honour the debts of the older. The debts that put them where they are. My master will ensure there is a reckoning, depend on that.”
bs: — Nažalost, mlađa generacija odbija ispoštovati dugove starije. Dugove koji su ih doveli ondje gdje jesu. Moj gospodar pobrinut će se da uslijedi naplata, budite uvjereni u to.

en: Orso laughed so hard he snorted sherry out of his nose, had to submit to a dabbing down by his footman while he continued to helplessly giggle.
bs: Orso se tako glasno nasmija da mu je šeri grunuo iz nosa, te je morao trpjeti brisanje koje mu je priredio sobar dok se i dalje nemoćno kikotao.

en: “How could I sit through this?” snapped Savine, standing with jaw, fists and bladder clenched in a paralysis of helpless fury.
bs: — Kako bih mogla sjediti i gledati ovo? kresnu Savin stojeći stisnute čeljusti, šaka i mjehura u paralizi bespomoćnog bijesa.

en: “Cannon will fire in order from my right,” he roared, holding up his fist, “and continue firing until the order is given to cease!”
bs: — Topovi će opaliti redom s moje desne strane, zaurlao je, podižući stisnutu šaku, i nastaviti paljbu dok se ne izdade zapovijed za prekid!

en: Clover winced. What the hell Stour planned to do with a hill in the middle of Midderland was anyone’s guess. Graze sheep on it? But the Great Wolf wanted it. So that was that.
bs: Klover se trgnu. Bog sveti zna što je Staur namjeravao s brdom usred Miderlanda. Pasti ovce na njemu? Ali Veliki Vuk ga je htio. Prema tome, stvar je bila jasna.

en: The plan had been so simple. How could it have come apart so badly? Confusion in combat was one thing, but he’d lost control of his army before they’d made the slightest contact with the enemy. He stared over at the Open Council’s self-inflicted chaos on the right, then at Stour’s self-inflicted chaos on the left, then at the earthworks straight ahead. He took a long breath.
bs: Plan je bio tako jednostavan. Kako se mogao tako loše raspasti? Zbrka u borbi bila je jedno, ali izgubio je kontrolu nad vojskom prije nego što su ostvarili i najmanji kontakt s neprijateljem. Zagledao se u kaos što su ga pripadnici Otvoreno Councila sami sebi stvorili s desne strane, potom u Staurov samonametnuti kaos s lijeve, pa u utvrde ravno pred sobom. Duboko je udahnuo.

en: “Lord Steebling owns most of this land,” said Savine through gritted teeth. “Leo says we’re here to support his rights, not to take them away.”
bs: — Lord Steebling posjeduje većinu ove zemlje, prozborila je Savin stisnutih zuba. — Leo kaže da smo ovdje kako bismo podržali njegova prava, a ne da mu ih oduzmemo.

en: He slid the warhammer from his belt and felt the steel haft tight in his grip. Fit there, like a key in a lock. He bared his teeth and walked faster.
bs: Izvukao je ratni čekić iz pojasa i osjetio kako mu čelična drška čvrsto leži u stisku. Pristajala mu je ondje poput ključa u bravi. Ogolio je zube i ubrzao korak.

en: Like the Arch Lector, standing in his pure white coat on the summit of the hill. That hard-faced woman, too. Most frightening pair o’ bastards he ever saw. Looked like they never felt a human thing between ’em. He swallowed as he glanced away, swabbed the cannon down and left it steaming.
bs: Poput Arhilektora, koji je stajao u svom snježnobijelom kaputu na vrhu brda. I ona žena oštra lica. Najstrašniji par gadova što ih je ikad vidio. Izgledali su kao da nikad u životu nisu osjetili ništa čovječno. Progutao je knedlu i odvratio pogled, oprao top i ostavio ga da se puši.

en: He turned over and shuffled through a slurry of fallen fruit to a twisted tree trunk where several other Kantics were sheltering, along with a Union man in the oddest uniform, half-green, half-brown. He realised as he got close that the man was dead, and the brown half was blood from his arm, which was utterly mangled. He pushed the corpse away with his shoe and wriggled into the place it had occupied, and did not even feel ashamed at his mistreatment of the dead.
bs: Okrenuo se i oteturao kroz kašu od opalog voća do iskrivljena debla stabla pod kojim se sklanjalo nekoliko drugih Kantika, zajedno s Unijinim vojnikom u najčudnovatijoj odori, napola zelenoj, napola smeđoj. Kad se primaknuo, shvatio je da je čovjek mrtav, a ona smeđa polovina zapravo bijaše krv iz njegove ruke, koja je bila strašno unakažena. Odgurnuo je leš cipelom i ugurao se na mjesto koje je ovaj dotad zauzimao, ne osjećajući ni trunku srama zbog svoga nepoštovanja prema mrtvima.

en: He shoved a low branch aside and was out from among the trees. Things were no less confused in the open. Dead and wounded everywhere. One dissolving unit was half moving forward, half back, breaking open in the middle and scattering yellow-jacketed men in every direction. A riderless horse frisked maddened through the chaos, empty stirrups bouncing at its flanks.
bs: Odgurnuo je nisku granu i izbio iz šikare. Na čistini nije ništa manje vladao kaos. Mrtvi i ranjeni ležali su posvuda. Jedna se razbijena postrojba napola kretala naprijed, napola natrag, pucajući po sredini i rasipajući vojnike u žutim jaknama na sve strane. Konj bez jahača mahnito je jurišao kroz metež, dok su mu prazni stremeni udarali o bokove.

en: “Damn it,” he whispered, giving his horse a moment to rest and easing his helmet back to wipe his sweaty forehead.
bs: — Prokletstvo, prošaptao je, dopustivši konju da malo odmori i pomaknuvši kacigu unatrag kako bi obrisao znojno čelo.
