Just to blow away the cobwebs. “Someone should bloody do something.” As the burning at the back of his nose faded, that feeling became sharper. So sharp it made him shiver, the hairs on the backs of his arms standing up. You could try doing something to be proud of, his mother had said. Might this be his chance? He had scarcely eve
bs: — Oprosti! reče Orso. — Užasno mi je žao, ali… Sjevernjaci! Napali su! Lavovi i vukovi i što god već! Zgrabio je svoju kutijicu i ušmrkao prstohvat bisernog praha u svaku nosnicu. Tek toliko da otjera paučinu. — Netko bi, do vraga, trebao nešto poduzeti. Kako je žarenje u korijenu nosa jenjavalo, taj se osjećaj izoštrio. Toliko oštro da ga je prožela jeza, a dlačice na rukama mu se nakostriješile. Mogao bi pokušati učiniti nešto na što bi bio ponosan, rekla mu je majka. Bi li ovo mogla biti njeg

en: They looked at each other for a moment, then both burst out laughing. “You’ve a hell of a sense of humour,” said Orso’s father, raising his glass in a little toast. “No one could ever deny that.”
bs: Pogledali su se na trenutak, a zatim prasnuli u smijeh. — Imaš paklen smisao za humor, reče Orsin otac, podižući čašu u kratkoj zdravici. — To nitko nikada ne bi mogao poreći.

en: “Always, young pup!” The king sprang forward, jabbing. Their long steels feathered together, pinged and scraped. The king stabbed with his short steel but Orso caught it on his own, held it, turned. They broke apart, circling one another, Orso’s eyes on the point of his father’s long steel, but flicking occasionally to his leading foot. His Majesty had a habit of twisting it before he struck.
bs: — uvijek, mladunče! Kralj iskoči naprijed, zadajući udarac. Njihovi su se dugi čelici susreli, zazvonili i sastrugali. Kralj ubode svojim kratkim čelikom, ali Orso ga dočeka svojim, zadrži ga i okrene. Razdvojili su se, kružeći jedan oko drugoga, Orsovih očiju uprtih u Kruna očeva dugog čelika, ali povremeno bi pogledom švignuo prema njegovu prednjem stopalu. Vaša Uzvišenosti imalo je naviku zakrenuti ga prije nego što bi udarilo.

en: “Two to one,” said Orso, slashing at the air. Wouldn’t do to let the old man win too easily. No one ever values what they get without trying, after all.
bs: — Dva prema jedan, rekao je Orso, sijekući zrak. Ne bi bilo dobro pustiti starca da pobijedi previše lako. Naposljetku, nitko ne cijeni ono što dobije bez imalo truda.

en: “True enough. But it’s the enemies inside our borders that cost me sleep. The wars in Styria have left everyone out of pocket and out of patience. The Open Council never stops complaining. If the nobles didn’t hate each other even more than me, I swear they’d already be in open rebellion. The peasants may have quieter voices but they’re every bit as dissatisfied. I face disloyalty everywhere.”
bs: — Istina. Ali neprijatelji unutar naših granica su ti koji mi kradu san. Ratovi u Stiriji ostavili su svakoga bez novca i strpljenja. Vijeće se nikada ne prestaje žaliti. Kunem se, da plemići ne mrze jedni druge još više nego mene, već bi bili u otvorenoj pobuni. Seljaci možda imaju tiše glasove, ali su jednako nezadovoljni. Svugdje nailazim na nelojalnost.

en: “Two each!” cackled Orso’s father. “Nothing like a bit of self-pity to bring the hothead rushing in!”
bs: — Dvaput za svakoga! kreštavo se nasmijao Orsov otac. — Nema ničeg boljeg od malo samosažaljenja da potakne usijanu glavu na brzopleto trčanje!

en: “Well, they’re bloody good stories!” The king straightened a moment, lowering his steels and giving Orso a quizzical little frown. “You really want this, don’t you?”
bs: — Pa, to su krvavo dobre priče! Kralj se na trenutak uspravi, spustivši mač i uputivši Orsu znatiželjan, sitan mrki Oko. — Ti to zbilja želiš, zar ne?

en: “Then I bloody well will!” He’d got all he’d get by losing. He felt like winning for once. “Defend yourself, Your Majesty!”
bs: — Onda ću, u pičku materinu, i podići! Dobio je sve što je mogao izvući kroz poraz. Osjećao je želju da jednom u životu pobijedi. — Brani se, Vaša Uzvišenosti!

en: “People say we can expect no better with a woman leading our troops.” Savine lunged, steel clashing as Gorst caught her sword on his own and steered it wide.
bs: — Folk govore da ne možemo očekivati ništa bolje kad žena vodi naše trupe. Savine iskoči, čelik zazveči dok Gorst uhvati njezin mač svojim i skrene ga u stranu.

en: She darted at Gorst as if to go right, switched to the left with a savage cut at head height. He dropped points and jerked away, fast as a snake in spite of his size, eyes focused on the blade as it whistled past his nose.
bs: Nasrnula je na Gorsta kao da će krenuti udesno, pa se prebacila ulijevo divljačkim zamahom u visini glave. On spusti vrhove i trzne se u stranu, brz poput zmije unatoč svojoj veličini, očiju prikovanih za oštricu koja je zazviždala pokraj njegova nosa.

en: Savine took a hard breath, pulling her padded tunic open to let some air in. She had sweated clean through her shirt. She wondered, as she scrubbed her shaved head with a towel, whether the fine gentlemen of the Solar Society would recognise her now, without powder, jewels, dress, wig. More than likely they would smell money through the sweat and swarm around her just the same.
bs: Savine udahnu zrak punim plućima, otkopčavajući podstavljenu tuniku kako bi pustila malo zraka. Bila se oznojila do gole kože ispod košulje. Dok je ribala obrijanu glavu ručnikom, zapitala se bi li je fini Majstor iz Solarnog društva sada prepoznao, bez pudera, dragulja, haljine i perike. Veća je vjerojatnost da bi nanjušili novac kroz znoj i navalili na nju potpuno isto.

en: Her father gave a snort of disgust, bitter even for him. “The moment your arse hits the wood, you realise what they’re worth. You think the Closed Council really rule? Or the king and queen? We’re all no more than dancing puppets. There to draw the eye. To take the blame.”
bs: Otac joj odbrunu s gnušanjem, gorkim čak i za njega. — Čim ti guzica dotakne drvo, shvatiš koliko zapravo vrijede. Misliš li da Zatvoreno vijeće doista vlada? Ili kralj i kraljica? Svi smo mi tek pokretne lutke. Tu da privučemo Oko. Da primimo krivnju na sebe.

en: “We never left it.” She parried, and again, sidestepped a sluggish lunge. For a man renowned for his ferocity, Gorst was scarcely hitting at all. “Prices are tumbling up there. Do I sell out or get deeper in?”
bs: — Nikad ga nismo ni napustili. Ona odbi napad i ponovno izbječe trome nasrtaje. Za čovjeka poznatog po svojoj žestokosti, Gorst jedva da je ikako udarao. — Cijene ondje padaju. Da rasprodam sve ili da zagrizem dublje?

en: “Swords are always a good investment,” admitted the Arch Lector as he watched her swat Gorst’s away with her own.
bs: — Mačevi su uvijek dobra investicija, prizna Vrhovni Lektor promatrajući je kako vlastitim mačem odbija Gorstov.

en: “I want to know how it feels to be attacked by a dangerous man who means it.” Savine set herself again, confident in her stance, confident in her grip, confident in her abilities. “Otherwise what’s the point?”
bs: — Želim znati kakav je osjećaj kad te napadne opasan muškarac koji to misli ozbiljno. Savine se ponovno namjestila, sigurna u svoj stav, sigurna u svoj stisak, sigurna u svoje sposobnosti. — Inače, čemu sve ovo?

en: She had not been ready for his strength after all. The force of it numbed her arm from fingertips to shoulder, rattled the teeth in her head. She stumbled back, gasping, but his short steel was already coming at her, crashing into her long, ripping it from her numb fingers and sending it skittering across the floor. She flapped blindly with her short, all training and technique forgotten, saw a flash of metal—
bs: Ipak nije bila spremna na njegovu snagu. Silina joj je umrtvila ruku od vrhova prstiju do ramena i zatresla joj zube u glavi. Posrnula je natrag, hvatajući zrak, ali njezin je kratki čelik već išao prema njoj, srušivši se na njezinu dugu oštricu, istrgnuvši joj je iz umrtvljenih prstiju i poslavši je da klizi preko poda. Divlje je mahala kratkim mačem, zaboravivši svu obuku i tehniku, i ugledala bljesak metala –

en: Gorst squatted before her, notched steels in one hand. “I should warn you that I was still holding back.”
bs: Gorst je čučnuo pred njom, držeći u jednoj ruci urezane čelike. — Moram te upozoriti da sam se još suzdržavao.

en: There was a crack, next to a yellowed blister on the limewash. Felt like he’d been staring at it all night. Staring at it as the sun crawled up over the narrow buildings, through the washing strung between them and into the narrow street, through the narrow window and into the one-room cellar they were living in.
bs: Pukotina se nalazila pokraj požutjelog mjehura na vapnenom premazu. Činilo mu se kao da u nju zuri cijelu noć. Zureći dok se sunce uspinjalo iznad tijesnih zgrada, kroz rublje razapeto između njih i u usku ulicu, kroz malen prozor i u jednosobni podrum u kojem su živjeli.

en: They lay there, she looking at him, he not daring to look at her. Not wanting to see the disappointment in her eyes. The worry. The fear. Even if it was only his own disappointment, and worry, and fear reflected back, like in a mirror.
bs: Ležali su ondje, ona gledajući u njega, on ne usuđujući se pogledati je. Ne želeći vidjeti razočaranje u njezinim očima. Brigu. Strah. Čak i ako je to bilo samo njegovo vlastito razočaranje, i briga, i strah koji su se zrcalili, poput odraza u ogledalu.

en: “The farm was done anyway. That life was done. Would’ve been better for you and May if I’d never come back.”
bs: — Farma je ionako propala. Taj je život gotov. Bilo bi bolje za tebe i Mej da se nikad nisam vratio.

en: Cadman’s Ales was printed in gilded paint above the sliding warehouse doors, the bang and clatter of work booming from inside. A brewery. He’d spent half his time in Styria drunk and the rest aiming to get drunk. He’d promised no trouble, and he knew that for him, every bottle had trouble at the bottom.
bs: Cadman’s Ales bila su ispisana pozlaćenom bojom iznad kliznih vrata skladišta, dok je tutnjava i larma rada bučala iznutra. Pivovara. Proveo je pola svog vremena u Stiriji pijan, a ostatak s namjerom da se napije. Obećao je da neće biti troblija, a znao je da za njega svaka boca na dnu nosi nevolju.

en: “Can’t say I do,” muttered Broad, thinking of his own valley. The green trees in the breeze, the green grass soft around his ankles. He knew things were always better in your memory and the farm had been hard work for lean rewards, but it had been green. There was nothing green in Valbeck. Except the river, maybe, stained with great coloured smears from the dyeing works upstream.
bs: — Ne bih rekao, promrmlja Brod, misleći na svoju dolinu. Zeleno drveće na povjetarcu, meka zelena trava oko gležnjeva. Znao je da je u sjećanju sve uvijek ljepše, a farma je značila Trdak rad za mršave plodove, ali bila je zelena. U Valbeku ničega zelenog nije bilo. Osim možda rijeke, umrljane velikim šarenim mrljama iz tvornica boja uzvodno.

en: “True enough,” said the old man, right away making Broad wish he’d never spoken. “Why, I remember back when I was a lad—”
bs: — Istina, reče starac, čime je Brod odmah požalio što je uopće progovorio. — Znaš, sjećam se kad sam bio mladić…

en: Took everything he had not to smash this bastard’s skull. But he’d promised Liddy. So Broad just took a step forwards, so the spit from his bared teeth flecked the man’s scarred cheek.
bs: Trebalo mu je sve što ima da ne smrska lubanju tom gadnom stvoru. Ali obećao je Lidi. Zato Brod samo zakorači naprijed, tako da ga je pljuvačka s njegovih ogoljenih zuba poprskala po ožiljku na obrazu.

en: “The decent thing.” Broad winced as he worked his fingers open. Seemed the only time they didn’t hurt was when his fists were clenched. “Don’t even know what that is any more.”
bs: — Ono što je pošteno. Brod se zgrozio dok je razgibavao prste. Činilo se da ga ne bole jedino kad su mu šake bile stisnute. — Više ni sam ne znam što je to.

en: A lean man with a sandy beard and a stained apron had come striding out of the brewery, hands on hips. Broad knew the face, but it took a while to riddle out where he’d seen it before and slot it into the world he lived in now. “Sarlby?”
bs: Mršav čovjek pješčane brade i umrljane pregače krupnim je koracima izišao iz pivovare, držeći ruke na bokovima. Brod je prepoznao lice, ali trebalo mu je vremena da dokuči gdje ga je prije vidio i smjesti ga u svijet u kojem sada živi. — Sarlbi?

en: “Then you’re hired.” Malmer dipped his pen, calmly tapped it off and let it hover over his ledger. “So… Bull? Or Broad?”
bs: — Onda si primljen. Malmer je umočio pero, mirno ga otresao i pustio da lebdi iznad knjige. — Dakle… Bull? Ili Brod?

en: Sarlby didn’t hear that, either. He’d always been a great one for not hearing things he didn’t want to. Maybe everyone is. He leaned close, like he’d a secret to share. “You heard of the Breakers?”
bs: Sarlbi ni to nije čuo. Oduvijek je bio majstor u nečujnosti onoga što nije želio čuti. Možda su svi takvi. Nagnuo se blizu, kao da ima tajnu za podijeliti. — Jesi li čuo za Lomljače?

en: “Maybe.” Broad felt a tickle of excitement, a stab of joy, but he pushed it away, twisted his own hand up into his sleeve as far as it would go. “But I’ve fought enough.”
bs: — Možda. Brod osjeti trnce uzbuđenja, probod radosti, ali ga odgurne, zavukavši vlastitu ruku u rukav koliko je god mogao. — Ali ja sam se dovoljno borio.

en: She glanced each way, but the drizzle was on their side, the lane almost empty. The blood thudded in her head as she walked to the gate. Fear creeping up her throat and making her want to rush, want to shout. She told herself she’d been in tighter corners and knew it was true. She kept her breaths deep, her steps slow.
bs: Osvrnula se na obje strane, no izmaglica je bila na njihovoj strani, a ulica gotovo pusta. Krv joj je udarala u sljepoočnice dok je koračala prema vratima. Strah joj se penjao uz grlo, tjerajući je da potrči, da vikne. Govorila je sebi da je bila u težim situacijama i znala je da je to istina. Disala je duboko, koračala polako.

en: A waft of heat spilled from inside. The furnaces, and the engines, and the forges still giving off a welcoming glow. It’d never be cold in here, never be dark. Vick picked out the black outlines of the ironwork. The skeleton of the building. The pillars where they’d pack the powder.
bs: Val topline sukljao je iz unutrašnjosti. Peći, strojevi i kovačnice još su isijavali dobrodošao žar. Ovdje nikad neće biti hladno, nikad mračno. Vik je razabrala crne obrise željeznih konstrukcija. Kostur zgrade. Stupove uz koje će nagurati barut.

en: She helped him up, nearly falling herself, pulled him on, her breath and his hissing and wheezing, their slapping footfalls echoing from the roof high above. She glanced back, saw lights twinkling, a flicker of movement, heard shouts in the darkness.
bs: Pomogla mu je ustati, zamalo i sama pala, vukla ga dalje; dah im je hropio i pištao, a bat njihovih koraka odzvanjao je s krova visoko iznad njih. Osvrnula se, ugledala treperava svjetla, plamteći pokret i čula povike u tmini.

en: “No,” she hissed. “No, no, no!” She had her hands to his throat but it was ripped right open, blood welling black. Nothing she could do. Her hands were sticky to the elbows already. Her trousers soaked with blood as it spread in a great warm slick.
bs: — Ne, siknula je. — Ne, ne, ne! Pritiskala je rukama njegov grkljan, ali bio je potpuno razrezan, a krv je navirala Black poput ugljena. Nije mogla ništa učiniti. Ruke su joj već do laktova bile ljepljive. Hlače su joj se natopile krvlju dok se širila u velikoj, toploj lokvi.

en: He wasn’t tall, but solid as a tree, great meaty gut, great meaty forearms, great meaty neck and jowls, thumbs tucked into a weathered sword-belt. He might’ve been the same height as Rikke, but easily twice her weight. One of his cheeks was all puckered with an old scar.
bs: Nije bio visok, ali bio je čvrst poput stabla, s velikim mesnatim trbuhom, velikim mesnatim podlakticama, velikim mesnatim vratom i podbratkom, palčeva zataknutih za iznošen opasač za mač. Možda je bio iste visine kao Rike, ali zasigurno dvostruko teži. Jedan mu je obraz bio naboran od starog ožiljka.

en: She knew it now. A rocky edge, sprouting with sick grass, clung to by stunted little trees, beaten water thundering below. She saw Isern spring, arching back in the air, spear over her head. She saw her clear the gap, a daunting four strides wide at least, roll through the wet moss and ferns clinging to the far side and come smoothly to her feet.
bs: Sada je to znala. Stjenovit rub, iznikao bolesnom travom, za koji su se držala zakržljala stabla, dok je ispod tutnjala razbijesnjela voda. Vidjela je Izern kako skače, izvijajući se u zraku s kopljem iznad glave. Vidjela je kako preskače ponor, Brod barem četiri zastrašujuća koraka, kako se kotrlja kroz mokru mahovinu i paprat na suprotnoj strani i glatko se dočekuje na noge.

en: Earth thudded into her stomach and drove all her wind out in a great spitty wheeze. She clutched desperately at wet leaves, wet roots, wet grass, no strength, no breath, dirt sprinkling in her eyes as she started sliding over the edge, fingernails uselessly scrabbling.
bs: Country joj je udarila u trbuh i izbila sav zrak iz pluća u hropcu popraćenom pljuvačkom. Očajnički se hvatala za mokro lišće, mokro korijenje, mokru travu, bez snage, bez daha, Country joj je sipala u oči dok je počela kliziti preko ruba, a nokti su joj beskorisno grebali po tlu.

en: She looked over her shoulder, through the slackening rain saw dogs yapping and growling and prowling at the ravine’s edge and, a few strides above them, a man kneeling in the trees. Close enough she could see the frown on his dirty face, the frayed edge of his archery guard, the bow drawn in his hand.
bs: Osvrnula se preko ramena i kroz kišu koja je slabjela ugledala pse kako laju, reže i njuškaju na rubu klanca, a nekoliko koraka iznad njih čovjeka kako kleči među stablima. Bio je dovoljno blizu da je mogla razaznati mrštenje na njegovu prljavom licu, otrcani rub njegova štitnika za luk i zategnutu tetivu u njegovoj ruci.

en: There was a bead of blood on the tip of her forefinger. Arrowhead must’ve grazed it. And a quivering shiver went all the way through her. She hadn’t really believed it till this moment, not even when she saw Uffrith burning, just like in her dream. But now there was no denying it.
bs: Na vrhu kažiprsta blistala je kapljica krvi. Kruna strijele ju je jamačno okrznuo. Prošla ju je groznička Šivers od pete do glave. Do ovog trenutka u to zapravo nije vjerovala, čak ni kad je vidjela Afrit kako gori, baš kao u snu. No sada se to nije moglo poreći.

en: She thought she heard fighting behind them. Men screaming. Dogs whimpering. Scrape and clatter of steel. The trees echoed with it, everywhere and nowhere. Branches whipped at her and Rikke clawed them away, broke through into a boggy clearing. The rain was down to a drizzle, a broken wall of mossy rock ahead, slick with trickling water.
bs: Učinilo joj se da iza njih čuje borbu. Ljude kako vrište. Pse kako cvile. Struganje i zveckanje čelika. Stabla su odjekivala tim zvukovima, svuda i nigdje. Grane su je šibale, a Rike ih je razmicala, probivši se do blatnjave čistine. Kiša je oslabila u rosulju, a pred njima se uzdizao slomljeni zid mahovinom obraslih stijena, sklizak od vode koja se slijevala niz njega.

en: Wet leaves rustled and a man stepped into the clearing. A big man in a weather-stained coat, holding a scarred shield and a sword with a silver letter near the hilt. Even through the grey hair hanging lank across his face, Rikke could see the awful scar, from his forehead through his brow and across his cheek to the corner of his mouth, and in the misshapen socket of his left eye there was no eye at all, but a bright ball of dead metal, gleaming as the sun broke through above.
bs: Mokro lišće je zašuštalo i muškarac je zakoračio na čistinu. Krupan čovjek u kaputu umrljanom od nevremena, držeći izbrazdan štit i mač sa srebrnim slovom blizu balčaka. Čak i kroz sijedu kosu koja mu je mlitavo visjela preko lica, Rike je mogla vidjeti užasan ožiljak, od čela preko obrve i obraza do kuta usana, a u izobličenoj duplji njegova lijeva oka nije bilo oka, već sjajna kugla mrtvog metala, koja je zasvijetlila kad je sunce probilo oblake iznad njih.

en: “Don’t doubt it.” Shivers puffed out cheeks scattered with silver stubble as he squatted beside her. “But you’ve got the arrow.” And he poked at it with one big finger and made her grimace.
bs: — Ne sumnjam u to. Šivers napuha obraze prošarane srebrnom bradom dok je čučnuo pored nje. — Ali imaš strijelu. I gurne je jednim velikim prstom, natjeravši je da se grimasom zgrči.

en: Clover treated her to his aggrieved look. “As do the broadly sober.” He’d a wonderful aggrieved look. Lots of practice. “I find myself aggrieved. Have you ever seen me lose a fight on account of drunkenness?”
bs: Klover je počasti svojim uvrijeđenim pogledom. — Kao i oni koji su uglavnom trijezni." Imao je prekrasan uvrijeđen Oko. Mnogo vježbe. — Osjećam se povrijeđeno. Jesi li me ikada vidjela izgubiti u borbi zbog pijanstva?

en: “She came through right where you were supposed to be!” snapped a bastard of Stour’s called Greenway. If legends were built on sneering, he’d have had quite a place in the songs. “Did you see her?”
bs: — Prošla je točno tamo gdje si ti trebao biti! odbrusi Staurov kopile po imenu Grinvej. Da se legende grade na podsmjehu, zauzeo bi prilično mjesto u pjesmama. — Jesi li je vidio?

en: Clover shrugged it off. “I’m eager to serve, great prince, but I can’t just turn into a butterfly. Your father sent me for my cunning, not my running. Why, you might as well order the river to blow and the wind to flow.”
bs: Klover slegne ramenima. — Željan sam služiti, Great prinče, ali ne mogu se tek tako pretvoriti u leptira. Tvoj me otac poslao zbog moje lukavosti, a ne zbog brzine. Pa, mogao bi jednako tako narediti rijeci da puše, a vjetru da teče.

en: Wonderful and Clover burst out laughing at the exact same time. He leaned forward, hands on his knees, and she leaned back, fist on his shoulder, and no doubt they made quite a picture chortling away but they really couldn’t help ’emsleves.
bs: Vonderful i Klover prasnuli su u smijeh u istoj sekundi. On se nagnuo naprijed, s rukama na koljenima, a ona se nagnula unatrag, sa šakom na njegovu ramenu, i nedvojbeno su bili prizor dok su se hihotali, ali si nisu mogli pomoći.

en: “It was a bloody one. Sadly, I walked away with the wrong lessons. Enough that I ended up taking a challenge or two myself…” Clover found he was scratching at his scar, and made himself leave it alone. “If you want my advice, stay out of the Circle.”
bs: — Bio je krvav. Nažalost, otišao sam s njega poučen krivim lekcijama. Toliko krivima da sam se i sam upustio u izazov ili dva… Klover primijeti da češka ožiljak pa se prisili spustiti ruku. — Ako želiš moj Vijeće, kloni se Kruga.

en: Stour opened his arms wide, opened his eyes wide, put on the big act. “The only chain I want is a chain of blood!” Made not the slightest sense. How could you make a chain out of blood anyway? Terrible metaphor. But Magweer and Greenway and the rest of the arse-lickers gave a chorus of warlike growls and shaken fists. “I don’t want to be like the Bloody-Nine. I want to be the Bloody-Nine!” Stour hitched his crazed smile a little wider in a reasonable impression of the Bloody-Nine in his worse mo
bs: Staur raširi ruke, razrogači oči i zauze veliku predstavu."Jedini lanac koji ja želim jest lanac od krvi!" Nije imalo nikakvog smisla. Kako uopće napraviti lanac od krvi? Užasna metafora. No Magvir, Grinvej i ostali ulizice ispustiše korus ratničkih reži i uzdignutih šaka."Ne želim biti poput Krvave Devetke. Ja želim biti Krvava Devetka!" Staur razvuče svoj luđački osmijeh još malo šire u prilično vjernoj imitaciji Krvave Devetke u njegovim najgorim trenutcima."Nema slavnijeg čovjeka. Nema straš

en: “Murder the bastard.” Clover grinned up at the blue sky, where the sun was starting to finally show some warmth. “But I wouldn’t want to spoil such a wonderful afternoon with murder, would you?”
bs: — Ubiti kopile. Klover se nasmiješio gledajući u plavo nebo, gdje je sunce napokon počelo pokazivati malo topline. — Ali ne bih htio pokvariti tako divno poslijepodne ubojstvom, zar ne?

en: Leo tossed his shirt over Jurand’s head. “A champion never knows what he’ll have to fight with. That’s why I always let you bastards pick the weapons.” It was a cold morning, so he started bouncing on his toes to get the blood moving. “That’s why I beat Barniva with a heavy sword, and Antaup with a spear. Why I beat Whitewater Jin with a mace and you with long and short steels. That’s why I test my archery against Ritter. Used to, that is.” The poor dead fool. “But I never yet beat Glaward with
bs: Leo baci košulju Džurandi preko glave. — Prvak nikad ne zna s čime će se morati boriti. Zato uvijek dopuštam vama gadovima da birate oružje." Bilo je hladno jutro, pa poče poskakivati na prstima kako bi potaknuo krvotok. — Zato sam pobijedio Barnivu teškim mačem, a Antaup kopljem. Zato sam pobijedio Whitewater Jina buzdovanom, a tebe dugim i kratkim čelikom. Zato sam testirao svoje streličarstvo protiv Rittera. Nekad, barem." Jadni mrtvi luđak. — Ali još nikad nisam pobijedio Glavarda golim ruka

en: “This is manly,” she said, propping a muddy boot on the rail of the fence, its tongue flopping from bodged laces. “Do they charge for the spectacle?”
bs: — Imam oči. Mlađa ga je promatrala podbočivši bradu o dlanove, Šef joj je poskakivala svaki put kad bi nešto žvakala. Doista je imala oči. Velike, posvijetljene i vrlo prodorne.

en: He’d have won no laurels for his acting but Glaward was blessed with more muscle than imagination. He charged in with no caution at all, readying a punch they’d be talking about for years. But Leo had his wits back. He dropped under it, rolled smoothly, caught Glaward’s big calf on the way past and sprang up, pulling the leg with him.
bs: Nije mogao računati na lovorike za glumu, ali Glavard je imao više mišića nego mašte. Jurnuo je bez imalo opreza, spremajući udarac o kojem će se pričati godinama. No Leo je povratio bistrinu uma. Sagnuo se ispod njega, glatko se otkotrljao, uhvatio Glavardovu golemu potkoljenicu u prolazu i skočio, povlačeći nogu sa sobom.

en: She looked him up and down. “Well, he has grown.” And much to his surprise, she threw her arms around him, gripped him behind the head and pressed his face into her shoulder.
bs: Ona ga je odmjerila od glave do pete. — Pa dobro, narastao je. — I na njegovo veliko iznenađenje, zagrlio ga je, uhvatio iza glave i pritisnulo mu lice na svoje rame.

en: Rikke stuck her fists in Leo’s face and pushed a finger up for each point. “I’ve been starved, slapped, pissed on, shot at, chased by dogs, threatened with being fucked by a pig, slept under a hanged man, near fell down a gorge, killed a boy and shat myself, so, you know,” and she shrugged, head falling to one side and her shoulders right up around her ears, “I’m hoping next week’ll be easier going, let’s say that.”
bs: Rike je zabila šake Leoocu u lice i ispružila po jedan prst za svaku stavku. — Bila sam gladna, ošamarena, popišana, na mene su pucali, gonili me psi, prijetili mi da će me silovati svinja, spavala sam ispod obješenog čovjeka, umalo pala u provaliju, ubila dječaka i uneredila se u gaće, tako da, znaš — i slegnula ramenima, pavši glavom na jednu stranu dok su joj se ramena podigla skroz do ušiju — nadam se da će sljedeći tjedan biti lakši, eto toliko.

en: “Better’n being fucked by a pig, I reckon,” said Isern-i-Phail, grunting softly as she lifted her bandaged leg from the fence and turned hobbling away. “I need to steer this leaky skiff back to her father before she drifts off course again. I gave my word!”
bs: — Bolje i to nego da te jebe svinja, rekla bih, dobacila je Izern-i-Fejl, tiho gunđajući dok je podizala zavijenu nogu s ograde i šepajući se udaljila. — Moram ovu šuplju olupinu vratiti njezinu ocu prije nego što opet skrene s kursa. Dala sam riječ!

en: “Well, if you’d rather wrestle…” Antaup licked his finger and thumb and gave that loose curl at the front of his hair a little tweak. “It’d be a shame to leave such a promising field unploughed…”
bs: — Pa, ako bi se radije hrvao… Antaup je liznuo prst i Palioc te malo namjestio onaj opušteni pramen kose na čelu. — Bila bi šteta ostaviti takvo obećavajuće polje nepoorano…

en: A man came in. Or was brought in. He sat in a strange chair on wheels, pushed by a Practical of monstrous size. He was silver-haired, his skin almost as pale as his spotless white coat and deeply lined, as if stretched too tight over the bones. His face was twisted, left eye twitchily narrowed. On his little finger he wore a ring of office with a great purple stone, but even without it there was no mistaking him.
bs: Ušao je muškarac. Ili su ga unijeli. Sjedio je u neobičnoj stolici na kotačima koju je gurao Praktik čudovišne veličine. Kosa mu je bila siva, koža gotovo blijeda poput njegova besprijekorno bijelog kaputa i duboko izbrazdana, kao da je prenapeta preko kostiju. Lice mu je bilo izobličeno, lijevo oko živčano stisnuto u prorez. Na malom prstu nosio je službeni prsten s golemim ljubičastim dragim kamenom, ali i bez njega nije ga se moglo zamijeniti ni s kim drugim.

en: Arch Lector Glokta watched her, the trace of a smile on his twisted face, as though he guessed her every thought. “And the clothes, please.”
bs: Vrhovni lektor Glokta promatrao ju je s tragom osmijeha na izobličenom licu, kao da naslućuje svaku njezinu misao. — A odjeću, molim te.

en: She made her own chair squeal as she stood, ignoring the ache in her stiff hip. “Don’t worry.” And she shook the shirt out and started pulling it on.
bs: Natjerala je vlastitu stolicu da zaškripi dok je ustajala, ignorirajući bol u ukočenom kuku. — Ne brinite." Protresla je košulju i počela je navlačiti.

en: She had a sense he saw through her. “If they did not, you have demonstrated your commitment. If they did, you have gone one better and demonstrated your loyalty.”
bs: Imala je osjećaj da vidi kroz nju. — Ako nisu, dokazala si svoju predanost. Ako jesu, učinila si i korak više te dokazala svoju lojalnost.

en: “Because that is the nature of people. And their little more must be taken from someone else, and that someone else will be less than delighted. One cannot eliminate unhappiness any more than one can eliminate darkness. The goal of government, you see,” and the Arch Lector prodded at the air with his bony forefinger, “is to load the unhappiness onto those least able to make you suffer for it.”
bs: — Jer to je ljudska priroda. A njihovo "malo više" mora se uzeti nekome drugome, a taj netko drugi neće biti nimalo oduševljen. Nesreća se ne može iskorijeniti ništa više nego što se može iskorijeniti tama. Cilj vlasti, vidiš – i Arhilektor je koščatim kažiprstom probadao zrak – "jest svaliti nesreću na one koji su najmanje sposobni natjerati te da zbog toga patiš.

en: Just one more try, maybe. Vick sat forward, clasping her hands. “With your permission—I think the boy Tallow might be turned.”
bs: Možda još samo jedan pokušaj. Vik se nagnula naprijed, sklopivši ruke. — Uz vaše dopuštenje, mislim da bi se dječak Talou mogao pridobiti.

en: He looked at her for a long moment, and she wondered if he might scream insults at her. If he might kick and scratch and go wild. But he was too clever or too scared. He just looked down at the stained tabletop and said, “Oh.”
bs: On je promatraše dugačak trenutak, a ona se upita hoće li je početi zasipati uvredama, hoće li početi udarati nogama, grepsti i pomahnitati. No bio je odviše pametan ili odviše prestrašen. Samo je oborio Oko na umrljanu ploču stola i prozborio: — Aha.

en: “So you understand what you owe me.” She got up, slipping the key out, and unlocked his chains. Then she tossed him his clothes. “Get dressed. Then get some sleep. We’ll be leaving for Valbeck in the morning. Need to know where those dullards got three barrels of Gurkish Fire.”
bs: — Da shvatiš što mi duguješ. Ustala je, izvukla ključ i otključala njegove okove. Zatim mu je bacila odjeću. — Obuci se. A onda se naspavaj. Ujutro krećemo za Valbek. Moram doznati gdje su oni tupavci nabavili tri bačve Gurkish vatre.

en: Brint gave a bitter snort. “I only wish there’d be one! Those money-grubbing swindlers on the Closed Council refuse to release the funds. Can you believe it?”
bs: Brint gorko odvrati: — Samo bih volio da ga i bude! Oni gramzivi prevaranti u Zatvorenom Vijeću odbijaju odobriti sredstva. Možete li to vjerovati?

en: “My father has promised me a battalion of the King’s Own, as well as his First Guard, Bremer dan Gorst, who I understand is worth a company himself,” and he gave a laugh which Brint by no means returned, “but I do require… somewhere in the region of, well, five thousand more?”
bs: — Otac mi je obećao bataljun Kraljeve garde, kao i svog prvog čuvara, Bremer dan Gorsta, za kojeg sam čuo da vrijedi koliko i cijela satnija, nasmijao se, dok mu Brint nimalo nije uzvratio, ali trebam… recimo, još pet tisuća Folk?

en: “Your Highness,” and Lord Marshal Brint gave a sigh that bespoke an infinite weariness, “it is always a question of money.”
bs: — Vaša Uzvišenosti, uzdahnuo je lord maršal Brint uz izraz beskrajnog umora, uvijek je pitanje novca.

en: “I wish he’d asked my opinion.” Orso gave what he hoped was a disarming chuckle. “I scarcely want one nation, let alone two.”
bs: — Volio bih da je pitao mene za mišljenje. Orso se nasmijao onim što je trebalo djelovati razoružavajuće. — Jedva da želim jednu naciju, a kamoli dvije.

en: Orso restrained his mounting frustration. “But you must see we have to do something about these Northmen!”
bs: Orso je suspregnuo rastuću frustraciju. — Ali morate shvatiti da moramo nešto poduzeti o ovim Sjevernjacima!

en: “Your Eminence,” said Orso. “Thank you so much for seeing me at such short notice. I know you must be a very busy man.”
bs: — Vaša Eminencijo, reče Orso. — Hvala vam što ste me primili u ovako kratkom roku. Znam da morate biti jako zauzet čovjek.

en: “Then I applaud your patriotic sentiments, Your Highness.” To give Glokta his due, he showed not the slightest trace of mockery. “But this is a military matter. Perhaps you should raise it with Lord Marshal Brint—”
bs: — Onda pozdravljam vaše domoljubne osjećaje, Vaša Uzvišenosti. Moralo se priznati Glokti, nije pokazivao ni najmanji trag podsmijeha. — Ali ovo je vojno pitanje. Možda biste to trebali iznijeti pred lorda maršala Brint…

en: A chilly breeze drifted through the Arch Lector’s stark, hard office then, making the great heaps of papers on the tables shift and crackle like restless spirits. For a moment, Orso found himself wondering how many of them were the confessions of guilty traitors. Or innocent ones. But he was decidedly pleased with the way he kept his face blank, despite the sudden surge of guilty horror, not to mention healthy fear, produced by the question. Orso might not have excelled in all the areas his moth
bs: Hladan povjetarac prostrujao je strogim, tvrdim uredom Lektora, tjerajući velike hrpe papira na stolovima da se pomiču i šušte poput nemirnih duhova. Na trenutak se Orso zapitao koliko je među njima priznanja krivih izdajnika. Ili onih nedužnih. No bio je odlučno zadovoljan načinom na koji je zadržao bezizražajno lice, unatoč iznenadnom naletu krivnje i užasa, da ne spominjemo zdrav strah koji je to pitanje izazvalo. Orso možda nije briljirao u svim područjima u kojima bi njegova majka voljela d

en: “Thoroughly modern. In my youth, for someone to make a considerable fortune in that way, let alone a woman, would have been unthinkable. Savine may be a pioneer, but there are others following. We are entering a new age, Your Highness.”
bs: "Temeljito moderno. U mojoj mladosti, da netko tako stekne pozamašno bogatstvo, a kamoli žena, bilo bi nezamislivo. Savine je možda pionirka, ali drugi slijede. Ulazimo u novo doba, Uzvišenost.

en: “Change, Your Highness. At a pace and of a kind that has never been seen before. An order that has stood for centuries buckles and twists. Traditional barriers, however we might try to shore them up, collapse like sandcastles before the tide. Men fear to lose what they have, covet what they do not. It is a time of chaos. Of fear.” The Arch Lector shrugged, tentatively, as though even that gave him pain. “A time of opportunity, if you are as clever as my daughter, but a time of great danger, too.
bs: — Promjene, Uzvišenost. Brzinom i vrstom kakve dosad nisu viđene. Poredak koji je opstajao stoljećima savija se i krivi. Tradicionalne prepreke, ma koliko se trudili poduprijeti ih, ruše se poput pješčanih kula pred plimom. Folk se boje da će izgubiti ono što imaju, a žude za onim što nemaju. Ovo je vrijeme kaosa. Vrijeme straha. Vrhovni Lektor slegnu ramenima, oprezno, kao da mu je i taj pokret zadavao bol. — Vrijeme prilika, ako si mudar poput moje kćeri, ali i vrijeme golemih opasnosti. Nedav

en: “I wish we were free to do what we thought right. I truly do.” The Arch Lector glanced up at a huge, dark portrait on the wall. Some fearsome bald bureaucrat of the past, glowering down watchfully upon the little people. Zoller, maybe. “But we simply cannot risk any overseas adventures, however well intentioned, however deeply desired, however apparently necessary.” He clasped his long, thin hands and gazed levelly at Orso, eyes glittering in skull-like sockets. “Put simply, the government of th
bs: — Volio bih da smo slobodni činiti ono što smatramo ispravnim. Zaista bih volio. Lektor je pogledao prema golemom, tamnom portretu na zidu. Nekakav zastrašujući, ćelavi birokrat iz prošlosti, koji je budno i prijeteći promatrao malene ljude ispod sebe. Možda Zoller. — Ali jednostavno ne možemo riskirati nikakve prekomorske pothvate, ma koliko dobronamjerni bili, ma koliko duboko željeni, ma koliko naizgled nužni. Sklopio je svoje duge, tanke ruke i mirno pogledao Orsa, dok su mu oči svjetlucale

en: “There’s no point bullying that idiot,” said Tunny, managing to smoke a chagga pipe, stare at Orso through narrowed eyes and deal expertly all at once. “He’s an idiot.”
bs: — Nema smisla maltretirati tog idiota, reče Tani, uspijevajući istovremeno pušiti lulu, zuriti u Orsa suženih očiju i vješto dijeliti karte. — On je idiot.

en: “She’s never wrong about numbers,” said Tunny, shifting his chagga pipe from one side of his mouth to the other using only tongue and teeth.
bs: — Ona nikad ne griješi s brojkama, potvrdi Tani, premještajući lulu s chagga duhanom iz jednog kuta usta u drugi služeći se samo jezikom i zubima.

en: “He bloody would be. The only thing he enjoys more than his own suffering is other people’s. Why you play with swords is quite beyond me.”
bs: — Vjerujem da jest. Jedina stvar u kojoj uživa više nego u vlastitoj patnji jest tuđa. Zašto se igraš mačevima, to mi nikako ne ide u glavu.

en: Savine’s turn to sigh. Another of the lord marshal’s tales of derring-do on the frontier and she might be obliged to drown herself in the canal rather than extend it. But business was business.
bs: Došao je red na Savine da uzdahne. Još jedna priča lorda maršala o junačkim pothvatima na granici i možda će biti prisiljena utopiti se u kanalu radije nego ga proširivati. Ali posao je posao.

en: It was an informal event, so it only took four of them to dress her. Freid was handling the wardrobe on her own. Lisbit was face-maid, on paint, powder and perfume. Metello—a hatchet-featured Styrian who had once been chief dresser to the Duchess of Affoia—barely spoke a word of common but expressed herself with unmatched eloquence through the medium of wigs. Zuri, meanwhile, attended to book and jewels and ensured that the others did not make a mess of anything all at once.
bs: Bio je to neobavezan događaj, stoga su joj trebale samo četiri sluškinje da je odjenu. Freid se sama brinula za garderobu. Lisbit je bila zadužena za lice, s bojom, puderom i parfemom. Metelo — Stirijka oštrih crta lica koja je nekoć bila glavna garderobijerka vojvotkinje od Affoije — jedva je govorio opći jezik, ali se izražavala bez premca rječitošću posredstvom perika. Zuri se u međuvremenu bavila knjigama i draguljima te pazila da ostale ne naprave nered u isto vrijeme.

en: People liked to think of beauty as some natural gift, but Savine firmly believed that just about anyone could be beautiful, if they worked hard at it and spent enough money. It was merely a question of emphasising the good, disguising the bad and painfully squeezing the average into the most impressive configuration. Very much like business, really.
bs: Folk su voljeli smatrati ljepotu nekim prirodnim darom, ali Savine je čvrsto vjerovala kako bi otprilike svatko mogao biti lijep ako se u to uloži dovoljno truda i novca. To je naprosto bilo pitanje naglašavanja onoga što je dobro, prikrivanja lošeg i bolnog stiskanja prosječnosti u najimpresivniju moguću formu. Posve nalik biznisu, uistinu.

en: Some might have said that made her self-serving, shallow and poisonous. She would have replied that the self-serving, shallow, poisonous people always seemed to come out on top. Then she would have laughed ever so sweetly, and whispered to Zuri to place a note in the book for their future destruction.
bs: Neki bi rekli da je to čini sebičnom, površnom i otrovnom. Ona bi im odgovorila da se čini kako sebični, površni i otrovni Folk uvijek izlaze kao pobjednici. Zatim bi se nasmijala vrlo slatko i prošaptala Zuri da stavi zabilješku u knjigu za njihovo buduće uništenje.

en: “We should pay him a visit. Make sure our partners realise that our eyes are always on the details. And we have plenty of other interests in Valbeck. There never was a city so ill-conceived, ill-built and ill-tempered, but there really is a great deal of money to be made there. Zuri, clear a few days somewhere in the next month so you and I can—”
bs: — Trebali bismo ga posjetiti. Pobrini se da naši partneri shvate kako su naše oči uvijek uprte u detalje. A imamo i pregršt drugih interesa u Valbeku. Nikada nije postojao grad tako loše osmišljen, loše izgrađen i loše ćudi, ali ondje se uistinu može zaraditi mnogo novca. Zuri, oslobodi nekoliko dana negdje u idućem mjesecu kako bismo ti i ja –

en: Since Savine’s father first introduced her, a friendless exile in desperate need of a position, Zuri had made herself indispensable in a dozen ways. But it was more than that. Savine’s acquaintance was immense. A great web of favours, partnerships and obligations that stretched across the Union and beyond. But the truth was she had no friends at all. Apart from the one she paid.
bs: Otkako ju je Savinin otac prvi put dovio, kao izgnanicu bez igdje ikoga, očajnički potrebnu zaposlenja, Zuri se učinila nezamjenjivom na bezbroj načina. No bilo je tu još nečega. Savinino poznanstvo bilo je golemo. Velika mreža usluga, partnerstava i obveza koja se protezala diljem Unije i dalje. Ali istina je bila da nije imala baš nijednog prijatelja. Osim one koju je plaćala.

en: “Tall tales spread by people who should know better,” said Savine, sternly. “Lisbit, you will be my companion while Zuri is away. You’d enjoy a trip to Valbeck, wouldn’t you?”
bs: — Prazne priče koje šire Folk koji bi trebali znati bolje, reče Savine, strogo. — Lisbit, ti ćeš biti moja pratilja dok je Zuri odsutna. Uživala bi u putu do Valbeka, zar ne?

en: Savine felt that familiar flutter in her stomach, that familiar heat in her face. “When am I due at the Rucksteds’?”
bs: Savine je osjetila onaj poznati leptirić u želucu, onu poznatu toplinu u licu. — Kada moram biti kod Ruckstedovih?

en: Hildi sourly pulled her cap off. She had a surprising mass of pinned-up, pale-blonde hair underneath. Metello gave a hum of interest, hopped from her stool to poke at it with a comb, rubbed a lock between finger and thumb, finally made Hildi squawk as she jerked a strand from her head and held it up to the light. She gave Savine a significant look from under her grey brows.
bs: Hildi kiselo skine kapu. Ispod nje izroni iznenađujuća griva spletene, pepeljastoplave kose. Metelo zazuja od zanimljivosti, poskoči sa stolca da je bocne češljem, protrlja pramen među prstima i napokon natjera Hildi da vrisne kad joj trgnu vlasi s glave i podigne ih prema svjetlu. Ispod sivih obrva uputi Savine značajan Oko.

en: “Talk first?” She narrowed her eyes. She was still pleasantly soft, flushed and shuddery all over, but if he thought to slip something by her, he would have a rude awakening. “What are you after?”
bs: — Razgovarati prvo? — Ona suzi oči. Još je bila ugodno mekana, zajapurena i sva u drhtajima, ali ako je mislio nešto prokrjumčariti pokraj nje, doživio bi grubo buđenje. — Što hoćeš?

en: In fact, she thought she might be the only one who did. “I’m here, aren’t I?” She pulled him back down, and pushed her hand through his hair, and held his head against her chest. “What did the great men tell Your Highness?”
bs: Zapravo, pomislila je da je možda jedina koja ga shvaća. — Tu sam, zar ne?" Povukla ga je natrag dolje, provukla prste kroz njegovu kosu i privila mu glavu na svoja prsa. — Što su Great Folk rekli Vašoj Uzvišenosti?

en: There was a silence. As the expression gradually formed on his face, he looked more suspicious than grateful. And who could blame him? What the hell was she doing? “Just… like that? All of it?”
bs: Nastala je tišina. Kako se izraz postupno oblikovao na njegovu licu, izgledao je više sumnjičavo nego zahvalno. A tko bi ga mogao kriviti? Što je, dovraga, radila? — Samo… tako? Sav novac?

en: “I’ll be in touch,” he whispered in her ear, making her neck tingle. “Or Sworbreck will, at least.” And the door clattered shut behind him.
bs: — Javit ću se, prošaptao joj je na uho, od čega su joj trnci proželi vrat. — Ili će se Svorbrik javiti, barem. I vrata su prasnula za njim.

en: She felt suddenly as weak at the knees as she had when Bremer dan Gorst rammed her into the wall. She had to slump back on Sworbreck’s desk, staring down at her discarded drawers, rumpled on the floor.
bs: Odjednom su joj koljena postala mekana kao u trenutku kad ju je Bremer dan Gorst pribio uz zid. Morala se nasloniti na Svorbrikov stol, zagledana u svoje odbačene gaćice, zgužvane na podu.

en: Broad kept sweeping. He’d learned in Styria there’s a lot of things that are better just not thought about. Couldn’t be a coincidence that the happiest men Broad ever knew were generally the stupidest.
bs: Brod je nastavio mesti. U Stiriji je naučio da postoji mnoštvo stvari o kojima je bolje jednostavno ne razmišljati. Nije moglo biti slučajno da su najsretniji Folk koje je Brod ikad poznavao uglavnom bili i najgluplji.

en: “Aye.” Broad gave a sigh. “Always been good with a needle, Liddy. Good at whatever she turns her hand to. She’s the one with the talent.”
bs: — Da. Brod uzdahnu. — Lidi je oduvijek bila vična igli. Dobra u svemu čega se primi. Ona je ta koja ima talenta.

en: “I’m no fool, Bull. I know what the world is. But maybe we can spread the wealth about a little. Maybe we can take some rich bastards out of those palaces on the hill and some poor families out of those cellars on Meadow Street. Maybe we can give each man an honest wage for an honest day’s work. Stop the false clocks and the fines and the girls pressed into night work. Put an end to the butchers selling tainted meat, and the flour bulked out with chalk, and the ale watered down with rotten water
bs: — Nisam budala, Bull. Znam kakav je svijet. Ali možda možemo malo preraspodijeliti bogatstvo. Možda možemo izvući neke bogate gadove iz onih palača na brdu i neke siromašne obitelji iz onih podruma u Meadow Streetu. Možda možemo svakom čovjeku dati poštenu plaću za pošten rad. Zaustaviti lažne satove, kazne i djevojke prisiljene na noćni rad. Stati na kraj mesarima koji prodaju pokvareno meso, brašnu punjenom kredom i pivu razvodnjenom trulom vodom. Možda možemo barem osigurati da više nema dječ

en: Broad and Sarlby stared at each other, Broad seeing his own helpless horror mirrored in his old comrade’s face.
bs: Brod i Sarlbi zagledali su se jedan u drugoga; Brod je u licu svog starog suborca vidio odraz vlastitog bespomoćnog užasa.

en: A brick came grinding free and the wash of heat made Broad jerk his face away. He wedged the bar in the gap, used it as a lever, popped more bricks out.
bs: Jedna se cigla uz škripu oslobodila, a val vrućine natjera Broda da trzne glavom. Zaglavio je polugu u procjep, iskoristio je kao polugu i izbio još nekoliko cigala.

en: “I thought you said the west side…” Broad turned to see the sweep standing there, the little lad next to him, staring. “I thought you said—”
bs: — Mislio sam da si rekao zapadna strana… Brod se okrene i ugleda dimnjačara kako stoji ondje, a maleni dječak zuri pokraj njega. — Mislio sam da si rekao —

en: Rikke flopped down, misjudged it and sat so hard she bit her tongue and gave her backside quite the bruising. Isern had to shoot out a quick hand to stop her chair going over backwards.
bs: Rike se srušila, krivo procijenila i sjela tako silovito da se ugrizla za jezik i pošteno natukla stražnjicu. Izern je morala hitro ispružiti ruku kako joj se stolica ne bi prevrnula unatrag.

en: “I said shush!” Her cracked voice rang out across the now-silent barn, and her father cleared his throat, and Rikke felt all eyes on her and her face burned and she squashed herself down as low as she could go and took a stealthy slurp from her cup.
bs: "Rekla sam pšššt!" Njezin napukli glas odjeknuo je sada već tihom štalom, otac joj je pročistio grlo, Rike je osjetila kako su sve oči uprte u nju dok joj je lice gorjelo pa se stisnula što je niže mogla i kradomice otpila iz čaše.

en: “I’d like to raise a cup myself!” Rikke clambered onto the table with a hand on her father’s shoulder and held her cup over her head. Ale slopped out and spattered on the wood, though it was already so ale-spattered no one could’ve noticed the difference. “To all o’ you sorry bastards who were so hopelessly lost, but thanks to the tender guidance of Isern-i-Phail, were able to find your way back to me!”
bs: — I ja bih htjela nazdraviti! Rike se popela na stol, oslonivši se rukom na očevo rame, i podigla vrč iznad glave. Pivo se prolilo i poprskalo drvo, premda je ono već bilo toliko natopljeno pivom da nitko ne bi primijetio razliku. — Za sve vas jadne kopiljane koji ste bili tako beznadno izgubljeni, ali ste zahvaljujući nježnom vodstvu Izern-i-Fejl uspjeli pronaći put natrag do mene!

en: “Maybe. But they shouldn’t have to. I’m just not sure…” He frowned out at the barnful of drunk warriors like he hardly saw them. Like he was staring through them with the Long Eye and saw something horrible beyond. “Not sure I got the bones for the fight any more.”
bs: — Možda. Ali ne bi trebali. Samo nisam siguran… Namrštio se gledajući staju punu pijanih ratnika kao da ih jedva vidi. Kao da ih promatra kroz Oko i vidi nešto užasno nasuprot tome. — Nisam siguran imam li više snage za borbu.

en: “Weren’t your fault! Or mine. Scale Ironhand attacked us! Black Calder burned Uffrith! Stour fucking Nightfall chased me through the woods. They trampled your garden…” she finished, lamely.
bs: — Nije bila tvoja krivnja! Ni moja. Ljuska Željezna Ruka nas je napao! Black Kalder je spalio Afrit! Jebeni Staur Najtfol me gonio kroz šumu. Zgazili su tvoj vrt… završila je tiho.

en: “You’ve got bones, Rikke, and you’ve got brains. You like to hide it. Even from yourself, maybe.” He looked out at the room, and the shouting men that filled it. “I reckon they’ll need your bones and your brains, when all this is over. But they’ll need your heart, too. When I’m gone.”
bs: — Imaš ti i kostiju i pameti, Rike. Voliš to skrivati. Možda čak i od same sebe. Pogledao je prostoriju i razularene ljude koji su je ispunjavali. — Mislim da će im trebati tvoje kosti i tvoja pamet kad sve ovo završi. Ali trebat će im i tvoje srce. Kad mene više ne bude.

en: He looked at her hand on his shoulder, then up at her, and didn’t smile at all. “Why were you never scared of me?”
bs: Pogledao je njenu ruku na svom ramenu, zatim nju, i uopće se nije nasmiješio. — Zašto se ti nikad nisi bojala mene?

en: “… but I shan’t cramp you any longer,” Rikke heard her say as she came closer. “Someone has to manage this retreat, after all.”
bs: — … ali neću te više gnjaviti, čula je Rike kako govori dok se približavala. — Netko ipak mora voditi ovo povlačenje.

en: “I noticed,” he said, raising his brows at it. Her thumb, not her chest. Though maybe he was taking a sly look at that, too. She somewhat hoped so but was too drunk to tell. Seemed every word between them had an edge to it. A little danger, like the jabs in a duel. A little thrill, like each breath was a gamble.
bs: "Primijetio sam, rekao je, podignuvši obrve. Njezin Palioc, ne njezina prsa. Iako je možda kriomice bacio Oko i na njih. Pomalo se nadala da jest, ali bila je previše pijana da bi bila sigurna. Činilo se da svaka riječ između njih ima oštricu. Malo opasnosti, poput uboda u dvoboju. Malo uzbuđenja, kao da je svaki dah kockanje.

en: He’d been frowning at first, but she was pleased to see it crumble into a sheepish smile. “You’re right. I’m being a prick.”
bs: U početku se mrštio, no sa zadovoljstvom je primijetila kako mu se lice razvlači u pomalo stidljiv osmijeh. — U pravu si. Ponašam se kao kreten.

en: “Trouble with seeing the future is you don’t want to spoil the surprise.” She stood up, nearly tripping over her own stool, but steadying herself masterfully by clutching at the edge of the table. “I’ll show you.”
bs: — Trobli s viđenjem budućnosti jest u tome što ne želiš pokvariti iznenađenje. Ustane, umalo se spotaknuvši o vlastiti stolac, ali se majstorski osloni uhvativši se za rub stola. — Pokazat ću ti.

en: Then they were kissing, hungry, messy, lips sucking and teeth scraping and tongues lapping and Rikke reflected that she was quite an excellent kisser even if she did say so herself and he wasn’t at all bad either. No point pecking away like a sparrow at the seed. You’ve got to get stuck in. They broke apart to catch their breath and he swayed a bit and wiped his mouth, his eyes darting all over her face in a slightly flustered, slightly excited, slightly drunk sort of way that made her feel flus
bs: Zatim su se poljubili, gladni, neuredni, usne usisavajuće, zubi grebući, jezici lizajući, i Rike je razmišljala da je prilično izvrsna poljubiteljica, barem po svom mišljenju, i da on nije baš loš. Nema smisla pikati kao vrana po sjemenkama. Treba se baciti u to. Razdvojili su se da uhvate dah, on je malo zatreperio, obrisao si usne, a oči su mu lutale po njezinom licu na način koji je bio pomalo zbunjen, pomalo uzbuđen i pomalo pijan, što ju je učinilo zbunjenom, uzbuđenom i pijanom također. Za

en: “Not sure I’ll be this drunk by then,” she said, already wriggling out of her trousers. Before she got them past her hips, her hand slipped and she flopped over and got a mouthful of straw, hissed and spat, giggled and burped, and they were kissing again, both her hands on his face, his jaw sharp and the stubbled skin rough under her fingertips.
bs: — Nisam sigurna da ću dotad biti ovako pijana, dometnu ona, već se izvlačeći iz hlača. Prije nego što ih je uspjela svući preko bokova, ruka joj kliznu te se srušila i puna usta napunila slamom, prozviždukala i pljunula, kikotala se i podrigivala, pa su se opet počeli ljubiti, obiju ruku položenih mu na lice, oštre čeljusti i hrapave kože od neobrijane brade pod njezinim prstima.

en: “Oh,” she said, stupidly. They always surprised her, somehow, cocks. Strange bloody piece of anatomy. Still, she knew her way around one, even if she did say so herself. No point flicking away like you’re scared of it. You’ve got to get stuck in.
bs: — O, reče blesavo. Uvijek bi je nekako iznenadili, ti kurčevi. Čudan, proklet komad anatomije. Ipak, znala se ona s tim nositi, makar to sama rekla. Nema smisla dirkati okolo kao da te je strah. Moraš se primiti posla.

en: Rikke lay in the hay, arms flung heedlessly wide, gold ring through her nose gleaming with the morning light, tangled mass of chains and runes and talismans shifting as she breathed, a stray strand of hair across her face. In spite of his headache, he found he was smiling.
bs: Rike je ležala u sijenu, ruku bezbrižno raširenih, zlatni prsten u nosu blistao je na jutarnjem svjetlu, zamršena masa Chainsa, runa i talismana pomicala se dok je disala, a zalutali pramen kose prekrivao joj je lice. Unatoč glavobolji, primijetio je da se smiješi.

en: She slid a hand into his hair, gripped him hard and kissed him deep. Hungry, tonguey kisses that left nothing to the imagination. She rolled him over, getting up onto one elbow, biting at her lip as she started undoing his belt and he squirmed back into the hay, breath coming fast again, headache forgotten—
bs: Zavukla mu je ruku u kosu, čvrsto ga uhvatila i strastveno poljubila. Gladni, pohotni poljupci koji nisu ostavljali mjesta mašti. Prevrativši ga, oslonila se na lakat i grizući usnicu stala mu otkopčavati remen, dok se on izvijao natrag u sijeno, ubrzana daha i zaboravljene glavobolje —

en: He nearly fell as his bare foot slid on the other side, tottered a few steps and was charging on, through the Northmen’s campsite, smoky fires and the smell of cooking and someone singing in a rumbling bass as he pissed into the trees.
bs: Skoro je pao kad mu se golo stopalo poskliznulo nasuprot tome, teturajući je napravio nekoliko koraka i nastavio juriti kroz logor Sjevernjaka, pokraj dimnih vatri, mirisa kuhanja i nekoga tko je pjevao dubokim basom dok je mokrio u grmlje.

en: “By the dead,” grunted Isern, kneeling beside her and putting a hand on her shoulder. “Help me hold her, then!” And Leo knelt, too, one hand on Rikke’s arm and one on her knee while Isern rooted through her hair to look at the cut. It was then he realised Rikke was stark naked and he wasn’t far off.
bs: — Tako mi mrtvih, prozborila je Izern kleknuvši kraj nje i stavivši joj ruku na rame. — Pomozi mi držati je, dakle! I Leo je kleknuo, jednom rukom držeći Rike za ruku, a drugom za koljeno, dok je Izern pretraživala njezinu kosu ne bi li vidjela posjekotinu. Tada je shvatio da je Rike potpuno gola, a ni on nije bio daleko od toga.

en: “There’s my girl!” said Isern, the edge back on her voice. Leo closed his eyes and gave a sigh of relief. She was all right. And he realised he was still gripping her tight even though she’d stopped jerking, and he let go quickly, saw the marks of his fingers pink on her arm.
bs: — To je moja cura!, rekla je Izern, dok joj se oštrina vratila u glas. Leo zatvori oči i odahnu s olakšanjem. Bila je dobro. I shvatio je da je još čvrsto drži iako se prestala trgati, pa je brzo pustio, vidjevši ružičaste tragove svojih prstiju na njezinu ramenu.

en: Savine flashed her artfully constructed artless smile, the one people usually could not help returning. “And he’s not a man who gives praise lightly.”
bs: Savine namjesti svoj vješto skrojen, naizgled bezazlen osmijeh, onaj na koji Folk obično nisu mogli ostati ravnodušni. — A on nije čovjek koji lako udjeljuje pohvale.

en: “Coal is changing the world,” she observed, nudging the window down to get a little more air in and swishing her fan a touch faster.
bs: — Ugljen mijenja svijet, primijeti spuštajući prozor kako bi pustila malo više zraka i mašući lepezom nešto brže.

en: “Once commander of the King’s Own First Regiment. Too inflexible to work under Mitterick. Is he flexible enough to work under you?”
bs: — Nekadašnjeg zapovjednika Prve kraljeve pukovnije. Prenefleksibilan da radi pod Miterikom. Je li dovoljno fleksibilan da radi pod vama?

en: Now Teufel smiled. Just a little curl at the corner of her mouth. Considered, like every expression of hers. As though she had been over her budget and decided she could afford one.
bs: Tojfel se sada nasmiješila. Tek jedva primjetnim pokretom u kutu usta. Odmjerenim, kao i svaki njezin izraz lica. Kao da je pomno zbrojila svoje zalihe i zaključila kako si može priuštiti jedan osmijeh.

en: Not a hair of Savine’s eyebrows, not a thread of her clothes, not a speck of her powder was out of place, even in the heat. All so porcelain-perfect it was a surprise whenever she moved, talked, breathed like ordinary humans. She wore a ridiculous little sword with jewels on the hilt. She wore a tiny, pointless hat fastened with a crystal pin. She fluttered a fan made from fillets of iridescent seashell gracefully back and forth, back and forth. She had a nest of golden braids which only a dunce
bs: Niti jedna dlaka na Savinim obrvama, niti jedna nit njezine odjeće, niti jedna mrvica pudera nisu bile na krivome mjestu, čak ni po ovoj vrućini. Sve je na njoj bilo tako porculanski savršeno da bi čovjeka svaki put iznenadilo kada bi se pomaknula, progovorila ili udahnula poput običnih smrtnika. Nosila je smiješan mali mač ukrašen draguljima na dršku. Nosila je majušan, beskoristan šešir pričvršćen kristalnom iglom. Elegantno je mahala lepezom napravljenom od listića sedefastih školjki — tamo-a

en: It wasn’t mockery, exactly. They just both knew that Savine had more manners, money and beauty in one quim hair than Vick could’ve dug from her whole acquaintance. She sat safe on invisible cushions of power and privilege, knowing she could buy and sell Vick on a whim.
bs: Nije to bilo baš izrugivanje. One su samo dobro znale da Savine ima više manira, novca i ljepote u jednoj dlačici s pizade nego što bi Vik mogla iskopati iz cijeloga svog kruga poznanika. Ona je sjedila sigurna na nevidljivim jastucima moći i privilegija, znajući da bi Vik mogla kupiti i prodati u tren oka.

en: “It’s true one must be careful who one is seen with.” Savine opened her eyes very wide as the carriage rattled to a halt. “My mother likes to tell me a lady’s reputation is all she has. Ironic, really. Her reputation is dismal.”
bs: "Istina je da se mora paziti s kim te viđaju." Savine širom rastvori oči dok se kočija zaustavljala uz tutnjavu. — Moja majka voli mi govoriti kako je ženina reputacija sve što ima. Ironično, doista. Njezina je reputacija grozna.

en: Tallow gave a little gasp as he caught it, fumbled it, managed to stop it falling and finally clasped it tight to his chest. “Don’t know what to say,” he breathed.
bs: Talou je kratko dahnuo dok ju je hvatao, nespretno je pridržao, uspio spriječiti da padne i naposljetku je čvrsto privio na prsa. — Ne znam što bih rekao, prošaptao je.

en: The Vallimir residence, high on the hill where most of the affluent citizens of Valbeck had their houses, was a lesson in the dangers of excessive wealth and inadequate taste. Everything—furniture, cutlery and guests most of all—was too weighty, too fancy, too shiny. Mistress Vallimir’s dress was a misjudged purple, the curtains a garish turquoise, the soup a lurid yellow. The colour of urine with a taste not far removed.
bs: Rezidencija Valimir, visoko na brijegu gdje su imućniji građani Valbeka imali svoje domove, bila je lekcija o opasnostima pretjeranog bogatstva i pomanjkanja ukusa. Sve — namještaj, pribor za jelo, a ponajviše gosti — bilo je preteško, prenabićeno ukrasima, previše sjajno. Haljina gospa Valimir bila je promašene ljubičaste boje, zavjese napadne tirkizne, a juha sablasno žuta. Boje mokraće, a ukusa koji od nje nije bio daleko.

en: “Positively booming,” said Vallimir. “The third shed is up and running and the mill working at full capacity. Costs down, profits up.”
bs: — Pozitivno cvjetaju, reče Valimir. — Treća šupa je podignuta i u pogonu, a mlin radi punim kapacitetom. Troškovi dolje, dobit gore.

en: “One can never be too careful,” echoed Superior Risinau, leaning close to touch Savine’s shoulder with entirely too much familiarity. “But you need have no fear, Lady Savine.”
bs: "Opreza nikad nije dosta", dometnuo je Superior Risinau, nagnuvši se blizu kako bi dotaknuo Savinino rame s posve prevelikom prisnošću. — No ne morate se bojati, lady Savine.

en: Every face turned towards Savine, then silence, the only movement the wobbling of those horrible little jellies.
bs: Svako se lice okrenulo prema Savine, a potom nastupi tišina, u kojoj se jedino kretalo podrhtavanje onih groznih malih želatina.

en: “Even if you believe such monsters exist, you will find none here,” said Risinau. “The workers of Valbeck are without grievances.”
bs: "Čak i ako vjerujete da takva čudovišta postoje, ovdje nećete naći nijedno", ustvrdi Risinau. — Radnici Valbeka nemaju nikakvih pritužbi.

en: She blinked at Savine, then at Mistress Vallimir, then blushed bright pink and tidied a loose strand of hair behind her ear. “May, my lady. May Broad.”
bs: Ona trepnu prema Savine, zatim prema gospi Valimir, pa se zacrvenje u jarkoružičastu boju i namjesti pramen kose iza uha. — Mej, milostiva. Mej Brod.

en: “Foolish, wayward girl,” snapped Mistress Vallimir, the moment she had pulled the overpolished door shut, her fanning turned positively savage.
bs: — Luda, svojom glavom poljuljana djevojka, oštro odbrusi Gospa Valimir čim je privukla preizglancana vrata, dok joj je lepeza radila sve agresivnije.

en: “Better if I go to them. Having come all this way, I must see the improvements you have made first hand.”
bs: — Bit će bolje da ja odem njima. Kad sam već potegnula toliki put, moram vlastitim očima vidjeti poboljšanja koja ste uveli.

en: Vick had picked over her story a hundred times. Picked over Tallow’s, too, until the lies were like a second skin, more familiar than the truth. She had an answer for every question, a story for every suspicion, a set of excuses that left her looking good but not too good. The one thing she hadn’t been prepared for was the one thing she found.
bs: Vik je stotinu puta pretresla svoju priču. I Talouovu također, sve dok laži nisu postale poput druge kože, poznatije od istine. Imala je odgovor za svako pitanje, priču za svaku sumnju, skup izgovora zbog kojih je izgledala dobro, ali ne previše dobro. Jedina stvar za koju se nije pripremila bila je upravo ono na što je naišla.

en: It was a habit from the camps to think about how she’d bring a man down. This one you’d make sure was on your side. Or run away from him, fast as you could. Whole thing felt like a trap to Vick. But then everything did, and she told herself that was a good thing. It’s the moment you feel safe that you make your last mistake.
bs: Bila je to navika iz logora, razmišljati o tome kako bi oborila čovjeka. Ovog bi se pobrinula imati na svojoj strani. Ili pobjeći od njega, što je brže mogla. Vik se sve činilo kao zamka. No uostalom, sve joj se tako činilo, a govorila si je da je to dobra stvar. U trenutku kad se osjetiš Sejf, napraviš svoju posljednju pogrešku.

en: Must’ve been five hundred people crowded close in there. It was hot as an oven and noisy as a slaughterhouse and it smelled of old tar, unwashed bodies and rage. It was ill-lit by torches and the flickering of fire lent everything an edge of madness. Against one wall, someone had unfurled a huge banner made from old bedsheets, the words Now or Never daubed across it.
bs: Moralo je ondje biti nagurano pet stotina Folk. Bilo je vruće kao u peći, bučno kao u klaonici, a mirisalo je na stari katran, neoprana tijela i bijes. Bilo je slabo osvijetljeno bakljama, a treperenje vatre dalo je svemu primjesu ludila. Uz jedan je zid netko razvio golemu zastavu načinjenu od starih plahti, s ispisanim riječima Sad ili nikad.

en: “Burn it all!” squealed one of the children from the rafters, so excited she nearly fell, and others took up the chant.
bs: — Spalite sve! zacvililo je jedno od djece s greda, toliko uzbuđeno da je umalo palo, a ostali su prihvatili skandiranje.

en: Judge folded her arms across her battered breastplate and sneered at Malmer down her nose, but the rest of the crowd settled to hear him speak.
bs: Džadž prekrsti ruke na svojem izubijanom oklopu i prezirno odmjeri Malmer s visoka, no ostatak se gomile utišao kako bi ga čuo.

en: Judge grinned as she held out her hand to pull someone up onto the wagon. A plump man in a dark, well-tailored suit, soft and pale, oddly out of place in this rough company.
bs: Džadž se nasmiješi pruživši ruku da nekoga povuče gore na kola. Bucmasti muškarac u tamnom, dobro krojenom odijelu, mekan i blijed, neobično stran u tom grubom društvu.

en: “The cock in the Agriont!” sneered Judge, grabbing hold of her groin to much laughter among the crowd while the children jumped on the rafters and made the dummy king dance.
bs: — Onaj pijetao u Agriontu!, podsmjehnu se Džadž, hvatajući se za međunožje uz silan smijeh okupljenih, dok su djeca skakala po gredama i natjerala lutku kralja da pleše.

en: “He tells me the market must be free to operate. The world must be free to advance. Progress cannot be chained, apparently. Who knew the Arch Lector was so firmly set against manacles?” Some laughter at that. “When one man knowingly kills another, they call it murder! When society causes the deaths of thousands, they shrug and call it a fact of life.” Growls of agreement, and Risinau crushed the letter in his fist and tossed it away. “The time for talk is done, my friends! No one is listening. N
bs: — On mi govori kako tržište mora slobodno djelovati. Svijet mora slobodno napredovati. Naprijed se, očito, ne može okovati. Tko bi rekao da je vrhovni Lektor toliko odlučno protiv okova? Netko se na to nasmijao. — Kad jedan čovjek svjesno ubije drugoga, nazovu to ubojstvom! Kad društvo prouzroči smrt tisuća, oni slegnu ramenima i nazovu to životnom činjenicom. Začulo se mrmljanje odobravanja, a Risinau zgužva pismo u šaci i baci ga. "Vrijeme za razgovor je završeno, prijatelji moji! Nitko ne slu

en: Vick wanted to follow. Badly. But she had to get to the hill and find Savine dan Glokta, maybe there was still time to put out a warning—
bs: Vik je htjela poći za njim. Jako. No morala je stići do brijega i pronaći Savine dan Glokta, možda je još bilo vremena da oda počast upozorenju —

en: Judge was staring at her with those black, empty eyes, head dropped to one side. Vick couldn’t tell whether she was putting on a hell of an act or if she really was as mad as she looked.
bs: Džadž ju je promatrala onim crnim, praznim očiju, nagnute glave u stranu. Vik nije mogla dokučiti glumi li pakleno dobro ili je doista luda onoliko koliko izgleda.

en: “One can have perfectly cordial relationships with one’s competitors, but rarely with one’s employees.” Savine glanced over her shoulder at the ten armoured guards filing through the gate after them, fingers tickling their weapons. It did nothing for her nerves that heavily armed men looked even more nervous than she did. “Do we really need such a conspicuous escort?”
bs: — Čovjek može imati posve srdačne odnose sa svojim konkurentima, ali rijetko sa svojim zaposlenicima. Savine je bacila Oko preko ramena na deset oklopnih stražara koji su u koloni prolazili kroz vrata za njima, a prsti su im nemirno prebirali po oružju. Nimalo joj nije pomoglo to što su teško naoružani muškarci izgledali još nervoznije od nje. — Imamo li doista potrebu za tako upadljivom pratnjom?

en: Vallimir winced. “I am not sure you would be… comfortable inside. It is extremely noisy. Very warm. Not at all a suitable place for a lady of your standing.”
bs: Valimir se zgrči. — Nisam siguran da bi vam unutra bilo… ugodno. Izuzetno je bučno. Vrlo toplo. Nipošto prikladno mjesto za damu vašega položaja.

en: “They are children.” She let no emotion enter her voice at the word. Hundreds of children, lean and filthy, gathered in long rows about the looms, darting among the machines, rolling spindles of yarn as tall as they were, bent under bolts of finished cloth.
bs: — To su djeca. Ne dopusti da joj ijedna emocija uđe u glas pri toj riječi. Stotine djece, mršave i prljave, okupljene u dugim redovima oko tkalačkih stanova, kako se vrzmaju među strojevima, kotrljaju vretena pređe visoka poput njih samih, pognute pod balama dovršena platna.

en: “Purchased.” Savine let no emotion enter her voice at that word, either. “Like any other piece of machinery.”
bs: — Kupiti. Savine ni uz tu riječ ne dopusti da joj emocija prozuji glasom. — Kao i bilo koji drugi komad stroja.

en: She wondered if so much wilful human misery had ever been created in one space before. She put a hand on Vallimir’s shoulder. “When it comes to business, profit is the only right. Loss the only wrong.”
bs: Upitala se je li tolika svjesna ljudska bijeda ikad prije stvorena na jednome mjestu. Položi ruku Valimiru na rame. — Kad je riječ o poslu, dobit je jedino pravo. Gubitak jedini kriv.

en: “Luxury is wasteful,” said Savine, “but hardship can reduce productivity. In my experience, there is a balance to be struck. With better conditions, you might manage longer shifts after all.”
bs: — Luksuz je rasipan, reče Savine, ali neimaština može smanjiti produktivnost. Prema mom iskustvu, valja pronaći ravnotežu. S boljim uvjetima mogli biste naposljetku izdržati dulje smjene.

en: Savine kept blandly smiling. A lady of taste always smiles. “Better not to show weakness. To our employees or our partners.” She was not a woman to be deterred by hatred: not from her workers, not from her rivals, not from the men she bullied, bribed or blackmailed to get her way. It is when they truly hate you, after all, that you know you have won. So she met the seething dislike with effortless superiority, paraded past with her shoulders back and chin high. If she was to be cast as the villa
bs: Savine se i dalje blago smješkala. Žena od ukusa uvijek se smiješi. — Bolje ne pokazivati slabost. Ni našim zaposlenicima ni našim partnerima." Nije bila žena koju bi mržnja mogla pokolebati: ni mržnja njezinih radnika, ni njezinih suparnika, ni muškaraca koje je maltretirala, potkupljivala ili ucjenjivala kako bi ostvarila svoje ciljeve. Uostalom, tek kad te istinski mrze, znaš da si pobijedio. Stoga je na taj uzavreli prezir odgovarala s naporom bez premca, kročeći uzdignute glave i zabačenih

en: The street outside was deserted. All at work, of course, and what but work would bring anyone to this lane of spiked walls and barred gates, of towering mills and rumbling machinery? Yet there was something wrong about the quiet. A weight on the air, like the calm before a thunderstorm. Savine frowned out at the empty lane, biting at her lip, wondering if she could leave now without—
bs: Ulica vani bila je pusta. Svi na poslu, a što bi drugo ikoga dovelo u ovu uličicu ojačanih zidova i rešetkastih vrata, golemih predionica i tutnjajućih strojeva? Pa ipak, s tom je tišinom nešto bilo u redu. Težina u zraku, poput zatišja pred oluju. Savine se namrštila promatrajući praznu uličicu, grizući usnu i pitajući se bi li mogla otići sada a da ne —

en: Vallimir’s guards were holding them back in a desperate crescent at the bottom of the steps but they were outnumbered twenty-to-one. Savine’s eyes darted in horror over that ugly swarm. That mob.
bs: Valimirovi stražari držali su ih u očajničkom polumjesecu na dnu stuba, ali bili su u manjini, dvadesetero naprama jedan. Savinine su oči u strahu prelijetale preko te ružne gomile. Te rulje.

en: She could hear her own snatched breath. The breath of a hunted animal. Foolishly, with fumbling fingers, she drew her sword. That was what one was supposed to do when one’s life was in danger. Was her life in danger? The noise was louder outside, closer. Over the endless whirr of the machinery she heard screaming, swearing, mindless growling, the clash of steel. A long, high shrieking started which would not stop.
bs: Čula je vlastiti isprekidani dah. Dah lovljene životinje. Ludo je, nespretnim prstima, izvukla mač. To je ono što je čovjek trebao učiniti kada mu je život u opasnosti. Je li joj život bio u opasnosti? Buka vani bila je glasnija, bliža. Preko beskonačnog zujanja strojeva čula je vrištanje, psovanje, bezumno ricanje i sudar čelika. Započelo je dugo, prodorno vrištanje koje nije prestajalo.

en: “I’m going to count to five, bitch!” That voice from outside the door, boiling over with violence now. “Five, then we’re coming in!”
bs: — Brojat ću do pet, kučko! Taj glas nasuprot tome vrata, sada uzavreo od nasilja. — Pet, i dolazimo unutra!

en: She saw her sword gleaming in the shadows, closed her fist around the grip and started to crawl, keeping low, slithering along in the dust behind the barrels. That unearthly shrieking was still going on, pausing every now and then for a whooping breath then starting again.
bs: Ugledala je svoj mač kako blista u sjeni, čvrsto obgrlila dršku i počela puzati držeći se nisko, provlačeći se kroz prašinu iza bačava. Ono onostrano pištavi jecanje još je trajalo, zastajkujući povremeno za uzdah, a onda ponovno počinjalo.

en: There was a lurch, a slow grinding, the guard’s scream turning to a bubbling wail, then the machinery lurched on, wheels turning. Savine tried not to look. Keep her eyes ahead. This wasn’t happening. None of it was happening. How could it be happening? Men were shouting. Barking like a pack of dogs. She couldn’t make out words, only anger and the shuddering blows on the door above.
bs: Uslijedio je trzaj, sporo mljevenje, stražarjev vrisak prešao je u grgljavi jauk, a zatim je stroj ponovno trgnuo i kotači su se pokrenuli. Savine je pokušala ne gledati. Držati oči uprte naprijed. Ovo se nije događalo. Ništa od ovoga se nije događalo. Kako se to moglo događati? Muškarci su vikali. Ljali poput čopora pasa. Nije razabirala riječi, samo bijes i tutnjajuće udarce po vratima iznad.

en: When she finally reached the hole in the wall, she almost sobbed with relief. Clutched at the ragged bricks and dragged herself through, tumbled into a dark passageway, sprawled in ankle-deep water and took a fetid mouthful, spat it out, retching.
bs: Kad je napokon stigla do rupe u zidu, umalo je zaplakala od olakšanja. Uhvatila se za otrcane cigle i odvukla kroz otvor, survala se u mračan prolaz, zagazila u vodi do gležnjeva i udahnula smrdljivi gutljaj, pa ga ispljunula hvatajući zrak uz nagon za povraćanjem.

en: She pressed her tongue into the roof of her mouth as she tried to judge the gap. What if she did not fit? Would she be dragged under and drowned? Dragged into the gears and ripped limb from limb? Would her skull be crushed like a walnut between wheel and supports? Would she be slashed, cut, nipped and nibbled as she struggled to get free, bleeding to death from a hundred wounds while she was spun helplessly over, and over, and over? She thought of that guard’s despairing wail as his arm was crus
bs: Pritisnula je jezik uz nepce dok je pokušavala procijeniti širinu procjepa. Što ako se ne provuče? Hoće li je povući pod vodu i utopiti? Hoće li je uvući u zupčanike i raskomadati joj udove? Hoće li joj lubanja biti smrskana poput oraha između kotača i nosača? Hoće li biti sječena, rezana, štipana i grickana dok se bori da se oslobodi, krvareći nasmrt od stotinu rana dok je bespomoćno vrtoglavo okreću ukrug? Pomislila je na onaj očajnički jecaj stražara kad mu je stroj smrskao ruku. No drugog iz

en: The river slurped past, purple and orange and green with great blooms of unnatural colour from the dye-works upstream, bobbing with refuse, churned to stinking froth by dozens of hammering waterwheels. On the left bank was a kind of beach, streaked with tidemarks of dead brown weed, scattered with the city’s flotsam, with rags and skins and broken chairs and splintered glass and rusted wire and things too far rotted to be identified, all vomited up by the tortured waters and pecked at by flocks
