bs: Kralj Ljuska je pio. Što bi drugo radio? Pio je i gromko se smijao pričama o bitci, već nadut od laži poput razvodnjena piva. Njegov nećak, moćni Staur Najtfol, ukrašen pokojom svježom posjekotinom i modricom, cvao je slušajući o vlastitim pothvatima, još i više o izmišljotinama negoli o činjenicama. Oko ove dvojice heroja stari su ratnici i Juvens kupali se u sunčevu sjaju pobjede koju još nisu ni izvojevali.

en: “The Young Lion, they call him, and my spies tell me he’s formidable. How often have I said to you—never fear your enemy, but always respect him? Every duel is a risk and we don’t need to gamble. The enemy are fought out and we have fresh warriors. Flatstone can come around on the flank and the ground is—”
bs: — Zovu ga Juvens Lav, a moji špijuni kažu da je zastrašujući. Koliko sam ti puta rekao — nikad se ne boj neprijatelja, ali ga uvijek poštuj? Svaki je dvoboj rizik i ne moramo se kockati. Neprijatelj se istrošio, a mi imamo svježe ratnike. Flatstone se može zaobiti s bokova, a teren je —

en: Clover had been telling Stour for near half a year and made no mark, like shooting a quiver full of daffodils at a man in full plate armour. But one more daffodil could do no harm. He spread his hands as if he held out a platter covered in fine advice. “There’s no bigger foolishness than to choose to face a dangerous man on equal terms. Look at me. Lost everything in the Circle.”
bs: Klover je to govorio Stauru već gotovo pola godine, ali bez ikakva učinka, kao da puca tobolac pun narcisa na čovjeka u punom oklopu. No još jedan narcis ne može štetiti. Raširi ruke kao da drži pladanj prepun mudrih savjeta. — Nema veće ludosti nego izabrati sučeljavanje s opasnim čovjekom pod jednakim uvjetima. Pogledaj mene. Sve izgubio u Krugu.

en: Calder stood quiet a moment longer, face a rigid mask. “Warriors,” he hissed, like it was the worst insult he could think of, then turned on his heel and stalked from the room.
bs: Kalder je ostao mirovati još trenutak dulje, lica ukrućenog poput maske. — Ratnici, prozborio je kroz zube, kao da je to bila najgora uvreda kojom se mogao dosjetiti, a zatim se okrenuo na petama i izašao iz prostorije krupnim koracima.

en: “That’s why I’d stay even further from the Circle than I would from the sword,” said Clover. “Money, land, fame, friends, even your name—lose them but keep your life, with time and hard labour you can always win ’em back.” He’d lost his name, hadn’t he? And won a new? He could still smell the sweet clover in his nose as he lay there in the Circle, waiting for the end. “But there’s no beating the Great Leveller. No man comes back from the mud.”
bs: — Zato bih se ja od Kruga držao još dalje nego od mača, reče Klover. — Novac, Country, slava, prijatelji, pa čak i vlastito ime – izgubi li ih čovjek, a sačuva glavu, uz vrijeme i Trdak rad uvijek ih može vratiti. Izgubio je svoje ime, zar ne? I stekao novo? Dok je ležao ondje u Krugu i čekao kraj, u nosu mu je još mirisala slatka djetelina. — Ali Velikog ravnjača se ne može pobijediti. Nitko se iz blata još nije vratio.

en: Leo gritted his teeth. “My point is, I need to focus. It’s a shame about Barniva. He was a brave man. A good friend. Always there when you needed him.” He felt his voice quavering a little. “If he hadn’t put his shield across me…” Perhaps he’d still be alive. All his tedious warnings about the horrors of war seemed wise words now. Leo never thought he might have missed them. “It’s a damn shame about Barniva, but we’ll have to mourn him later. Right now, we need to make his sacrifice worthwhile.
bs: Leo stisnu zube. — Poanta je u tome da se moram usredotočiti. Šteta za Barnivu. Bio je hrabar čovjek. Dobar prijatelj. Uvijek tu kad ti zatreba. — Osjeti kako mu glas pomalo podrhtava. — Da nije stavio svoj štit preda me… — Možda bi još bio živ. Sva njegova naporna upozorenja o strahotama rata sada su se činila mudrima. Leo nikada ne bi pomislio da bi mu mogla nedostajati. — Prokleto mi je žao Barnive, ali morat ćemo tugovati za njim kasnije. Trenutno moramo njegovu žrtvu učiniti smislenom. Njeg

en: “You’re all missing the point,” snapped Leo. “You take a weapon, but you never know if you’ll fight with it, or hand it to your opponent and fight with whatever he brings. What you need is something you can use but the other bastard can’t.”
bs: — Svi propuštate poantu — kresnu Leo. — Uzmeš oružje, ali nikad ne znaš hoćeš li se boriti njime ili ga dati protivniku, a boriti se onim što on donese. Ono što ti treba jest nešto što ti možeš upotrijebiti, a drugi kopile ne može.

en: “I once saw this Gurkish woman whip swords out of men’s hands. At a show. They came up from the audience, and, well, it was quite something. She whipped a girl’s dress half-off without cutting her, too.” And he grinned at the memory.
bs: — Jednom sam vidio jednu ženu iz Gurkish kako bičem izbija mačeve iz ruku muškarcima. Na nekoj predstavi. Izašli su iz publike i, eto, bilo je doista impresivno. Bičem je i djevojci napola skinula haljinu a da je nije porezala. I zaškilji uz Brod osmijeh sjećajući se toga.

en: Rikke gave a haughty sniff and made the ring through her nose twitch. “Isern said I should be taking the reins.”
bs: Rike nadmeno potegnu zrak kroz nos i natjera prsten u nosu da joj zatreperi. — Izern je rekla da bih trebala preuzeti uzde.

en: “No. You don’t.” She took his face now, with both hands. “The lion beat the wolf. I’ve seen it.” Her big, pale eyes were full of certainty, and he took heart from that. Started to feel braver. To feel himself again. The Young Lion! She was just what he needed then. A spring of belief in a desert of doubt. It’s like they say, every good man needs a good woman beside him. Or under him, anyway.
bs: — Ne. Ne znaš. Ona mu obuhvati lice objema rukama. "Lav je pobijedio vuka. Vidjela sam to." Njezine krupne, blijede oči bijahu prepune sigurnosti, a njemu to uli nadu. Poče osjećati veću hrabrost. Poče se osjećati kao sam svoj ponovno. Juvens Lav! Bilo mu je upravo to potrebno u tom trenutku. Vrelo vjere u pustinji sumnje. Kao što kažu, svakom dobrom muškarcu treba dobra žena uz njega. Ili pod njim, u svakom slučaju.

en: “You don’t need luck.” Rikke twisted his face back towards her and kissed him, gentle and serious, and full of belief. “I’ve seen it.”
bs: — Ne treba ti sreća. Rike mu okrenu lice natrag prema sebi i poljubi ga, nježno, ozbiljno i prožeto vjerom. — Vidjela sam to.

en: Strange, in a way, for men who’d been fixed on killing each other a few hours before to be happily mingling, stamping and blowing and polishing their shield-rims, mulling over fights long past, the fight just done and the fight to come. But then warriors on different sides always had more in common with each other than with anyone else.
bs: Bilo je to nekako čudno – da se Folk koji su se do prije nekoliko sati namjeravali pobiti sada veselo druže, tapkaju i pušu od hladnoće te glačaju rubove svojih štitova, razglabajući o bitkama davno prošlim, onoj koja je upravo završila i onoj koja tek predstoji. No ratnici s različitih strana oduvijek su imali više zajedničkoga međusobno nego s bilo kim drugim.

en: Shivers gave that weary nod again, looking off towards the hills. “We should talk, sometime. One scarred old warhorse to another.”
bs: Šivers ponovno umorno kimnu i odvrati Oko prema brežuljcima. — Trebali bismo jednom popričati. Stari ratni konj s ožiljcima s jednim drugim.

en: “About what you’d expect from someone they call the Great Wolf. Certainly no better. What about Brock?”
bs: — Otprilike onakav kakvog bi očekivao od nekoga koga zovu Great Vuk. ništa bolji. A što je s Brokom?

en: “Helps to have someone worth being loyal to.” The cheers and grumbles were reversed as a lean old man with long hair and a pointed face clambered stiffly onto the seats opposite.
bs: — Pomaže kad imaš nekoga tko je vrijedan te odanosti. Klicanje i gunđanje se izokrenuše dok se mršavi starac duge kose i šiljasta lica ukočeno vjere na sjedala preko puta.

en: “Aye. Rikke. I’ll make no promises for her odour but she’s worth talking to.” He nodded towards the platform, where a girl was clambering over the back, all knees and elbows, to wedge herself between the Dogman and a pale, hard Union woman Clover reckoned to be the one-time Lady Governor of Angland.
bs: — Da. Rike. Neću davati nikakva obećanja o njenom mirisu, ali vrijedna je razgovora. Kimnu prema podiju, gdje se neka djevojka verala preko naslona, sva u koljenima i laktovima, kako bi se uglavila između Psa Čovjeka i blijede, čvrste žene iz Unije za koju je Klover smatrao da je nekadašnja visoka namjesnica Englenda.

en: Rikke had been hoping the hate would melt when she finally saw Stour Nightfall’s face, because her hate for him was getting to feel like quite the weight to carry. She’d look in his eyes and see he wasn’t the monster who’d whined his hopes for her horrible murder, who’d burned her father’s garden and killed good folk she knew, but just a man with loves and fears like any other, and her hate would melt.
bs: Rike se nadala da će mržnja iščeznuti kad napokon ugleda lice Staura Najtfola, jer joj je mržnja prema njemu počinjala predstavljati priličan teret. Pogledala bi mu u oči i vidjela da on nije čudovište koje je cviljelo o svojim željama da ona bude mučki ubijena, koje je spalilo vrt njezina oca i pobilo dobre ljude koje je poznavala, nego tek običan čovjek s ljubavima i strahovima kao i svi drugi, pa bi se njezina mržnja rastopila.

en: “You’re Rikke, then?” he called out, giving her a slow look up and down with those wet eyes, his mouth open and his tongue showing. “You’re prettier’n I thought you’d be.”
bs: — Ti si dakle Rike? dobaci on, odmjeravajući je polako od glave do pete tim vlažnim očima, otvorenih usta tako da mu se vidio jezik. — Ljepša si nego što sam mislio.

en: “Easy,” muttered her father, pulling her back down by the elbow. “Hard words are for fools and cowards. Stour might be both, but you’re neither.”
bs: — Polako, promrmlja joj otac, povukavši je natrag za lakat. — Teške riječi služe budalama i kukavicama. Staur možda jest oboje, ali ti nisi ni jedno ni drugo.

en: Leo flinched as the wall of shields clattered shut behind him, like a prisoner might at the turning of the jailer’s key. He’d said he loved her. Wasn’t that she thought he was lying. Just that she doubted he’d ever love anyone more than himself.
bs: Leo se trgnu kad se zid od štitu zatvori iza njega uz prasak, poput zatvorenika na okretanje tamničareva ključa. Govorio je da je voli. Nije stvar bila u tome što je mislila da laže. Već u tome što je sumnjala da će ikada voljeti ikoga više nego samog sebe.

en: “I’m Isern-i-Phail! My da, Crummock-i-Phail, judged the fight between Fenris the Feared and the Bloody-Nine. He was a well-known bastard.” Some laughter and hoots of agreement. “But he was well known! And being a hillman, the closest thing to a neutral party anyone could find. I am as well known as he.” And she lifted her chin and gestured at herself. “But for my piercing wits and haunting beauty.” More laughter. “Seems it’s fallen to me as a hillwoman to judge this bout.” She grinned over at St
bs: — Ja sam Izern-i-Fejl! Moj stari, Crummock-i-Fejl, sudio je u borbi između Fenrisa Strašenog i Krvava Devetka. Bio je nadaleko poznat kopile. Prolomi se smijeh i odobravanje. — Ali bio je poznat! A kao brđanin, najbliže nepristranoj osobi koju je ikad netko mogao pronaći. I ja sam poznata kao i on. Podigne bradu i mahne prema sebi. — Ali po svojoj oštroumnosti i sablasnoj ljepoti. Još smijeha. — izgleda da je na meni, kao brđanki, da sudim u ovom dvoboju. Nasmiješila se Stauru. — Iako moram odma

en: “Your next question!” called Isern. “What are these two fools going to kill each other over? Mostly a matter of manly pride, as is proper in a duel, but there’s also the rich, dark earth o’ the North. The winner takes the patch of it men call the Protectorate, which stretches from the Whiteflow to the Cusk and includes the city of Uffrith. Stour Nightfall wins, it belongs to King Scale. Leo dan Brock wins, it stays with the Dogman in the loving embrace o’ the Union. All happy with the terms?”
bs: — Vaše sljedeće pitanje!, povika Izern. — Zbog čega će se ova dvojica luđaka poubijati? Uglavnom zbog muškog ponosa, kako se i priliči u dvoboju, ali tu je i bogata, tamna Zemlja Sjevera. Pobjednik uzima komad zemlje koji Folk zovu Protektorat, a proteže se od Whiteflowa do Cuska i obuhvaća grad Afrit. Pobijedi li Staur Najtfol, ona pripada kralju Skejlu. Pobijedi li Leo dan Brok, ostaje kod Dogmana u toplom zagrljaju Unije. Jesu li svi zadovoljni uvjetima?

en: “Men!” And Isern rolled her eyes. “They never can commit. You’ll fight with what you brought, then.” She tossed the shield back to Shivers, plucked her spear from the ground and pointed it at the men about the Circle, shields all facing inwards now, rims grating as they locked them together into a wall. “You lot, keep these two in here till it’s settled. And no more interfering than is seemly.” She spat chagga juice, wiped her chin and nodded, like it was all set up to her satisfaction. “Let’s g
bs: — Muškarci!, Izern prevrnu očima. — Nikad se ne mogu odlučiti. Borit ćete se s onim što ste donijeli. Ona baci štit natrag Šiversu, iščupa Pajk iz zemlje i uperi ga u ljude okupljene oko Circlea, čiji su štitovi sada bili okrenuti prema unutra, a rubovi im strugali dok su ih spajali u zid. — Vas nekoliko, držite ovu dvojicu unutra dok se sve ne riješi. I bez previše miješanja. Ispljune sok od čage, obrisa bradu i kimnu glavom, kao da je sve bilo namješteno po njezinu ukusu. — Latimo se posla.

en: “Leo!” roared Glaward, shaking his shield. But Stour was already on him again, three cuts so quick, Leo only dodged the first two by the barest instinct. He reeled away from the third, fishing with his sword in a weak effort to keep his opponent back. Stour was the whirlwind. Leo was the leaf blown around the Circle.
bs: — Leo! — zarežao je Glavard mašući štitom. Ali Staur mu je već bio za petama, tri udarca tako brza da im je Leo izmakao samo pukim instinktom. Teturajući se izmaknuo trećem, mlatarajući mačem u slabom pokušaju da zadrži protivnika podalje. Staur je bio vihor. Leo je bio list nošen oko Kruga.

en: Steel scraped as Stour caught Leo’s blade on his, held it up short, the edge almost brushing the pointed tip of his nose. They snarled in each other’s faces, straining for the upper hand, crosspieces grinding, knuckles almost rubbing together, shifting their stances in a bid to gain some hair of an advantage, locked together in a furious, frozen struggle while the crowd made a mindless thunder in which encouragement could hardly be told from insults.
bs: Čelik je zaškripao dok je Staur dočekao Leovu oštricu na svoju, držeći je visoko i blizu, a sječivo mu je umalo češljalo Kruna nosa. Režali su jedan drugom u lice, napinjući se ne bi li nadmašili suparnika, križevi mačeva su se strugali, zglavci prstiju gotovo su im se dodirivali, pomičući stavove u pokušaju da izbore makar i najmanju prednost, stisnuti u bijesnoj, zaleđenoj borbi dok je svjetina stvarala bezumnu grmljavinu u kojoj se ohrabrivanje jedva moglo razaznati od uvjerenja.

en: The crowd roared. For a moment, Leo thought it was for him. Then he felt something tickling his cheek. Stour’s point had scratched his face, so quick and so sharp he’d hardly felt it. It was blood the crowd were cheering for. His blood.
bs: Svjetina je zaurlala. Na tren je Leo pomislio da navijaju za njega. Zatim je osjetio nešto kako ga golica po obrazu. Staurov Kruna ogrebao mu je lice, toliko brzo i oštro da jedva da je to i osjetio. Svjetina je klicala krvi. Njegovoj krvi.

en: There wasn’t much in the world to get your heart pumping harder than watching two men fight to the death. Only being one of ’em. He felt a guilty surge of excitement as Stour dashed forward again. Felt the eager grin on his own lips as Brock parried and fell back. No doubt he was a fine swordsman. But Stour was making him look ordinary. More so with every moment. He used that big sword nimbly as a dressmaker might her needle, all wrist and flick and effortless mastery.
bs: Nije bilo mnogo toga na svijetu od čega bi čovjeku srce zaigralo snažnije nego kad gleda dvojicu kako se bore na život i smrt. Jedino biti jedan od njih. Osjetio je grčevit val uzbuđenja kad je Staur ponovno jurnuo naprijed. Osjetio je željni osmijeh na vlastitim usnama kad je Brok parirao i ustuknuo. nesumnjivo, bio je vješt mačevalac. No Staur je učinio da izgleda sasvim prosječno. I to sve više sa svakim trenutkom. Služio se tim velikim mačem okretno poput krojačice koja barata iglom, sve sam

en: By the dead, the tension. The long-drawn aching in her throat, worse and worse as the two of them circled, watchful, twisting like dogs after a scent, sniffing for an opening. Rikke’s sore mouth tasted of vomit and fear while the men with the shields shouted, stomped, bellowed their hatred and their encouragement.
bs: Tako mi mrtvih, ta napetost. Dugotrajna, mučna bol u grlu, sve gora dok su se njih dvojica kružili, budni, vrteći se poput pasa u potrazi za tragom, njušeći ne bi li pronašli pukotinu. Rike su bolna usta imala okus po povraćanju i strahu, dok su Folk sa štitovima vikali, gazili, ričući mržnju i podršku.

en: She gasped as Nightfall came forward, switched direction in a blink. Steel rang once, twice, Leo lashed back, but too slow and Stour slipped around it, his sword catching Leo’s leg and making him stagger.
bs: Trgnula se kad je Najtfol krenuo prema naprijed, promijenivši smjer u tren oka. Čelik je zazvonio jednom, dvaput, Leo je uzvratio udarac, ali previše sporo, te mu se Staur provukao iza leđa, zahvativši mačem Leovu nogu i natjeravši ga da posrne.

en: Rikke curled back her lips, and clenched her fists, and squeezed her jaw so hard it felt like her teeth might crack, and she stared at the Circle as if she was staring into a gale.
bs: Rike razvuče usne u grč, stisnu šake i stegnu vilicu tako silno da pomisli kako će joj zubi napuknuti, pa se zagleda u Round kao da gleda u olujni vjetar.

en: His friends, their shields drooping. Glaward chewing his lip. Jin tearing his beard. Antaup crestfallen. Jurand wincing as if he felt every wound himself. He caught a glimpse of his mother, stricken, pale, staring. The Dogman sat grim beside her, and Rikke, glaring into the Circle, fiddling with the ring through her nose.
bs: Prijatelji njegovi, spuštenih štitova. Glavard Grise usnu. Jin čupa bradu. Antaup shrvan. Džurand se trza kao da svaku ruku osjeća na vlastitom tijelu. Ugleda majku, shrvanu, blijedu, ukočenog pogleda. Pas Covjek sjede mrk pored nje, a Rike, upiljila u Round, igra se prstenom u nosu.

en: He darted one way, switched in an instant and whipped past on the other side, quick as the wind and as hard to pin down. Leo was left stranded, gasped as the edge of Stour’s sword whipped across his thigh, left a cold line that soon turned burning hot. It was the most he could do to stay standing as the blood soaked into his trouser leg.
bs: Jurnuo je na jednu stranu, u trenu se okrenuo i projurio onamo s druge, brz kao vjetar i jednako neuhvatljiv. Leo je ostao stajati ukopan, zinuo kad mu je oštrica Staurova mača ošinula bedro i ostavila hladnu crtu koja se ubrzo pretvorila u žarku žegu. Jedva se uspio održati na nogama dok mu se krv upijala u nogavicu.

en: Stour could’ve finished Brock five times now but he was enjoying hooking him so much, he kept letting him wriggle free so he could hook him again. Clover thought that ill-advised, to say the least. You take no risks in the Circle and give no chances, not with all you’ve got and all you’ll ever have in the balance. It only takes a little twist of fate to land you back in the mud, and fate can be a twisty little bastard.
bs: Staur je mogao dokrajčiti Broka već pet puta, ali toliko je uživao u poigravanju s njim da mu je stalno dopuštao da se otme kako bi ga mogao iznova loviti na udicu. Klover je to smatrao barem nepromišljenim. U Krugu se ne poduzimaju nikakvi rizici i ne daju se nikakve prilike, pogotovo kad je na kocki sve što imaš i sve što ćeš ikada imati. Dovoljan je samo mali obrat sudbine pa da ponovno završiš u blatu, a sudbina zna biti prevrtljiva gadura.

en: Leo winced as Stour’s blade caught him across the belly. Not a killing blow. Just a kiss. A slash that spotted the shields beside him with blood. Leo stumbled, fell to his knees, sword slipping from his hand into the grass.
bs: Leo se trgnuo kad ga je Staurova oštrica presjekla preko trbuha. Nije to bio smrtonosni udarac. Tek poljubac. Zarez koji je poprskao štitove pokraj njega kapljicama krvi. Leo se zanio, pao na koljena, a mač mu je skliznuo iz ruke u travu.

en: She saw it in the Great Wolf’s scabbard, whipped free as the duel began, cut and thrust, the Circle full of the bright ribbons of its passing.
bs: Vidjela je mač u koricama Velikog vuka, izvučen u trenu kad je dvoboj počeo, posjekao je i probo, a Round se ispunio sjajnim vrpcama njegova prolaska.

en: He could hardly hear for his own thudding heartbeat, hardly tell the roaring of the crowd from the roaring of his breath. He’d clutched up a handful of grass along with his sword. Bloody grass. Bloody dirt.
bs: Jedva je čuo išta od vlastita tutnjavog otkucaja srca, jedva je razlikovao riku svjetine od Rike vlastitog daha. S mačem je u šaci stisnuo i grumen trave. Krvavu travu. Krvavu zemlju.

en: Leo pulled his sword free and Nightfall tottered, spluttering bloody spit, rearing up on his good leg, raising his sword high so the blade glimmered red with the setting sun.
bs: Leo je izvukao mač, a Najtfol se zatresao, pljujući krvavu pjenu, podižući se na zdravoj nozi i podižući mač visoko, tako da je oštrica blistala crveno u zalazećem suncu.

en: No doubt Nightfall would’ve killed Leo, if he’d been the one lying there, helpless. Would’ve killed him in the slowest, most painful, most shameful way he could. Would’ve crowed his victory from the rooftops of Uffrith and laughed as the skalds sang the story back to him for years to come.
bs: Nema sumnje da bi Najtfol ubio Leoa, da je on bio onaj koji leži tamo, nemoćan. Ubio bi ga na najsporiji, najbolniji, najponižavajući način koji bi mogao. Hvalio bi se svojom pobjedom s krovova Afrita i smijao se dok bi skaldi pjevali priču natrag njemu godinama.

en: “Stour Nightfall,” he mumbled. Even speaking was a mighty effort then, each word a great stone to lift. “I spare… your life.”
bs: — Staur Najtfol, promrmljao je. Čak je i govoriti tada bio golem napor, svaka riječ kao velika stijena koju treba podignuti. — Poštedio sam… tvoj život.

en: “Best never to make a decision based on trust,” said Vick, like trust was some fantastic beast only children believed in. “Just on what’s best for most.”
bs: "Najbolje je nikada ne donositi odluke na temelju povjerenja", reče Vik, kao da je povjerenje nekakva fantastična zvijer u koju vjeruju samo djeca. — Samo na temelju onoga što je najbolje za većinu.

en: Couple of months ago at those big meetings, folk would’ve fallen over themselves to list all the wrongs they’d die to put right. Now no one offered Malmer a reason. The causes had turned hazy, lately. Like far-off chimneys through the vapours, you could hardly tell if they were there or just a trick of your mind.
bs: Prije par mjeseci, na onim velikim sastancima, Folk bi se otimali tko će prije nabrojati sve nepravde za koje bi dali život da ih isprave. Sada nitko nije ponudio Malmeru razlog. Uzroci su u posljednje vrijeme postali magloviti. Poput dalekih dimnjaka kroz izmaglicu, jedva da si mogao razaznati jesu li tamo ili su samo varka tvoga uma.

en: “Thought we were doing good,” said Malmer, worn face crunched up with wrinkled disbelief. “Sure we were doing good.”
bs: — Mislili smo da činimo dobro, reče Malmer, izbrazdanog lica zgrčenog u nevjerici."Sejf smo činili dobro."

en: Wasn’t long after the taste of bread faded that Broad was back to the worried old killer he’d been that morning. The sun slunk down towards distant woods and the cold came on and they reached a knot of blank-faced soldiers collecting weapons. There was a mismatched arsenal heaped up on either side of the road—old pikestaffs, rusted swords, butchers’ cleavers and gardener’s hatchets.
bs: Nije prošlo dugo nakon što je okus kruha izblijedio, a Brod se vratio u onog zabrinutog starog ubojicu kakav je bio tog jutra. Sunce je klizilo prema dalekim šumama, hladnoća se uvlačila, a oni su stigli do skupine bezizražajnih vojnika koji su prikupljali oružje. S obje strane ceste gomilao se nespojiv arsenal — stare kopljanice, zahrđali mačevi, mesarske satare i vrtlarske sjekirice.

en: Another hour of shuffling and the sky started to darken, the mood darkening with it. Folk muttered that the Inquisition were up ahead, asking questions. Pulling people from the column. Anyone who’d been tight with the Breakers. Soldiers on horseback prowled the fields to either side of the road, torches in gauntleted fists. Some wanted to think the best. Others were sure they’d all be hanged for treason on the spot. No one left, though. Like lambs queueing up for the slaughterman’s knife, they o
bs: Nakon još Straža vremena kretanja, nebo se počelo mračiti, a s njime i raspoloženje. Folk su mrmljali da je Inkvizicija Naprijed njih i da postavljaju pitanja. Izvlače ljude iz kolone. Svakoga tko je bio blizak s Lomljačima. Vojnici na konjima krstarili su poljima s obje strane ceste, s bakljama u rukavicama. Neki su se nadali najboljem. Drugi su bili sigurni da će ih sve na licu mjesta objesiti zbog izdaje. Ipak, nitko nije otišao. Poput janjadi koja čeka u redu za mesarev nož, samo su se još č

en: “They’d see us, think we’ve something to hide. Might be best if you two move away from me.” Might’ve been best if they’d moved away from him a long time ago. But May wouldn’t hear of it.
bs: — Vidjet će nas, pomislit će da imamo što skrivati. Možda bi bilo najbolje da se vas dvoje maknete od mene. Možda bi bilo najbolje da su se od njega maknuli još davno. No Mej nije htjela ni čuti za to.

en: But there was something different about her voice. So pure, and smooth, and commanding. Something different about the way she held herself, stiffly upright with her shoulders back, her long, thin neck stretched out and her sharp jaw proudly raised. She looked half a head taller of a sudden.
bs: No bilo je nečeg drukčijeg u njezinu glasu. Tako čistog, glatkog i zapovjedničkog. Nečeg drukčijeg u načinu na koji se držala, ukočeno uspravljena, povijenih ramena, dugačkog, tankog vrata izduženog i oštre čeljusti ponosno uzdignute. Odjednom je izgledala pola glave viša.

en: “I’m surprised as you are,” muttered Broad, then nearly bit his tongue as the man shoved him and his boot caught in a rut. He was sorely tempted to punch him in the head, but it would only have got him killed and perhaps his family, too. Fighting every fight you’re offered doesn’t make you a big man, it makes you a fool.
bs: — Iznenađen sam jednako kao i ti, promrmljao je Brod, a zatim se gotovo ugrizao za jezik kad ga je čovjek gurnuo, a njegova se čizma zaplela u kolotrag. Silno ga je mamilo da ga udari u glavu, no to bi ga samo stajalo života, a možda i njegove obitelji. Boriti se u svakoj ponuđenoj tučnjavi ne čini te velikim čovjekom, čini te budalom.

en: But all she felt was a constant, nagging terror. More like a hostage taken than a prisoner freed. As bad as when she fled through the crazed streets of Valbeck on the day of the uprising. Worse, because then fear had made sense. Now, she was supposed to be safe.
bs: No, osjećala je samo stalan, nagrizajući užas. Više kao talac nego kao oslobođena zatvorenica. Bilo je to jednako loše kao i onoga dana kada je bježala kroz pomahnitale ulice Valbeka tijekom ustanka. Čak i gore, jer tada je strah imao smisla. Sada je trebala biti na sigurnom.

en: She could not smother a bark of bitter laughter. “You always were a champion liar, Orso, but that one’s a little too big even for you to lift.”
bs: Nije mogla zatomiti kratak, gorak smijeh. — Oduvijek si bio vrhunski lažljivac, Orso, ali ova je malo preteška čak i za tebe.

en: There had been a time she could talk for hours and beautifully say nothing. Now it felt obscene. Swapping light-hearted pleasantries while one party is shitting themselves all over the floor.
bs: Bilo je vrijeme kad je mogla satima razgovarati i krasno ne reći ništa. Sad joj se to činilo opscenim. Razmjenjivati bezbrižne ljubaznosti dok se jedna strana usrano trese od straha.

en: “That’s why…” He took a hard breath. As if readying himself for some great act of courage. Savine lifted her chin. As if to give the headsman an easier task. He looked up at her. Guilty. Haunted. Ashamed.
bs: — Zato… Duboko je udahnuo. Kao da se priprema za neko veliko djelo hrabrosti. Savine je podignula bradu. Kao da želi šefu krvnika olakšati posao. Pogledao ju je. Kriv. Progonjen. Posramljen.

en: He could have had anyone. But he wanted her. And not her money, not her connections, not her wigs and her dresses and her jewels. Not the idea of her. But her. At her worst. Even now. Even like this. Not just as his lover. As his wife. As his queen.
bs: Mogao je imati bilo koga. Ali želio je nju. I ne njezin novac, ne njezine veze, ne njezine perike, haljine i dragulje. Ne ideju o njoj. Nego nju. U njezinu najgorem izdanju. Čak i sada. Čak i ovakvu. Ne samo kao svoju ljubavnicu. Kao svoju ženu. Kao svoju kraljicu.

en: She caught his head, gripped it with both hands, teeth scraping, ugly grunting, undignified slurping. Awkward and fierce and urgent, as if they were running out of time. Nothing like the neat routines they used to go through in Sworbreck’s office, with all the polite back and forth of a formal dance, a dignified game in which they both kept their cards close. Now everything was on the table and it felt deadly serious, her heart thudding in her ears just as it had the day of the uprising.
bs: Uhvatila ga je za glavu, čvrsto je stisnula objema rukama, uz struganje zubi, ružno roktanje i nedostojanstveno mljackanje. Nespretno, žestoko i hitro, kao da im ponestaje vremena. Ništa nalik na uredne rutine kroz koje su prolazili u uredu Svorbrika, uz svu onu uljudnu izmjenu riječi poput formalnog plesa, dostojanstvene igre u kojoj su oboje skrivali svoje karte. Sada je sve bilo na stolu i djelovalo je smrtno ozbiljno, a srce joj je udaralo u ušima baš kao onoga dana kad je izbila pobuna.

en: In the overwritten romances her mother pretended not to read, the prince would always ride to the heroine’s rescue and whisk her from danger in the nick of time, and she would fall into his bed, swooning with gratitude, so pathetically predictable. Savine had always felt nothing but contempt for reading that nonsense, and here she was actually doing it. She didn’t care.
bs: U pretjerano napisanim romanima koje je njezina majka pretvarala da ne čita, princ bi uvijek galopirao u spas herojine i odnio je iz opasnosti u posljednji tren, a ona bi se srušila u njegovu postelju, vrtoglavica od zahvalnosti, toliko patetično predvidljivo. Savine je uvijek osjećala samo prezir za čitanje te gluposti, a evo je, zapravo to i radila. Nije joj bilo stalo.

en: “I think I can handle him,” she said. The prisoner’s wrists were shackled behind his back, after all, and chained to the chair for good measure, the bag over his head shifting as he breathed.
bs: — Mislim da ga mogu obraditi, reče. Zatvorenikove su ruke, naposljetku, bile vezane na leđima i za svaki slučaj okovane za stolicu, a vreća na njegovoj glavi pomicala se dok je disao.

en: “That’s true. But you must’ve known there’d be questions.” She looked him full in the face, so she could judge every twitch or tick or movement of his eyes. So she could sense the truth. “Where’s Risinau?”
bs: — To je istina. Ali morao si znati da će biti pitanja. Pogledala ga je ravno u lice, kako bi mogla procijeniti svaki trzaj, tik ili pokret njegovih očiju. Kako bi mogla osjetiti istinu. — Gdje je Risinau?

en: “What do you owe Risinau?” she asked. “He used you all. A blow for the common man? Don’t make me laugh. Who’s the Weaver?”
bs: — Što duguješ Risinauu? upitala je. — Iskoristio vas je sve. Udarac za običnog čovjeka? Nemoj me nasmijavati. Tko je Weaver?

en: “The honour is very much mine. That was remarkable work in Valbeck, Inquisitor. Both subtle and bold. Both cunning and courageous. Without you, this uprising might have had a far bloodier ending. But I should not be surprised. His Eminence has always had the trick of picking the right person for a job.”
bs: — Čast je potpuno moja. Bio je to izvanredan rad u Valbeku, Inkvizitorice. I suptilan i odvažan. I lukav i hrabar. Bez vas bi ova pobuna mogla imati mnogo krvaviji kraj. Ali ne bih trebao biti iznenađen. Njegova je Eminencija uvijek imala njuh za odabir prave osobe za posao.

en: “We should talk at some point, you and I.” Pike was one of those people with a nasty habit of calling you back, just to show he could.
bs: — Trebali bismo jednom popričati, ti i ja. Pajk je bio od onih Folk s gadnom navikom da te dozovu natrag, tek toliko da pokažu kako mogu.

en: But there she lay, beside him. Eyes closed, lips slightly parted, sharp collarbones gently shifting with her breath.
bs: No ona je ležala ondje, pored njega. Oči zatvorene, usne blago razdvojene, oštre ključne kosti nježno se podižu i spuštaju u ritmu njezina daha.

en: He whisked his Suljuk silk dressing gown around his shoulders, unable to wipe his grin away. There were a hundred roles he had tried and failed at, often spectacularly. Husband was one of the few remaining at which he might yet achieve dazzling success. He would not let the opportunity slip through his fingers. Not this time.
bs: Omotao se u svoju suljušku svilenu haljinu, nesposoban da skrije osmijeh s lica. Postojalo je sto uloga koje je pokušao i u kojima je propao, često spektakularno. Suprug je bila jedna od malog broja preostalih u kojima bi mogao postići sjajan uspjeh. Ne bi dopustio da mu se prilika izmakne iz ruku. Ne ovaj put.

en: This uprising had been appalling, of course, but perhaps good could come of it. It could be the moment he ceased to be a disappointment. To the world and to himself. With Savine at his side, he could do anything. Be anything. He strode up and down his tent, the ideas spilling over each other. Facing the day used to be an unbearable effort. Now he could hardly wait to get started.
bs: Ovaj ustanak bio je, …, strašan, ali možda će iz njega proizaći dobro. To bi mogao biti trenutak kada prestane biti razočaranje. Svijetu i sebi. Uz Savine uz bok, mogao je sve. Biti bilo što. Hodaše naprijed-natrag po svom šatoru, ideje se prelijevale jedna preko druge. Suočavanje s danom nekada je bilo nepodnošljiv napor. Sada je jedva čekao početi.

en: “And yet I sense the slightest frisson of hostility. Grievances are like a drunkard’s bed, Hildi. Always better aired.”
bs: "Ipak osjećam najmanji frisson neprijateljstva. Žalbe su poput kreveta pijanca, Hildi. Uvijek ih je bolje izreći naglas."

en: An officer saluted him with a hearty, “Your Highness!” and Orso could not even bring himself to acknowledge it. He wanted very much not to approach the gibbet but he had no choice, the camp mud cold on his bare feet as he picked his way closer.
bs: Časnik ga je pozdravio srdačnim: — Uzvišenost!, a Orso nije mogao ni uzvratiti pozdrav. Silno je želio ne približavati se vješalima, ali nije imao izbora; blato u taboru hladilo mu je bose noge dok je oprezno koračao prema njima.

en: “We are gibbetting two hundred of the ringleaders at quarter-mile intervals along the road from Valbeck,” droned Pike, as though Orso’s despairing shriek had been a straightforward request for information without the slightest emotional element. As though the issue was the precise positioning of the corpses, not that there were any.
bs: — Vješamo dvjesto kolovođa na razmacima od Trg milje duž ceste iz Valbeka, izrecitirao je Pajk, kao da je Orsov očajnički krik bio tek izravan upit za informaciju, lišen i najmanjeg traga emocije. Kao da je Trobli bio u preciznom rasporedu leševa, a ne u činjenici da oni uopće postoje.

en: “But I fear there was never really an alternative.” Yoru Sulfur was lying on the back of the wagon, perfectly at ease among the hanging posts with one hand behind his head. His highly specific diet evidently allowed fruit, as he had a half-eaten apple in the other. He had different-coloured eyes, Orso noticed as he gazed up calmly at the gibbet, one blue, one green. “I have seen many cases like this and, take my word for it, justice must fall like lightning. Swift and merciless.”
bs: — Ali bojim se da alternative zapravo nikada nije ni bilo. Joru Salfur ležao je na stražnjem dijelu kola, savršeno opušten među stupovima za vješanje, s jednom rukom iza glave. Njegova strogo određena prehrana očito je dopuštala voće, jer je u drugoj ruci držao napola pojedenu jabuku. Imao je oči različitih boja, primijetio je Orso dok je mirno gledao prema vješalima: jedno plavo, drugo zeleno. — Vidio sam mnogo ovakvih slučajeva i, vjerujte mi na riječ, pravda mora udariti poput munje. Brzo i n

en: Sulfur stripped his apple to the stalk and flicked it away, lazing back in the gibbet’s shadow with one hand behind his curly head. “I don’t doubt you will have made him very proud. My master, too.”
bs: Salfur je ogolio jabuku do peteljke i odbacio je, zavalivši se u sjenu vješala s jednom rukom iza kovrčave glave. — Ne sumnjam da si ga učinio vrlo ponosnim. I mog Majstora također.

en: Orso considered flinging the tea in his face, but his mouth really was very dry, so he took a sip instead. Above, the gibbet groaned and Malmer turned slowly away.
bs: Orso je razmišljao o tome da mu baci čaj u lice, ali usta su mu bila zaista vrlo suha, pa je radije otpio gutljaj. Iznad njih, vješala su zaškripala, a Malmer se polako okrenuo.

en: “The Union has been at war with the North, on and off, ever since Casamir took Angland. We cannot beat the Northmen with swords, Leo. Not for good. We will always be fighting to keep them out.” She spoke very softly. “Unless we invite them in.”
bs: — Unija je u ratu sa Sjeverom, s prekidima, otkad je Kazimir zauzeo Englend. Ne možemo pobijediti Sjevernjake mačevima, Leo. Ne zauvijek. Uvijek ćemo se boriti da ih zadržimo vani. Govorila je vrlo tiho. — Osim ako ih ne pozovemo unutra.

en: “They offer more than that,” she said, looking back to the letter. “You are invited to Adua for a triumph. A grand parade, to celebrate your victory over the Northmen! I suspect the Closed Council want the king and his son to bask in your reflected glory.”
bs: — Nude oni i više od toga, reče pogledavši ponovno pismo. — Pozvan si u Aduu na trijumf. Velika povorka, da se proslavi tvoja pobjeda nad Sjevernjacima! Sumnjam da Vijeće želi da se kralj i njegov Filio sunčaju u tvojoj reflektiranoj slavi.

en: “They don’t have to like us, as long as they don’t kill us.” Leo was starting to suspect this had been a very bad idea. But it would hardly have been his first. He put his head back and tried to walk as if he was looking for another duel right now.
bs: — Ne moraju nas voljeti, sve dok nas ne ubiju. Leo je počeo sumnjati da je ovo bila vrlo loša ideja. No, teško da bi mu bila prva. Zabacio je glavu unatrag i pokušao hodati kao da upravo sada traži novi dvoboj.

en: Leo nodded towards the glowering warriors. “Your men have no business squatting on the Dogman’s land, specially with such warlike looks. High time they went back to their families and remembered how to smile.”
bs: Leo kimne prema namrštenim ratnicima. — Tvoji Folk nemaju što tražiti na zemlji Pas Covjek Čovjeka, osobito s takvim ratobornim pogledima. Krajnje je vrijeme da se vrate svojim obiteljima i sjete se kako se smiješi.

en: Stour’s eyes gleamed in the half-light. Like a wolf’s eyes in the darkness of the forest. “And I hear you poke his scrag of a daughter.”
bs: Staurove su oči zasvijetlile u polumraku. Poput vučjih očiju u šumskoj tami. — A čujem i da prcaš njegovu kćer.

en: “I complain about it, but yes.” He was no diplomat, after all. Bluntness would win the day, or nothing would. “She’s a very clever woman.”
bs: — Žalim se na to, ali da. Naposljetku, nije bio diplomat. Izravnost će prevagnuti ili neće biti ničega. — Ona je vrlo bistra žena.

en: The room was silent again. Just the rustle as a log shifted in the fireplace. Stour had turned thoughtful, eyes fixed on Leo. Two handsome young heroes at the height of their strength. A lord governor and a king-in-waiting, ready to step out from the long shadows of their parents. A pair of champions, men of action, already with great victories under their belts, set to inherit the world and reforge it the way they saw fit.
bs: Soba ponovno utihne. Samo šuškanje dok se cjepanica pomicala u kaminu. Staur se zamislio, očiju prikovanih za Lea. Dva naočita mlada heroja na vrhuncu snage. Lord guverner i kralj u čekanju, spremni iskoračiti iz dugih sjena svojih roditelja. Par prvaka, Folk od akcije, već s velikim pobjedama pod pojasom, spremni naslijediti svijet i prekovati ga kako im drago.

en: “No one’s ever accused me of being clever. But we’ve tried being enemies.” Leo reached around the blade of Stour’s knife to scratch gently at his bandaged face. “Look where it’s got us.”
bs: — Nitko me nikada nije optužio da sam mudar. Ali pokušali smo biti neprijatelji. Leo posegne oko oštrice Staurova noža kako bi nježno počešao svoje lice pod zavojima. — Pogledaj kamo nas je to dovelo.

en: Leo bared his teeth as he walked, leaning hard on a stick. That sprinkled some guilt on her anger. He’d fought for them, after all. Risked his life for them on nothing more than her word he’d win. He stumbled, and she almost started forward to help him. But he glanced up, and saw her, and it was then he really started to look pained. As if he expected harsher treatment from her than his enemies. In that, if nothing else, he was wise.
bs: Leo je pokazivao zube dok je hodao, teško se oslanjajući na Sticks. To je njezinu ljutnju pomiješalo s krivnjom. Naposljetku, borio se za njih. Rizikovao je život na temelju njezine riječi da će pobijediti. Posrnuo je, a ona je gotovo krenula kako bi mu pomogla. No on je podigao Oko, ugledao je i tek tada mu se na licu pojavila prava bol. Kao da je od nje očekivao stroži tretman nego od svojih neprijatelja. U tome je, ako ni u čemu drugom, bio mudar.

en: Jurand loitered, frowning at Rikke, one hand out as if to catch Leo if he fell. “Do you want me to stay?”
bs: Džurand je oklijevao, mršteći se na Rike, s jednom rukom ispruženom kao da želi uhvatiti Lea ako padne. — Želiš li da ostanem?

en: Leo had that sulky-child look he got around his mother. Rikke was feeling more sympathy with her by the day. “The heir to the North owes me his life now. He’s bound to me. That’s a valuable thing—”
bs: Leo je imao onaj izraz uvrijeđenog djeteta koji bi poprimio u majčinoj blizini. Rike je iz dana u dan osjećala sve više suosjećanja prema njoj. — Nasljednik Sjevera mi sada duguje život. Vezan je uz mene. To je vrijedna stvar…

en: “Oh, aye, Ruthless Rikke, terror of the North. Seems none of the men in my life know me as well as they think. The fact is, being nice gets nothing done. You have to make of your heart a stone, Leo. You should’ve killed him.”
bs: "O, da, Nemilosrdna Rike, strah i trepet Sjevera. izgleda da me nijedan muškarac u mom životu ne poznaje onoliko dobro koliko misli. činjenica je da se ljubaznošću ništa ne postiže. Moraš pretvoriti srce u kamen, Leo. Trebao si ga ubiti."

en: “Leo dan bloody Brock,” she snarled, and in case someone had somehow missed the point, added, “that preening dunce!”
bs: — Leo dan prokleti Brok, zarežala je, a za slučaj da netko nekako nije shvatio poantu, dodala: — taj kočopereni glupan!

en: “You should only ask for promises you know are going to be kept,” said her father. “And we’re talking of the Circle.” He gave a helpless shrug. “Things happen. You’ve got to try to look on the sunny side or you’ll spend your life in darkness.”
bs: — Trebala bi tražiti samo ona obećanja za koja znaš da će biti ispunjena, reče njezin otac. — A mi govorimo o Krugu. Bespomoćno slegne ramenima. — Stvari se događaju. Moraš pokušati gledati na vedriju stranu, inače ćeš provesti život u tami.

en: All that dug from him was a wistful wince. “Wish I had some wisdom to give you. Wish I had the answers.”
bs: Sve što je time izvukao iz njega bio je sjetan trzaj. — Volio bih da ti imam kakvu mudrost pružiti. Volio bih da imam odgovore.

en: “I need to go back to Uffrith, with you. Tend to the garden, and whatever.” Though she’d never had much patience for it, and less than ever these days.
bs: — Moram se vratiti u Afrit, s tobom. Pobrini se za vrt i što već treba. Iako nikada nije imala previše strpljenja za to, a danas manje nego ikada.

en: “The feuds,” said her father, and of a sudden, he looked so tired. “The grudges. The enemies. Take it from a man with a wealth o’ bitter experience. Vengeance is just an empty chest you choose to carry. One you have to go bent under the weight of all your days. One score settled only plants the seeds of two more.”
bs: — Svađe, reče njezin otac i odjednom je izgledao tako umorno. — Zlopamćenja. Neprijatelje. Poslušaj čovjeka s bogatim iskustvom gorčine. Osveta je samo prazan sanduk koji odlučiš nositi. Sanduk pod čijom težinom moraš pognuto hodati sve svoje dane. Jedan podmiren dug samo sije sjeme za dva nova.

en: Broad looked at Liddy, and swallowed, and she looked back, eyes wide, and neither one of them had a thing to say. Footmen helped them down from the carriage. Footmen with emerald-green jackets and mirror-polished boots and great flapping lace cuffs. May stared at the man when he offered her his spotless white-gloved hand as if she was worried her fingers might stain it.
bs: Brod pogleda Lidi i proguta knedlu, a ona uzvrati pogledom, širom otvorenih očiju; nijedno od njih nije imalo što reći. Poslužitelji su im pomogli izaći iz kočije. Poslužitelji u smaragdnozelenim jaknama, s čizmama uglačanim do zrcalnog sjaja i velikim, lepršavim čipkastim manšetama. Lidi je zurila u čovjeka kad joj je ponudio svoju besprijekorno bijelu rukavicu, kao da se boji da bi je njezini prsti mogli uprljati.

en: Savine stepped forward and caught her in a hug. “It’s so good to see you, Zuri. I can’t tell you how good.”
bs: Savine zakorači naprijed i zagrli je. — Tako mi je drago vidjeti te, Zuri. Ne mogu ti opisati koliko mi je drago.

en: Rabik couldn’t have been much older than May, slight and bright-eyed, glossy black hair to his collar. He gave a quick little bow, lots of teeth in an easy smile. “And we thank you for this refuge from the chaos in the South.”
bs: Rabik nije mogao biti mnogo stariji od Mej, sitan i bistra pogleda, s crnom kosom sjajnom do ovratnika. Brzo se naklonio, pokazavši mnogo zubi u opuštenom osmijehu. — I zahvaljujemo vam na ovom utočištu od kaosa na Southu.

en: Zuri was studying him, no longer so welcoming, her black eyes hard and cautious. Broad couldn’t blame her. He and Liddy had lost the power of speech altogether. Fell to May to speak up for the family. That seemed to happen more and more.
bs: Zuri ga je proučavala, više ne tako gostoljubivo, njezine crne oči bijahu tvrde i oprezne. Brod joj nije mogao zamjeriti. On i Lidi potpuno su izgubili moć govora. Na Mej je palo da progovori u ime obitelji. Činilo se da se to događa sve češće.

en: They passed a kitchen where a woman was giving some dough a thorough pounding, another sawing away at some fish with a filleting knife. “How many people work for her?” asked Liddy.
bs: Prošli su pokraj kuhinje u kojoj je žena temeljito mijesila tijesto, dok je druga pilila ribu nožem za filetiranje. — Koliko Folk radi za nju?" upita Lidi.

en: “We are. But if I ever forgot that I am also her servant and she is also my mistress, we would not stay friends for very long.” She looked to Broad again. “What else?”
bs: — Jesmo. Ali da ikad zaboravim da sam i njezina sluškinja, a ona i moja gospa, ne bismo dugo ostale prijateljice. Oko se vratio na Borda. — Što još?

en: “I wanted to get clean first. It seems like months since I was clean.” She did not feel clean even now. However she scrubbed, the aimless dread still stuck to her like a clammy second skin.
bs: — Prvo sam se htjela očistiti. Čini mi se kao da su prošli mjeseci otkako sam bila čista. Nije se osjećala čistom ni sada. Ma koliko se ribala, besciljni užas još uvijek se lijepio za nju poput ljepljive druge kože.

en: Savine jerked herself back from the slums of Valbeck. Sipped at her glass though she’d rather have swigged from the decanter. “Where’s Father?”
bs: Savine se trznu, otjeravši od sebe prizore Valbeka. Otpila je gutljaj iz čaše, premda bi najradije potegnula iz boce. — Gdje je otac?

en: Her mother’s eyes went very wide. “Bloody hell.” She finished her glass with one long swallow. “Are you sure? Given what you’ve been through—”
bs: Majčine su se oči široko otvorile. — Prokletstvo." Ispila je čašu jednim dugim gutljajem. — Jesi li sigurna? S obzirom na ono što si prošla…

en: And she had to admit it felt fine to say it. Perhaps the snake of ambition twisted around her innards had not died in the uprising after all, only slept through it. At so heady a sniff of power, it jerked awake with twice its old hunger.
bs: Morala je priznati da joj je bilo ugodno to izgovoriti. Možda zmija ambicije, što joj se ovijala oko utrobe, ipak nije uginula u ustanku, već je samo prespala kroz njega. Na toliko opojan miris moći trznula se i probudila dvostruko gladnija nego prije.

en: Savine squatted in front of her. Caught her hands in hers. They were cold. Corpse hands. “Don’t worry. He will speak to the queen. He will speak to the king. They’ve wanted him to marry for years, they’ll be relieved he’s marrying a human! And if they’re not, he’ll convince them! I know him. I trust him. He’ll—”
bs: Savine je čučnula Naprijed nje. Uhvatila je njezine ruke svojima. Bile su hladne. Mrtvačke ruke. — Ne brini. Razgovarat će s kraljicom. Razgovarat će s kraljem. Godinama žele da se oženi, bit će im laknulo što ženi običnu smrtnicu! A ako ne budu, on će ih uvjeriti! Poznajem ga. Vjerujem mu. On će…

en: “We were lovers.” Her mother gave a helpless shrug. “Then everyone found out he was King Guslav’s bastard, and he was elected king himself and had to marry where politics dictated. But I… was already with child.”
bs: — Bili smo ljubavnici. Majka nemoćno slegne ramenima. — Onda su svi saznali da je on kopile kralja Guslava, pa je sam izabran za kralja i morao se oženiti onako kako je politika nalagala. Ali ja… ja sam već bila trudna.

en: “I’m so sorry,” murmured her mother, patting her back as though that might do the slightest good. “I’m so sorry.” She took Savine’s face in her hands and twisted it towards her. Twisted it with surprising firmness. “But you cannot tell anyone. Not anyone. Especially not Orso.”
bs: — Tako mi je žao, promrmlja majka, tapšući je po leđima kao da bi to moglo imalo pomoći. — Tako mi je žao. Uhvati Savine za lice i okrene ga prema sebi. Okrene ga iznenađujućom čvrstinom. — Ali ne smiješ nikome reći. Nikome. A pogotovo ne Orsu.

en: Tunny shrugged. “The rich folk seem to like you more than ever.” It was true that a polite crowd of well-dressed well-wishers had been gathered at the gates of Adua to welcome him. “And they can express their love financially.”
bs: Tani slegne ramenima. — izgleda da te bogati puk voli više nego ikada." Bila je istina da se pristojna gomila dobro odjevenih simpatizera okupila na vratima Adue kako bi ga dočekala. — A oni svoju ljubav mogu izraziti financijski.

en: Orso went straight to the decanter and pulled out the stopper. It was hard to think of a good reason for the stopper ever to be in, really. “I find I can hardly compete with the victories of the Young Lion, however.”
bs: Orso je otišao ravno do bokala i izvukao čep. Doista je bilo teško pronaći valjan razlog zašto bi čep uopće trebao biti unutra. — S tim da jedva mogu konkurirati pobjedama Mlada Lava.

en: The queen’s head snapped towards him like that of a hawk that has spotted a vole in the bracken. “You mean it?”
bs: Kraljičina Šef trgnula se prema njemu poput jastrebove koja je ugledala voluharicu u paprati. — Misliš ozbiljno?

en: He was interrupted by a knock at the door. It creaked open a crack and Hildi’s head slid through. She fumbled off her cap to reveal blonde curls for some reason cropped short. “I’ve got that message you’ve been waiting for, Your Highness.” And she showed the letter. Just a square of white paper with a white seal. Such a small package to hold all his dreams.
bs: Prekinulo ga je kucanje na vratima. Škripnula su, otvorila se tek toliko da se provuče Šef Hildi. Nespretno je skinula kapu otkrivši plave uvojke, iz nekog razloga kratko ošišane. — Imam poruku koju ste čekali, Uzvišenost." Pokazala je pismo. Tek Trg bijelog papira s bijelim pečatom. Tako malen paket, a sadržavao je sve njegove snove.

en: And now came a flood of cold loss. Like that, all his dreams were ruined. It was a note that left no room for hope. No room for wheedling, even by a veteran wheedler like him. I would ask you not to contact me again. Ever. There would never be another woman who understood him the way she did. There would never be another woman like her at all. She had never felt so dazzlingly desirable as she did now he could never have her.
bs: A sada je naišla plima hladnog gubitka. Tek tako, svi njegovi snovi bili su uništeni. Bila je to poruka koja nije ostavljala mjesta nadi. Nije bilo mjesta za nagovaranje, čak ni za vještog nagovarača poput njega. Molim te da me više ne kontaktiraš. Nikada. Nikada više neće biti žene koja ga je razumjela kao ona. Nikada više neće biti žene poput nje. Nikada mu nije djelovala tako zasljepljujuće poželjno kao sada, kada je nikada neće moći imati.

en: “It’s me,” said Tallow, with his flair for stating the obvious. Vick had known it would be him. Wasn’t as if she got a lot of visitors.
bs: —— Ja sam, reče Talou, uz svoj dar za izgovaranje očitih stvari. Vik je znala da će to biti on. Nije kao da je imala mnogo posjetitelja.

en: Tallow nodded in a way that seemed to say no thanks to you. Or maybe she just thought it did. She nudged a chair out with her boot and he slipped into it, around the squares board. Wasn’t easy, even thin as he was.
bs: Talou kimne na način koji je govorio ne zahvaljujući tebi. Ili je ona samo mislila da govori to. Gurnula je stolicu čizmom i on se skliznuo u nju, oko ploče za igru na Trgu. Nije bilo lako, čak ni njemu tako mršavom.

en: “I’ll take a double serving o’ that, then.” Tallow glanced about her narrow, bare apartment with those big eyes of his, the walls mottled with damp around the dirty window. “So this is what you do it for?”
bs: — Onda ću uzeti duplu porciju toga. Talou je svojim krupnim očima prešao preko njezina tijesnog, ogoljenog stana, zidova išaranih vlagom oko prljavog prozora. — Dakle, zbog ovoga to radiš?

en: He swallowed, sharp knobble on the front of his throat shifting, then he reached out and swept the coin off the table. Just like she’d known he would. She had to smile at that. Hell, but he was like her brother.
bs: Progutao je knedlu, oštra se jabučica na njegovu grlu pomaknula, a zatim je posegnuo i pokupio novčić sa stola. Baš kao što je znala da hoće. Morala se nasmiješiti na to. Do vraga, bio je poput njezina brata.

en: “As if either one of us will find rest this side of the grave.” Glokta gave her his hollow smile. “You did an excellent job in Valbeck. You showed quick thinking, courage and loyalty. Superior Pike was most impressed, and he is a hard man to impress.”
bs: — Kao da će itko od nas pronaći spokoj s ove strane groba. Glokta joj uputi svoj šuplji osmijeh. — Obavila si izvrstan posao u Valbeku. Pokazala si brzinu razmišljanja, hrabrost i odanost. Superior Pajk bio je vrlo impresioniran, a njega je teško impresionirati.

en: “I know exactly what’s wrong with them. I used to live in them. When I served my predecessor, Arch Lector Sult.”
bs: — Točno znam što s njim ne valja. I sam u njemu živio. Dok sam služio svome prethodniku, Lektoru Sultu.

en: “They were taxed heavily to pay for the king’s wars in Styria.” Glokta scarcely moved his thin lips as he spoke. “They demanded reforms to compensate, acquired a great deal of common land. Many lined their pockets handsomely. Nonetheless, most of the Open Council recently signed a letter of complaint to the king.”
bs: — Bili su silno opterećeni porezima kako bi platili kraljeve ratove u Stiriji. Glokta jedva da je pomaknuo svoje tanke usne dok je govorio. — Zahtijevali su reforme kao kompenzaciju, prisvojili golemu količinu općinskog zemljišta. Mnogi su dobro napunili svoje džepove. Ipak, većina Otvorenog Vijeća nedavno je potpisala pismo žalbe upućeno kralju.

en: She’d heard it was big. Everyone had heard that. If anyone went to Adua, they’d come back scratching their heads and saying, “It’s big,” but she’d never expected it to be this big. You might’ve fitted a hundred Uffriths into it and still had room for a hundred Carleons. Her eye couldn’t make sense of the scale. The number of buildings, the number of ships, the number of people, like ants in an anthill. A thousand anthills. The thought of it was making her head spin. Or spin more, maybe. She look
bs: Čula je da je velik. Svi su to čuli. Tko god bi otišao u Aduu, vratio bi se češući se po glavi i govoreći: — Velik je, ali nikada nije očekivala da će biti toliko velik. Mogla je u njega nagurati stotinu Afrita, a još bi ostalo mjesta za stotinu Carleona. Njezino Oko nije moglo pojmiti tu Ljusku. Broj zgrada, broj brodova, broj Folk, poput mrava u mravinjaku. en: He glanced towards her and she made sure she looked away. Him catching her looking would be like he’d scored a point somehow. But looking away from Leo meant looking back to this bald bastard, who was still considering her as if he found her of quite some interest.
bs: Bacila je Oko prema njemu, a on se pobrinuo da odvrati svoj. Da je uhvati kako ga gleda, značilo bi da je nekako osvojio bod. No, skretanje pogleda s Lea značilo je vraćanje pogleda na onog ćelavog gadčića, koji ju je i dalje promatrao kao da joj pridaje priličnu važnost.

en: “Speak for yourself,” she said, shifting her chagga pellet across her mouth and chomping it on the other side. “I’ve been blessed with the Long Eye.” At that moment, she glimpsed the faintest phantom of a sinking ship, its mast tipping towards them as it foundered on a stormy sea. She cleared her throat, doing her best to ignore the ghostly sailors toppling into the brine. “Or possibly cursed with it.”
bs: — Govori u svoje ime, odvrati ona, prebacujući zalogaj čage s jedne strane usta na drugu i zagrizavši ga s druge. — Ja sam blagoslovljena Dugim okom. U tom trenutku ugledala je blijedu utvaru lađe koja tone, čiji se jarbol nagnuo prema njima dok se nasukavala na olujnom moru. Pročistila je grlo, dajući sve od sebe da ignorira sablasne mornare koji su padali u slanu vodu. — Ili možda prokleta njime.

en: Bayaz gave a disappointed sigh, like the governess in Ostenhorm when she tried to explain to Rikke what deportment was. “People must sometimes be allowed to make their own mistakes.”
bs: Bajaz uzdahne razočarano, poput guvernante u Ostenhormu kada je pokušavala Rike objasniti što je to pristojno ponašanje. — Ljudima se ponekad mora dopustiti da čine vlastite pogreške.

en: He was cranking himself up to bitter outrage when he caught sight of her, waving her arms in that mad way she had while she talked to some bald old man, and all he felt was sad, and guilty, as if he’d wandered off the right path and couldn’t find his way back. The truth was, he bloody missed her. Wasn’t long ago he’d said he loved her, and he’d at least half meant it. But he was damned if he was apologising. It should be her begging forgiveness—
bs: Baš se spremao prepustiti ogorčenju kad ju je ugledao kako mlara rukama na onaj svoj ludi način dok razgovara s nekim ćelavim starcem, a sve što je osjećao bili su tuga i krivnja, kao da je zalutao s pravog puta i ne može pronaći izlaz. Istina je bila da mu je silno nedostajala. Nije prošlo tako davno otkad joj je rekao da je voli, a to je barem upola mislio ozbiljno. No neka ga Tojfel odnese ako joj se bude ispričao. Ona je trebala moliti za oprost —

en: “Your Grace, I am Lord Chamberlain Hoff, son of Lord Chamberlain Hoff.” He paused, as though expecting gales of laughter. None came. No doubt bureaucrats were a regrettable necessity, like latrines, but Leo didn’t have to like them. Especially when bureaucracy became a family business. “And this is—”
bs: — Vaša Visosti, ja sam lord komornik Hoff, Filio lorda komornika Hoff. Zastao je, kao da očekuje gromoglasan smijeh. Smijeha nije bilo. Birokrati su nesumnjivo bili žalosna nužnost, poput nužnika, ali Leo ih nije morao voljeti. Pogotovo kad bi birokracija postala obiteljski posao. — A ovo je —

en: “Huh.” Leo had spent more than enough of his life worrying about his mother’s feelings. He abruptly changed the subject. “I would’ve loved to train with you while I’m here, but… I fear I’m in no fit state. Maybe I could observe?”
bs: — Hm. Leo je potrošio više nego dovoljno vremena brinući se o majčinim osjećajima. Naglo promijeni temu. — Volio bih da sam mogao trenirati s vama dok sam ovdje, ali… bojim se da nisam u stanju. Možda bih mogao promatrati?

en: Rikke raised her brows as a whole column of dark-skinned soldiers tramped out of a side street, gilded standards flashing and spears lowered. Wasn’t until a wagon rattled right through ’em she realised they weren’t there.
bs: Rike podigne obrve dok je čitava kolona tamnoputih vojnika marširala iz sporedne ulice, sa pozlaćenim stjegovima koji su sijevali i spuštenim kopljima. Tek kad su kola protutnjala ravno kroz njih, shvatila je da nisu stvarni.

en: By the dead, the air. Close and sticky and full of odd smells. There was a catch and a scratch in her throat, a sting at her eyes, like far-off burning. And the noise. The babbling in a dozen languages she didn’t know, pleading, shouting, fighting, everyone shoving on to nowhere as if they were all endlessly late for everything. Hammers clanging, wheels turning and fires burning, so many it became a low rumble that made the ground buzz. As though the city itself were alive, and tortured, and ang
bs: Mrtvih mi, taj zrak. Gust i ljepljiv, pun čudnih mirisa. Osjećala je grebanje i stezanje u grlu, peckanje u očima, kao od nekog dalekog Velikog Gorenja. A tek buka. Žamor na desetak jezika koje nije razumjela, preklinjanje, vikanje, borba; svi su se gurali nekamo kao da beskrajno kasne na sve. Čekići su odzvanjali, kotači se okretali, a vatre gorjele – toliko ih je bilo da su se pretvorile u nisko brujanje od kojeg je tlo podrhtavalo. en: Bayaz smiled. He was a hard bastard to rattle, the First of the Magi. “The figurehead goes at the front of the ship. Braves the terror of wind and waves, takes the risks and reaps the glory. But it’s an unnoticed fellow hidden away near the back who does the steering.” He smiled up towards the head of the column. “No leader worth a damn ever led from the front.”
bs: Bajaz se nasmiješio. Bio je to tvrd orah, taj Prvi među Magi. — Figura na pramcu krasi brod. Prkosi strahotama vjetra i valova, preuzima rizike i ubire slavu. Ali onaj neprimijećeni lik skriven negdje straga upravlja kormilom." Pogledao je prema čelu kolone. — Nijedan vođa vrijedan spomena nikada nije vodio s čela.

en: Sulfur smiled wider, his eyes never leaving her face, and she realised they were different colours, one blue, one green. “We relics of the Age of Magic really should stick together.”
bs: Salfur se još šire nasmiješio, očiju koje nisu napuštale njezino lice, a ona shvati da su različitih boja, jedno plavo, jedno zeleno. — Mi relikvije iz Doba Magije doista bismo se trebali držati zajedno.

en: His Eminence made Leo wait an insultingly long time before he finally looked up, winced as he leaned to drop his pen into its bottle of ink, and smiled. On that gaunt, waxy, wasted face, etched by deep grimace-lines, a yawning gap where the four front teeth should’ve been, it was an expression as painfully unsettling as a leg bent the wrong way at the knee. Na tom suhom, voštanom, izmučenom licu, izbrazdanom dubokim borama od grimasa, sa zjapećom prazninom gdje su trebala biti četiri prednja zuba, taj je izraz bio bolno uznemirujuć, poput noge savijene u pogrešnom smjeru u koljenu. en: The Arch Lector’s eyelid flickered and a tear rolled down his cheek. He wiped it gently away with a fingertip. “His Highness won a famous victory of his own recently, putting down a rebellion in Valbeck—”
bs: Vrhovnom Lektoru zatreperio je kapak, a suza mu se otkotrljala niz obraz. Nježno ju je obrisao vrhom prsta. — Njegovo je Visočanstvo nedavno izvojevalo vlastitu glasovitu pobjedu, ugušivši pobunu u Valbeku…

en: “No further concessions?” asked Glokta, his eyes glittering in their deep, bruised sockets. “No ongoing assurances?”
bs: — Nikakvih daljnjih ustupaka? upita Glokta, dok su mu oči sjajile u dubokim, modrim dupljama. — Nikakvih trajnih jamstava?

en: “I…” Leo could hardly believe it. “I made a friend of the next King of the Northmen! I’m a soldier, not a bloody diplomat!”
bs: — Ja… Leo jedva povjerova. — Sprijateljio sam se s budućim kraljem Sjevernjaka! Ja sam vojnik, a ne jebeni diplomat!

en: So Broad reckoned he was a coachman now. He had the livery, anyway. Bright green jacket with brass buttons, better than most officers had got in Styria. Shiny new boots, too, though they were prone to pinch. He might’ve felt quite the fool in all the finery, if it hadn’t been so clear that anyone within a hundred paces would be staring at Savine instead, and that included him.
bs: Brod je dakle zaključio da je sada kočijaš. u svakom slučaju, nosio je livreju. Jarkozelenu jaknu s mjedenim gumbima, bolju nego što su je imali većina časnika u Stiriji. I sjajne nove čizme, premda su ga imale običaj žuljati. Vjerojatno bi se osjećao posve smiješno u toj nakinđurenoj odjeći da nije bilo očito kako će svatko u krugu od stotinjak koraka umjesto toga zuriti u Savine, u što je spadao i on sam.

en: “Lady Savine, I am delighted to see you well.” Kort gave Broad a slightly troubled smile. Broad didn’t return it. He was getting the sense he hadn’t been brought there to smile. “Everyone has been… extremely worried.”
bs: — Gospođo Savine, presretan sam što vas vidim dobrog zdravlja. Kort uputi Brodu blago zabrinut osmijeh. Brod mu ga ne uzvrati. Obuzimao ga je dojam da ondje nije doveden kako bi se smiješio. — Svi su bili… iznimno zabrinuti.

en: Kort shifted uncomfortably in his chair. “The banking house of Valint and Balk was kind enough to act as her backer, and she was kind enough to act as mine. Lady Savine, I was really given no choice—”
bs: Kort se nemirno promigolji u stolici. — Bankarska kuća Valint i Balk bila je ljubazna stati iza nje kao jamac, a ona je bila ljubazna stati iza mene. Gospođo Savine, doista nisam imao izbora…

en: He knew exactly what Savine wanted. He’d seen that look in her eye before, on some of the men he’d fought with. The ones you had to watch. The ones you had to worry about. He knew he’d had the same look. A kind of mad delight that it had come to this.
bs: Točno je znao što Savine želi. Već je vidio taj izraz u njezinim očima, na nekim ljudima s kojima se borio. Onima na koje si morao paziti. Onima zbog kojih si se morao brinuti. Znao je da je i sam imao isti izraz. Nekakav suludi užitak što je došlo do ovoga.

en: “You displease me,” said Savine. “And I am in a mood to see things which displease me broken. Broken in such a way that they will not go back together.”
bs: — Nezadovoljna sam tobom, rekla je Savine. — A raspoložena sam vidjeti kako se stvari koje me čine nezadovoljnom lome. Lome na takav način da se više neće moći sastaviti.

en: “Marvellous.” Savine pulled on one of her gloves while Zuri slipped her hat back on with masterful precision and slid the hatpin home. “I would hate to have to send Master Broad to see you without my restraining influence. Who knows what might happen?”
bs: — Divno. Savine je navukla jednu rukavicu dok je Zuri majstorskom preciznošću nataknula Hat natrag na glavu i gurnula šeširnu iglu do kraja. — Bilo bi mi mrsko morati poslati Majstora Broda da te posjeti bez mog obuzdavajućeg utjecaja. Tko zna što bi se moglo dogoditi?

en: “If he was set that firmly against it…” And Zuri smiled as she closed his aching fist around the coin and gave it a fond pat. “Why would he make men like you?”
bs: — Da je bio toliko čvrsto protiv toga… Zuri se nasmiješila zatvarajući njegov bolni dlan oko novčića i nježno ga potapšala. — Zašto bi stvarao ljude poput tebe?

en: “It’s an outrage, if you ask me,” murmured a tall man maybe ten years older than Leo, though his carefully swept hair was pure white.
bs: — To je nečuveno, ako mene pitate, promrmlja visok muškarac možda desetak godina stariji od Lea, iako mu je pažljivo začešljana kosa bila posve bijela.

en: “My father knew your father well.” Barezin’s jowls shook with feeling. “Such a wonderful man, he was always telling me, such a man’s man, such an exemplar of the noble virtues! They were close friends.” As far as Leo could remember, his father had always written the Open Council off as a nest of vipers. But this was a new generation, and he reckoned you can never have too many friends.
bs: — Moj otac je dobro poznavao tvoga oca. Obrazi su se Barezinovi tresli od emocija. — Kakav divan čovjek, stalno mi je govorio, pravi muškarac, oličenje plemenitih vrlina! Bili su bliski prijatelji. Koliko se Leo mogao prisjetiti, njegov je otac Vijeće oduvijek smatrao leglom zmija. No ovo je bila nova generacija, a držao je da čovjek nikad ne može imati previše prijatelja.

en: “Really?” asked Leo, getting just a bit suspicious of their close-harmony flattery. “I heard he was a traitor.”
bs: — Zbilja? upita Leo, počevši sumnjati u njihovo usklađeno podilaženje. — Čuo sam da je bio izdajica.

en: Selest. Had a nice ring to it. And she had this breathless way of acting as though every word he said was a delightful surprise.
bs: Selest. Zvučalo je privlačno. I imala je taj zadihani način ponašanja, kao da mu je svaka izgovorena riječ bila divno iznenađenje.

en: Everyone was so clean. Everyone smelled so good. Everyone’s shoes were so shiny. They all had these little smiles, worn like masks, so you’d no notion what they were really thinking. They all spoke in whispers, like everything was a secret meant only for particular ears and those ears certainly weren’t hers. At least the Long Eye was leaving her alone for now. The only ghosts in attendance were her own awkward reflections, wincing at her, profoundly unimpressed, from the mirrored walls of the ha
bs: Svi su bili tako čisti. Svi su mirisali tako lijepo. Svačije su cipele bile tako uglancane. Svi su nosili te male osmijehe poput maski, tako da nisi imao pojma što doista misle. Svi su govorili u šapatima, kao da je sve bila tajna namijenjena samo određenim ušima, a te uši zasigurno nisu bile njezine. Barem ju je Long Eye za sada ostavljala na miru. Jedini duhovi koji su prisustvovali bili su njezini vlastiti nespretni odrazi koji su se zgražali nad njom, duboko razočarani, s ogledalskih zidova

en: By the dead, this one was even more beautiful than the other. Her skin had this sheen, like she wasn’t made of meat but some magic alloy of flesh and silver, every gesture finished off right to the tips of her long fingers like it was part of a dance, endlessly practised and utterly perfected.
bs: Tako mi mrtvih, ova je bila još ljepša od one druge. Koža joj je imala onaj sjaj, kao da nije stvorena od mesa, već od neke čarobne legure puti i srebra, a svaki joj je pokret bio dovršen do vrhova njezinih dugih prstiju, kao da je dio plesa, beskrajno uvježbanog i posve usavršenog.

en: “Is it?” Rikke stared at those shining braids coiled and piled and swept up like a nest of spun gold. “Looks like hair, just… more so.”
bs: — Stvarno? Rike zuri u one sjajne pletenice, smotane, naslagane i podignute poput gnijezda od ispredenog zlata. — Izgleda kao kosa, samo… još više.

en: She actually seemed to mean it, and she’d been kind, in a way. “Here.” Rikke took the runes off and slipped them gently over the woman’s head. “Maybe they’ll work better for you.”
bs: Djelovalo je kao da to uistinu misli, a bila je, na svoj način, ljubazna. — Evo." Rike je skidala rune i nježno ih prebacivala ženi preko glave. — Možda će tebi bolje služiti.

en: Whenever someone expressed their disingenuous condolences over her ordeal, or their unconvincing relief at her safe return, she wanted to knock them down and grind her heel into their eye. She’d been sniffing pearl dust all day. Just a pinch at sunup to chase off the nightmares. Then a pinch at breakfast to keep her head above water. Maybe a couple more before lunch. Only rather than keeping her sharp, the way it used to, it was making her twitchy and savage and strangely reckless.
bs: Kad god bi joj netko izrazio neiskrenu sućut zbog njezine muke, ili neuvjerljivo olakšanje zbog njezina sigurnog povratka, poželjela bi ih oboriti na tlo i zabiti petu u njihovo oko. Cijeli je dan ušmrkavala biserni prah. Samo prstohvat u zoru da otjera noćne more. Zatim prstohvat uz doručak da zadrži glavu iznad vode. Možda još koji prije ručka. No, umjesto da je drži oštrom, kao što je nekad činila, činila ju je nervoznom, divljom i čudno nepromišljenom.

en: Savine put a finger under her chin to tip her face into the light. “Fine strong bones. Excellent teeth. And your eyes, of course.” Huge and pale and so very expressive. “I’ve never seen anything quite like them.”
bs: Savine joj podvuče prst pod bradu kako bi joj lice okrenula prema svjetlosti. — Dobre, čvrste kosti. Izvrsne zube. I tvoje oči." Ogromne, blijede i silno izražajne. — Nikad nisam vidjela ništa slično.

en: She had to stop herself flinching at the sight of Orso, draped against a pillar, looking drunk and despondent. It was as though there was a hook in her throat, and every glimpse of him was a painful tug on it. She was ashamed to admit it, but she wanted him no less. She certainly wanted to be queen no less. Her one desire was to go over to him and put her hand in his and say yes, and kiss him, and hold him, and watch the smile spread across his face…
bs: Morala se suzdržati da ne pretrne pri pogledu na Orsa koji se naslanjao na stup, izgledajući pijano i malodušno. Bilo je to kao da joj netko drži udicu u grlu, a svaki njegov prizor bio je bolan trzaj iste. Sramila se to priznati, ali željela ga je ništa manje. Cijenila bi manje i to da postane kraljica. Jedina joj je želja bila otići do njega, staviti svoju ruku u njegovu, reći da, poljubiti ga, zagrliti ga i promatrati kako mu se osmijeh širi licem…

en: “Please excuse me,” she managed to whisper, turning so fast she almost stumbled. She took a wobbling step or two, weak at the knees.
bs: — Molim vas, ispričajte me, uspjela je prošaptati okrenuvši se tako naglo da se zamalo spotaknula. Napravila je korak-dva teturajući, slaba u koljenima.

en: The temptation to bite her was almost overwhelming. But Savine only shrugged. “I was far from the only one who suffered.”
bs: Napast da je ugrize bila je gotovo neizdrživa. No Savine je samo slegnula ramenima. — Nisam bila ni blizu jedina koja je patila.

en: “Or lucky cowardice, in my case. I saw one of the guards dragged into the machinery. His arm was ripped off in the gears.”
bs: — Ili sretnog kukavičluka, u mom slučaju. Vidjela sam kako jednog stražara vuku u strojeve. Zupčanici su mu otkinuli ruku.

en: “I stumbled upon some decent people and… they took me in. They kept me alive, until Prince Orso delivered the city.” Selest dan Heugen knew when she was beaten. She snapped her fan open and drifted off. The chill satisfaction of victory was the closest Savine had come to pleasure in some time. She might never be Queen of the Union, but she still reigned supreme over the ballroom. “And here I am.”
bs: — Naletjela sam na neke pristojne ljude i… primili su me. Održali su me na životu sve dok princ Orso nije oslobodio grad. Selest dan Heugen znala je kada je poražena. Naglo je otvorila lepezu i odlepršala. Hladna zadovoljština pobjede bila je najbliže što je Savine u posljednje vrijeme došla užitku. Možda nikada neće biti kraljica Unije, ali je i dalje suvjereno vladala plesnom dvoranom. — I evo me.

en: “It must be hard to tell the genuine admiration from the empty breath. Surrounded by people, but all alone.” She gave a theatrical sigh. “Everyone trying to make use of you.”
bs: — Mora biti teško razlikovati iskreno divljenje od praznog zduha. Okružena ljudima, a potpuno sama. Izdala je teatarski uzdah. — Svi pokušavaju iskoristiti tebe.

en: Well, to be precise, he stood, and drank, and watched Savine. Surreptitiously, to begin with. But less surreptitiously with every drink. Just watching her was torture. Watching her with that square-jawed oaf Leo dan Brock was triply so. A torture that for some reason he could not stop inflicting on himself.
bs: Dobro, točnije, ustao je, popio i promatrao Savine. Na početku diskretno. Ali sve manje diskretno s svakim gutljajem. Samo Straža je bilo mučnina. Straža je s tim kvadratno-bradim budalom Leom Brokom bilo trostruko gorše. Mučnina koju je iz nekog razloga ne mogao prestati nanositi sebi.

en: “One must trim one’s style to the times,” said Bayaz, holding up his cane and admiring the way the light shone through the crystal knob. “My master used to say that knowledge is the root of power, but I rather suspect power has a golden root these days. We have met before, in fact, Your Highness. Though you, I think, cannot have been more than four years old.”
bs: — Čovjek mora prilagoditi svoj stil vremenu, odvrati Bajaz podignuvši Sticks i diveći se kako svjetlost prosjajuje kroz kristalnu kuglu na vrhu. — Moj je Majstor znao govoriti kako je znanje korijen moći, premda sumnjam da danas moć ima zlatni korijen. Uostalom, već smo se upoznali, Vaše Visočanstvo. Mada mislim da tada nisi mogao imati više od četiri godine.

en: “Hugely,” echoed Orso, anger stabbing at him through the fug of drunkenness. “Indeed, he made himself useful in the hanging of two hundred innocent people. People I had promised amnesty!”
bs: "I te kako", ponovi Orso dok ga je bijes probadao kroz izmaglicu pijanstva. — Doista, bio je silno koristan pri vješanju dviju stotina nevinih Folk! Folk kojima sam obećao pomilovanje!

en: He would have been furious with her, but he could no more hate her than a drunk can the bottle. He would have been furious with Leo dan Brock, but he had done nothing wrong, the horribly but justifiably vain, magnificently manly, utterly superficial bastard. He was doing exactly what Orso would have done in his place, only looking like a hero while he did it.
bs: Bio bi bijesan na nju, ali mrziti je mogao onoliko koliko pijanac može mrziti bocu. Bio bi bijesan na Lea dan Broka, ali on nije učinio ništa pogrešno, taj užasno, ali opravdano tašt, veličanstveno muževan, do srži površan gad. Činio je upravo ono što bi i Orso učinio na njegovu mjestu, samo što je pritom izgledao poput heroja.

en: He had always been the most wretched judge of what he needed, but what he needed right now might be the woman who was least like Savine in the world. And here, as if by magic…
bs: Uvijek je bio očajan procjenitelj vlastitih potreba, ali ono što mu je u ovom trenutku trebalo možda je bila žena koja je najmanje nalikovala Savine na svijetu. I gle, kao čarolijom…

en: “Witch, no. Future, sometimes.” She winced, pressed a hand to her left eye as though it hurt. “A bit too much, lately.”
