bs: — Vještica, ne. Budućnost, ponekad. Zgrčila se i pritisnula dlan na lijevo oko kao da je boli. — Malo previše, u posljednje vrijeme.

en: “Somewhere far from prying eyes, I suppose.” Leo nudged him in the ribs with his elbow. “Wouldn’t want to cause a scandal, would we?”
bs: — Nekamo daleko od znatiželjnih pogleda, pretpostavljam. Leo ga laktom gurne u rebra. — Ne bismo željeli izazvati skandal, zar ne?

en: “Cheer up.” Leo hugged him roughly with one arm, looking back to the building. The one lit window. “There are plenty of ladies for all of us.” Though he couldn’t think of any close to Savine dan Glokta’s class.
bs: — Razvedri se. Leo ga grubo zagrli jednom rukom, osvrćući se prema zgradi. Prema onom jednom osvijetljenom prozoru. — Ima dovoljno dama za sve nas. Iako se nije mogao sjetiti se nikoga tko bi bio ravan Savine dan Glokti.

en: It seemed a long way up that darkened staircase, his heart beating so loud they could’ve heard it in the street, the chink of light below the black door getting steadily closer, promising so much. He’d no idea what to expect. Wouldn’t have shocked him to find Savine waiting with a loaded flatbow. Or stretched out naked on a tiger skin. Or both, for that matter.
bs: Činilo se da je to mračno stubište dugačko unedogled, srce mu je tuklo toliko glasno da su ga mogli čuti na ulici, a procjep svjetlosti ispod crnih vrata bivao je sve bliži, obećavajući toliko toga. Nije imao pojma što može očekivati. Ne bi se iznenadio da zatekne Savine kako čeka s napetim samostrelom. Ili ispruženu nagu na tigrovoj koži. Ili oboje, uostalom.

en: “Why did I come here?” he asked, pushing the door shut, half a weak effort at a joke, half actually wanting an answer.
bs: — Zašto sam onda došao ovamo? upita zatvarajući vrata, napola u šali, napola stvarno želeći odgovor.

en: The truth was, Leo had never been that comfortable around women. But perhaps comfortable is the last thing romance should be. Perhaps it should have an edge. And every moment with Savine felt as thrilling and dangerous as stepping into the Circle with the Great Wolf.
bs: Istina je bila da se Leo nikad nije osjećao osobito ugodno u ženskom društvu. No možda je opuštenost posljednja stvar koju bi ljubav trebala pružati. Možda bi trebala imati oštricu. A svaki trenutak sa Savine bio je uzbudljiv i opasan poput ulaska u Round s Velikim vukom.

en: “Only if you press—ah!” She very deliberately pressed it, her teeth savagely bared for an instant, and made him flinch away, twisted even more uncomfortably over the desk.
bs: — Samo ako pritisneš… ah! — Vrlo namjerno pritisnula je, na trenutak divljački ogolivši zube, i natjerala ga da se trzne, još se neugodnije izvijajući preko stola.

en: “Ah, by the dead!” Fire burned to the back of his throat, out into his ears, down into his teeth, brought tears to his eyes. A horrible sensation. “Why the hell would anyone—”
bs: — Ah, tako mi mrtvih! — Palioc mu je pekla stražnji dio grla, širila se u uši, spuštala u zube i natjerala suze na oči. Užasan osjećaj. — Zašto bi itko, do vraga…

en: He gave a lion’s growl as he caught her face, thumb under her jaw, caught the strap of her dress and gripped it, twisted it, his knuckles pressing hard into her shoulder, making her gasp, turning her, until he was the one shoving her up against the edge of the desk. He caught his foot on his sword, staggered, and she kicked it away with one pointed shoe, blade half falling out of the scabbard as it clattered into the lion-carved feet of the printing press.
bs: Zarežao je poput lava dok joj je obuhvatio lice, palcem pod bradom, uhvatio naramenicu njezine haljine i stisnuo je, zasukao, sa zglobovima čvrsto prislonjenim uz njezino rame, natjeravši je da zadišano uzdahne i okrene se, sve dok ju nije počeo gurati prema rubu pisaćeg stola. Zapleo se nogom o mač, posrnuo, a ona ga je otisnula vrhom cipele dok mu je oštrica napola kliznula iz korica i zveckajući udarila o lavlje noge tiskarskog stroja.

en: She was lying with a sheet tangled around her hips, one leg sticking out, which she knew must be hers ’cause she could wriggle the toes. She was stark naked but for her shirt, the sleeve all rucked up around one wrist and the rest spread out limp across the bed like a flag of surrender.
bs: Ležala je s plahtom zapletenom oko bokova, s jednom nogom koja je virila van, za koju je znala da mora biti njezina jer je mogla micati prstima. Bila je potpuno gola, osim košulje čiji se rukav zgužvao oko jednog zapešća, dok se ostatak tkanine opušteno širio po krevetu poput zastave predaje.

en: “There’s no point being a crown prince if you mean to do all the hard work. But look, I carried it from the door to the bed.” And he gestured at the path he’d taken. “As you observed last night, fucking a crown prince is no great distinction, even if you did it rather bloody well—”
bs: — Nema smisla biti prijestolonasljednik ako namjeravaš obavljati sav Trdak posao. Ali pogledaj, donio sam ga od vrata do kreveta. Pokazao je rukom put kojim je prošao. — Kao što si primijetila sinoć, jebati prijestolonasljednika nije neka velika čast, čak i ako si to učinila prilično jebeno dobro —

en: She gave a disbelieving snort. “Hear this shit. ‘His Highness was observed leaving the function in the company of the beautiful and mysterious Witch of the North…’”
bs: Zlovoljno je frknula. — Poslušaj ovo sranje. ‚Uzvišenost je viđeno kako napušta primanje u društvu lijepe i tajanstvene Vještice s Sjevera…’"

en: Orso’s mouth twisted. “I don’t deserve a parade. Unless it happened to be stomping over me, I suppose.” And he flopped down on his back, staring up at the gilded leaves on the ceiling.
bs: Orsu su se iskrivile usne. — Ne zaslužujem nikakvu paradu. Osim ako bi se ona slučajno sastojala od gaženja po meni, pretpostavljam." I srušio se na leđa, zureći u pozlaćene listiće na stropu.

en: The queen made an arch of one perfect brow. “When it comes to building close diplomatic ties with the future King of the Union, one cannot fault her commitment.”
bs: Kraljica je podigla savršenu obrvu. — Kada je riječ o izgradnji bliskih diplomatskih veza s budućim kraljem Unije, ne može joj se zamjeriti predanost.

en: “Wonderful.” Orso was looking down at her, too, the ghost of a smile about his lips. He brushed her neck with a fingertip, then slid it down until it caught the hem of the sheet, and started to drag that down, too. “We may be able to fit in a brief round of diplomacy before the parade.”
bs: — Vonderful. Orso je također gledao u nju, s naznakom osmijeha na usnama. Vrškom prsta okrznuo joj je vrat, a zatim ga spustio dok nije zahvatio rub plahte te ga počeo povlačiti prema dolje. — Možda stignemo odraditi kratku rundu diplomacije prije parade.

en: Leo realised with a twinge of guilt that Rikke was probably among them. He wondered what she’d done after the ball last night. Probably sat on her own in the darkness, plotting his doom. He turned his eyes hastily forward, towards the magnificent standard flying at the very head of the column, its white horse rearing against a golden sun. Just the sight of it made the embers of Leo’s patriotic fervour flare back into life. A relic of a better time, when the Union was ruled by righteous warriors,
bs: Uz trunčicu grižnje savjesti, Leo shvati kako je među njima vjerojatno i Rike. Zapita se što li je radila sinoć nakon bala. Vjerojatno je sjedila sama u mraku i kovala njegovu propast. Žurno odvrati Oko prema naprijed, usmjerivši ga na veličanstvenu zastavu koja se vijorila na samome čelu kolone, dok joj se bijeli konj propinjao na prednjim nogama protiv zlatnoga sunca. Već je sam Oko na nju natjerao žeravicu Leova domoljubnog žara da ponovno plane. Relikt iz boljih vremena, kada su Unijom vlada

en: Leo’s eye was caught by a knot of dark-skinned beggars in the crowd. “Lot of brown faces around,” he said, frowning.
bs: Leovu je oku zapelo za skupinu tamnoputih prosjaka u gomili."Puno je smeđih lica naokolo", reče namrštivši se.

en: Leo frowned. He hadn’t actually thought of that. “Just… hardly feels like the Union’s the Union any more.”
bs: Leo se namrštio. Zapravo o tome uopće nije razmišljao. — Jednostavno… jedva da se više čini kako je Unija – Unija.

en: “I think I can deduce it.” Orso’s voice sounded strangled, but Leo had never been much good at finding the hidden meaning in things. He was a straightforward fellow. So he carried on. Straightforwardly. Was that a word?
bs: — Mislim da mogu zaključiti. Orsov je glas zvučao prigušeno, no Leo nikad nije bio osobito vješt u pronalaženju skrivenih značenja. Bio je jednostavan čovjek. Stoga nastavi. Jednostavno. Postoji li uopće ta riječ?

en: Everyone had cheered for Leo dan Brock, up on his own at the front of the parade, a famous hero from head to toe. Things quietened down a lot as the great men of the Open Council followed.
bs: Svi su klicali Leu dan Broku, izdvojenom na čelu parade, slavnome junaku od glave do pete. Sve se prilično utišalo kad su uslijedili velikaši Otvorenoga vijeća.

en: “Shame!” someone roared. “Down wi’ the crown prince!” A tall man with a thick black beard, standing on tiptoe to shout over the heads of those in front. Folk frowned around at him but he’d the light of madness in his eyes and didn’t back down a step. “Murderer!”
bs: — Sramota! — zaurla netko. — Dolje s prijestolonasljednikom! — Visok muškarac s gustom crnom bradom stajao je na prstima kako bi nadglasao glave onih sprijeda. Folk se namrštio oko njega, ali u očima mu je tinjalo ludilo i nije uzmaknuo ni koraka. — Ubojica!

en: “No!” hissed Liddy. Was only then Broad noticed her hand on his arm. Both hands, dragging him back as hard as she could. “No more trouble!” Was only then he noticed his every muscle was stiff and his fists clenched trembling tight and his lips curled back in a snarl.
bs: — Ne! – prosikta Lidi. Tek tada Brod je opazio njezinu ruku na svojoj. Obje ruke, povlačeći ga unatrag svom snagom. — Nema više Troblija! Tek tada osjetio je kako mu je svaki mišić ukočen, šake stisnute u drhtav grč, a usne izvijene u režeći izraz.

en: Savine had always loved grand events. The bigger the crowd, the more opportunities to turn strangers into acquaintances, acquaintances into friends, and friends into money. They were a chance to be seen, and therefore admired, and therefore kept powerful. Because power is a mountain one is always sliding down. A mountain one must claw and strive and scramble always to keep one’s place upon, let alone to climb higher. A mountain made not of rock, but of everyone else’s writhing, struggling, grasp
bs: Savine je oduvijek voljela velike događaje. Što je gomila veća, to je više prilika da se neznanci pretvore u poznanike, poznanici u prijatelje, a prijatelji u novac. One su bile prilika da te vide, pa stoga i da ti se dive, te da se tako održi moć. Jer moć je planina s koje se neprestano klizi. Planina po kojoj valja grebati, truditi se i penjati ne bi li se sačuvao vlastiti položaj, a kamoli uspinjalo još više. Planina sačinjena ne od stijene, nego od tuđih tijela koja se migolje, bore i grče n

en: Leo dan Brock had been a pleasing diversion. From the neck down, he was astonishing. When she opened his shirt, she had spent a moment just staring. It was as if he was carved from flesh-coloured marble by a sculptor intent on exaggeration. There had been a moment when he lifted her clean off her feet so effortlessly, it felt as if she might never come down…
bs: Leo dan Brok bio je ugodna diverzija. Od vrata nadolje bio je zapanjujući. Kad bi mu otkopčala košulju, provela bi trenutak samo promatrajući ga. Izgledao je kao da ga je od mramora boje mesa isklesao kipar sklon pretjerivanju. Bilo je trenutaka kad ju je podignuo s tla tako bez napora da se činilo kako se možda nikad više neće spustiti…

en: “Lady Savine…” Zuri glanced carefully about the royal box. Her stumble had evidently been noticed. They were always watching, the fucking vultures, hoping for fresh meat to rip at. “You do not seem yourself.”
bs: — Lady Savine… Zuri je oprezno pogledala oko kraljevske lože. Njezin je posrtaj očito bio primijećen. Uvijek su promatrali, ti jebeni lešinari, nadajući se svježem mesu koje mogu rastrgati. — Ne činiš se svojom.

en: “The last thing I need is a fucking lecture,” she snarled, and suddenly, entirely unbidden, entirely inappropriate, a memory welled up. That dark-skinned little girl, wet eyes lit by flames, pleading with her in a filthy alley in Valbeck. Please, please, please, over and over, the crushing terror and the stink of burning.
bs: "Posljednje što mi treba je jebeno predavanje", zarežala je, a iznenada, posve nepozvano, posve neprikladno, navrlo je sjećanje. Ona tamnoputa djevojčica, vlažnih očiju obasjanih plamenom, kako je preklinje u prljavoj uličici u Valbeku. Molim te, molim te, molim te, iznova i iznova, taj razarajući užas i smrad Velikog Gorenja.

en: Several people had evidently caught the anger of their exchange, curious faces turned towards them. One in particular. The First of the Magi stood beside the king, dressed in robes with a dash of the arcane now, for a public appearance. He smiled, a knowing little smile, and gave her a nod of acknowledgement.
bs: Nekoliko Folk očito je primijetilo ljutnju u njihovu razgovoru; znatiželjna lica okrenula su se prema njima. Jedno posebno. Prvi od Magi stajao je pored kralja, odjeven u haljine s dozom arkanog, za javni nastup. Nasmiješio se onim znajućim, sitnim osmijehom i Dow joj čvorić u znak prepoznavanja.

en: Savine slowly straightened, rubbing at the livid marks her father’s fingers had left on her wrist. She wanted to punch him in his toothless mouth. She wanted to scream at the mad top of her voice, right in the king’s face. She wanted at least to storm furiously away.
bs: Savine se polako ispružila, trljajući ljubičaste tragove koje su joj očevi prsti ostavili na zapešću. Željela ga je udariti u bezuba usta. Željela je vikati na ludu visinu svoga glasa, pravo kralju u lice. Bare bi željela bijesno otići.

en: “We stomp all over it. What are you doing back here with the chaff? Not enough width on one street for two heads so swollen as yours and Leo dan Brock’s?”
bs: — Mi ih gazimo nogama. Što radiš ovdje natrag s običnim pukom? Nije li jedna ulica dovoljno široka za dva tako napuhana Šefa kao što ste ti i Leo dan Brok?

en: She watched Orso even more intently than Shivers, if anything, one hand blue with tattoos, her stony-hard face shifting rhythmically as she chewed at something. Without breaking eye contact, she turned her head and savagely spat.
bs: Promatrala je Orso još intenzivnije nego Šivers, ako je to uopće bilo moguće; jedna joj je ruka bila modra od tetovaža, a njezino kameno lice ritmično se pomicalo dok je nešto žvakala. Ne prekidajući kontakt očima, okrenula je glavu i divljački pljunula.

en: When it came to feeding the people, or housing them better than dogs, there were always harsh limits on what government could afford. But for a royal triumph, the Closed Council would find a way. Someone who’d starved in the camps, who’d lied her way into the hearts and beds of good people, who’d tricked and tortured to betray a cause she halfway believed in for the sake of one she didn’t at all, might’ve felt a little bitter at seeing all this money wasted.
bs: Kada je trebalo nahraniti Folk ili ga smjestiti u bolje uvjete od pasa, uvijek su postojala stroga ograničenja onoga što si vlast može priuštiti. No za kraljevski trijumf, Vijeće bi uvijek pronašlo način. Netko tko je gladovao u logorima, tko se laganjem uvukao u srca i krevete dobrih Folk, tko je varao i mučio kako bi izdao cilj u koji je napola vjerovao radi onoga u koji nije vjerovao nimalo, možda bi osjetio tračak gorčine gledajući sav taj bačen novac.

en: “Nothing really!” Worried she’d get him into trouble. “Just that he was doing some work for you, and so you were looking after me while he was doing it.” She glanced up, fearful. “Is the work done?”
bs: — Zapravo ništa! Uplašila se da ga ne uvali u nevolje. — Samo da radi za vas, pa da vi pazite na mene dok on obavlja posao. Pogledala je gore, uplašeno. — Je li posao gotov?

en: Orso’s applause was quieter, especially at this end of the square, and what there was had the overblown quality of coming from purse rather than heart. The prince had few friends among the nobility, even fewer among the common folk. From what Vick could see of his expression, he knew it, too.
bs: Pljesak za Orsa bio je tiši, osobito na ovom kraju trga, a ono malo što ga je bilo, zvučalo je isforsirano, kao da dolazi iz novčanika, a ne iz srca. Princ je imao malo prijatelja među plemstvom, a još manje među običnim pukom. Prema onome što je Vik mogla vidjeti na njegovu licu, znao je to i on sam.

en: Trouble at both ends of the social scale. Trouble all over. Vick frowned at Prince Orso, then at that Northern girl with the hair like a bird’s nest blown from its tree. She was staring at her own hand with the oddest expression. From what Vick could tell, it was shaking. She scrambled drunkenly from her horse and took something on a thong around her neck and wedged it in her mouth.
bs: Trobli na oba kraja društvene Ljuske. Trobli posvuda. Vik se namrštio prema princu Orsu, a zatim prema onoj sjevernjačkoj djevojci s kosom poput ptičjeg gnijezda otpuhanog s drveta. Zurila je u vlastitu ruku s najčudnijim izrazom. Koliko je Vik mogla procijeniti, ruka joj je drhtala. Pijano se skotrljala s konja, uzela nešto na uzici oko vrata i zagrizla to.

en: “An old chieftain, dead, in a high hall lit with candles. Men gathered about the body, looking down. All of ’em wondering what they could get from it. Like they were dogs, and that dead old man was the meat.” That fear grew worse and worse and Rikke’s eyes got wider and wider. “I have to go home.”
bs: — Stari poglavica, mrtav, u visokoj dvorani osvijetljenoj svijećama. Folk okupljeni oko tijela, gledaju dolje. Svi se pitaju što mogu ugrabiti od njega. Kao da su psi, a taj mrtvi starac meso. Strah joj je rastao sve jači, a Rikine su se oči sve više širile. — Moram kući.

en: “Aye.” Stour frowned at the floor, still a trace of yellow bruises around his eyes. “I’d have killed him, if things had gone the other way.”
bs: — Jest. Staur se namršti gledajući u pod, a oko očiju mu se još nazirao trag žutih modrica. — Bio bih ga ubio da su stvari krenule drugim tokom.

en: Wonderful frowned over at Stour and let a breath sigh through her nose. “Long as I’m done babysitting this bastard, I really don’t care.”
bs: Vonderful se namršti prema Stauru i pusti uzdah kroz nos. — Sve dok sam završila s dadiljanjem ovog kopileta, zapravo me nije briga.

en: “Would’ve won if it wasn’t for that fucking witch!” sneered Greenway, as bitter as if it was him who’d lost. “Fucking Long Eye, or whatever. Fucking cheating, that’s what that was. They should all have the bloody cross cut in ’em.”
bs: — Pobijedio bi da nije bilo one jebene vještice! podrugljivo će Grinvej, ogorčen kao da je on izgubio. — Jebeno Oko, ili kako već. Jebeno varanje, eto što je to bilo. Svi bi oni trebali imati urezan prokleti križ.

en: The word was cut off in a kind of sickly squelch, and the king puked blood and ale and Clover saw to his great surprise that Stour had buried a knife in his uncle’s neck.
bs: Riječ mu presiječe nekakav mučan zvuk cijeđenja, a kralj povrati krv i pivo te Klover na svoje veliko iznenađenje ugleda kako je Staur zabio nož u vrat svoga strica.

en: Didn’t take more than a few breaths for the old cunts to be sent back to the mud, the young to stand over ’em with smiles on their red-speckled faces.
bs: Nije trebalo proći više od nekoliko udaha da ti stari gadovi budu vraćeni u blato, a Juvens stanu nad njima s osmijesima na licima poprskanima krvlju.

en: “You make out you’re a silly bastard.” Stour took a little sip from his cup and licked his lips. “But you’re a clever bastard, too. The wise fool, eh? Always thought your lessons were coward’s nonsense but, looking back, I see you had the right of it all along.” He wagged his bloody dagger at Clover. “Like what you said about knives and swords. Spent twenty years training with a sword every morning and every dusk, but I won more with one knife-thrust. I’d like you to stick with me. Might be you’
bs: — Praviš se da si blesava budala. Staur je otpio maleni gutljaj iz šalice i polizao usne. — Ali ti si i pametna budala. Mudra luda, zar ne? Uvijek sam mislio da su tvoje lekcije kukavičke gluposti, ali kad malo bolje razmislim, vidim da si sve vrijeme bio u pravu. Zamahnuo je krvavim bodežom prema Kloveru. — Baš kao ono što si govorio o noževima i mačevima. Proveo sam dvadesetero godina vježbajući s mačem svako jutro i svaku večer, ali više sam toga osvojio jednim ubodom nožem. Volio bih da osta

en: “No.” Clover had seen a lot of corpses. Made a fair few himself. But he was having trouble thinking of Wonderful as dead. Any moment, she’d laugh it off. Make some joke about it. Cut him down to size with a raised brow.
bs: — Ne. — Klover je vidio mnogo leševa. I sam ih je prilično stvorio. No teško mu je bilo pojmiti da je Vonderful mrtva. Svakog bi se trena nasmijala tomu. Istresla neku šalu na taj račun. Spustila ga na zemlju uzdignutom obrvom.

en: “Chosen not to wait.” Stour peeled Scale’s fat head from the table by one ear and dragged the chain from around his shoulders, its dangling diamond red with blood. Greenway giggled and the others grinned, all well satisfied with the outcome.
bs: — Izabrao sam ne čekati. — Staur odvoji Skejlovu debelu glavu od stola držeći je za jedno uho pa povuče lanac s njegovih ramena, čiji su viseći dijamanti bili crveni od krvi. Grinvej se zahhotao, a ostali se isceriše, posve zadovoljni ishodom.

en: Stour gave a hiss, somewhere between disgust and boredom. “Folk say a lot o’ things about my grandfather, Bethod this and Bethod that, but I never even met the bastard.” He winced as he lifted his wounded leg and propped it up on the murdered king’s fat back. “I got my own dreams to think about.”
bs: Staur je ispustio šištanje, negdje između gađenja i dosade. — Folk svašta priča o mom djedu, Bethod ovo i Bethod ono, ali ja tog kopileta nikad nisam ni upoznao." Trgnuo se dok je podizao ranjenu nogu i naslonio je na debela leđa ubijenoga kralja. — Imam ja svojih snova o kojima trebam misliti.

en: She said nothing, only glided down the chilly hallway, decorated with berries for the new year festival, so quickly he had to take the odd running step to keep up.
bs: Ona nije rekla ništa, samo je klizila hladnim hodnikom, ukrašenim bobicama za novogodišnji festival, tako brzo da je morao potrčati kako bi je sustigao.

en: Suddenly he felt that there had been so much he needed to say to his father. He had always supposed they would discuss the important things later. The profound things. But it would never happen. There had only been a fixed time in his presence, and Orso had pissed it all away talking about the weather, and there would be no more.
bs: Odjednom osjeti da je ocu morao reći još toliko toga. Oduvijek je pretpostavljao da će o važnim stvarima raspravljati kasnije. O onim dubokoumnima. No to se više nikada neće dogoditi. Vrijeme koje mu je bilo darovano u njegovoj blizini bilo je ograničeno, a Orso ga je cijelo proćerdao razgovarajući o vremenu, i novoga više neće biti.

en: The great machinist, Gillian Redfearn. Because every Jezal knows, deep down, he ain’t shit without Bayaz.
bs: Velikoj meštrici, Gillian Redfearn. Jer svaki Džezal u dubini duše zna da Aren pišljiva boba ne vrijedi bez Bajaza.

en: Victarine dan Teufel—an ex-convict, daughter of a disgraced Master of the Mints, now striking a blow for the common man.
bs: Victarine dan Tojfel — bivša osuđenica, kći osramoćenog Majstora kovnice, koja se sada bori za malog čovjeka.

en: The Prophet Khalul—former Second of the Magi, now arch-enemy of Bayaz. Rumoured to have been killed by a demon, plunging the South into chaos.
bs: Prorok Khalul — bivši drugi među Magi, sada zakleti neprijatelj Bajaza. Kruže glasine da ga je ubio demon, bacivši South u kaos.

en: All eyes turned towards him. Apart from those of Bayaz, down at the foot of the table. The legendary wizard continued to gaze out of the window, towards the palace gardens which were just beginning to bud.
bs: Sve oči se okrenuše prema njemu. Osim onih Bajazovih, na začelju stola. Legendarni čarobnjak nastavio je zuriti kroz prozor, prema dvorskim vrtovima koji su tek počinjali pupati.

en: Orso had never wanted to be king. He enjoyed it even less than being crown prince, if that was possible. But now that he was king, he was determined to do some good with it.
bs: Orso nikada nije želio biti kralj. Uživao je u tome čak manje nego u ulozi prijestolonasljednika, ako je to uopće bilo moguće. No sada kada jest bio kralj, bio je odlučan učiniti nešto dobro s tim.

en: “But they are far from eradicated. And those that escaped have become… even more extreme in their opinions.”
bs: — Ali daleko su od iskorjenjivanja. A oni koji su pobjegli postali su… još ekstremniji u svojim stajalištima.

en: “We have destroyed a dozen presses,” grated Glokta, “but they build new ones, and smaller all the time. Now any fool can write, and print, and air their opinions.”
bs: — Uništili smo desetak tiskara, promrmlja Glokta, "ali oni grade nove, sve manje. Sada svaka budala može pisati, tiskati i iznositi svoja mišljenja."

en: “One might almost say our approach has made matters worse,” observed Orso. A memory of Malmer drifted up, legs dangling from his cage as it swung with the breeze. “Perhaps we could make some gesture. A minimum wage? Improved working conditions? I heard a recent fire in a mill led to the deaths of fifteen child workers—”
bs: — Gotovo bismo mogli reći da je naš pristup samo pogoršao stvari, primijetio je Orso. Sjećanje na Malmer pojavilo mu se pred očima; noge koje vise iz kaveza dok se njiše na povjetarcu. — Možda bismo mogli učiniti neku gestu. Minimalna plaća? Poboljšani uvjeti rada? Čuo sam da je nedavni Veliko Gorenje u jednom mlinu dovio do smrti petnaestero djece radnika…

en: “And they are busy in the shadows,” went on Matstringer, “sowing discord in Westport, enticing the Aldermen to sedition. Why, they have succeeded in scheduling a vote within the month which could see the city secede from the Union!”
bs: — A zauzeti su i u sjenama, nastavio je Matstringer, siju razdor u Vestportu, mame Vijećnike na pobunu. Zamislite, uspjeli su zakazati glasovanje unutar mjesec dana koje bi moglo dovesti do toga da se grad odcijepi od Unije!

en: “I will not see a man condemned for the actions of his grandfather!” snapped Orso, whose own grandfathers had enjoyed mixed reputations, to say the least. “Leo dan Brock risked his life fighting a duel on my behalf!”
bs: — Neću dopustiti da se čovjeka osuđuje zbog postupaka njegova djeda! odbrusi Orso, čiji su djedovi, blago rečeno, uživali dvojbene reputacije. — Leo dan Brok riskirao je život boreći se u dvoboju u moje ime!

en: Glokta’s permanent grimace became even further contorted. “I hoped we might settle that matter without bothering His Majesty.”
bs: Gloktina trajna grimasa još se više iskrivi. — Nadao sam se da ćemo tu stvar riješiti bez uznemiravanja Njegovog Veličanstva.

en: “He could at least lose control of himself in the absence of seventeen witnesses,” observed Gorodets, and there was some light laughter.
bs: — Mogao je barem izgubiti kontrolu u odsutnosti sedamnaest svjedoka, primijeti Gorodets, na što se prolomio lagan smijeh.

en: Everyone nodded as though they had been treated to the most profound statement of all time. It was a wonder they did not rise and give a standing ovation. Orso was left in no doubt at which end of the table the power in the White Chamber truly lay. He remembered the look on his father’s face as Bayaz spoke. The fear. He made one more effort to claw his way towards his best guess at the right thing.
bs: Svi kimnuše glavom kao da su upravo čuli najdublju misao svih vremena. Pravo je čudo što nisu ustali i priredili ovacije. Orso nije dvojio na kojem kraju stola u Bijeloj dvorani uistinu leži moć. Sjetio se izraza na očevu licu dok je Bajaz govorio. Strah. Učinio je još jedan napor kako bi se izborio za ono što je smatrao ispravnim.

en: Superior Lorsen lowered the letter, frowning at Vick over the rims of his eye-lenses. He looked like a man who had not smiled in some time. Perhaps ever.
bs: Superior Lorsen spusti pismo, namrštivši se na Vik preko rubova svojih naočala. Izgledao je kao čovjek koji se dugo nije nasmiješio. Možda i nikada.

en: “Then may I present to you our unruly workers: the Aldermen of Westport.” And Lorsen stepped to the balustrade and gestured down below.
bs: — Onda vam mogu predstaviti naše neposlušne radnike: Vijećnike Vestporta. Lorsen zakorači do balustrade i pokaza prema dolje.

en: “We joined the Union because of their military might!” A truly mighty voice boomed out, finally cutting through the hubbub. The speaker was thickset, dark-skinned and shaven-headed with strangely gentle gestures. “Because the Empire of Gurkhul threatened us from the south and we needed strong allies to deter them. But membership has cost us dear! Millions of scales in treasure and the price forever rises!”
bs: — Pridružili smo se Uniji zbog njihove vojne moći! Doista moćan glas zagrmi i napokon probije žamor. Govornik bijaše zdepast, tamnoput i obrijane glave, čudno blagih pokreta. — Zato što nam je Carstvo Gurkhul prijetilo s juga i trebali su nam snažni saveznici da ih odvratimo. No članstvo nas je skupo stajalo! Milijuni Ljuski u blagu, a cijena neprestano raste!

en: Loud boos, but even louder cheers. Lorsen shook his head in disgust. “If this were Adua, we could march in there, drag him from his seat, force a confession and ship him off to Angland on the next tide.”
bs: Glasno negodovanje, ali još glasnije klicanje. Lorsen zgroženo odmahne glavom. — Da je ovo Adua, mogli bismo ušetati tamo, izvući ga sa sjedala, iznuditi priznanje i otpremiti ga u Englend s prvom plimom.

en: Lorsen took a weary breath. “I have my hands full protecting our own Aldermen. The ballots are cast in nineteen days, and we cannot afford to lose a single vote.”
bs: Lorsen uzdahne umorno. — Imam pune ruke posla štiteći naše vlastite Vijećnike. Glasovi se daju za devetnaest dana i ne smijemo izgubiti niti jedan glas.

en: “His Eminence wants me to keep Westport in the Union.” She headed for the door with Tallow at her heels. “At any cost.”
bs: — Njegova Eminencija želi zadržati Vestport u Uniji, rekla je i krenula prema vratima, dok joj je Talou bio za petama. — Pod svaku cijenu.

en: “You’re fucking right there.” Savine dipped behind her fan to sniff up a pinch of pearl dust. Just to lift her out of the bog. Just to keep some wind in the sails.
bs: — Tu si u pravu, jebote. Savine se sakrila iza lepeze kako bi ušmrkala prstohvat bisernog praha. Tek da se izvuče iz gliba. Tek da zadrži malo vjetra u jedrima.

en: “Confidence has been struck,” lamented Curnsbick. “Markets are in turmoil. But from chaos, opportunity can come.” He gave his lectern another blow. “Opportunity must be made to come. His August Majesty King Orso will lead us into a new age. Progress cannot stop! Will not be permitted to stop! For the benefit of all, we of the Solar Society will fight tirelessly to drag the Union from the tomb of ignorance and into the sunny uplands of enlightenment!”
bs: — Povjerenje je uzdrmano, jadikuje Kurnsbik. — Tržišta su u rasulu. Ali iz kaosa se može izroditi prilika. Ponovno je udario po govornici."Prilika se mora stvoriti. Njegovo Uzvišeno Vaša Uzvišenosti kralj Orso povest će nas u novo doba. Naprijed ne smije stati! Neće mu se dopustiti da stane! Za dobrobit svih, mi iz Solar Societyja neumorno ćemo se boriti da izvučemo Unija iz groba neznanja i uvedemo ga u sunčane visine prosvjetljenja!"

en: She squeezed her face into a smile, snapped out her fan and forced herself into the midst of the press with Zuri at her shoulder. Eyes turned in her direction, expressions harder than she was used to. Assessing, rather than admiring. Scornful, rather than envious. They used to crowd around her like pigs around the one trough in the farmyard. Now the most tempting morsels went elsewhere. Savine could scarcely see Selest dan Heugen through the swarm of gentlemen competing for her attention. Only a
bs: Namjesti lice u osmijeh, otvori lepezu i prisili se ući u središte gomile sa Zuri za petama. Oči su se okretale prema njoj, izrazi lica tvrđi nego što je navikla. Procjenjivački, umjesto divljenja. Prijekorni, umjesto zavidnih. Nekada su se oko nje tiskali kao svinje oko korita na farmi. Sada su najprimamljiviji zalogaji odlazili drugdje. Savine je jedva mogla vidjeti Selest dan Heugen kroz roj gospode koja se borila za njezinu pažnju. Samo bljesak one kričave crvene perike. Isječak onog groznog

en: “… heard Valint and Balk called in his loans. Magnate in the morning, beggar by afternoon. Salutary lesson for all of us…”
bs: — … čula sam da su Valint i Balk opozvali njegove kredite. Ujutro magnat, popodne prosjak. Poučna lekcija za sve nas…

en: “And so you see, Lady Savine,” Sleisholt was working up to a grand finale, “the power of the Whiteflow is languishing unharnessed, like a stallion unbridled, and—”
bs: — I tako vidite, Lady Savine, Sleisholt se spremao za Great finale, snaga Whiteflowa čami neiskorištena, poput pastuha bez uzde, i…

en: “You have no fucking idea what I lost in Valbeck!” He stepped back, startled, and she realised she had her fist clenched tight around her folded fan and was shaking it in his face. “You… have no idea.” She was shocked to find the pain of tears at the back of her nose, had to snap her fan open again so she could dab at her lids, struggling not to smudge her powder. Never mind her judgement, it was getting to the point where she could hardly trust her own eyes.
bs: "Ti nemaš jebene predodžbe što sam izgubio u Valbeku!" Odstupio je, zatečen, a ona shvati da joj je šaka čvrsto stisnuta oko sklopljene lepeze i da njome maše pred njegovim licem. — Ti… nemaš pojma." Ostala je šokirana osjetivši peckanje suza u korijenu nosa; morala je ponovno otvoriti lepezu kako bi potapkala kapke, boreći se da ne razmaže puder. Neka ide k vragu njezina prosudba, dolazilo je do toga da jedva može vjerovati vlastitom Oku.

en: “Never fear, Master Curnsbick.” Orso clapped him on the shoulder like an old friend. “I can’t imagine I would have been much help with the technical details.”
bs: — Bez brige, Majstore Kurnsbik. Orso ga potapša po ramenu kao starog prijatelja. — Ne mogu zamisliti da bih bio od velike pomoći s tehničkim detaljima.

en: “Lady Selest!” she heard Orso say, his heel clicking sharply as he turned away. “Perhaps you might show me around?”
bs: — Lady Selest!, začula je Orsa kako govori, dok mu je peta oštro kliknula pri okretu. — Možda biste me mogli provesti uokolo?

en: A strip of light down the side of Zuri’s dark face made one eye gleam. “When did your menses last come?” she asked, softly.
bs: Tračak svjetlosti uz rub Zurina tamnog lica učinio je da joj jedno oko zasvijetli. — Kada ste posljednji put imali mjesečnicu?, upitala je tiho.

en: She doubled over and brought up more sick. Just an acrid trickle this time. Retching and giggling at once. She spat it out and wiped her face on the back of her glove. Her hand was shaking again.
bs: Savila se i izbacila još žuči. Ovoga puta samo opor mlaz. Povraćajući i hihotajući se istodobno. Ispljunula je sadržaj i obrisala lice nadlanicom rukavice. Ruka joj je opet drhtala.

en: “We ate peelings and drank from puddles,” said Liddy, forking another slice of meat onto Broad’s plate.
bs: — Jeli smo kore i pili iz lokvi, rekla je Lidi, vilicom prebacujući još jednu krišku mesa na Brodov tanjur.

en: Liddy was still smiling as she tipped her face up, lips soft against his. She’d put weight on. They all had, since the lean times in Valbeck. She had that curve to her figure and that glow to her cheek she’d had when they first courted. That same smell she’d had when they first kissed. All that time passed, and he loved her just the same.
bs: Lidi se još uvijek smiješila dok je podizala lice, usana mekih poput dodira. Dobila je na težini. Svi su dobili, još od oskudnih vremena u Valbeku. Imala je onu oblinu na tijelu i onaj sjaj na obrazima koji je imala dok su se tek udvarali. Onaj isti miris koji je imala kad su se prvi put poljubili. Toliko je vremena prošlo, a on ju je volio jednako kao i tada.

en: Their guest sat in one of three battered old chairs, hands tied to the back, ankles to the legs. Broad stopped in front of him, frowning down. “You’re Gaunt?”
bs: Njihov je gost sjedio na jednoj od triju izubijanih starih stolica, ruku vezanih za naslon, a gležnjeva za nogare. Brod se zaustavio Naprijed njega, namršteno ga promatrajući. — Ti si Gaunt?

en: “That’s right. We hear you’ve been organising, Master Gaunt. We hear you’ve persuaded the workers to down tools.”
bs: — Tako je. Čuli smo da si organizirao ljude, majstore Gaunt. Čuli smo da si nagovorio radnike da obustave rad.

en: Gaunt stuck his chin up, still defiant. Broad liked him. They could’ve been on the same side. He supposed they had been, not that long ago. “I can help the others. The likes of you wouldn’t understand.”
bs: Gaunt podiže bradu, još uvijek prkosan. Brodu se svidio. Mogli su biti na istoj strani. Pretpostavljao je da jesu, ne tako davno. — Mogu pomoći drugima. Oni poput tebe to ne bi razumjeli.

en: “Boast of?” Broad stared back, over the rims of his lenses, so Gaunt was just a sparkly blur in the lamplight. “Fuck, no. I wake up with the sweats. I cry, sometimes. In the quiet times. Don’t mind admitting it.”
bs: — Hvaliti? Brod uzvrati pogledom, preko rubova svojih naočala, pa je Gaunt bio tek svjetlucava mrlja na svjetlosti svjetiljke. — Do vraga, ne. Budim se obliven znojem. Ponekad plačem. U trenucima tišine. Ne sramim se to priznati.

en: It was Zuri. She looked worried, and that made him worried. She was about as hard to rattle as anyone Broad had ever met.
bs: Bila je to Zuri. Djelovala je zabrinuto, a to je i njega zabrinulo. Bila je otprilike jednako otporna na uzrujavanje kao itko koga je Brod ikada upoznao.

en: Broad glanced over at Zuri, her black eyes gleaming in the darkness. “We all are fingers on God’s hand,” she murmured, with a sorry shrug.
bs: Brod baci Oko prema Zuri, čije su crne oči svjetlucale u tami. — Svi smo mi prsti na Božjoj ruci, promrmlja ona uz žalostan sleg ramena.

en: It spattered in his lap, spattered the warehouse floor, and Bannerman stepped back, frowning down at his shiny new boots. “Oh, we got a gusher.”
bs: Bljuvotina je poprskala njegovo krilo i pod skladišta, a Banerman se odmaknuo, mršteći se na svoje sjajne nove čizme. — O, pa mi imamo fontanu.

en: The lad stared around, tears tracking his face. Broad wished he could have a drink. He could almost taste it, on his tongue. A drink made everything easier. Easier at the time, anyway. Harder afterwards. He pushed the thought away.
bs: Mladić je zurio uokolo, dok su mu suze brazdale lice. Brod je poželio popiti piće. Gotovo ga je mogao osjetiti na jeziku. Piće je sve činilo lakšim. U tom trenutku, barem. Kasnije je bilo teže. Odgurnuo je tu misao od sebe.

en: Broad straightened up, blinking. “Oh, that’s good news.” Didn’t feel like good news. Deep down inside it felt like quite the disappointment. It was an effort, to make his fists unclench. An effort, to take the lenses from his shirt pocket, hook them back over his ears. Too delicate for his aching fingers. “Your son’ll stay with us, though, just to make sure you don’t have a change of heart.”
bs: Brod se uspravio i trepnuo. — O, to su dobre vijesti." Nije se osjećalo kao dobra vijest. Duboko u sebi osjećao je to kao pravo razočaranje. Trebalo mu je truda da opusti šake. Truda da izvadi naočale iz džepa košulje i zakači ih natrag iza ušiju. Bile su previše nježne za njegove bolne prste. — Tvoj Filio će ipak ostati s nama, tek da budemo sigurni kako se nećeš predomisliti.

en: “Eight.” A good liar sticks to the truth whenever possible. She had been eight when that bout took place, but she’d been huddled in the blackness of a stinking ship’s hold, shackled to a great chain with her family and a few-score other convicts. All on their way to the prison camps of Angland, from which only she would return. She doubted that memory would’ve brought quite the same delight from Filio, though, his eyes shining at the memory of past glories. People are rarely made happy by all th
bs: — Osam. Dobar lažljivac drži se istine kad god je to moguće. Imala je osam godina kada se taj dvoboj odvijao, ali tada je bio stisnuta u tami smrdljivog brodskog potpalublja, okovana velikim lancem zajedno s obitelji i nekoliko desetaka drugih osuđenika. Svi na putu prema zatvorskim logorima u Englendu, iz kojih se samo ona vratila. Sumnjala je da bi to sjećanje izazvalo jednako oduševljenje kod Filija, čije su oči sjajile pri pomisli na prošle slave. Ljude rijetko usrećuje sva istina.

en: “I do! I have, all my life. My grandfather was one of those who brought us in to begin with.” Filio’s smile faded. “But there are difficulties. King Jezal was a known quantity but King Orso is young…” Filio winced as his nephew gave a showy flourish of his steels. “And has, by reputation, a surfeit of all the young man’s faults. Your bungling in the wars against Styria was far from helpful. And then we have Solumeo Shudra!” Filio clicked his tongue. “Have you heard him speak?”
bs: — Vjerujem! Cijelog sam života vjerovao. Moj djed bio je jedan od onih koji su nas uopće uveli u to. Filiov se osmijeh izgubio. — No, postoje poteškoće. Kralj Džezal bio je poznata veličina, ali kralj Orso je mlad… Filio se zgrozio dok je njegov nećak izvio razmetljiv zamah čelicima. — I ima, po glasu koji ga bije, previše svih mana mladog čovjeka. Vaše nespretno vođenje ratova protiv Stirije nimalo nije pomoglo. A tu je i Solumeo Šudra! Filio je kliknuo jezikom. — Jeste li ga čuli kako govori?

en: “Then we should talk again. As the future takes shape.” Vick stood, ignoring a sudden twinge through her bad hip, snapped her heels together and gave a stiff bow.
bs: — Onda bismo trebali ponovno razgovarati. Kako budućnost bude poprimala oblik. Vik ustane, ignorirajući iznenadno sijevanje u bolnom kuku, spoji pete i ukočeno se nakloni.

en: “I have that misfortune.” Vick had reckoned the aristocratic overtones of her full name, however awkwardly it fit her now, would suit this meeting best. Mozolia was said to be a hard-headed woman of business, so Vick had chosen to present herself as a practical Aduan lady on a trip abroad. Hair neatly braided, coiled and pinned. Top button left undone, for a hint of relaxed approachability. It had been a while since she wore a skirt, and she felt no more comfortable in it than she did in her nam
bs: — Imam tu nesreću. Vik je procijenila da će aristokratski prizvuk njezina punog imena, koliko god joj sada nezgrapno pristajao, najbolje odgovarati ovom sastanku. Za Mozoliu se pričalo da je tvrdoglava poslovna žena, pa je Vik odlučila predstaviti se kao praktična Aduanka na putovanju u inozemstvu. Kosa uredno ispletena u pletenice, smotana i pričvršćena ukosnicama. Gornji gumb otkopčan, za nagovještaj opuštene pristupačnosti. Prošlo je dosta vremena otkako je nosila suknju i nije se u njoj osje

en: “People here talk of little else. A momentous decision. But not one that you and I can take any part in. Women cannot be Aldermen, after all.”
bs: — Folk ovdje ni o čemu drugom ne govore. Odluka od presudne važnosti. No, to nije nešto u čemu ti i ja možemo sudjelovati. Žene, na koncu, ne mogu biti vijećnici.

en: “Or should we do exactly what the men do, and put sentiment to the side, and follow the greatest profit?”
bs: — Ili bismo trebale činiti upravo ono što čine muškarci, ostaviti osjećaje po strani i slijediti najveću dobit?

en: Vick nudged the over-heavy drapes aside to peer into the street. The sun was setting on a largely wasted day, a muddy flare above the maze of mismatched rooftops, the thirsty treetops, the puffing chimneys, the spires of a hundred temples to a dozen versions of the Almighty. She wondered if it helped, to believe in God. Whether it was reassuring or terrifying, to look at all this shit and know for sure it was part of some grand plan.
bs: Vik je odgurnula preteške zastore kako bi zavirila na ulicu. Sunce je zalazilo nad uglavnom protraćenim danom, blatnjav odsjaj iznad labirinta neusklađenih krovova, žednih krošnji, dimnjaka koji su sukljali dim i tornjeva stotina hramova posvećenih desetak verzija Svemogućeg. Pitala se pomaže li to, vjerovati u Boga. Je li utješno ili zastrašujuće gledati sve to sranje i znati zasigurno da je dio nekog velikog plana.

en: She wondered what Sibalt would’ve said if he’d seen her dressed like this. I wish I’d met you sooner, maybe. Things might have been different. And she’d have said, You didn’t and they’re not. And he’d have given that weary smile of his and said, You’re a hard case, Vick, and he’d have been right. She caught herself missing him at the oddest times. Missing the warmth of him, the weight of him in her arms, the weight of his arms around her. Missing having someone she could touch.
bs: Pitala se što bi Sibalt rekao da ju je vidio ovako dotjeranu. Volio bih da sam te sreo ranije, možda. Stvari bi mogle biti drukčije. A ona bi rekla: Nisi, i nisu. On bi uputio onaj svoj umorni osmijeh i rekao: Ti si tvrd orah, Vik, i bio bi u pravu. Uhvatila se kako joj nedostaje u najčudnijim trenucima. Nedostajala joj je njegova toplina, njegova težina u njezinim rukama, težina njegovih ruku oko nje. Nedostajalo joj je imati nekoga koga može dotaknuti.

en: Her mouth twisted to spit the answer. Because she owed a debt to His Eminence. Because blackmail and betrayal was the only profession she’d ever excelled at. Because you stand with the winners. She had half a dozen answers to hand. It was just that none of them were any good. Truth was, she could have done anything. Run off to the Far Country like she and Sibalt had always joked about. But the moment His Eminence said, “Westport,” she’d started packing. She was still standing there, mouth half-o
bs: Usta su joj se iskrivila u namjeri ispljunuti odgovor. Zato što je dugovala Eminenciji. Zato što su ucjena i izdaja bile jedine vještine u kojima se ikada istaknula. Zato što čovjek staje na stranu pobjednika. Imala je na umu pola tuceta odgovora. Samo što nijedan od njih nije bio dobar. Istina je bila da je mogla učiniti bilo što. Pobjeći u Country, baš kao što su se ona i Sibalt uvijek šalili. No, onoga trenutka kada je Eminencija izgovorio: — Vestport, počela je pakirati stvari. Još je stajal

en: “One cannot have great growth without a little pain,” said Vick. “The Union’s industry is the envy of the world. Westport would be cutting herself off from her rightful place in the future. I’ve already spoken to several like-minded—”
bs: — Ne može se postići Great Naprijed bez malo boli, rekla je Vik. — Industrija Unije zavist je cijeloga svijeta. Vestport bi se odsjekao od svog zasluženog mjesta u budućnosti. Već sam razgovarala s nekolicinom istomišljenika…

en: And suddenly, all she could think of was the look on her brother’s face, so hurt and so surprised, when the Practicals stepped from the shadows.
bs: I odjednom, jedino o čemu je mogla misliti bio je izraz na licu njezina brata, tako povrijeđen i tako iznenađen, kada su Praktičari iskoračili iz sjene.

en: She hadn’t even thought about it. Hadn’t weighed the risks or the consequences. Hadn’t even considered where to hit him, or how to make sure he couldn’t hit back. If he’d been a tougher man, things could’ve gone very badly wrong.
bs: Nije o tome ni razmišljala. Nije vagala rizike ni posljedice. Nije čak ni razmišljala gdje ga udariti, ili kako osigurati da joj ne uzvrati. Da je bio čvršći čovjek, stvari su mogle poći jako po zlu.

en: “Could be worse. Now folk here’ll know what I’ve never doubted.” He gave her a stronger grin. “That you’re the wrong woman to mess with.”
bs: — Moglo je biti i gore. Sad će Folk ovdje znati ono u što nikad nisam sumnjao. Uputio joj je snažniji osmijeh. — Da si ti pogrešna žena s kojom se treba kačiti.

en: Jurand came on, grinning. “So you’ll bleed half to death, plainly be the worse fighter and only win because I’m an arrogant fool?”
bs: Džurand nasrne, cereći se. — Dakle, iskrvarit ćeš do smrti, očito biti lošiji borac i pobijediti samo zato što sam ja arogantna budala?

en: “No!” snarled Leo, slapping Jurand’s hand away. “The leg’s fucking worse than ever!” He was sick of pain. He was sick of sympathy. He was sick of being angry. He was sick of saying sorry for being angry. Then he saw the hurt on Jurand’s face and struggled to get a grip on himself. “I’m sorry. Always thought I could laugh off pain. But it’s all the time. I wake up with it. I go to sleep with it. Getting across a room is a struggle. Leaving something upstairs is a bloody disaster.”
bs: — Ne! zareži Leo, odgurnuvši Džurandovu ruku. — Noga je prokleta, gora nego ikad! Bilo mu je dosta boli. Bilo mu je dosta suosjećanja. Bilo mu je dosta ljutnje. Bilo mu je dosta ispričavanja zbog vlastite ljutnje. Tada je ugledao bol na Džurandovu licu i potrudio se pribrati. — Oprosti. Uvijek sam mislio da bol mogu otjerati smijehom. Ali ona je stalno tu. Budim se s njom. Lijegam s njom. Prelazak preko sobe je borba. Zaboraviti nešto na katu je prokleta katastrofa.

en: “And people hate the Styrians more than ever,” said Antaup. “I hear Westport’s a real powder keg. One spark and… poof.” He grinned as he mimed an explosion. “And the women over there…” He grinned wider as he mimed a bigger one.
bs: — A Folk mrze Styrijske više nego ikad, doda Antaup. — Čujem da je Vestport pravo bure baruta. Jedna iskra i… puf. Cerekajući se, rukama oponaša eksploziju. — A žene tamo…

en: “Can’t deny the weather’s good down there.” Jin patted Leo’s face with one big paw. “Get some colour back in those cheeks!”
bs: — Ne možeš poreći da je vrijeme dolje lijepo, Džin potapša Lea po licu svojom velikom šapom. — Vrati malo boje u te obraze!

en: Leo stood a moment, teeth bared, ready to fight. Then he sagged. He couldn’t stay angry with Jurand for longer than a breath or two. “You’re right, you bastard.”
bs: Leo je stajao trenutak, ogoljenih zubi, spreman za borbu. Zatim se opustio. Nije mogao ostati ljut na Džuranda dulje od daha ili dva. — U pravu si, gad jedan.

en: “What the shit?” Leo smashed at the table with a fist and made the papers and most of the old men jump. “The bloody arrogance of the bastards! In war, all they sent were good wishes and in peace all they send are demands! I swear they’d ask for my fruits in a bag if they thought they could get a good price for the damn things!”
bs: "Što je ovo, do vraga?" Leo šakom udari po stolu, od čega papiri i većina staraca poskoče. — Prokleta arogancija tih gadova! U ratu su slali samo lijepe želje, a u miru šalju samo zahtjeve! Kunem se, tražili bi i moje mošnje u vreći kad bi mislili da za te proklete stvari mogu dobiti dobru cijenu!

en: “Just an entreaty, Leo.” She took his hand, squeezed it in hers. “I share your annoyance, really I do, but you’re Lord Governor now. You have to be patient.”
bs: — Samo molba, Leo. Uzela ga je za ruku i stisnula je svojom. — Dijelim tvoju ljutnju, zaista je dijelim, ali ti si sada Lord Governor. Moraš biti strpljiv.

en: Leo took a breath. Forced his shoulders down. By the dead, he was always angry these days. “You’re right. I know you’re right.” The wind was chill outside. He dragged the window closed, gripped his thigh and took a few hobbling steps back to his chair—his prison—and dropped down into it.
bs: Leo je udahnuo. Prisilio ramena da se spuste. Tako mu mrtvih, uvijek je bio ljut ovih dana. — U pravu si. Znam da si u pravu." Vani je vjetar bio hladan. Navukao je prozor, zgrabio se za bedro i napravio nekoliko šepavih koraka natrag do svoje stolice — svog zatvora — i srušio se u nju.

en: “An odour is entirely natural, Your Grace.” The surgeon nudged his eye-lenses back up his nose with his wrist. You’d have thought a man who had to wear lenses but use his hands would at least find a pair that weren’t constantly sliding down his nose, but in this, as in so much else, it seemed Leo would be disappointed. “Some corruption has found its way into the wound.”
bs: — Neugodan miris je posve prirodan, Vaša Milosti. Kirurg je zapešćem gurnuo svoje naočale natrag na nos. Čovjek bi pomislio da bi netko tko mora nositi naočale, a pritom koristiti ruke, barem pronašao par koji mu neprestano ne klizi niz nos, no u tome, kao i u mnogo čemu drugome, činilo se da će Leo ostati razočaran. — Neka se trulež uvukla u ranu.

en: “I think I will.” Flashing steel used to delight him. Now the glint of the sun on the tiny blade was making him feel faint.
bs: — Mislim da hoću. Bljesak čelika ga je nekad oduševljavao. Sada mu je od samog odsjaja sunca na sićušnoj oštrici bilo slabo.

en: Tears made his sight swim. He wished Rikke was with him. She would’ve turned it into a joke, played the fool, made him… feel good. It was a long time since he’d felt good.
bs: Suze su mu zamaglile vid. Poželio je da je Rike s njim. Ona bi sve pretvorila u šalu, glumila bi budalu, učinila bi da se osjeća… dobro. Prošlo je mnogo vremena otkako se osjećao dobro.

en: “It’s just…” Flick straightened up, wiping his mouth. “A sort o’ snot coming out now.’ And he peeked at the display from the corner of his eye, as if looking sidelong might make it prettier.
bs: — Samo je… Flik se uspravio, brišući usta. — Neka vrsta sluzi sad izlazi. I bacio je Oko na prizor krajičkom oka, kao da bi ga bočni Oko mogao učiniti ljepšim.

en: “The flatheads left tracks. Took some sheep with ’em. Wool tufted on the trees. Tracks all over. Couldn’t have left bigger ones if they’d driven a wagon. I could track ’em easy. Want me to track ’em? I’ll track ’em, shall I?” Maybe she spent so much time on her own, only trees for company, that she’d poor judgement now on quantity of words. It was either too few in little stabs or too many in a flurry. “Want to follow, Chief?”
bs: — Plosnatoglavi su ostavili tragove. Uzeli su neke ovce sa sobom. Vuna zapela za drveće. Tragovi posvuda. Nisu mogli ostaviti veće ni da su vozili kola. Lako bih ih mogla pratiti. Želiš li da ih pratim? Pratit ću ih, hoću li? Možda je provodila previše vremena sama, samo s drvećem kao društvom, pa je sada loše procjenjivala količinu riječi. Bile su to ili rijetke, male ubode ili previše njih u naletu. — Želiš li poći za njima, Šefe?

en: Clover stood, trying to find a gap in the leaves so he could peer into the valley, grunted as he stretched one aching leg, then the other, then squatted down again. “The past. Choices made. Things done.”
bs: Klover je ustao pokušavajući pronaći prolaz u lišću kako bi zavirio u dolinu, zastenjao dok je istezao jednu bolnu nogu, pa drugu, a zatim ponovno čučnuo. — O prošlosti. O odlukama. O učinjenim stvarima.

en: Then Clover heard ’em, and the grin faded fast. A howling first, like a pack of wolves far off, making the hairs on his neck prickle. Then a clattering and clanking, like armoured men coming on the rush, making his mouth turn dry. Then a mad snuffling and gibbering and hooting somewhere between a crowd of hungry hogs and a gaggle of angry geese, setting his palms to itch.
bs: Tada ih Klover začu i osmijeh mu brzo iščeznu. Najprije zavijanje, poput čopora vukova u daljini, od kojega mu se naježi koža na vratu. Potom zveket i klopot, kao da jurišaju oklopljeni Folk, od čega mu se usta osušiše. Zatim mahnito njuškanje, mrmljanje i hukanje, nešto između krda gladnih svinja i jata razjarenih gusaka, zbog čega ga dlanovi zasvrbješe.

en: A vile mass they were, whooping and warbling, skittering and scuttling, limping on legs of different lengths, all teeth and claws and mad fury. All twisted and misshapen, mockeries of men, squashed from clay by children with no knack for sculpting.
bs: Bila je to odvratna masa, koja je klicala i cvilila, hitro se kretala i šuljala, šepajući na nogama različitih duljina, sve sami zubi, kandže i mahniti bijes. Sve izobličeno i nakazno, izrugivanje ljudima, kao da ih je od gline oblikovala djeca bez dara za kiparstvo.

en: “Arrows!” he roared, and men leaned out over the rocks at the sides of the gully. Bows sang and shafts fluttered down among the Shanka, bounced, rattled, stuck into flesh. He saw one flathead flailing, trying to reach with one twisted arm to where an arrow was sticking from its neck. The archers drew and strung and shot, easy as shooting lambs in a slaughter-pen. A spear went flying up the other way but bounced from a rock, harmless.
bs: — Strijelci! zaurla on, a Folk se nagnuše preko stijena s obje strane klanca. Lukovi su zapjevali, a strijele su zalepršale među Shanka, odbijale se, zveckale i zabadale u meso. Vidio je jednog ravnoglavca kako mlati rukama, pokušavajući dosegnuti iskrivljenim udom mjesto gdje mu je strijela virila iz vrata. Strijelci su napinjali, ciljali i pucali, lako kao da gađaju janjad u klaonici. Jedno Pajk poletjelo je natrag, ali se odbilo od stijene, bezopasno.

en: Still, when you’re sent to fight monsters, it’s a good idea to have a monster or two of your own. That, and the way he was never happier’n when he was charging at the Great Leveller reminded Clover of himself twenty years past, when they still called him Jonas Steepfield and misfortunes hadn’t taught him to tread lightly. He was just congratulating himself on staying well clear of the action when a spearman gave a screech, dropped clutching at his shoulder, and a giant flathead came roaring out
bs: Ipak, kada te pošalju da se boriš protiv čudovišta, pametno je imati pokoje čudovište i na svojoj strani. To, kao i činjenica da nije bio sretniji nego kada bi jurišao na Veliki Izravnavatelj, podsjetilo je Klovera na njega samoga prije Dvadesetero godina, kada su ga još zvali Jonas Stipfild, a nesreće ga nisu naučile da gazi oprezno. Upravo si je čestitao što se drži podalje od okršaja kada je kopljanik vrisnuo, ispustio oružje hvatajući se za rame, a divovski plosnatoglavi stvor ričući je izle

en: Downside watched ’em run, eyes wide and wild, spit in his beard and blood streaking his face. No one wanted to tell him to stop and honestly Clover didn’t much, either. But that’s the thing about being chief. You can’t just throw your hands up at everything and say it’s someone else’s problem.
bs: Dausaid ih je promatrao kako bježe, očiju širom otvorenih i divljih, sa slinom u bradi i krvlju koja mu je premazala lice. Nitko mu nije htio reći da stane, a iskreno, ni Kloveru se nije dalo. No, to je čar biti šef. Ne možeš samo dignuti ruke od svega i reći da je to tuđi Trobli.

en: “Some things don’t change,” said Sholla, busy trying to prise her dagger out o’ the big Shanka’s skull.
bs: — Neke se stvari ne mijenjaju, reče Šola, zauzeta pokušajima izvući svoj bodež iz lubanje velikog Shanka.

en: Some of the others laughed at that, ready to laugh at anything now the fight was done and they likely had a fat gild coming.
bs: Neki se od ostalih nasmijaše na to, spremni smijati se bilo čemu sada kada je borba završila i kada će vjerojatno dobiti masnu nagradu.

en: “Fits are getting worse,” croaked Rikke. Her teeth ached. Her head was splitting. She prised one eye open, then the other, saw Isern and her father looking down at her. “Least I didn’t shit this time.”
bs: — Napadi su sve gori, promuklo je izustila Rike. Zubi su je boljeli. Šef joj se cijepala. Prisilila je jedno Oko da se otvori, zatim i drugo, te ugledala Izern i oca kako gledaju u nju. — Barem se nisam usrala ovaj put.

en: “I guess.” Rikke’s father helped her up, the horribly familiar pain pulsing away behind her eyes. “You should eat something.”
bs: — Valjda. Rikin otac pomogao joj je ustati, a užasno poznata bol pulsirala je iza njezinih očiju. — Trebala bi nešto pojesti.

en: “We’re all like children, Rikke. The older you get, the more you realise the grown-ups won’t suddenly walk in and set things right. You want things right, you have to put ’em right yourself.”
bs: — Svi smo mi poput djece, Rike. Što si starija, to više shvaćaš da odrasli neće odjednom ušetati i sve popraviti. Želiš li da stvari budu kako treba, moraš ih sama popraviti.

en: “One can still kill politely.” It was then she noticed a building not far away was on fire. Going up like a torch, it was, flames gouting from the windows and burning straws whirling from the thatch.
bs: — Čovjek može ubijati i pristojno. Upravo je tada primijetila da jedna zgrada nedaleko gori. Uzdizala se poput baklje, plamenovi su sukljali iz prozora, a zapaljena slama letjela je sa slamnatog krova.

en: Rikke stared at that burning building that wasn’t really burning. The one next door had caught fire, too, now, just patches among the thatch. By the dead, she wanted to reach for a bucket, but how do you put out flames that aren’t there yet? Or that burned out long ago? “Fire and discord,” she muttered.
bs: Rike je zurila u onu goruću zgradu koja zapravo nije gorjela. I ona do nje se zapalila, tek zakrpe među slamom. Tako joj mrtvih, htjela je posegnuti za kantom, ali kako ugasiti plamenove kojih još nema? Ili koji su odavno izgorjeli? — Palioc i nesloga, promrmljala je.

en: Something was forced between her jaws and she gagged, tried to twist in a sudden panic but couldn’t move, gripped tight as swelling ice might grip a drowned corpse.
bs: Nešto joj na silu uguraše među čeljusti, ona se zagrcnu i pokuša trznuti u iznenadnoj panici, ali nije se mogla pomaknuti; bila je stisnuta čvrsto, poput leda koji steže utopljenikov leš.

en: Isern looked more and more scared with every word. Rikke never saw her look scared before. Except just before, in the vision. It made Rikke feel even more scared than the last time it happened.
bs: Izern je sa svakom izgovorenom riječi izgledala sve prestrašenije. Rike je nikada prije nije vidjela uplašenu. Osim maločas, u viziji. Zbog toga se Rike osjećala još prestrašenije nego prošli put.

en: “Don’t speak if silence will do,” grunted Vick, dragging him on. “To these folk, ‘no’ is the start of a conversation. There he is.”
bs: — Ne govori ako tišina može poslužiti, frknula je Vik vukući ga dalje."Ovom Folk svijetu, 'ne' je tek početak razgovora. Eno ga."

en: “Very likeable,” said Vick. That’s what made him such a threat. She felt the metal in her pocket knock against her stiff hip as she turned to follow him. “But knives kill likeable men just as easily as unlikeable ones.”
bs: — Vrlo dopadljiv, reče Vik. Upravo ga je to činilo takvom prijetnjom. Osjetila je kako je metal u njezinu džepu udario o ukočen kuk dok se okretala da ga slijedi. — Ali noževi ubijaju dopadljive ljude jednako lako kao i one nedopadljive.

en: Vick bent down, trying to catch sight of Shudra through the forest of legs, then up on tiptoe. She waved towards a rooftop. One of her hired men was on a scaffold there, pretending to work at a crumbling chimney. He caught her eye, nodded at an alley.
bs: Vik se sagnula, pokušavajući ugledati Šudru kroz šumu nogu, a zatim se podigla na prste. Mahnula je prema krovu. Jedan od njezinih unajmljenih Folk nalazio se na skeli, pretvarajući se da radi na trošnom dimnjaku. Uhvatio je njezin Oko i kimnuo prema uličici.

en: Vick scorned them, pitied them, but underneath, well hidden, she envied them, too. Wondered what it would be like, to believe in something that much. Enough to die for it. Like Sibalt had. Like Malmer had. Like her brother had. How wonderful it must feel, to be certain. To know you stand on the right side, instead of just the winning one. But you can’t just choose to believe, can you?
bs: Vik ih je prezirala, žalila ih je, ali duboko u sebi, dobro skriveno, pomalo im je i zavidjela. Pitala se kakav je osjećaj vjerovati u nešto toliko snažno. Dovoljno snažno da bi čovjek za to umro. Kao Sibalt. Kao Malmer. Kao njezin brat. Kako li je divan osjećaj biti siguran. Znati da stojiš na pravoj strani, umjesto samo na onoj pobjedničkoj. Ali ne možeš tek tako izabrati u što ćeš vjerovati, zar ne?

en: And now she saw the hooded figure. Just where she’d guessed he’d be. Walking towards Shudra, not too fast, not too slow, not looking right at him, no one to remark upon.
bs: I tada ugleda figuru s kapuljačom. Upravo ondje gdje je pretpostavila da će biti. Hodao je prema Šudru, ne prebrzo, ne presporo, ne gledajući izravno u njega, ne privlačeći ničiju pozornost.

en: Vick caught his wrist as the knife went up and hauled it down, pulling him backwards and punching him as hard as she could in the side of his knee.
bs: Vik ga je uhvatila za zglob dok se nož dizao i povukla ga prema dolje, trgnuvši ga unatrag i udarivši ga svom snagom u bočnu stranu koljena.

en: “But you might want to head home and bar the door,” she said as she stood, frowning into the crowd for any other threats. “Maybe stay off the streets until the vote.”
bs: — No možda biste se trebali vratiti kući i zabraviti vrata, rekla je ustajući i namršteno pretražujući gomilu u potrazi za drugim prijetnjama. — Možda bi bilo pametno ne izlaziti na ulice do glasanja.

en: “You dare to talk to me about windows, you crippled remnant?” snarled Wetterlant. “Your Majesty, please, I know you are a reasonable man—”
bs: — Usuđuješ se govoriti mi o prozorima, ti osakaćeni ostatku? zareža Vetelant. — Vaša Uzvišenosti, molim vas, znam da ste razuman čovjek…

en: Wetterlant looked from Glokta to Bruckel to Orso, and evidently found little cause for encouragement. “Things have got entirely out of hand. It was simple high spirits.”
bs: Vetelant pogleda od Glokte prema Bruckelu i Orsu te očito ne nađe mnogo razloga za ohrabrenje. — Stvari su potpuno izmakle kontroli. Bila je to samo mladenačka obijest.

en: The door was shut behind them with a clunk like the fall of a headsman’s axe. Orso gave the faintest shiver as he strode away, deeply grateful to be on the right side of it.
bs: Vrata se za njima zatvore uz tresak poput pada dželatove sjekire. Orso se blago strese dok je koračao dalje, duboko zahvalan što se nalazi s prave strane tih vrata.

en: Lady Wetterlant turned a glare on the high justice that might have frozen milk. “Mine is an old family, Your Majesty. We have many friends.”
bs: Lady Vetelant uputi visokom sucu Oko od kojeg bi se mlijeko moglo zalediti. — Moja je obitelj stara, Vaša Uzvišenosti. Imamo mnogo prijatelja.

en: “Do the right thing, Your Majesty!” Lady Wetterlant shrieked after him, her voice so sharp it made him hunch his shoulders. “I beg you, for my sake. For your sake. Do the right thing!”
bs: — Učinite pravu stvar, Vaša Uzvišenosti! povikala je lady Vetelant za njim, glasom toliko oštrim da se Orso zgrčio."Preklinjem vas, radi mene. Radi vas samih. Učinite pravu stvar!"

en: “Chaos in Westport, chaos in Valbeck, chaos among the commoners, chaos among the nobility?” Orso gave a sorry grunt. “Things could be smoother.”
bs: — Kaos u Vestportu, kaos u Valbeku, kaos među pukom, kaos među plemstvom? Orso ispusti žalostan zvuk. — Stvari bi mogle biti glatkije.

en: “Well-written villains, maybe. You wouldn’t believe Wetterlant in a book! How the hell does a man end up like that?”
bs: — Dobro napisani zlikovci, možda. Ne bi povjerovao da je Vetelant stvaran da čitaš o njemu u knjizi! Kako dovraga čovjek uopće postane takav?

en: “Magic fades from the world. I destroyed the Prophet’s indestructible Hundred Words. Those few of his Eaters that remain skulk about the South, trying to hold together the shreds of their ruined empire. A man is measured by his enemies. Worthy ones can be more missed than friends.” Bayaz gave a sigh, then a shrug. “Magic fades from the world but, in truth, most problems have always been better solved with a few sharp words. Or a little sharp steel.”
bs: — Umijeće blijedi iz svijeta. Uništio sam Prorokov neuništivi Sto riječi. Oni rijetki njegovi Proždirači koji su preostali vrzmaju se po Southu, pokušavajući zadržati krhotine svog uništenog carstva. Čovjeka se mjeri po njegovim neprijateljima. Oni vrijedni mogu nedostajati više od prijatelja. Bajaz uzdahne, a zatim slegne ramenima. — Umijeće blijedi iz svijeta, ali, iskreno, većina se problema oduvijek bolje rješavala s nekoliko oštrih riječi. Ili malo oštrog čelika.

en: “An astonishing room,” murmured Isher, suitably awestruck as he gazed up at the ceiling, carved in the minutest detail as a forest canopy, gold and silver clockwork birds dotted among the branches. They had sung, once, when fully wound, though the mechanism had failed long ago. It was, without a doubt, impressive, which was why Orso had picked it for this interview. He could not escape the thought, however, that whatever monarch constructed the place could simply have frolicked in one of the doz
bs: — Zapanjujuća prostorija, promrmljao je Išer, prikladno zadivljen dok je zurio u strop, izrezbaren do najsitnijih detalja kao šumska krošnja, s pticama od zlata i srebra koje su bile razmještene među granama. Nekada su pjevale, kada bi mehanizam bio navijen, premda je taj mehanizam odavno otkazao. Bilo je to, nesumnjivo, impresivno, zbog čega je Orso i odabrao ovo mjesto za razgovor. Ipak, nije se mogao oteti dojmu da je monarh koji je sagradio ovo mjesto mogao jednostavno uživati u jednoj od de

en: “Nor me.” Orso waved the man away and shuffled to the edge of his chair. “In my youth I loved to dance, but since taking the crown I prefer to get straight to the matter. I wish to speak to you, man to man, on the subject of Fedor dan Wetterlant.”
bs: — Ni za mene. Orso je otjerao čovjeka rukom i pomaknuo se na rub stolice. — U mladosti sam volio plesati, no otkako sam preuzeo Krunu, draže mi je odmah prijeći na stvar. Želim razgovarati s vama, čovjek čovjeku, o temi Fedor dan Vetelant.

en: “It is a solution that makes sense from their perspective, but… if I may?” Orso waved him on. “It would satisfy no one. Wetterlant would continue to bleat for justice from his cell, and his friends in the Open Council would bleat on his behalf, and his mother would be a continual thorn in everyone’s side—”
bs: — To je rješenje koje ima smisla iz njihove perspektive, ali… ako smijem? Orso ga je potaknuo rukom. — To nikoga ne bi zadovoljilo. Vetelant bi iz svoje ćelije nastavio blejati za pravdom, njegovi prijatelji u Otvorenom Vijeću blejali bi u njegovo ime, a njegova majka svima bi bila neprestani trn u oku —

en: “I believe, with their help… I could get broad support in the Open Council for a lengthy prison sentence.”
bs: — Vjerujem da bih, uz njihovu pomoć… mogao dobiti široku potporu u Otvorenom Vijeću za dugu zatvorsku kaznu.

en: Squeak, squeak, squeak, went the wheel of her father’s chair. Savine narrowed her eyes at it. Gritted her teeth at it. Struggled with every turn of that wheel not to scream.
bs: Škrip, škrip, škrip, odjekivalo je očevim kolicima. Savine je suzila oči gledajući u njih. Stisnula je zube. Borila se sa svakim okretajem tog kotača kako ne bi vrisnula.

en: “You let Kort off with a warning? I thought you might have had him skinned as an example to your other partners.”
bs: — Pustila si Korta samo s upozorenjem? Mislio sam da ćeš ga dati oderati kao primjer ostalim partnerima.

en: “A charming picture!” A sturdy man in a superbly tailored coat was blocking their path. Bayaz himself, Savine realised, sun gleaming from his hairless pate, looking less like a legendary wizard than a highly prosperous merchant. “My own brothers and sisters are forever feuding. It warms my heart to see a father and daughter enjoying each other’s company.”
bs: — Šarmantna slika! Snažan muškarac u vrhunski krojenom kaputu prepriječio im je put. Sam Bajaz, shvati Savine, dok mu se sunce odbijalo od ćelave glave, izgledajući manje poput legendarnog čarobnjaka, a više poput iznimno imućnog trgovca. — Moja se braća i sestre vječno svađaju. Srce mi grije vidjeti oca i kćer kako uživaju u zajedničkom društvu.

en: “Very little worth anything is ever given away. I am sure you know that, too.” Bayaz smiled at Savine’s father. The one in the chair, not the one immortalised in stone. “I have no doubt your father will stand here one day. Who has sacrificed more for the Union, after all? Except perhaps your uncle.” Bayaz turned to look up at the statue of Lord Marshal West. “Who gave his life defending it.”
bs: — Vrlo se malo toga vrijednog ikada poklanja. Siguran sam da i vi to znate. Bajaz se nasmiješi Savininu ocu. Onomu u stolici, ne onomu ovjekovječenom u kamenu. — Nemam nimalo sumnje da će vaš otac jednoga dana stajati ovdje. Tko je, uostalom, žrtvovao više za Unija? Osim možda vašega ujaka. Bajaz se okrenu kako bi pogledao kip lorda maršala Westa. — Koji je Dow svoj život braneći ga.

en: “The Banking House of Valint and Balk! An attack on enterprise. On progress. On the very future! If the current administration cannot get a grip on the situation… we must find someone who can.”
bs: "Bankarsku kuću Valint i Balk! Napad na poduzetništvo. Na Naprijed. Na samu budućnost! Ako sadašnja administracija ne uspije zauzdati situaciju… moramo pronaći nekoga tko to može."

en: Her father gave a bitter snort. “The First of the Magi never gives, only takes. That was not an offer to you, it was a threat to me.”
bs: Otac joj gorko odvrati frktanjem. — Prvi među Magi nikada ne daje, samo uzima. To nije bila ponuda tebi, to je bila prijetnja meni.

en: “I realise. But the scriptures say those lost in the desert should take such water as they are offered.” She gently swung open the door. “No matter who it comes from.”
bs: — Svjesna sam toga. Ali svete knjige kažu da oni izgubljeni u pustinji trebaju prihvatiti svaku vodu koja im se ponudi. Ona blago otvori vrata. — Bez obzira od koga dolazila.

en: Savine assumed her sweetest smile while she tried to work out what was going on. “As I am a great admirer of yours as a Lady Governor.”
bs: Savine namjesti najslađi osmijeh dok je u glavi pokušavala dokučiti što se događa. — Kao što sam i ja velika obožavateljica vaših, kao guvernerice.

en: “I don’t care for the feeling of being ambushed,” said Savine, looking from one woman to the other, both formidable in their own ways and as a pair positively daunting.
bs: — Ne sviđa mi se osjećaj da mi namještaju zasjedu, odvrati Savine, prebacujući Oko s jedne žene na drugu, od kojih je svaka bila zastrašujuća na svoj način, a zajedno posve obeshrabrujuće.

en: Savine stared from her mother to her prospective mother-in-law. It was an ambush. An expertly prepared pincer movement, and she was outflanked on both sides.
bs: Savine je prelazila pogledom s majke na svoju buduću svekrvu. Bila je to zasjeda. Vješto pripremljen kliješta-manevar, a ona je bila opkoljena s obje strane.

en: “It’s a shame youth has to end,” sang Savine’s mother, fluttering her eyelashes. Then she gave Savine’s knee a parting pat and sat back, murmuring out of the corner of her mouth, “You see that bluntness won’t be a problem.”
bs: — Šteta što mladost mora proći, zapjeva Savinina majka, trepćući trepavicama. Zatim je još jednom potapšala Savine po koljenu i naslonila se, mrmljajući kroz kut usana: — Vidiš da ta izravnost neće biti Trobli.

en: Savine had spent her whole life scheming, plotting, striving to control events. There was a certain relief in yielding to the inevitable. “No,” she said, almost a sigh. “I don’t suppose there is.”
bs: Savine je cijeli život provela smišljajući spletke, planirajući i nastojeći kontrolirati događaje. Postojalo je određeno olakšanje u prepuštanju neizbježnom. — Ne, reče, gotovo uzdahnuvši. — Pretpostavljam da ne postoji.

en: “Congratulations on your forthcoming marriage.” Leo winced at a twinge in his leg as he broke free. “Haven’t seen my mother this excited in years.” He turned slowly around, looking up towards the gilded dome high, high above. “Doubt you could find a grander venue.”
bs: — Čestitam na nadolazećem vjenčanju. Leo se trgnuo zbog sijevajuće boli u nozi dok se izvlačio iz zagrljaja. — Nisam vidio majku ovako uzbuđenu godinama. Polako se okrenuo, gledajući prema pozlaćenoj kupoli visoko, visoko iznad. — Sumnjam da bi mogao naći veličanstvenije mjesto.

en: “He offers not the slightest check to Old Sticks and the rest of those withered bastards on the Closed Council. It’s all liars and swindlers in the White Chamber.”
bs: — On ne nudi ni najmanju prepreku za Sticks i ostatak onih sasušenih gadova u Zatvorenom vijeću. U Bijeloj dvorani su sami lažljivci i prevaranti.

en: “A bloody scandal,” lamented Isher. “Still. Nothing compared to what they’re doing to poor Fedor dan Wetterlant.”
bs: "Krvavi skandal", jadao se Išer. — Ipak. Ništa u usporedbi s onim što rade jadnom Fedoru dan Wetterlantu.

en: “He’s appealed for the king’s justice. Anyone with a seat on the Open Council has the right to a trial here with His Majesty as the judge but, well… I doubt there’s any justice to be had in the Union these days.”
bs: — Zatražio je kraljevsku pravdu. Svatko tko ima mjesto u Vijeću ima pravo na suđenje ovdje, s Vašim Veličanstvom kao sucem, ali, dobro… sumnjam da se u Uniji danas može išta postići pravdom.

en: Crown Prince Orso had struck him as a good enough sort, but the throne only amplifies a man’s bad qualities, and his Closed Council were the same corrupt old worms who’d driven King Jezal’s reign into the ditch. What the Union needed was men of courage, men of passion, men of action.
bs: Krunski princ Orso činio mu se sasvim u redu, ali prijestolje samo pojačava čovjekove loše osobine, a njegovo Zatvoreno vijeće bili su isti oni korumpirani stari crvi koji su vladavinu kralja Džezal otjerali u propast. Ono što je Uniji trebalo bili su Folk od hrabrosti, Folk od strasti, Folk od akcije.

en: At that moment, it seemed more likely he’d faint than she would. “We’ve… met. Just the once.” The same number of times they’d fucked. Might’ve been better not to think of that, but now he couldn’t stop. “When I was last in Adua. Four months ago, was it? She struck me as a very attractive…” Terrible choice of word! “I mean… formidable woman.”
bs: U tom se trenutku činilo vjerojatnijim da će se on onesvijestiti nego ona. — Upoznali… smo se. Samo jednom." Isti broj puta koliko su se jebali. Možda je bilo bolje da o tome nije razmišljao, ali sada se nije mogao zaustaviti. — Kad sam posljednji put bio u Adui. Prije četiri mjeseca, je li tako? Dojmila mi se kao vrlo privlačna…" Grozan odabir riječi! "Mislim… imponzantna žena."

en: “But lions are not suited to administration. I know you want to do it all, but the last few months have proved to us both that you cannot govern Angland on your own.”
bs: — No lavovi nisu stvoreni za administraciju. Znam da bi sve htio sam, ali protekli su nam mjeseci oboje dokazali da ne možeš sam upravljati Englendom.

en: Leo swallowed. “Well, I won’t deny I’m not suited to administration. I don’t deny I need help. I can’t deny Savine’s beautiful, tasteful, refined and all the rest of it, I mean, she’s…” He thought back to that night, and not for the first time. “A hell of a woman.”
bs: Leo proguta knedlu. — Pa, ne poričem da nisam stvoren za administraciju. Ne poričem da mi treba pomoć. Ne mogu poreći da je Savine lijepa, ukusna, profinjena i sve to, mislim, ona je…" Prisjetio se te noći, i to ne prvi put. — Žena i pol.

en: “Then you appreciate the responsibilities that emerge with them.” Lady Ardee took a nip from a flask she’d produced as if by magic, then offered it around. “Drink?”
bs: — Onda shvaćaš odgovornosti koje s njima dolaze. Lady Ardi otpije gutljaj iz ploske koju je izvukla kao čarolijom, a zatim je ponudi ostalima. — Piće?

en: Savine stood at the parapet, the Agriont spread out below her as if she owned it. Somehow, he’d expected her to have turned matronly, rosy-cheeked, bloated out with child.
