bs: Lomljači su jurnuli. Nije im trebala zapovijed. Nisu se mogli zaustaviti čak ni da su htjeli, toliki je bio pritisak onih iza njih. Čitava Narodna armija za njihovim leđima. Svaki izrabljivani radnik u Uniji. No Smiler se nije želio zaustaviti. Htio je smrskati cijelo ovo korumpirano mjesto. Te gramzive gadove koji su njegove prijatelje slali u smrt u Stiriju, u smrt u tvornice, u smrt u podrume. Želio je spaliti trulež i stvoriti zemlju za njezine ljude.

en: “You’re a hero!” And a woman with a strong chin and her hair bound in a red scarf craned up to plant a great soft kiss on his jaw. “You’re all bloody heroes!”
bs: — Ti si heroj! Žena snažne čeljusti, s kosom povezanom crvenim rupcem, izvila se i utisnula snažan, mekan poljubac na njegovu čeljust. — Vi ste svi redom krvavi heroji!

en: They carried Risinau in on a gilded chair they must’ve torn from some chamber, some office, some hall. Adnes grabbed at a leg of it, one in a forest of hands, helping it pass, and Risinau laughed, and they laughed, and the joyous crowd cheered as they carried him bobbing down the aisle between the curved benches, and set him on the great table.
bs: Unijeli su Risinaua na pozlaćenoj stolici koju su morali otrgnuti iz neke odaje, nekog ureda, neke dvorane. Adnes se uhvatila za njezinu nogu, tek jedna u šumi ruku, pomažući joj proći, a Risinau se smijao, i oni su se smijali, dok je radosna gomila bodrila noseći ga kako se njihao niz prolaz između zakrivljenih klupa i smjestila ga na Great stol.

en: The soldier caught her hand, and there were tears on his face, too, but he was smiling. He’d a fine smile, she thought. “I don’t know your name.”
bs: Vojnik ju je uhvatio za ruku i na njegovu su licu bile suze, ali se smiješio. Imao je lijep osmijeh, pomislila je. — Ne znam ti ime.

en: “There’s one!” He heard footsteps clapping from the buildings. “Stop him!” Now he ran, but not far. Someone caught him under the arm and threw him down. A flash of a bearded face, armour that looked new-forged. He was dragged up again by the elbow. A strange gang. Like the people you might see at one of the cheap markets. Only furious.
bs: — Eno ga jedan! Čuo je topot koraka koji su odjekivali iz zgrada. — Zaustavite ga! Sada je potrčao, ali ne daleko. Netko ga je uhvatio ispod ruke i bacio na tlo. Bljesak bradatog lica, oklop koji je izgledao kao da je tek iskovan. Ponovno su ga povukli za lakat. Čudna skupina. Poput Folk koje biste mogli vidjeti na nekoj od jeftinih tržnica. Samo bijesni.

en: Something hit Ettenbeck on the side of his face and he fell. The ground cracked him hard. He wobbled up to his hands and knees. His jaw was throbbing. “Oh,” he muttered, blood pattering on the cobbles. “Oh dear.” A tooth fell out of his numb mouth.
bs: Nešto je pogodilo Ettenbecka u stranu lica i on se srušio. Tlo ga je grubo dočekalo. Uspio se teturajući podići na ruke i koljena. Čeljust mu je pulsirala. — O, promrmljao je, dok mu je krv kapala po kaldrmi. — O, ne." Zub mu je ispao iz utrnulih usta.

en: And they shoved his face into the water. Through the gurgle of the fountain he heard shouting. Singing. Laughing. He fought his way up, just for a moment, gasped in a breath, saw the mad crowd surging on towards the House of Questions. They shook swords and spears in the air. One had a severed head spiked on it, bobbing obscenely over the mob. Absurd. Like a cheap prop in a badly produced play. Except it was real.
bs: I gurnuli su mu lice u vodu. Kroz klokotanje fontane čuo je viku. Pjesmu. Smijeh. Borio se da izroni, tek na trenutak, udahnuo zrak, vidio pomahnitalu gomilu kako nadire prema Kući pitanja. Mahali su mačevima i kopljima u zraku. Jedno je imalo nabijenu odsječenu glavu, koja se neprilično njihala iznad rulje. Apsurdno. Poput jeftinog rekvizita u loše produciranoj predstavi. Samo što je bilo stvarno.

en: A face showed at the gap. Not the black-masked Practical he’d expected. A small woman, cheeks full of broken veins. She looked nervous, like she hadn’t known what to expect, then when she saw him standing there, she broke into a beaming smile. “Brother! You’re free!”
bs: Lice se pojavilo u procjepu. Ne onaj Praktik s crnom maskom kojeg je očekivao. Sitna žena, obraza punih popucalih kapilara. Djelovala je nervozno, kao da nije znala što očekivati, a onda, kad ga je vidjela kako ondje stoji, razvukla je Brod osmijeh. — Brate! Slobodan si!

en: She just sat against the wall, floppy as a rag doll. “Is it… Grise?” she whispered. Broad saw one of her hands was all smashed, crooked fingers bloated like sausages.
bs: Sjedila je naslonjena uza zid, mlohava poput krpene lutke. — Je li to… Grise?" prošaptala je. Brod je primijetio da joj je jedna šaka potpuno smrskana, a iskrivljeni prsti natečeni poput kobasica.

en: Broad had to push against a joyful current of people to get up the steps, into a wider, brighter hallway. A man in a leather apron ran past laughing, a wedge of documents clutched to his chest, papers slipping out and flapping to the floor. Another man bashed at a lock with a heavy ale flagon. This was where the music was coming from, a woman sitting cross-legged with some clerk’s tall hat jammed down to her eyebrows, eyes closed as she tooted jauntily on her flute.
bs: Brod se morao probijati kroz radosnu struju Folk kako bi se popeo stubama u širi, svjetliji hodnik. Čovjek u kožnoj pregači protrčao je smijući se, stišćući na prsima svežanj dokumenata iz kojeg su papiri ispadali i lepršali po podu. Drugi je muškarac teškom kriglom piva udarao po bravi. Odatle je dopirala glazba; žena je sjedila prekriženih nogu, s činovničkim visokim šeširom nabijenim do obrva, zatvorenih očiju veselo svirajući na fruli.

en: Broad had no answer. He held out his other hand to Brock. The one with the tattoo on the back. You could see how much it hurt him, to need the help. But this was no time for pride. Wasn’t easy, steering a pregnant woman and a one-legged man through that jostling crowd of rescuers and looters. Beyond a set of broken double doors men smashed and laughed, turned over furniture, flinging armfuls of fluttering papers in the air.
bs: Brod nije imao odgovora. Pruži drugu ruku Broku, onu s tetovažom na nadlanici. Moglo se vidjeti koliko ga boli to što mora tražiti pomoć. No sada nije bilo vrijeme za ponos. Nije bilo lako provesti trudnicu i jednonogog čovjeka kroz tu uznemirenu gomilu spasitelja i pljačkaša. Iza niza razbijenih dvokrilnih vrata Folk su divljali i smijali se, prevrtali namještaj i bacali u zrak naramke papira koji su lepršali.

en: “It’s the Young Lion!” someone called, and suddenly folk were crowding around them, reaching out for Leo. “Look, it’s Leo dan Brock!”
bs: — To je Juvens Lav! netko vikne i u trenu se gomila sjati oko njih, pružajući ruke prema Leu. — Gledajte, to je Leo dan Brok!

en: “I was at Stoffenbeck!” the fellow with the brows was snarling. “And he didn’t fight for the fucking people, all he did—”
bs: — Bio sam u Štopenbeku! režao je onaj s obrvama. — I on se nije borio za jebeni Folk, sve što je učinio —

en: Broad frowned down at his tattoo. He realised there was a little piece of tooth stuck between two of his scarred knuckles.
bs: Brod se namrštio gledajući svoju tetovažu. Shvatio je da mu je komadić zuba zapeo između dva izbrazdana zgloba na prstima.

en: He watched in stunned horror as Union flags were torn down, vandals dancing in triumph on the roofs. A few buildings remained in loyal hands, but they were islands in a stormy sea, hopelessly besieged. Here and there, bloody little dramas unfolded. Tiny figures chased down a street. Tiny figures tumbling from a window. Tiny figures hanged from trees.
bs: Gledao je u zaprepaštenom užasu kako se zastave Unije kidaju, dok su vandali trijumfalno plesali po krovovima. Nekoliko je zgrada ostalo u odanim rukama, ali bile su poput otoka u uzburkanom moru, beznadno opkoljene. Tu i tamo odvijale su se krvave male drame. Sićušne figure koje jure ulicom. Sićušne figure koje padaju kroz prozor. Sićušne figure obješene o drveće.

en: “No!” Orso struggled to put some authority into his voice. “No one shoots! I won’t kill my own people. No more… of my own people,” he added lamely, memories of the mass graves at Stoffenbeck floating up unbidden.
bs: — Ne! Orso se trudio unijeti malo autoriteta u svoj glas. — Nitko ne puca! Neću ubijati vlastiti Folk. Nema više… moga naroda, dodao je mlako, dok su mu sjećanja na masovne grobnice u Štopenbeku nepozvano navirala.

en: “A far more fearsome enemy than this rabble!” croaked Lord Marshal Rucksted, whose appearance had degraded far past artfully rugged and into the realm of total disarray.
bs: — Daleko strašnijem neprijatelju od ove rulje! promuklo će Lord Maršal Rucksted, čiji se izgled davno srozao s umjetnički zapuštenog na razinu potpunog rasula.

en: “As for the Eaters,” he went on, “it was the First of the Magi who dealt with them, and he destroyed half the Agriont doing it. Bayaz is noticeable by his absence today. Even Master Sulfur appears to have pressing business elsewhere.” Orso looked towards the House of the Maker, rising stark and black and decidedly unhelpful beyond the Agriont’s walls. “I fear the age of wizards is truly over. And one does wonder, after all, whether their price was ever really worth paying.”
bs: — Što se tiče Proždrljivaca, nastavio je, Prvi među Magima bio je taj koji se obračunao s njima, a pritom je uništio pola Agrionta. Bajaz je danas zamjetan po svojoj odsutnosti. Čak se i Majstor Salfur čini zauzetim neodgodivim poslom negdje drugdje. Orso je pogledao prema Kući Tvorca, koja se uzdizala oštro, crno i odlučno beskorisno izvan zidina Agrionta. — Bojim se da je doba čarobnjaka doista prošlo. I čovjek se, naposljetku, zapita je li njihova cijena ikada bila vrijedna plaćanja.

en: “I can, and for once I am.” He glanced at the mayhem beyond the walls. “The time has come for someone to nobly sacrifice themselves. In the absence of anyone better qualified… it will have to be me.”
bs: — Mogu, i ovaj put jesam. Baci Oko na kaos s onu stranu zidina. — Došlo je vrijeme da se netko plemenito žrtvuje. U nedostatku nekoga kvalificiranijeg… morat ću to biti ja.

en: “Of course not! You’re making a tactical withdrawal. If I come through this, I’ll be a prisoner. I’m going to need someone loyal to help me escape. Bake lockpicks into a cake or something.”
bs: " da nećeš! Izvodiš taktičko povlačenje. Ako preživim ovo, bit ću zatvorenik. Trebat će mi netko odan da mi pomogne pobjeći. Ispeci turpije za brave u kolaču ili nešto slično.

en: He wondered if there had been some choice he made, or didn’t. Some way to avoid this. If there had, it had passed without his even noticing. Probably he had been worrying about his mother, or the hook at his collar, or what people thought of him. He wished he had been a touch more purposeful. But people are what they are.
bs: Zapitao se je li postojao neki izbor koji je donio, ili možda propustio. Neki način da se ovo izbjegne. Ako ga je i bilo, prošao je a da ga nije ni primijetio. Vjerojatno se brinuo za majku, ili za kopču na ovratniku, ili za to što Folk misle o njemu. Volio bi da je bio malo odlučniji. No Folk su takvi kakvi jesu.

en: “Well?” he said, firmly and plainly. A little sternly, even. The voice of a disappointed father. A tone his own father had often been called on to use. “Here I am.” His eyes came to rest on an elderly woman in a patched dress and stained apron, sleeves rolled up even in the cold to show heavy pink forearms. “Might I ask your business, madam?”
bs: — I? reče čvrsto i razgovijetno. Čak pomalo strogo. Glas razočaranoga oca. Ton kojim je i njegov otac često morao govoriti. — Evo me. Njegovo se oko zaustavilo na starijoj ženi u zakrpanoj haljini i umrljanoj pregači, zasukanih rukava unatoč hladnoći kako bi se vidjele teške ružičaste podlaktice. — Smijem li upitati što trebate, gospođo?

en: But rather than falling on him like hungry wolves, the silent mob parted, revealing a man in a simple, dark suit of clothes. A hairless man, his face hideously burned, and at his side a hard-looking woman with a hard-looking frown.
bs: No umjesto da navale na njega poput gladnih vukova, tiha se svjetina razdvoji, otkrivajući muškarca u jednostavnom, tamnom odijelu. Muškarca bez kose, jezivo opečenog lica, a uz njega Trdak ženu mrka pogleda.

en: “Well. I surrender the palace, I suppose. I ask that you show mercy to my guards and retainers. They have only tried to serve me.”
bs: — Dobro. Predajem palaču, pretpostavljam. Molim vas da pokažete Grace prema mojim stražarima i pratnji. Oni su se samo trudili služiti mi.

en: “Ain’t it?” And Rikke rubbed her hand against it, fine and white and so very soft, stitched onto that red cloth Savine dan Brock gave her, to make a cloak fit for a queen of legend. “A gift from the people of Carleon.”
bs: — Zar ne? Rike ga je protrljala rukom; bilo je fino, bijelo i tako mekano, prišiveno na onaj crveni platneni ogrtač koji joj je dala Savine dan Brok kako bi izgledala kao kraljica iz legendi. — Dar od Folk iz Carleona.

en: Rikke could hear the commotion now. A crowd of gabbling voices, happy and angry at once. The warrior’s favourite mood. She shoved her hood back and scrubbed some life into her flattened hair with her fingernails, heart suddenly pounding. “They’ve got him?”
bs: Rike je sada mogla čuti komešanje. Gomila glasova koji su se nadglasavali, istodobno sretni i ljuti. Ratničko omiljeno raspoloženje. Odgurnula je kapuljaču i noktima protrljala kosu kako bi joj vratila život, dok joj je srce naglo lupalo. — Jesu li ga uhvatili?

en: Stour tried to push himself up, arms trembling, making a blubbing whimper all the way. Then Hardbread stepped up and kicked him in the guts, and knocked him flat again.
bs: Staur se pokušao podignuti, dršćućih ruku, ispuštajući pritom nekakvo grleno cmizdrenje. Tada je Hardbred istupio, šutnuo ga u trbuh i ponovno ga srušio na pod.

en: Stour hung his head. “He’d give anything… to get me back.” Something dripped on the floor. Bastard was crying. To suffer bravely takes practice, and he’d never had any. “I’m the future o’ the North,” he mumbled, like even he could hardly believe it might ever have been true. No matter how much pride a man has, it don’t take much, in the end, to beat it all out of him. To make him want nothing but for the beating to stop. “Please.”
bs: Staur objesi glavu. — Dow bi sve… samo da me vrati." Nešto je kapnulo na pod. Kopile je plakalo. Hrabro podnositi patnju zahtijeva vježbu, a on je nikada nije imao. — Ja sam budućnost Sjevera, promrmlja, kao da je i sam jedva vjerovao da je to ikada moglo biti istina. Koliko god čovjek ponosa imao, na kraju ne treba mnogo da ga se izbije iz njega. Da poželi samo jedno – da premlaćivanje prestane. — Molim te.

en: “I’m sorry,” he whispered, curling up on his side, broken hand trembling over his bloody face. “Don’t hurt me.”
bs: — Oprosti, prošaptao je sklupčavši se na bok, a slomljena mu je šaka drhtala preko krvavog lica. — Nemoj me ozlijediti.

en: “Black Calder even less so.” Clover watched the Nail manhandling Stour across the floor. “Just can’t see any future where this bastard breathing is a good thing for us.”
bs: — Black Kalder još i manje. Klover je promatrao kako Najl vuče Staura po podu. — Jednostavno ne vidim budućnost u kojoj je za nas dobro da taj gad diše.

en: “They made it stupid for me not to betray ’em. I’m hoping you’ll be craftier.” And he slid something from an inside pocket. A golden chain of weighty links, its dangling diamond sparkling in the light from the tall windows. The one she’d seen Scale Ironhand wear at the duel. The one she’d seen Stour Nightfall wear at her father’s funeral. The chain Bethod had forged, before she was born, when he forced the North together with fire and sword. “Guess this should come to you now.”
bs: — Učinili su glupost ne izdavši me. Nadam se da ćeš ti biti lukavija. Izvukao je nešto iz unutarnjeg džepa. Zlatni lanac teških karika, čiji je viseći dijamant svjetlucao na svjetlosti s visokih prozora. Onaj koji je vidjela na Ljuski Željezna Ruka tijekom dvoboja. Onaj koji je vidjela na Stauru Najtfolu na očevu sprovodu. Lanac koji je Bethod iskovao prije njezina rođenja, kada je vatrom i mačem prisilio Sjever na ujedinjenje. — Pretpostavljam da bi ovo sada trebalo pripasti tebi.

en: “And half the North besides,” crowed Hardbread, “and Nightfall’s men are trickling back wounded and ruined and Black Calder hasn’t much left to fight with, I reckon.”
bs: — I pola Sjevera uz to, zakrekuta Hardbred, a Folk iz uporišta Najtfol vraćaju se natrag ranjeni i uništeni, dok Black Kalder ionako više nema s čim ratovati, ako se mene pita.

en: “Patience,” she said, softly, tapping at the peeled paint on the arm of Skarling’s Chair with her fingernail. “We need to chew what we’ve bit before we bite off more. While you boys were having fun on the way from Uffrith there’s been work to do up here.”
bs: — Strpljenja, prozbori tiho, nježno kuckajući noktom po oguljenoj boji na naslonu Skarlingove Stolice. — Moramo prožvakati to što smo zagrizli prije nego što zagrizemo previše. Dok ste se vi momci zabavljali na putu iz Afrita, ovdje gore bilo je posla.

en: “I still reckon the moon would smile upon him face down in the mud.” Isern prodded at the bars with one blue finger, making the cage turn gently, the Great Wolf limp as a heap of filthy rags inside. “Remember when he chased us through the woods, all cold and hungry and gnat-nibbled? Remember how bitter your feelings then?”
bs: — I dalje mislim da bi se mjesec nasmiješio da mu je lice zaronjeno u blato. Izern gurne rešetke plavim prstom, natjeravši kavez da se polako okrene, dok je Great Vuk unutra ležao mlohav poput hrpe prljavih krpa. — Sjećaš li se kad nas je lovio po šumi, promrzle, gladne i izgrizene od mušica? Sjećaš li se koliko su ti osjećaji tada bili gorki?

en: She gave the Nail a considering look. You could not have called him pretty, slouched long and loose against the wall with his thumbs in his belt and his elbows stuck out and his chin stuck forward. But then Rikke doubted pretty was the first word anyone would’ve picked for her these days. And there was something about him. All calm, and confident, and in no hurry. Like he was happy in his own skin, the very thing she’d never been. We’re always drawn to our opposites. Drawn to them and scared by
bs: Promotrimo Najla. Nije se mogao nazvati zgodnim dok je tako dugo i opušteno visio uza zid, palčeva zataknutih za pojas, laktova izbačenih i brade isturene naprijed. No, Rike je sumnjala da bi itko ovih dana za nju odabrao riječ "zgodna. A bilo je nečega u njemu. Potpuna smirenost, samopouzdanje i nimalo žurbe. Kao da je sretan u vlastitoj koži, upravo ono što ona nikada nije bila. Uvijek nas privlače naše suprotnosti. Privlače nas, a istovremeno nas plaše. A gdje je zabava u nekome tko te barem

en: Not quite the sultry swagger she’d planned. Maybe she’d got too cocky after all. But there was nothing for it now but to see it through. She wriggled into Skarling’s Chair, trying to arrange her fine new cloak in a manner that preserved the delicate balance between too much mystery and not enough.
bs: I nije to baš bila zavodljiva šetnja kakvu je planirala. Možda se ipak previše osilila. No sad joj nije preostajalo ništa drugo nego izgurati stvar do kraja. Uvukla se u Skarlingovu stolicu, nastojeći namjestiti svoj novi skupocjeni ogrtač tako da pogodi savršenu ravnotežu između odviše tajnovitosti i premalo.

en: He gave a little giggle. “Grand.” And he tossed the empty bottle out of the window, leaned down over the chair, a hand on each arm, and kissed her on the mouth. A delicate, polite little kiss, it was, catching her top lip between both of his, and then her bottom lip. So delicate and polite she almost laughed.
bs: Tiho se zahihotao. — Odlično." Bacio je praznu bocu kroz prozor, nagnuo se preko stolice oslonivši se objema rukama o naslone te ju poljubio u usta. Bio je to nježan, uljudan poljubac; uhvatio joj je gornju usnu objema svojima, a potom i donju. Toliko nježan i uljudan da se umalo nasmijala.

en: A faint voice echoed from beyond the monstrous, studded doors in the towering, spike-topped wall of that fortress of a bank. “I can hear you.”
bs: Slabašan glas odjeknuo je nasuprot tome monstruoznih, zakovicama okovanih vrata u visokom zidu, nalik na utvrdu, koji je opasivao banku. — Čujem vas.

en: Tallow watched the whole business while blowing into his cupped hands with his usual air of hangdog resignation. “So… we’re not the Inquisition any more?”
bs: Talou je promatrao cijelu stvar dok je puhao u sklopljene dlanove sa svojim uobičajenim izrazom pokunjene rezignacije. — Dakle… mi više nismo Inkvizicija?

en: “Good.” She regretted saying it right away. New Union or old, letting a feeling show was like pointing out a chink in your armour. An invitation to stick the knife in. She frowned sideways at Tallow. With his sister released, he’d no real reason to work with her. Still less to be loyal to her. “You’re still here, though, I notice.”
bs: — Dobro. Odmah je zažalila što je to izrekla. Bio novi Unija ili stari, pokazati osjećaje značilo je isto što i otkriti pukotinu u oklopu. Poziv nekome da ti zapiči nož u leđa. Sumnjičavo je pogledala Taloua krajičkom oka. Kad mu je sestra bila na slobodi, nije imala nikakav stvarni razlog surađivati s njom. A još manje biti joj lojalan. — Ipak, primjećujem da si još ovdje.

en: All shot and no powder summed it right up. She’d just have to blow the door down with lies, like usual. “Get the match-cord lit at least, make it look like we think the damn thing works.” She cleared her sore throat and turned back to the bank. “Can you hear me in there?”
bs: Svi pucnjevi, a baruta nigdje – to je najbolje opisivalo situaciju. Morat će provaliti vrata lažima, kao obično."Upalite barem taj fitilj, neka izgleda kao da mi mislimo da ta prokleta stvar radi." Pročistila je bolno grlo i okrenula se natrag prema banci. — Čujete li me unutra?

en: “Why’s the Commissioner so interested in banks, anyway?” muttered Tallow. “Why not, I don’t know, the armouries, or the barracks, or the granaries?”
bs: — Zašto je povjerenik uopće toliko zainteresiran za banke? promrmlja Talou. — Zašto ne, ne znam, oružarnice, ili vojarne, ili žitnice?

en: “Well…” He glanced about nervously, but no one fell over themselves to take responsibility. “I suppose I am the longest serving member of staff on site. I am Ario Matterno, senior over-clerk for loans—”
bs: — Pa…, nervozno je pogledao oko sebe, no nitko se nije otimao za preuzimanje odgovornosti. — Pretpostavljam da sam ja najdugovječniji član osoblja na lokaciji. Ja sam Ario Matterno, viši nadčinovnik za kredite…

en: “Have you been outside lately? Wisdom is not at a premium, madness is the fashion, the balance sheets are all torn up and the friends that were assets have become liabilities.” Vick kept walking. “Threats for tomorrow don’t cut very deep when today is so damn threatening. You might want to keep ’em to yourself.”
bs: — Jeste li bili vani u posljednje vrijeme? Razum nije na cijeni, ludilo je u modi, bilance su poderane, a prijatelji koji su bili imovina postali su obveze. Vik je nastavila hodati. — Prijetnje za sutra ne bole previše kada je današnjica tako prokleto prijeteća. Možda bi bilo bolje da ih zadržite za sebe.

en: Matterno swallowed, and slipped a key from his pocket, and offered it out. A very long, thin, delicate key for such an immensity of door, wards so complex they looked like a tiny maze. “I only have one. You need the other.”
bs: Matterno je progutao knedlu, izvukao ključ iz džepa i pružio ga. Bio je to vrlo dugačak, tanak i nježan ključ za takvu masivnost vrata, s mehanizmom toliko složenim da je izgledao poput sićušnog labirinta. — Imam samo jedan. Treba vam drugi.

en: There had been votes in the districts of Adua, apparently. Votes from every Midderland-born man, no matter how mean and ignorant, resulting in a body of representatives, as far as Orso could tell, every bit as mean and ignorant as they were. Votes. He could only imagine his mother’s reaction to that. The tyranny of the majority. Representatives would be elected in other cities of the Union in due course, but those benches were still empty while the Assembly argued over the rules. They argued eve
bs: U okruzima Adua navodno su se održali izbori. Glasovi svakog muškarca rođenog u Miderlandu, ma koliko prost i neuk bio, rezultirali su tijelom predstavnika koje je, koliko je Orso mogao zaključiti, bilo jednako prosto i neuko kao i oni sami. Glasovi. Mogao je samo zamisliti majčinu reakciju na to. Tiranija većine. Predstavnici će se s vremenom izabrati i u drugim gradovima Unije, no te su klupe još uvijek bile prazne dok se Vijeće prepirala oko pravila. Svađali su se čak i više nego što je to či

en: It would have helped at least a little if all the old denizens of the Open Council had lost their places in the Great Change, but a smattering of Orso’s worst enemies had managed to cling to their seats. Lord Isher had slithered from hiding, Lord Heugen had slipped out of prison and the Young Lion sat in the front row along with several other surviving aristocratic rebels. Those few noblemen who had stayed loyal to the Crown were languishing in cells beneath the House of Truth. The world was tur
bs: Bilo bi barem malo lakše da su svi stari stanovnici Otvorenog Vijeća izgubili svoja mjesta u Velikoj promjeni, ali nekolicina Orsovih najgorih neprijatelja uspjela se održati na svojim položajima. Lord Išer se izmigoljio iz skrovišta, lord Heugen se iskrao iz zatvora, a Juvens Lav sjedio je prvenstveno zajedno s još nekoliko preživjelih aristokratskih pobunjenika. Oni rijetki plemići koji su ostali vjerni Kruni čamili su u ćelijama ispod Kuće istine. Svijet se uistinu okrenuo naglavačke. Izdajni

en: There was the scrape of a nib crossing out. “Thorny, isn’t it, once you start drafting? Not at all like fiction.”
bs: Začulo se struganje pera koje precrtava. — Nezgodno, zar ne, jednom kad počneš pisati nacrt? Nimalo nalik fikciji.

en: His eyes met Corporal Tunny’s for a moment, slumped upon a bench towards the back. It hurt Orso more than it should have, to see his old standard-bearer seated among his enemies. But one can hardly expect paid hangers-on to keep hanging on after the pay dries up, and it could not be denied that no one better represented the faithlessness, degradation and low character of the commons than Corporal Tunny.
bs: Oko mu se na trenutak susreo s pogledom desnika Tunnyja, koji se slomljeno izvalio na klupi pri dnu. Orsa je to pogodilo više nego što je trebalo, vidjeti svog starog barjaktara kako sjedi među neprijateljima. No jedva da se moglo očekivati od plaćenih parazita da nastave visjeti nakon što presuše isplate, a nije se moglo poreći da nitko bolje nije predstavljao nevjeru, posrtanje i niski karakter pukih masa od desnika Tunnyja.

en: Leo got as near a smile as he could. A skull’s rictus. “Fine.” He’d never been much of a liar, but this must’ve been one of his very worst.
bs: Leo se nasmiješio koliko je mogao. Lubanjin grč. — Dobro sam." Nikada nije bio vješt lažljivac, no ovo je morala biti jedna od njegovih najgorih izvedbi.

en: Isher sprang up. The man could move fast, when he wanted to. Scurrying from the Battle of Stoffenbeck, for instance. Or scurrying back, once he saw something to gain.
bs: Išer skoči na noge. Taj se čovjek mogao brzo kretati kad je htio. Bježeći iz bitke kod Štopenbeka, primjerice. Ili vraćajući se, čim bi vidio priliku za dobitak.

en: The thought of standing terrified him, but there must still have been some stubborn remnant of the Young Lion, hidden deep inside. Better to do it, than live with the fear of it, the Dogman used to say. Leo might have lost a leg and an arm, but he’d show these bastards he still had his heart.
bs: Sama pomisao na ustajanje ispunjavala ga je užasom, no negdje duboko u njemu morala je još postojati Steadfast ostatak Mladog Lava. Bolje to učiniti nego živjeti u strahu od toga, znao je govoriti Pas Covjek Čovjek. Leo je možda izgubio nogu i ruku, ali pokazat će ovim gadovima da još ima srce.

en: “Walls… won’t protect us now, only unity!” By the dead, the hall was swimming. “Those who’ve enjoyed great privileges must make great sacrifices.” They needed some noble gesture. He bared his teeth. “So I give up the ‘dan’ in my name! I renounce it! I cut it out! We must all… be equal.”
bs: — Tell… nas sada neće zaštititi, samo jedinstvo! Tako mu mrtvih, dvorana mu se vrtjela pred očima. — Oni koji su uživali velike povlastice moraju podnijeti velike žrtve. Trebala im je neka plemenita gesta. Ogoli zube. — Stoga se odričem 'dan' u svom imenu! Odričem ga se! Izrezujem ga! Svi moramo… biti jednaki.

en: More cheering. One more hopping, lurching step and Leo collapsed onto the front bench. Isher caught him under the arm, clapped him on the back, waving to the public gallery.
bs: Još klicanja. Još jedan poskakujući, teturavi korak i Leo se srušio na prednju klupu. Išer ga je uhvatio pod ruku, potapšao po leđima i mahnuo javnoj galeriji.

en: Broad thought of Valbeck. The streets strewn with rubbish. The mobs and the fires. Wallpaper being boiled for soup. “Folk want bread,” he said. “Then safety. Then shelter. Freedom’s far down the list, and principles far behind that.”
bs: Brod je mislio na Valbek. Ulice zatrpane smećem. Svjetina i požari. Tapete koje se kuhaju za juhu. — Folk želi kruha, reče. — Zatim sigurnost. Potom krov nad glavom. Sloboda je nisko na popisu, a načela još niže.

en: Broad winced. Everyone was furious all the time. Everyone looking for someone to blame. Everything teetering on the brink of violence. He felt like he had in Styria, in the war. A clenched fist, itching to strike. And the worst thing about it—he wasn’t sure he didn’t like the feeling.
bs: Brod se trzne. Svi su bili bijesni cijelo vrijeme. Svatko je tražio nekoga za okriviti. Sve je visjelo na rubu nasilja. Osjećao se kao u Stiriji, u ratu. Stisnuta šaka koja svrbi da udari. A najgore od svega — nije bio siguran da mu se taj osjećaj ne sviđa.

en: As the old man dropped spent into his seat, the rest of the Representatives were rising to applaud their Chairman. They did that a lot. Broad clenched his fists tighter and glanced towards Judge, flopped loose in her chair with her head resting on the back, scratching gently at her stretched-out throat. With something stuck between horror and excitement, he realised she was looking right back at him.
bs: Dok je starac iscrpljeno utonuo u svoje sjedalo, ostatak zastupnika ustao je kako bi zapljeskao svom predsjedavajućem. Činili su to često. Brod je stisnuo šake i bacio Oko prema Džadž, koja je opušteno klonula u stolici s glavom naslonjenom na naslon, nježno se češući po ispruženom vratu. Uz osjećaj negdje između užasa i uzbuđenja, shvatio je da ona gleda ravno u njega.

en: That got a murmur from the Assembly, and from the gallery, too. Broad raised a brow at Brint. The general could only shrug. Not much would’ve surprised any of them now. If a dragon had risen from the benches, it would likely have been calmly dismissed on a point of order.
bs: To je izazvalo žamor u skupštini, kao i na galeriji. Brod je podigao obrvu prema Brintu. General je samo slegnuo ramenima. Malo toga bi ih sada moglo iznenaditi. Da se Zmija uzdigao iz klupa, vjerojatno bi ga mirno otpravili pozivanjem na poslovnik.

en: who will save us from Bayaz?” More laughter, and more anger, and Risinau flashed that prim little smile. “General Brint, could you see our visitor out? The age of wizards is over, Master Sulfur. An age of reason has dawned!”
bs: Tko će nas spasiti od Bajaza?" Još smijeha i još gnjeva, a Risinau uputi onaj svoj ukočeni mali osmijeh. — Generale Brint, možete li ispratiti našeg posjetitelja van? Doba čarobnjaka je završeno, Majstore Salfur. Svanulo je doba razuma!

en: “Of course not, I apologise. The times take some adjusting to.” He spoke in the blandest of drones. As if they were discussing the weather and he by no means had his fingers in her quim. “You can push if you feel the need—”
bs: — da ne, ispričavam se. Na ova se vremena treba naviknuti. Govorio je najbezličnijim mogućim tonom. Kao da razgovaraju o vremenu, a ne kao da mu se prsti nalaze u njezinu međunožju. — Možete tiskati ako osjetite potrebu…

en: People came and went. Barged in with water, with cloths, with muttered messages. Naked on her hands and knees with her arse in the air, honking like a sow, she barely even cared. If anything she was grateful for the waft of breeze when the door opened.
bs: Folk su dolazili i odlazili. Upadali su s vodom, s krpama, s promrmljanim porukama. Gola na rukama i koljenima, s guzicom u zraku, ričući poput krmače, jedva da joj je bilo stalo. Štoviše, bila je zahvalna na dašku vjetra kad bi se vrata otvorila.

en: She screamed again. She screamed her face off. She screamed her guts out. She screamed as if she was being murdered. She felt as if she was being murdered. A stinging, burning, ripping to add to all the rest and she ran out of breath, her scream dying off into a wheezing groan as she felt something slither out.
bs: Vrisnula je ponovno. Vrisnula je iz sveg glasa. Vrisnula je iz petnih žila. Vrisnula je kao da je ubijaju. Činilo joj se kao da je ubijaju. Žarenje, Veliko Gorenje, deranje koje se pridružilo svemu ostalom i ostala je bez daha, a njezin je vrisak zamro u hropcu kad je osjetila kako nešto klizi van.

en: There was the odd absence, of course, among her circle. Those with particularly bad relations with their workers, or those with particularly bad luck. She heard the most appalling stories. Such-and-such was found drowned in the canal, by the way. And what’s-his-face knifed and stripped in a sewer, did you hear? She pretended they were nothing more than stories. She pretended she could not recall the faces of those people, laughing at some function before the Great Change.
bs: Bilo je tu, neobičnih izostanaka u njezinu krugu. Onih koji su imali osobito loše odnose sa svojim radnicima ili onih koje je pratila iznimno loša sreća. Čula je najstrašnije priče. Onaj-i-onaj je, usput rečeno, pronađen utopljen u kanalu. A onaj-drugi izboden i oguljen u kanalizaciji, jesi li čula? Pretvarala se da su to tek priče. Pretvarala se da se ne može sjetiti se lica tih Folk, koji su se smijali na nekom prijemu prije Velike promjene.

en: Savine had been drifting on the edge of sleep. Lamplight sparkled in her wet eyes as she opened them. Zuri stood over her, offering something out. A clean white bundle, carefully wrapped, like a present. A white bundle with a tiny, squashed-in face.
bs: Savine je lebdjela na rubu sna. Svjetlost svjetiljke zaiskrila joj je u vlažnim očima dok ih je otvarala. Zuri je stajala iznad nje, pružajući joj nešto. Čist bijeli zavežljaj, pažljivo umotan, poput dara. Bijeli zavežljaj s malenim, zgnječenim licem.

en: They all say, Yours will seem beautiful, of course. In a smugly knowing way, as if shitting out a child comes with secret knowledge, like joining the Order of Magi. They all say it, but you tell yourself the poor things are just trying to wring some shred of advantage from the curse of parenthood and let them have their self-delusion.
bs: Svi kažu: Tvoje će ti se činiti prekrasnim. Na onaj samozadovoljan, sveznajući način, kao da sranje djeteta dolazi s tajnim znanjem, poput pristupanja redu Magi. Svi to govore, ali čovjek sam sebi kaže da jadnici samo pokušavaju izvući kakvu-takvu korist iz prokletstva roditeljstva, pa im dopusti da žive u zabludi.

en: “We have a son— Ah!” She gritted her teeth at a sudden, stabbing pain through her stomach, down into her legs. “Ah!” And another, even worse, that made her jerk up.
bs: "Mi imamo sina… Ah!" Stisnula je zube zbog iznenadne, probadajuće boli kroz trbuh, sve do nogu. — Ah!" I još jedne, još gore, koja ju je natjerala da se trzne.

en: As a child, Orso had delighted in the sound of distant crowds. Crowds meant spectacles, festivals, excitement: the thrill of the Summer Contest, the pomp of a parade. As a young man, he had begun to find that noise tiresome. Crowds meant functions, rituals, responsibilities: the disappointment of grand banquets, the tedium of state visits. Now the sound of a crowd filled him with horror. In the new Union, crowds meant riots, terror, random violence. The baying of the mob.
bs: Kao dijete, Orso je uživao u zvuku udaljene svjetine. Svjetina je značila spektakle, festivale, uzbuđenje: ushit Ljetnog natjecanja, raskoš povorke. Kao mladić, taj mu je žamor počeo ići na živce. Svjetina je značila dužnosti, rituale, odgovornosti: razočaranje raskošnih banketa, dosadu državničkih posjeta. Sada ga je zvuk mase ispunjavao užasom. U novoj Unija, svjetina je značila nerede, teror, nasumično nasilje. Urlikanje rulje.

en: There was a clatter of machinery, weights dropped, cable whizzed and the dummy was jerked up by the neck to flop about in the wind some five strides above the platform. The crowd gasped, then began to applaud, to cheer, to hurl good-natured abuse. A carnival atmosphere. Orso winced and tried to loosen his collar with a finger.
bs: Začulo se zveckanje mehanizma, utezi su pali, sajla je zazviždala i lutka je trzajem povučena za vrat, da bi se zatim njihala na vjetru nekih pet koraka iznad platforme. Svjetina je udahnula, a zatim počela pljeskati, klicati, dobacivati dobronamjerne uvrede. Karnevalski ugođaj. Orso se zgrozio i pokušao prstom olabaviti ovratnik.

en: “Fellow Citizens!” Risinau never missed a chance to address a crowd. “We are gathered to see five enemies of the people receive their just deserts. To see righteous retribution on behalf of the Union’s oppressed. To wave farewell to the age of tyranny.” He spread his arms wide. “And to welcome the age of equality with open arms!”
bs: — Dragi građani! Risinau nikada nije propuštao priliku obratiti se mnoštvu. — Okupili smo se kako bismo vidjeli kako petero narodnih neprijatelja dobiva zasluženu kaznu. Kako bismo svjedočili pravednoj odmazdi u ime potlačenih u Uniji. Kako bismo mahnuli za zbogom dobu tiranije. Raširi ruke. — I kako bismo raširenih ruku pozdravili doba jednakosti!

en: “It’s me who should be sorry!” Orso rounded on Judge, Risinau and Pike. “Please! What crime are they accused of?”
bs: — Ja bih se trebao ispričati! Orso se okrenu prema Džadž, Risinauu i Pajku. — Molim vas! Za koji se zločin terete?

en: Risinau held up a hand to quiet her, his hard little eyes fixed on Orso. “If the king cannot remain silent while the People’s Justice is administered, he will have to be restrained. Captain Broad?”
bs: Risinau podigne ruku da je ušutka, a njegove tvrde, sitne oči bile su prikovane za Orsa. — Ako kralj ne može ostati tih dok se provodi Narodna pravda, morat ćemo ga obuzdati. Kapetane Brod?

en: Judge snapped her fingers again. Gorodets gave a whoop as he was whisked into the air. Pike watched his one-time colleagues dangle, emotionless, eyes glittering.
bs: Džadž ponovno pucne prstima. Gorodets uzvikne od uzbuđenja dok ga zavitlaše u zrak. Pajk je bez emocija, sjajnih očiju, promatrao kako njegovi nekadašnji kolege vise.

en: “Oh,” said Hildi, in a high little voice. Because she was so clever and so tough, Orso forgot, sometimes, how young she was. He wanted to put his hand over her eyes. He wanted to put his hand over his own. But it was far too late.
bs: — O, rekla je Hildi tankim, dječjim glasom. Budući da je bila tako pametna i tako čvrsta, Orso je katkad zaboravljao koliko je mlada. Htio joj je prekriti oči rukom. Htio je prekriti i svoje. No bilo je odveć kasno.

en: Corleth strode through the crowd ahead, down the rain-slick cobbled streets that led from Skarling’s Hall into the chilly city, a canvas bag over one shoulder.
bs: Corleth je koračala naprijed kroz gomilu, niz popločane ulice klizave od kiše koje su vodile iz Skarlingove dvorane u prohladan grad, s platnenom torbom prebačenom preko jednog ramena.

en: “She don’t look all that furtive.” Wasn’t like she was padding on tiptoe, or sliding around corners, or checking behind her, the way Rikke would surely have done if she was about some shifty business. “She’s just walking through town.”
bs: — Ne izgleda baš nešto kradomice. Nije baš koračala na prstima, niti se provlačila iza uglova, niti osvrtala za sobom onako kako bi Rike zasigurno činila da smjera nešto mutno. — Jednostavno hoda kroz grad.

en: But Isern was already thumping at the rickety door hard enough to rattle it in the frame. It whipped open and Corleth frowned out, somewhat suspicious to see the two of them crowded onto the doorstep. “What are you two doing here?”
bs: No Izern je već udarala po klimavim vratima dovoljno snažno da zazveče u okviru. Vrata su se naglo otvorila, a Corleth ih je sumnjičavo pogledala vidjevši ih kako se guraju na pragu. — Što vas dvije radite ovdje?

en: “My grandma lives here,” muttered Corleth, rubbing at her pink neck as Isern let her go. “I come see her when I can. Make sure she’s got wood for her fire. Bring her scraps for soup.”
bs: — Moja baka živi ovdje, promrmlja Corleth, trljajući ružičasti vrat dok ju je Izern pustila. — Dođem je vidjeti kad god mogu. Pobrinem se da ima drva za vatru. Donosim joj ostatke za juhu.

en: “All right, Granny,” said Corleth, waving her down. “We have to be watchful, it’s true. Just a misunderstanding, is all.”
bs: — U redu je, bakice, reče Corleth, mašući joj da se smiri. — Moramo biti na oprezu, istina je. Samo nesporazum, ništa više.

en: “No, I mean, she’s solid. Steady. Not likely to suddenly catch fire.” Rikke raised a brow at Isern. “Unlike some I could mention.”
bs: — Ne, mislim, ona je stabilna. Postojana. Nije vjerojatno da će se iznenada zapaliti. Rike podigne obrvu prema Izern. — Za razliku od nekih koje bih mogla spomenuti.

en: “That there is quite a story.” Trapper’s men were poking around, but not too carefully. It was chilly, and they were drifting over to the warmth, and that homely smell of cooking meat. “Sailed to Midderland with the Great Wolf and the Young Lion, felt seasick on the way over, got caught in a storm, fought a battle, lost, felt seasick on the way back.” They’d gathered about the other side of the fire, now, off guard. “Then Tricky Rikke sent me down here to have a word with you lot. Some doubts ov
bs: — To je prilična priča. Zamkačevi su Folk njuškali okolo, ali ne odveć oprezno. Bilo je prohladno, pa su se privlačili k toplini i onom domaćem mirisu pečenog mesa. — Otplovio sam u Miderland s Velikim Vukom i Mladićem Lavom, patio od morske bolesti putem, upao u oluju, vodio bitku, izgubio, patio od morske bolesti na povratku. Sad su se skupili nasuprot tome vatre, nespremni, opušteni. — Onda me lukava Rike poslala ovamo da popričam s vama. izgleda da postoje neke nedoumice oko toga gdje točno

en: “Fuck!” someone shouted. The old boy with the grey beard whirled about, axe all over the place. One of the others had to dodge it, nearly fell, stumbled back and kicked a shower of sparks from the fire. Trapper drew his sword. Another in a lambskin cloak took off running like a hare at a handclap. Total shambles.
bs: — U pičku materinu!, viknu netko. Starac s prosijedom bradom se okrenuo, mahnito vitlajući sjekirom. Jedan mu se morao izmaknuti, umalo je pao, oteturao se unatrag i nogom razbacao užarene Sparks iz vatre. Zamkač izvuče mač. Drugi, ogrnut u janjeću kožu, pobježe glavom bez obzira poput zeca na pljesak ruku. Čisti kaos.

en: “We see.” Trapper lowered his sword and dug it point-first into the ground. With bad grace the others swung bows from backs, pulled out axes and knives, set down spears, till there was quite a little armoury heaped up in front of the farmhouse.
bs: — Vidimo. Zamkač spusti mač i zabode ga vrhom u zemlju. S nelagodom su ostali skinuli lukove s leđa, izvukli sjekire i noževe, odložili koplja sve dok se Naprijed seoske kuće nije nagomilala prava mala oružarnica.

en: There was a sharp crack as Downside buried his axe in the man’s head and dragged him over backwards. His leg kicked so hard he kicked his boot off and it went flying high in the air, onto the roof of the barn, and that was the last move he made.
bs: Odjeknu Trdak prasak kad Dausaid zabije svoju sjekiru čovjeku u glavu i povuče ga unatrag. Noga mu se toliko trznula da je izuo čizmu koja poleti visoko u zrak, na krov štale, i to mu bijaše posljednji pokret.

en: Downside shrugged. “Sorry, Chief. Had the feel of a feud brewing, and it’s always best to settle a feud at the outset, rather’n let it fester.”
bs: Dausaid slegnu ramenima. — Oprosti, Šefe. Namirisao sam da se sprema krvna osveta, a krvnu je osvetu uvijek najbolje zatomiti na samom početku nego pustiti da se gnoji.

en: When he turned on Stour, he’d had no doubt it was the right choice. For his own sake, for Wonderful’s sake, for everyone’s sake. But he’d been sure Rikke would kill the bastard. Then she hadn’t, and he started to worry she might be too soft for the job. Siding with the winner is forever sensible, of course. The trouble starts when you’re not sure who the winner might be. Quite the pickle.
bs: Kada se okrenuo protiv Staura, nije sumnjao da je to ispravan izbor. Radi sebe, radi Vonderful, radi svih. Ali bio je siguran da će Rike ubiti tog gada. Kad ono nije, počeo se brinuti da je možda previše mekana za taj posao. Stajati uz pobjednika uvijek je razumno. Nevolja počinje kada nisi siguran tko bi pobjednik mogao biti. Prava zavrzlama.

en: “I’m saying no,” said Clover, firmly as he could without raising his voice. “It’s not a negotiation. No exceptions. It’s a no.”
bs: — Kažem ne, reče Klover, najodlučnije što je mogao a da ne povisi glas. — Ovo nije pregovaranje. Nema iznimaka. Odgovor je ne.

en: “Consequences. Which one do you think? There?” Clover shook his head. “By the dead, boy, you are dense as a stump.”
bs: — Posljedice. Koja bi druga bila? Ona? Klover odmahne glavom. — Mrtvih mi, momče, tupav si kao panj.

en: “I won’t just sit crying over lost glories. The future of the Union will be decided in the Assembly.” He looked at Savine in the mirror, propped up on the chaise in a mass of pale skirts with one of the babies to her breast and the other asleep beside her. He still couldn’t tell which of them was which.
bs: — Neću samo sjediti i plakati nad izgubljenom slavom. Budućnost Unije odlučivat će se u Skupštini. Pogledala je Savine u zrcalu; izležavala se na ležaljci okružena masom blijedih suknji, držeći jednu od beba na prsima dok je druga spavala pored nje. Još uvijek nije mogao razaznati koja je koja.

en: “We made mistakes.” He saw her swallow, and frown down at the floor. “We made terrible mistakes. But our marriage makes more sense than ever.”
bs: — Pravili smo pogreške. Vidio ju je kako je progutala knedlu i namršteno spustila Oko prema podu. — Pravili smo strašne pogreške. Ali naš brak ima više smisla nego ikad prije.

en: “The people still admire me. We can use that.” Being bounced on the shoulders of that mob outside the House of Questions hadn’t been pleasant. But a lot better than being torn to pieces by them. “That and my place on the Assembly.” Leo tried to force his scarred mouth into the easy-going smile he used to have, the one he’d worn when King Jezal handed him that badly balanced commemorative sword, but that felt like a thousand years ago. There was still a trace of the Young Lion there, if he tried.
bs: — Folk mi se još uvijek divi. To možemo iskoristiti. Biti nošen na ramenima one rulje Naprijed Kuće pitanja nije bilo nimalo ugodno, ali bilo je mnogo bolje nego biti rastrgan na komade. — To, i moje mjesto u Skupštini. Leo je pokušao izobličiti svoje ožiljcima prekriveno lice u onaj opušteni osmijeh koji je nekad imao, onaj koji je nosio kad mu je kralj Džezal uručio onaj loše izbalansirani svečani mač, no to se činilo kao prije tisuću godina. Još je uvijek bilo traga Mladog Lava, ako bi se pot

en: “You’re right.” Leo took a long breath and pressed the anger down. He couldn’t let himself be swept off by whatever emotion blew his way. “What about your man Broad? He’s close with the Breakers. A captain in the People’s Army.”
bs: — U pravu si. Leo je duboko udahnuo i potisnuo bijes. Nije si smio dopustiti da ga ponese bilo koja emocija koja bi ga zapljusnula. — Što je s tvojim čovjekom Brodom? Blizak je s Lomljačima. Kapetan u Narodnoj vojsci.

en: “I’ve always paid my debts. That’s just good business.” She frowned at him, the scar on her forehead puckering, and held her baby tight. Their baby. Whichever one it was. “Since we are being unsentimental, the Broads are not the only useful people left in Angland. What about your old friends Glaward and Jurand?”
bs: — Oduvijek sam plaćala svoje dugove. To je jednostavno dobar posao. Namrštila se na njega, ožiljak na čelu joj se naborao, i čvrsto privila dijete uz sebe. Njihovo dijete. Koje god od njih bilo. — Kad smo već kod nesentimentalnosti, obitelj Brod nisu jedini korisni Folk preostali u Englendu. Što je s tvojim starim prijateljima Glavardom i Džurandom?

en: “I caught them fucking,” he said, trying to sound like he hardly cared, even if his heart was pounding. “In Sipani.”
bs: — Uhvatio sam ih kako se jebu, rekao je, pokušavajući zvučati kao da ga se to jedva tiče, iako mu je srce lupalo. — U Sipani.

en: That memory bubbled to the surface again, but it was Leo’s hair Jurand’s long fingers were tangled in, and Leo’s ear he was biting at, whispering at, and Leo’s legs he was reaching down between…
bs: Sjećanje ponovno ispliva na površinu, no to su bile Leove vlasi u koje su se upleli Džurandovi dugi prsti, i Leovo uho koje je grickao, kojem je šaptao, i Leove noge između kojih je posezao…

en: There was a green space outside the Agriont where they’d taken to dumping the old statues. Noseless, handless, legless lords and ladies who’d once presided over palaces now ruled over a stretch of patchy grass that smelled of the rotting water-weed in the bottom of the drained moat. Here or there some monstrous remnant from the famous statues on the Kingsway loomed over the rest. A towering hand. A mighty boot. Half a majestic sneer.
bs: Izvan Agrionta nalazila se zelena površina kamo su odvozili stare kipove. Bez nosa, bez ruku, bez nogu, Lords i dame koji su nekoć stolovali u palačama sada su vladali prostranstvom kržljave trave što je zaudarala na truli vodeni korov s dna isušena opkopa. Tu i tamo, neki bi se nakazni ostatak slavnih kipova s Kingswaya nadvio nad ostalima. Ruka koja se uzdizala u nebo. Moćna čizma. Polovica veličanstvenog podsmjeha.

en: “I’m the one who’s honoured,” said Leo, matching lie for lie. “To be given a seat on the Assembly. A place in your great endeavour.”
bs: — Ja sam taj koji je počašćen, reče Leo, uzvraćajući laž na laž. — Dobiti mjesto u Skupštini. Mjesto u vašem velikom pothvatu.

en: “She certainly would.” Leo smiled as he imagined her kicking him in the face for his fucking cheek. “Fatherhood has made me think about the world I’ll leave to my children. The truth is… I’m worried about Angland.”
bs: — bi. Leo se nasmiješio zamišljajući kako ga udara nogom u lice zbog njegove jebene drskosti. — Očinstvo me natjeralo da razmišljam o svijetu koji ću ostaviti svojoj djeci. Istina je… zabrinut sam za Englend.

en: “I have to try. Let me write to my mother. Assure her of your good intentions. Assure her that I, and my wife, and her grandchildren, are here as willing believers in your cause.” Leo winced as he leaned hard on his cane and stood, so he could speak as one friend to another. “Let me bring like-minded men to represent the province in the Assembly. Trustworthy men. Blunt men. Men who can see first-hand the merit of the changes you’re making. The changes we’re making. Men who can support us, and ar
bs: — Moram pokušati. Dopustite mi pisati majci. Da je uvjerim u vaše dobre namjere. Da je uvjerim da sam ja, kao i moja supruga te njezini unuci, ovdje kao voljni vjernici u vaš cilj. Leo se zgrčio dok se teško oslonio na Sticks i ustao kako bi mogao govoriti kao prijatelj prijatelju. — Dopustite mi dovesti istomišljenike koji će predstavljati provinciju u Skupštini. Pouzdane ljude. Izravne ljude. Ljude koji mogu iz prve ruke vidjeti vrijednost promjena koje uvodite. Promjena koje mi uvodimo. Ljude

en: “Such insight.” Risinau looked at him with something close to admiration. “Such insight! Write your letters, Citizen Brock! I will see them delivered. We will stride into the new future together!” He slapped Leo on the shoulder as he turned away and strode off with his guards following.
bs: — Kakva pronicljivost. Risinau ga pogleda s nečim što je nalikovalo divljenju."Kakva pronicljivost! Piši svoja pisma, građanine Brok! Ja ću se pobrinuti da budu dostavljena. Zajedno ćemo zakoračiti u novu budućnost!" Potapšao je Lea po ramenu dok se okretao i odmarširao u pratnji svojih stražara.

en: “They’re the only kind I get.” Broad wiped his lenses, then hooked them carefully back over his ears. “But no worse’n I deserve, I guess.”
bs: — To su jedine okolnosti koje dobivam. Brod je obrisao naočale, a zatim ih pažljivo zakvačio natrag iza ušiju. — Ali valjda ne gore nego što zaslužujem.

en: Hard to say exactly what they were angry about. No doubt they all had their own recipe. Price of bread. Price of housing. Price of fuel as the weather got colder. Wages too low, hours too high, too many laws or too few. Pike had taught them a lesson—if enough people got angry enough, they could change things. Now anger was the answer to everything.
bs: Teško je bilo reći zbog čega su točno bili bijesni. Nema sumnje da je svatko imao svoj razlog. Cijena kruha. Cijena stanovanja. Cijena goriva kako je vrijeme postajalo hladniejsze. Nadnice preniske, radni sati predugi, zakona previše ili premalo. Pajk ih je naučio lekciju — ako se dovoljno Folk dovoljno razljuti, mogu promijeniti stvari. Sada je bijes bio odgovor na sve.

en: “I’m Chief Inspector Teufel!” called Vick. “Commissioner Pike sent me. The Weaver himself, you hear?” Some muttering at that, but none of the scowls went away. Vick clenched her teeth and took a hard breath. “Look, I get it! You’re disappointed! You’re frustrated! Let’s face it, you’re fucking furious! Believe me, so am I.”
bs: — Ja sam šefica inspektorica Tojfel! pozva Vik. — Povjerenik Pajk me poslao. Sam Weaver, razumijete li? Začulo se mrmljanje na to, ali nijedan se mrki Oko nije razvedrio. Vik stisnu zube i duboko udahne. — Slušajte, razumijem! Razočarani ste! Frustrirani ste! Budimo Sparks, jebeno ste bijesni! Vjerujte mi, i ja sam.

en: Something came spinning from the crowd, missed her by a stride and clonked from the shield of one of Broad’s men. They almost charged then. She could feel their fury, harder to hold in than to release, like dogs straining at the leash, but Vick held up a trembling hand, giving it one last go, preaching patience while she fast ran out of it.
bs: Nešto doleti iz gomile, promaši je za korak i odskoči od štita jednog od Brodovih Folk. Umalo su jurnuli u tom trenutku. Osjećala je njihovu jarost, koju je bilo teže suzdržati nego pustiti s lanca, poput pasa koji zatežu povodac, ali Vik podiže drhtavu ruku, dajući svemu još posljednju šansu, propovijedajući strpljenje dok joj je ono rapidno ponestajalo.

en: When the mob broke into the Agriont, they’d ransacked her mean little set of rooms. They’d taken what there was to take, which wasn’t much, smashed what there was to smash, which wasn’t much more, and left that ridiculous book Sibalt used to love torn on the floor. It had made her oddly furious.
bs: Kad je rulja provalila u Agriont, opustošili su joj jadne malene odaje. Uzeli su što se moglo uzeti, a toga nije bilo mnogo, razbili su što se moglo razbiti, a ni toga nije bilo mnogo više, te ostavili onu smiješnu knjigu koju je Sibalt volio rastrganu na podu. To ju je neobično razbjesnilo.

en: The anger could whip up in no time. But it could leak away just as fast. Those who weren’t running were a sorry sight now. All hanging heads and wobbly lips, like children caught talking after bedtime.
bs: Bijes se mogao rasplamsati u tren oka, ali mogao je isto tako brzo i splasnuti. Oni koji nisu bježali sada su bili jadan prizor – obješenih Šef i drhtavih usana, poput djece uhvaćene u razgovoru nakon vremena za spavanje.

en: “Don’t tell me,” said Vick as he peered at the ill-printed pages through his lenses. “The Great Change didn’t solve every problem, so the answer must be more of it.”
bs: — Nemoj mi ni govoriti, rekla je Vik dok je on kroz leće proučavao loše otisnute stranice. — Velika promjena nije riješila baš svaki Trobli, pa odgovor mora biti još više iste takve.

en: “A mob hanged two coal merchants the other day. They were already selling as cheap as they could. Prices are higher than before the Great Change. Higher than they’ve ever been. Folk broke into a shop, paid what they thought was fair. Then someone said they were profiteers. So they hanged ’em. Then they marched up the street to the flour merchant.”
bs: — Svjetina je neki dan objesila dvojicu trgovaca ugljenom. Prodavali su robu po najnižoj mogućoj cijeni. Cijene su više nego prije Velike promjene. Više nego ikada. Folk je provalio u trgovinu, platili su onoliko koliko su smatrali poštenim. A onda je netko rekao da su profiteri. Pa su ih objesili. Zatim su marširali ulicom do trgovca brašnom.

en: “We’re talking about dead shopkeepers. Not teeth. There are parts of the city we don’t go into at night. There are parts of the city we have to ask the Burners’ permission to go into at all.”
bs: — Govorimo o mrtvim trgovcima. Ne o zubima. Postoje dijelovi grada u koje noću ne zalazimo. Postoje dijelovi grada u koje moramo tražiti dopuštenje Palitelja da uopće uđemo.

en: She knew she couldn’t say what she was starting to think—that the Great Change was in danger of becoming a change for the greatly worse and that King Orso was beginning to look a paragon of leadership. She settled for second best. Or for second least worst, maybe. “You’re the Weaver. You started this.”
bs: Znala je da ne može reći ono što je tek počinjala misliti — da je Great Change opasno klizio prema promjeni na gore i da je kralj Orso u usporedbi s njime počeo izgledati poput uzora vodstva. Zadovoljila se drugim najboljim. Ili možda drugim najmanje lošim. — Ti si Weaver. Ti si ovo pokrenuo.

en: She smiled down at Ardee, fast asleep in her cot. She could watch them sleep for hours. Sit holding them for hours. Kiss the dark fuzz on their heads, over and over, and be delighted by the feeling every time. The smell of them. The softness of them. The unformed innocence of—
bs: Nasmiješila se gledajući Ardi, koja je čvrsto spavala u kolijevci. Mogla ih je satima gledati kako spavaju. Satima sjediti držeći ih. Iznova ljubiti tamne dlačice na njihovim glavicama i svaki put osjetiti ushit. Njihov miris. Njihovu mekoću. Neoblikovanu nevinost…

en: Savine felt a flood of relief as Zuri pushed the door wide to reveal her two brothers. The Great Change did not appear to have changed them, at least. Haroon was as solid and serious, and Rabik as smooth-faced and smiling, as ever.
bs: Savine obli val olakšanja kad Zuri širom otvori vrata i otkri njezinu dvojicu braće. Velika promjena ih, barem naizgled, nije promijenila. Harun bijaše jednako čvrst i ozbiljan, a Rabik jednako vedra lica i nasmiješen kao i uvijek.

en: “And you believe that?” Her voice sounded needy. With no beliefs of her own, she wanted at least to believe in someone else’s.
bs: — I ti u to vjeruješ? Glas joj je zvučao očajnički. Bez vlastitih uvjerenja, željela je barem vjerovati u tuđa.

en: “Lady Savine!” Kort had prospered, that was clear. His clothes were simply cut, of course, since simplicity was the fashion, but she knew expensive cloth when she saw it, and the broken-chain pin he wore to show allegiance with the common man was set with little diamonds.
bs: — Lady Savine! Kort se dobro snašao, to je bilo očito. Odjeća mu je bila jednostavno krojena, budući da je jednostavnost bila u modi, ali ona je znala prepoznati skupocjenu tkaninu kad bi je vidjela, a igla u obliku slomljenog lanca koju je nosio u znak solidarnosti s običnim čovjekom bila je ukrašena sitnim dijamantima.

en: “Yet I’ve never seen him absent from the Assembly, rain or shine. He proves to be a fine speaker.” Kort smiled beneficently down. “And this is?”
bs: — Pa ipak, nikad ga nisam vidio izostati sa Skupštine, ni po kiši ni po suncu. Pokazuje se izvrsnim govornikom. Kort se blagonaklono osmjehnu odozgo. — A ovo je?

en: “We are all equal now…” Though it had not been long ago that Savine had knelt before the king to beg for her husband’s life, and not long before that she had knelt before him in Sworbreck’s office for… other reasons.
bs: — Svi smo mi sada jednaki… Iako nije prošlo mnogo vremena otkad je Savine klečala pred kraljem moleći za život svoga muža, a ne tako davno prije toga klečala je pred njim u Svorbrikovu uredu iz… drugih razloga.

en: “There has been a Great Change.” Savine frowned towards the window, sure she had heard something outside. She waited a moment, but there was nothing. “We must change, too.”
bs: — Dogodilo se Veliko Gorenje. Savine se namrštila prema prozoru, uvjerena da je nešto čula vani. Pričekala je trenutak, no nije bilo ničega. — I mi se moramo promijeniti.

en: Kort stared at her, his mouth ajar. “I never supposed that you, of all people, would lack the nerve to seize what is right in front of you. Lady Savine—”
bs: Kort je zurio u nju otvorenih usta. — Nikad ne bih pomislio da će baš tebi, od svih Folk, nedostajati hrabrosti zgrabiti ono što ti je pred nosom. Lady Savine…

en: There was a crash outside and she gasped, nearly jumped up, staring towards the window, half-straightened legs trembling. Voices out there. Shouts. Then laughter, dying away. Disturbed in his feeding, Harod had started to cry. She settled herself, put him back to her breast, his head fishing desperately for what was right in front of him.
bs: Vani se začuo tresak, a ona je udahnula, gotovo poskočila, zureći prema prozoru dok su joj poluispravljene noge drhtale. Glasovi vani. Povici. Zatim smijeh koji se stišavao. Ometen u hranjenju, Harod je počeo plakati. Smirila se, vratila ga na dojku, a njegova je glavica očajnički tražila ono što mu je bilo nadohvat ruke.

en: “One who can make the paint look like there is no paint.” And Zuri turned towards the door, scribbling a note. Savine brought her up short.
bs: — Ona koja šminku može učiniti takvom da se čini kao da je nema. I Zuri se okrenu prema vratima, bilježeći zabilješku. Savine je grubo prekide.

en: “There has been a Great Change, Zuri. We must change— Ah!” She gasped as Harod chewed at her nipple again, pulled him angrily away and he started to cry. That helpless, desperate cry that felt like nails hammered directly into her red-rimmed eyes.
bs: — Dogodila se Velika promjena, Zuri. Moramo se mijenjati… Ah! Zastenjala je dok je Harod ponovno zagrizao njezinu bradavicu, ljutito ga odmaknula, a on je zaplakao. Onaj bespomoćan, očajnički plač koji je djelovao poput čavala zabijenih izravno u njezine crvene, natečene oči.

en: They laughed, and pointed, and Orso acknowledged them with a weary smile. “One humiliation after another,” he murmured, flicking open his napkin, tucking it ever so delicately into his collar, and letting Hildi nudge the little table towards him. She had to slip a dog-eared political pamphlet under a loose leg to stop it wobbling.
bs: Smijali su se i upirali prstom, a Orso ih je pozdravio umornim osmijehom. — Jedno poniženje za drugim, promrmljao je, otvarajući ubrus, zataknuvši ga vrlo pažljivo za ovratnik i dopustivši Hildi da mu primakne mali stol. Morala je podmetnuti izlizani politički pamflet pod klimavu nogu kako se ne bi ljuljao.

en: Orso couldn’t help glancing up, yet again. A man with a tall hat perched at a ridiculous angle leaned on the railing to leer at him, an overpainted woman giggling as she clung to his elbow.
bs: Orso nije mogao suspregnuti Oko, još jednom. Čovjek s visokim šeširom nakrivljenim pod smiješnim kutom naslonio se na ogradu kako bi ga prostrijelio pogledom, dok se pretjerano našminkana žena kikotala, čvrsto se držeći za njegov lakat.

en: “You’ll move when I say,” said Halder. One of the other guards pulled out his heavy stick. “Or we’ll move you to the House o’ Truth.”
bs: — Pomaknut ćeš se kad ja kažem, odvrati Halder. Jedan od drugih stražara izvukao je svoju tešku palicu. — Ili ćemo te premjestiti u Kuću istine.

en: “Oh, damn,” muttered Orso around a mouthful of carrot with the consistency of firewood. Who should be leading the next batch of gawkers but that noted member of the Assembly of Representatives, Corporal Tunny?
bs: — O, kvragu, promrmljao je Orso kroz zalogaj mrkve konzistencije drva za ogrjev. Tko bi drugi predvodio sljedeću skupinu radoznalaca nego onaj istaknuti član Skupštine predstavnika, kaplar Tani?

en: “Whereas I was always sure you were a cunt!” Hildi went for him, tried to claw at his face, but Tunny caught her arm and they tussled over the barrier. Orso sprang up, making his plate rattle.
bs: "Dok sam ja oduvijek bila sigurna da si ti obična pička!" Hildi navali na nj, pokušavajući ga izgrepsti po licu, ali Tani joj uhvati ruku te se stanu hrvati preko ograde. Orso skoči na noge, a tanjur mu zveckavo zveknu.

en: Apologies for the scorn. Apologies for anything said in the Assembly. Apologies to Hildi for the shove. Sorry Hildi! They have to think I am against you.
bs: Isprike na preziru. Isprike na svemu izrečenom u Skupštini. Isprike Hildi na guranju. Oprosti, Hildi! Moraju misliti da sam protiv vas.

en: He laid down his cutlery, and carefully tore the note up into strips, and slipped them into his mouth, and chewed with relish. Without doubt, the most enjoyable part of the meal.
bs: Odložio je pribor za jelo, pažljivo poderao poruku na trake, ubacio ih u usta i sa zadovoljstvom prožvakao. nesumnjivo, najugodniji dio obroka.

en: Leo snorted. “Have you seen that bloody palace Selest dan Heugen’s having built? Or that town house of Isher’s? There are plenty of people still living well.”
bs: Leo frknu. — Jesi li vidjela onu prokletu palaču koju si Selest dan Heugen daje graditi? Ili onaj Išerov gradski dvorac? Još je mnoštvo onih koji žive naveliko.

en: “Have you seen how many of them are homeless in the city?” Honestly, he hadn’t. He spent all his time out of doors focused on staying upright. “Gangs of them. Orphaned, abandoned, lacking the most basic necessities. Forced to prey upon each other, to thieve, to sell themselves. Children starving on our streets.”
bs: — Jesi li vidio koliko ih je beskućnika u gradu? Iskreno, nije. Sav svoje vrijeme izvan kuće provodio je usredotočen na to da ostane na nogama. — Puni su ih čopori. Siročad, napuštena djeca, lišena najosnovnijih potrepština. Prisiljena pljačkati jedni druge, krasti, prodavati se. Djeca koja gladuju na našim ulicama.

en: “I’m no bloody good at apologies,” wanting to shake her hand off but somehow wanting it to stay both at once.
bs: — Prokleto sam loš u ispričavanju, pomislio je, želeći stresti njezinu ruku, a istodobno silno želeći da ostane.

en: Leo hadn’t been ready for the rush of feeling. He could hardly breathe for it. He’d been stuck for months among traitors, thugs and cowards, and the sight of that familiar, trustworthy face, as handsome as ever, was like a lamp in a pitch-black room. It felt as if a part of him that died at Stoffenbeck—the best part of him, even—came suddenly to life again.
bs: Leo nije bio spreman na taj nalet osjećaja. Jedva je dolazio do daha. Mjesecima je bio zaglavljen među izdajicama, nasilnicima i kukavicama, a prizor tog poznatog, pouzdanog lica, zgodnog kao i uvijek, bio je poput svjetiljke u mrklom mraku. Osjećao se kao da se dio njega koji je umro kod Štopenbeka — čak i onaj najbolji dio — iznenada ponovno vratio u život.

en: He knew he couldn’t deny it. Being in his mother’s shadow used to feel unbearable. Now he saw how lucky he’d been to have her. He took a hard breath and drew himself up. “I’m sorry, Jurand. I’m… I’m very sorry. For the way it all turned out. If you’d been with me, at Stoffenbeck, things would’ve been… well.” He frowned down at his leg. At his crutch. “I was a fool.”
bs: Znao je da to ne može poreći. Biti u majčinoj sjeni nekada se činilo nepodnošljivim. Sada je vidio kakvu je sreću imao što ju je imao. Duboko je udahnuo i uspravio se. — Žao mi je, Džurand. Stvarno mi je… jako žao. Zbog svega što se dogodilo. Da si bio sa mnom u Štopenbeku, stvari bi bile… pa, bolje." Namrštio se gledajući u svoju nogu. U svoju štaku. — Bio sam budala.

en: Leo was left frozen, his mouth slightly open. It was a long time since he’d thought of the happy brotherhood who’d gone to war with him. Risked their lives for him. Most of his energy went into finding ways to do what used to be easy, the rest into twisting the future into a shape he could live with.
bs: Leo je ostao skamenjen, otvorenih usta. Prošlo je mnogo vremena otkako je mislio na onu sretnu družinu koja je s njim pošla u rat. Koja je riskirala živote za njega. Većinu energije trošio je na pronalaženje načina kako učiniti ono što je nekad bilo lako, a ostatak na oblikovanje budućnosti u nešto s čime bi mogao živjeti.

en: “Oh, there’s been a Great Change, it’s true.” Leo felt his own anger bubbling up, never far from the surface, and he slapped at his aching stump. “I’m fucked, and the world’s fucked, but there are still some things that—”
bs: — O, dogodila se Velika promjena, to je istina. Leo je osjetio kako vlastiti bijes kipi, nikad daleko od površine, i pljesnuo se po bolnom patrljku. — Ja sam sjeban, i svijet je sjeban, ali postoje neke stvari koje…

en: All she’d done was walk in with the children. Put aside the past, those little bundles of innocent potential seemed to say. Look to the future. As simply as that, the mood was changed.
bs: Sve što je učinila bilo je to da je ušla s djecom. Ostavite prošlost iza sebe, činilo se kao da govore ti mali smotuljci nevine potencije. Gledajte u budućnost. Tako jednostavno, raspoloženje se promijenilo.

en: “We could begin with seats in the Assembly.” Leo tickled his daughter under the chin and made her squirm. “For you, and for Glaward, then…
bs: — Mogli bismo početi s mjestima u Skupštini. Leo je zagolicao kćer pod bradom i natjerao je da se koprca. "Za tebe, i za Glavarda, tada…

en: “No need to pick! You’ve managed the pair!” He stalked out into grey daylight, raindrops prickling the chill puddles scattered about the yard, and she followed.
bs: — Ne moraš birati! Uspjela si spojiti oboje! Izašao je u sivu dnevnu svjetlost, kišne kapi bockale su hladne lokve razbacane po dvorištu, a ona ga je slijedila.

en: “Go on!” she screamed at their backs. “Back you go to your mummies, you batch o’ cowards! Not one decent set o’ bones in the lot of you! We’re well rid o’ you bloody chicken-fuckers! I never saw such a stack o’ fishy cunts! You bloody… bloody…” She’d run out of insults. Even bad ones. And the Nail and his boys had already made it to the gate of Carleon and vanished down the entrance tunnel. She was shouting herself raw at the wet air.
bs: — Samo naprijed!, vrisnula je za njihovim leđima. — Vratite se mamicama, vi hrpo kukavica! Nema među vama ni jedne poštene kosti! Dobro smo se riješili vas krvavih jebača kokoši! Nikad nisam vidjela takvu gomilu ljigavih pički! Vi krvavi… krvavi… Ponestalo joj je uvreda. Čak i onih loših. A Najl i njegovi momci već su stigli do kapije Carleona i nestali u ulaznom tunelu. Derala se iz petnih žila u vlažan zrak.

en: “Very funny.” Rikke pushed past her and strode back up the hill. “The Nail had his mind set on going after Calder now. If you can call it a mind. Bastard wouldn’t be argued down. Now, mark you! With winter coming on!”
bs: — Jako smiješno. Rike ju je odgurnula i krenula natrag uzbrdo. — Najl je naumio krenuti na Kaldera. Ako se to uopće može nazvati umom. Taj gad nije htio odustati. A sad, upamtite! Zima samo što nije!

en: Isern considered her, jaw muscles squirming as she chewed a chagga pellet. “When we were running for our lives through a freezing forest, d’you mean?”
bs: Izern ju je promotrila, mišići čeljusti su joj radili dok je žvakala kuglicu chagga. — Misliš li na ono kad smo bježale glavom bez obzira kroz zaleđenu šumu?

en: Stour was clean now, bruises mostly healed even if his legs never would be. He’d stopped begging. Stopped talking at all. Just sat there, one white hand up on the black bars, waiting. She felt his bright, wet eyes following her, and it made the hairs on her neck prickle.
bs: Staur je sada bio čist, modrice su uglavnom zacijelile, iako mu noge nikada neće biti kao prije. Prestao je moliti. Prestao je uopće govoriti. Samo je sjedio ondje, bijela ruka na crnim rešetkama, čekajući. Osjetila je kako je prate njegove svijetle, vlažne oči, što joj je naježilo kožu na vratu.

en: A brief pause, and Rikke got the feeling he was considering how to cast something in the best light. He did that a lot. “Some of ’em.”
bs: Nakon kraće stanke, Rike je stekla dojam da važe kako nešto prikazati u najboljem svjetlu. Često je to činio. — Neke od njih.

en: Rikke considered him a moment. Considered the position. Turned in the chair to consider Stour Nightfall, sitting calm in his cage, hungry eyes gleaming in the shadows. She weighed the words carefully. “Tell him I’m willing to deal. Peace in the North. In return for his son.”
bs: Rike ga je na trenutak promotrila. Promotrila je položaj. Okrenula se u stolici kako bi promotrila Staur Najtfola, koji je mirno sjedio u svom kavezu, dok su mu gladne oči svjetlucale u sjenama. Pažljivo je odvagala riječi. — Reci mu da sam voljna pregovarati. Mir na Sjeveru. U zamjenu za njegova sina.

en: “It was,” said Leo. The place his father had talked of as the cradle of noble ideals. Where the great lords of the Union had engaged in dignified debate. Where Arnault stood alone to challenge Morlic the Mad and changed the course of history. It was easy to forget. “They call it the Commons’ Round now.”
bs: —— Bio je, reče Leo. Mjesto o kojem je njegov otac govorio kao o kolijevci plemenitih ideala. Gdje su Great Lords Unije vodili dostojanstvene rasprave. Gdje je Arnault stajao sam kako bi izazvao Morlica Ludog i promijenio tijek povijesti. Bilo je lako zaboraviti. — Sada ga zovu Commons’ Round.

en: Sworbreck leaped up as if he was mounted on a spring. “Nothing would delight me more than to do so! The very instant we reduce the number, not to mention the corruption, of the traitors, profiteers and simple incompetents in this Assembly!”
bs: Svorbrik skoči kao da je na oprugama."Ništa me ne bi više obradovalo nego to učiniti! Istog trena kad smanjimo broj, a da ne spominjem korupciju, izdajnike, profitere i obične nesposobnjakoviće u ovoj Skupštini!"

en: In the clamour produced by Sworbreck’s latest offer of martyrdom, Representatives shouted over each other to be heard. It was noisy as a battle, and Leo watched the back and forth with the care of a general feeling out his moment to advance. A white-haired old merchant had kidnapped the floor now, his bass voice so powerful the benches seemed to vibrate.
bs: U vrevi koju je prouzročila Svorbrikova najnovija ponuda mučeništva, zastupnici su nadglasavali jedni druge kako bi ih se čulo. Bilo je bučno poput bitke, a Leo je promatrao to nadmudrivanje s pozornošću generala koji osluškuje pravi trenutak za napad. Jedan sijedi stari trgovac upravo je preuzeo riječ, a njegov bas bio je toliko snažan da su klupe naizgled podrhtavale.

en: The usual rage, meanwhile, from above. Crumpled pamphlets were flung down. An apple core bounced from the shoulder of an ex-lord a few seats away and Jurand flinched.
bs: U međuvremenu, uobičajeni bijes odozgo. Zgužvani leci letjeli su dolje. Ogrizak jabuke odbio se od ramena bivšeg lorda nekoliko mjesta dalje, a Džurand se trgnuo.

en: “The Young Lion!” someone screeched as Glaward guided him to standing, and the hall fell silent. As close as it ever got, anyway.
bs: — Juvens lav!, netko je ciknuo dok mu je Glavard pomagao da se uspravi, a dvorana je utihnula. Ili barem onoliko koliko je to ovdje bilo moguće.

en: “Only an idiot stands in front of this rabble to say something,” muttered Leo, wiping the fresh sheen of sweat from his forehead. “You shuffle a few of the right words together and make sure you look ’em in the eye.” He flashed the humble smile he’d been working on. Waved away the congratulations as men leaned from the benches behind to slap him on the shoulder. “You’re going for a feeling. Make them think you’re one of them. Prove the mob’s behind you. You want to get something done, you pick a
bs: "Samo idiot stoji pred ovom svjetinom da bi rekao nešto", promrmljao je Leo, brišući svježi sloj znoja s čela. — Složiš nekoliko pravih riječi i pobrineš se da ih pogledaš u oči." Bacio je onaj ponizan osmijeh na kojem je radio. Odmahnuo je rukom na čestitke dok su se Folk naginjali s klupa iza njega da ga potapšaju po ramenu."Ideš na osjećaj. Natjeraš ih da misle kako si jedan od njih. Dokažeš da je rulja iza tebe. Ako želiš nešto postići, odabereš nekoliko Folk s kojima ćeš razgovarati iza zat

en: “Oh, yes. People have always loved the Young Lion.” He still seemed to be the same honest Anglander, none of Sworbreck’s flowery style, but these days he was playing the mob like his own personal orchestra and leading the nervous ex-lords wherever he pleased. Now he had a dozen virile young heroes of Angland on the front benches ready to nod along at his every utterance as though it fell from the mouth of Euz himself. Orso was starting to think he was far more dangerous now than he had been with
bs: "O, da. Folk su Uvijek voljeli Mladog lava." Činio se još uvijek istim poštenim Anglanderom, bez Svorbrikova kićenog stila, ali ovih je dana svirao rulji kao vlastitom orkestru i vodio nervozne bivše lordove kamo god je poželio. Sada je imao desetak stasitih mladih heroja Englenda na prednjim klupama, spremnih kimati na svaku njegovu izgovorenu riječ kao da je pala iz usta samog Euz. Orso je počeo misliti da je sada daleko opasniji nego što je bio sa svim svojim udovima.

en: Orso jumped up. “Are we not all equal here?” He addressed the public gallery in a wailing mockery of Sworbreck’s overwrought delivery. “Does not every Citizen deserve an equal chance to speak? Even so base a creature as a king?”
bs: Orso je skočio. — Nismo li ovdje svi jednaki?" Obratio se javnoj galeriji u jadnoj parodiji Svorbrikova pretjeranog izlaganja. — Zar svaki građanin ne zaslužuje jednaku priliku govoriti? Čak i tako nisko stvorenje kao što je kralj?

en: Judge stopped before the High Table, hands on hips and her bare feet planted wide. “I have watched the fucking pantomime in this ill-behaved nursery with growing disgust,” she said.
bs: Džadž se zaustavila pred visokim stolom, ruku na bokovima i bosih stopala čvrsto razmaknutih. — Gledala sam ovu jebenu pantomimu u ovom nepristojnom dječjem vrtiću s rastućim gađenjem, izjavila je.

en: “With pleasure.” A rat-faced Burner with a red-spattered cap stepped forward, sliding his hand into his jacket pocket. He brought it out in front of the secretary. There was nothing there but his fist. He smashed it into her face and knocked her down, her head bouncing on the tiles. She was left gazing up in amazement with blood running from her broken nose.
bs: — Sa zadovoljstvom. Palioc štakorskog lica, s kapom poprskanom crvenom bojom, iskoračio je naprijed i zavukao ruku u džep jakne. Izvukao ju je pred tajnicu. U njoj nije bilo ničega osim stisnute šake. Zabio ju je u njezino lice i oborio je na pod, gdje joj je Šef odskočila od pločica. Ostala je ležati, zapanjeno gledajući uvis dok joj je krv curila iz slomljenog nosa.
