en: There were splashes of red everywhere. Broad lifted his head so he could peer through his lenses and saw red flatbows at the rail of the public gallery.
bs: Posvuda su bile mrlje crvene boje. Brod je podigao glavu kako bi pogledao kroz svoje leće i ugledao crvene samostrele na ogradi javne galerije.

en: No one did a thing as the Burners brought out chains and started to shackle the men and women gathered around Risinau. Not the king, sitting meekly on his little chair. Not the Young Lion, watching warily from among his Anglanders. Not the artists and the thinkers Risinau had brought to the Assembly. Even the rowdies in the public galleries had swallowed their tongues.
bs: Nitko nije učinio ništa dok su Palioci iznosili lance i počeli okivati muškarce i žene okupljene oko Risinaua. Ni kralj, koji je krotko sjedio na svojoj maloj stolici. Ni Juvens lav, koji je oprezno promatrao iz redova svojih Anglanđana. Ni umjetnici i mislioci koje je Risinau dovio u Skupštinu. Čak su i izgrednici na javnim galerijama progutali jezik.

en: “We need to kill these bastards with more guts,” she said. “We need something spectacular. Anyone got any ideas?”
bs: "Moramo ubiti te gadove s više hrabrosti", rekla je. — Treba nam nešto spektakularno. Ima li tko kakvu ideju?

en: “Huh.” Judge tipped her head back so she could gaze up towards the gilded dome, scratching gently at her rashy neck with the backs of her broken fingernails. Slowly, the smile spread across her face. “My thanks, Citizen Sworbreck, and the nation’s thanks.” She jerked her head towards the door. “Take ’em up the Tower of Chains. And push ’em off.”
bs: — Hm. Džadž zabaci glavu unatrag kako bi pogledala pozlaćenu kupolu, nježno češući nadraženi vrat stražnjom stranom polomljenih noktiju. Polako, osmijeh joj se razlio licem. — Moja hvala, građanine Svorbrik, i hvala cijele nacije. Trzajem glave pokaza prema vratima. — Odvedite ih na Toranj Chains. I gurnite ih dolje.

en: It was cold outside, but Broad’s face felt hot. Across the Square of Marshals, Square of Equality, Square of Murder, whatever they were calling it now, curious eyes following them all the way. He narrowed his own eyes as a chilly gust swept up, brown leaves chasing each other across the flagstones.
bs: Vani je bilo hladno, ali Brodu je lice gorjelo. Preko Trga maršala, Trga jednakosti, Trga ubojstava, kako mu drago da su ga sada zvali, radoznale su oči pratile svaki njihov korak. Suzio je oči dok je hladan nalet vjetra zapuhao, a smeđe lišće jurilo jedno za drugim preko kamenih ploča.

en: One of the prisoners was crying. Another tried desperately to wedge himself in the doorway to the tower, pressing his face to the stone. “No! No! No—”
bs: Jedan od zatvorenika je plakao. Drugi je očajnički pokušavao uglaviti se u dovratak tornja, pritišćući lice uz kamen. — Ne! Ne! Ne…

en: Out from the darkness and onto the roof and he blinked at a clear, crisp day. Adua spread out below them, the chimneys jutting, plumes of smoke carried off by the chill wind, tiny ships at tiny wharves in the bay. Toy people swarming in a toy city.
bs: Izronio je iz tame na krov i zaškiljio na vedar, Trdak dan. Adua se prostirala pod njima; dimnjaci su stršili, hladan vjetar nosio je pramenove dima, a u zaljevu su se nazirali sićušni brodovi privezani uz minijaturna pristaništa. Folk poput igračaka vrzmali su se po gradu-igrački.

en: Broad caught a fistful of the man’s jacket from behind, kicked his foot away and helped shove him up onto the box. He stood there, breathing hard, staring down in disbelief at the city below, feet level with the embrasure in front of him.
bs: Brod zgrabi čovjeka za jaknu straga, podbije mu nogu i pomogne mu gurnuti na sanduk. Stajao je ondje, teško dišući, nevjerno gledajući dolje u grad, stopala u ravnini s otvorom Naprijed sebe.

en: “Sorry,” he muttered, trying to get his foot up on the box but it was trembling so bad he couldn’t manage it. “So sorry.”
bs: — Oprostite, promrmljao je, pokušavajući podići nogu na sanduk, ali toliko mu je drhtala da nije uspijevao. — Tako mi je žao.

en: Broad blinked. Brint had been a good man. He was reasonably sure of that. He’d tried to do the right thing, when everything fell apart. But good or bad, right or wrong, the fall is still the fall.
bs: Brod je trepnuo. Brint je bio dobar čovjek. Bio je prilično siguran u to. Pokušao je učiniti pravu stvar kad se sve raspalo. Ali dobro ili loše, ispravno ili pogrešno, Dausaid je uvijek samo Dausaid.

en: Risinau looked near dead already from the climb. Face pale and beaded with sweat and tears, mouth hanging open, gasping for breath. “I wish…
bs: Risinau je izgledao kao da je već na izmaku snaga od uspona. Lice blijedo, orošeno znojem i suzama, usta otvorena, hvata zrak."Želio bih…

en: “The time for half-measures is past.” Pike looked evenly back at her. “Sometimes, the only way to improve something is to destroy it, so it can be rebuilt better.” There was a time she’d thought that burned face was a perfect mask for his feelings. Now she wondered whether there were any underneath. “Sometimes, to change the world, we must first burn it down.”
bs: — Vrijeme za polovična rješenja je prošlo. Pajk je mirno gledao. — Ponekad je jedini način da se nešto popravi uništiti to, kako bi se moglo izgraditi bolje. Postojalo je vrijeme kad je mislila da je to opečeno lice savršena maska za njegove osjećaje. Sada se pitala postoje li uopće ikakvi ispod nje. — Ponekad, da bismo promijenili svijet, moramo ga najprije spaliti do temelja.

en: He neglected to mention the worsening shortages of food, coal and raw materials, the dangers of riot and summary arrest, or the never-ending trials for profiteering, speculation and usury. The many empty seats in the audience testified to them more eloquently than even the Great Machinist ever could.
bs: Propustio je spomenuti sve gore nestašice hrane, ugljena i sirovina, opasnosti od nereda i prijekih uhićenja ili beskrajnih suđenja za ratno profiterstvo, špekulacije i lihvarenje. Mnogobrojna prazna mjesta u publici svjedočila su o tome rječitije nego što bi to ikada mogao i sam Great strojar.

en: Nothing was more changed by the Great Change than fashion. Rich men’s costume had gained workmen’s flourishes, while the ideal for women was the artless shepherdess. Cheeks were painted slapped-arse pink while fans had become a loathed aristocratic affectation. Some women had stopped wearing wigs altogether, proudly displaying their conspicuously lifeless actual hair as if it was a badge of revolutionary pride. Exotic curios had been all the rage; now anything foreign was scorned with a patrioti
bs: Ništa se nije toliko promijenilo uslijed Velike promjene kao moda. Odjeća bogataša poprimila je radničke detalje, dok je ideal za žene postala jednostavna pastirica. Obrazi su se bojili u ružičastu boju stražnjice, dok su lepeze postale omražena aristokratska izmišljotina. Neke su žene potpuno prestale nositi perike, ponosno pokazujući svoju upadljivo beživotnu prirodnu kosu kao da je riječ o znaku revolucionarnog ponosa. Egzotične su drangulije bile pravi hit; sada se na sve strano gledalo s do

en: Savine had once felt nowhere more at home than here, flitting from one opportunity to another, hopes and dreams left wrecked in her wake. Now all she wanted was to slit the laces of her corset and sag down with her children, slap the stopper from the decanter and never put it back.
bs: Savine se nekoć nigdje nije osjećala kao kod kuće, leteći iz jedne prilike u drugu, dok su joj se nade i snovi raspadali u prah i pepeo za petama. Sada je sve što je željela bilo rasparati vezice na korzetu i skljokati se s djecom, izbiti čep iz boce s likerom i nikad ga više ne vratiti.

en: That would once have been an insult punishable by a slow social death, meticulously engineered. Now it hardly drew a shrug.
bs: To bi nekad bila uvreda kažnjiva sporom društvenom smrću, pomno isplaniranom. Sada to jedva da je izazvalo slijeganje ramenima.

en: It was coming. She knew it was coming. They all would have their moment in the dock. She pressed a smile down on top of her dread like the lid on a box of snakes.
bs: Dolazilo je. Znala je da dolazi. Svi će oni doći na red na optuženičkoj klupi. Potisnula je osmijeh preko svoga užasa poput poklopca na kutiji sa zmijama.

en: “When I was a boy,” muttered Curnsbick, “patriotism was kissing the flag and pretending to love the king. Now, suddenly, it’s spitting on the king and having poor furniture. One must keep a close eye on the current definitions. To be unpatriotic would be terrible. To be patriotic in the wrong way could be fatal. I feel I can admit to you, as an old friend, that since the Great Change… I am constantly terrified.” He gave a little laugh, but she could see tears on his cheeks. He removed his lenses
bs: — Kad sam bio dječak, promrmljao je Kurnsbik, patriotizam je značio ljubljenje zastave i pretvaranje da voliš kralja. Sada je to, odjednom, pljuvanje po kralju i posjedovanje jadnog namještaja. Čovjek mora pomno pratiti trenutne definicije. Biti nepatriot bio bi užas. Biti patriot na pogrešan način moglo bi biti kobno. Osjećam da ti mogu priznati, kao staroj prijateljici, da od Great Changea… neprestano živim u strahu. Kratko se nasmijao, ali ona je vidjela suze na njegovim obrazima. Skinuo je n

en: “Then you will not be short of friends here. Commissioner Pike’s tireless crusade against the banks has made investment hard to come by.”
bs: — Onda ovdje zasigurno nećeš patiti od manjka prijatelja. Nemilosrdna križarska vojna povjerenika Pajka protiv banaka učinila je ulaganja rijetkima.

en: “But even more over those she turns down.” The softer he talked, the more worried she became. “A woman with secrets, especially.”
bs: — Ali još više na one koje odbije. Što je tiše govorio, to se više brinula. — Posebice žena s tajnama.

en: Savine saw Selest’s eyes dart over, as keen for any trace of opportunity as her own had once been. She tried to smile, but the muscles in her face would not work the way they used to. She could not see Zuri. The blood was pulsing behind her eyes.
bs: Savine je vidjela kako Selestove oči prelijeću, toliko željne bilo kakvog traga prilike koliko su i njezine nekad bile. Pokušala se nasmijati, ali mišići lica nisu poslušali kao nekad. Nije mogla vidjeti Zuri. Krv joj je pulsirala iza očiju.

en: “The banker lent the money,” bellowed Sworbreck, “so the miller could adulterate his flour, so the baker could sell bread at inflated prices, causing hunger and discord in the service of a Styrian plot to manipulate the markets and undermine the Great Change!”
bs: — Bankar je posudio novac, zagrmio je Svorbrik, kako bi mlinar mogao patvoriti svoje brašno, kako bi pekar mogao prodavati Hardbred po napuhanim cijenama, uzrokujući glad i razdor u službi stirijske urote da manipulira tržištima i potkopa Veliku promjenu!

en: The court was not without it. Judge was the voice of the mob. She was their bitter rage, their envy and their greed, but she was also their sentimental forgiveness. When the mood turned for some well-spoken old man, some innocent-looking young woman, first Judge’s chin would crinkle, then her lower lip would tremble, then her black eyes would well with tears. Sometimes she would vault from behind the High Table, kiss the accused, clasp their head to her rusted breastplate. Then they would be emb
bs: Sud nije bila bez nje. Džadž je bila glas rulje. Ona je bila njihov gorki bijes, njihova zavist i njihova pohlepa, ali bila je i njihovo sentimentalno oproštenje. Kada bi se raspoloženje okrenulo u korist nekog rječitog starca, neke nevine mlade žene, prvo bi se naborala brada Džadž, zatim bi joj zadrhtala donja usna, a onda bi joj se crne oči napunile suzama. Ponekad bi iskočila iza visokog stola, poljubila optuženika, privila mu glavu na svoj zahrđali oklop. Tada bi ih zagrlili uplakani straža

en: “Ah, so the government is to blame?” Sworbreck spread his arms towards the benches behind the dock, where the Representatives gravely shook their heads at such a slander. “And since the government consists of those chosen by the people…” Sworbreck leaned back, raised his arms to the balconies. “The people are to blame?”
bs: "Ah, dakle je vlada kriva?" Svorbrik raširi ruke prema klupama iza optuženičke klupe, gdje su zastupnici turobno vrtjeli glavama nad takvom klevetom. — A budući da se vlada sastoji od onih koje je Folk izabrao…" Svorbrik se nasloni unatrag i podigne ruke prema balkonima."Folk je kriv?"

en: “Usurer!” someone screeched. No doubt there were profiteers and speculators everywhere. Before the Great Change they had simply called that business, and the worst offenders had been celebrated as society’s greatest successes.
bs: — Kamataru! netko vrisnu. Nije bilo sumnje da svuda ima profitera i špekulanata. Prije Velike promjene to su jednostavno zvali poslom, a najgore prijestupnike slavilo se kao najveće društvene uspjehe.

en: Sarlby flung the ledger away, pages flapping, and it spun across the tiled floor. The banker stood gasping, eye-lenses skewed, collar torn, blood running from a gash on his scalp. “The numbers…” he breathed, astonished, “prove…”
bs: Sarlbi odgurnu knjigu koja se otkotrljala s listovima koji su lepršali preko popločanog poda. Bankar je stajao hvatajući zrak, s iskrivljenim lećama naočala, poderanog ovratnika, dok mu je krv curila iz posjekotine na tjemenu. — Brojevi…" prošapta zaprepašteno, dokazuju…

en: There was no need to pronounce a sentence. The only outcomes here were acquittal or the Tower of Chains. Hildi stared at Judge, and Broad, and Sarlby, and the red-smeared Burners jeering from the public gallery. “They’re monsters,” Orso heard her whisper.
bs: Nije bilo potrebe izricati presudu. Jedini ishodi ovdje bili su oslobađajuća presuda ili Kula lanaca. Hildi je zurila u Džadž, u Brod, u Sarlbyja i u krvlju umrljane Palitelje koji su se rugali s galerije za javnost. — Oni su čudovišta, čuo je Orso kako šapuće.

en: But Sibalt was the last man she hugged, and he ended up slitting his own throat. So she hawked up cold snot and sent it spinning into the frozen dirt beside the cart instead.
bs: No Sibalt je bio posljednji muškarac kojeg je zagrlila, a završio je tako što si je prerezao grlo. Stoga je iskašljala hladnu sluz i pljunula je u smrznuto tlo pokraj kolica.

en: Pike came striding from the cellar, pulling on his gloves. “Fine work, Chief Inspector Teufel,” he rasped as he watched the Constables file up the steps to dump armloads of papers into the cart, the odd one floating free to stick in the half-frozen mud. “A bank hidden in a wine-merchant’s cellars. We have driven them underground, like rats.”
bs: Pajk je izišao iz podruma koračajući krupnim koracima, navlačeći rukavice. — Izvrstan posao, glavni inspektore Tojfel, promuklo je dobacio dok je promatrao kako Straža u koloni izlazi uz stepenice istovariti naramke papira u kolica, pri čemu bi poneki list odlepršao i zalijepio se za napola smrznuto blato. — Banka skrivena u podrumu trgovca vinom. Otjerali smo ih pod zemlju, poput štakora.

en: The Commissioner turned, his breath a smoking cloud about his high collar. “What about everything else?”
bs: Povjerenik se okrenuo, a njegov je dah bio poput oblačića dima oko visokog ovratnika. — Što je sa svime ostalim?

en: “Burn it down,” she finished, softly. But it was sounding more and more like something a madman says to justify all the fires he loves to start. “If the manager’s in the city, we’ll find him.”
bs: — Spaliti ga do temelja, dovrši ona tiho. No to je zvučalo sve više kao nešto što luđak govori kako bi opravdao sve požare koje tako rado podmeće. — Ako je upravitelj u gradu, pronaći ćemo ga.

en: “Future generations might never believe that it happened.” She blew some yellow hair out of her face with a smoky breath and went back to sketching, charcoal hissing on paper. “Then it might happen again.”
bs: — Buduće generacije možda nikada neće povjerovati da se ovo dogodilo. Otpuhnula je žutu kosu s lica uz zadah dima i vratila se skiciranju, dok je ugljen šuštao po papiru. — Onda bi se moglo ponoviti.

en: “Lord Marshal Kroy stood on the other side,” said Shivers, “and thousands o’ Union soldiers, and your father, too. Three red days we had of it. Men struggled here with all they had for each step of ground. Died and killed for every handful of soil.” He frowned out at the crisp, quiet white, stretching away to the hazy fells all around, and shook his head like he couldn’t make it fit. “Now you’d never know. Few years passed and… it’s just fields.”
bs: — Lord maršal Kroy stajao je na drugoj strani, nastavi Šivers, i tisuće vojnika Unije, a i tvoj otac. Tri krvava dana smo imali. Folk su se ovdje borili svim silama za svaki pedalj zemlje. Ginuli i ubijali za svaku šaku tla. Namršteno je gledao u oštru, tihu bjelinu koja se protezala do izmaglicom prekrivenih brda uokolo i odmahnuo glavom kao da to ne može pojmiti. — Sada nikada ne bi rekao. Prošlo je nekoliko godina i… to su samo polja.

en: “How did they get the bastard things up here?” Her face was pinched and her chest raw from the winter but her body all sticky-hot from the climb under her cloak, so she couldn’t decide whether to draw it tight or fling it off. “Just getting myself up here was a struggle.”
bs: — Kako su, dovraga, uspjeli dopremiti ove stvari ovamo? Lice joj je bilo zgrčeno, a prsa nadražena od zime, dok joj je tijelo bilo ljepljivo i vruće od uspona pod ogrtačem, pa nije mogla odlučiti hoće li ga čvršće omotati ili odbaciti. — Samo penjanje ovamo bilo je prava muka.

en: “Then we can trot off ’fore he arrives,” said Isern. “You took Uffrith without his help, and you took Carleon without his help, and you’ve took half the North without his help, and now he slinks up, sniffing about like a badger at the henhouse. You don’t need his help getting your hands on the other half.”
bs: — Onda možemo odjezditi prije nego što stigne, reče Izern."Zauzela si Afrit bez njegove pomoći, zauzela si Carleon bez njegove pomoći i uzela si pola Sjevera bez njegove pomoći, a sada se on prikrada, njuškajući uokolo poput jazavca oko kokošinjca. Ne treba ti njegova pomoć da se dočepaš i druge polovice."

en: “There was a time your lessons smacked of wisdom, Isern-i-Phail. Now they smack of mad witterings summoned on the spot. Or worse yet, the maddest bits picked out from your father’s mad witterings, like a drunk squirrel picking nuts from a turd. I could do without the constant whittling down of my authority.”
bs: — Bilo je vrijeme kada su tvoje lekcije odisale mudrošću, Izern-i-Fejl. Sada odišu ludim brbljanjem smišljenim u trenu. Ili još gore, najluđim dijelovima izvučenim iz očeva ludog brbljanja, poput pijane vjeverice koja bira orahe iz govana. Mogla bih bez tog neprestanog potkopavanja moga autoriteta.

en: Corleth blinked at Isern, then at Rikke, and swallowed. “Honestly, I’d rather not get stuck between the two o’ you.”
bs: Corleth trepne prema Izern, pa prema Rike, i proguta knedlu. — Iskreno, radije ne bih zapela između vas dvije.

en: Isern was less pleased. Indeed, she’d had a look of gathering fury during that last speech which was slightly troubling and made Rikke wonder whether she might’ve taken at least one step too far. “Well, have a shit, then, you little ingrate maggot!” she snarled, spraying chagga juice and making Rikke flinch back. “You little painted piss-smear! You fucking one-eyed wanker!”
bs: Izern je bila manje zadovoljna. Zapravo, tijekom tog posljednjeg govora izraz lica joj se pretvorio u nakupljeni bijes, što je bilo pomalo uznemirujuće i natjeralo Rike da se zapita nije li možda ipak otišla korak predaleko. — Pa, odjebi onda, ti mala nezahvalna crvljivice!" zarežala je, prskajući sok od chagga bobica i tjerajući Rike da uzmakne. — Ti mala išarana pišalino! Ti jebeni jednooki šupku!

en: “Bayaz!” Rikke stowed her mood away and strolled towards him with a smile, boots crunching in that circle of fresh snow, the Heroes a ring of disapproving giants frowning on their meeting. “First of the Magi! First apprentice of great Juvens! Don’t I feel special to get an audience?”
bs: — Bajaz! Rike je potisnula svoje raspoloženje i krenula prema njemu s osmijehom, čizme su joj krckale u tom krugu svježeg snijega, a Heroes su poput prstena neodobravajućih divova gledali odozgo na njihov susret. — Prvi među Magi! Prvi šegrt velikog Juvensa! Zar se ne osjećam posebno što sam dobila audijenciju?

en: Rikke wasn’t above being pleased by flattery. But she was above letting it show. “Man o’ your age, outdoors in such bitter weather, figured it must be important.” And she grinned wide. Your best shield is a smile, her father used to say, and she’d a feeling she might need a shield or two in this conversation. “Besides, I was in the neighbourhood. Business in Osrung.” And she waved towards the thin smoke rising from the town’s chimneys, off down the river. “Been taking a little tour of the North.
bs: Rike nije bila imuna na laskanje, no bila je iznad toga da to i pokaže. — Čovjek tvojih godina, na ovakvoj ciči zimi, pomislila sam da mora biti važno." I široko se osmjehnula. Tvoj najbolji štit je osmijeh, govorio je njezin otac, a imala je osjećaj da bi joj u ovom razgovoru mogao zatrebati pokoji štit. — Uostalom, bila sam u blizini. Posao u Osrungu." Mahnula je prema tankom dimu koji se dizao iz gradskih dimnjaka, dolje uz rijeku. — Obilazim malo Sjever. Ili barem one dijelove za koje sam od

en: The magus smiled as he followed her with his eyes. “The past has never interested me. For better or worse it is done, and set, and littered with disappointments as a battlefield is littered with the dead. But the future is a ploughed field, full of potential. The future we can twist into wonderful shapes. With my help, the North could be yours. All of it, and not only for today. Imagine all the good we could do together.”
bs: Mag se osmjehnuo prateći je pogledom. — Prošlost me nikada nije zanimala. Bila dobra ili loša, ona je gotova, utvrđena i zatrpana razočaranjima kao što je bojište zatrpano mrtvima. Ali budućnost je preorano polje, puno potencijala. Budućnost možemo oblikovati u čudesne oblike. Uz moju pomoć, Sjever bi mogao biti tvoj. Sav, i to ne samo za danas. Zamisli samo sve dobro što bismo mogli zajedno učiniti.

en: Rikke doubted Bayaz became Bayaz by sharing more than he had to. “I see things, too,” she said, turning her left eye towards him and opening it very wide. “Who knows? Maybe even a thing or two you don’t. I know things haven’t gone smoothly for you lately. You left the North in Black Calder’s care and he pissed his trousers. His brother’s dead and his son’s in a cage and now you have to listen to me flap my lips. And then there’s your Union, where I saw you give such a fine address, the countless
bs: Rike je sumnjala da je Bajaz postao Bajaz dijeleći više nego što je morao. — I ja vidim stvari, reče, okrenuvši svoje lijevo oko prema njemu i širom ga otvorivši. — Tko zna? Možda čak i pokoju stvar koju ti ne vidiš. Znam da stvari u posljednje vrijeme ne idu glatko tebi. Napustio si Sjever pod skrbi Black Kaldera, a on se usrao od straha. Brat mu je mrtav, Filio u kavezu, a sada moraš slušati kako ja mlatim gubicom. A tu je i tvoj Unija, gdje sam te vidjela kako držiš onako lijep govor, bezbroj

en: “None alive know that.” Bayaz glared over at Corleth, and she swallowed, and blinked down at the ground. “They come from an age before the Old Time. They were ancient even when my master Juvens was born.”
bs: — Nitko živ to ne zna. Bajaz prostrijeli pogledom Corleth, a ona proguta knedlu i trepnu gledajući u tlo. — Oni potječu iz doba prije Starog vremena. Bili su drevni čak i kad se rodio moj Majstor Juvens.

en: His eyes narrowed, and he closed the gap between them with one step. She felt Shivers shift behind her, the faint rattle as he gripped his sword, and she had just the presence of mind to raise one finger to still him.
bs: Suzio je oči i jednim korakom premostio razmak između njih. Osjetila je kako se Šivers pomaknuo iza nje, začula je tiho zveckanje dok je stezao dršku mača, no imala je dovoljno prisebnosti podići prst i ušutkati ga.

en: “I expect so,” she said, trying to stop her voice quavering with relief. “He needs it. Perhaps, when I’ve settled with him, we should talk again. By that time, you might want to buy secrets from me! Fare you well, First of the Magi.”
bs: — Vjerojatno hoće, odvrati ona, pokušavajući spriječiti drhtanje glasa od olakšanja. — Potrebna mu je. Možda bismo, kad se s njim obračunam, trebali ponovno razgovarati. Do tada ćeš možda poželjeti kupiti tajne od mene! Sretno, Prvi među Magima.

en: Clover nudged some wet bushes out of the way and peered across the river. His eyes weren’t all they once were, but he’d an unpleasant sense there were some familiar faces at the far end of the bridge.
bs: Klover odmakne mokro grmlje i zagleda se preko rijeke. Vid ga više nije služio kao nekad, ali ga je obuzeo nelagodan osjećaj da na drugom kraju mosta vidi neka poznata lica.

en: Clover frowned down at the fine wolfskin cloak Stour used to wear. She had a point. Turning up to talk to Black Calder in his stolen son’s stolen finery would be less than wise. “Shit,” he said, undoing the buckle with some reluctance, since it was by no means the weather for disrobing, and tossed it over to Sholla. “If my luck’s a lot better’n usual, I’ll see you back here soon.”
bs: Klover pogleda skupocjeni ogrtač od vučje kože koji je nekad nosio Staur. Bila je u pravu. Pojaviti se pred Black Kalderom u ukradenoj odjeći njegova ukradenog sina ne bi bilo nimalo mudro. — Kvragu, opsuje otkopčavajući kopču s oklijevanjem, jer vrijeme nipošto nije bilo za skidanje, pa ga baci Šoli. — Ako me posluži sreća bolje nego inače, vidimo se uskoro.

en: “Right y’are.” Clover unbuckled his sword-belt and handed it over. Could scarcely remember the last time he drew the damn thing except to oil it anyway. “You should know I regret what happened last time we met,” he said, following Trapper up the muddy road. “Didn’t want anyone dead, but bloody Downside, he’s one o’ those bastards leaves a trail o’ wreckage with every stride.”
bs: — dogovoreno, reče Klover, otkopča opasač s mačem i pruži ga. Jedva se mogao sjetiti se kada ga je posljednji put izvukao, osim kad ga je trebalo nauljiti. — Trebao bi znati da žalim zbog onoga što se dogodilo prošli put kad smo se sreli, dodao je prateći Zamkača blatnjavim putem. — Nisam htio da itko strada, ali prokleti Dausaid, on je jedan od onih gadova koji za sobom ostavljaju pustoš kamo god krenu.

en: “Jonas Clover!” He spread his arms like he was greeting an old friend, a gesture which Clover found anything but reassuring. “Welcome to Currahome. What d’you think of the place?”
bs: — Jonas Klover! Raširio je ruke kao da pozdravlja starog prijatelja, gesta koju Klover nije smatrao nimalo umirujućom. — Dobrodošao u Currahome. Što misliš o ovom mjestu?

en: “Let’s get in out of the cold.” Calder turned towards the hall. “You’re a connoisseur of sword-work, you’ll enjoy this.”
bs: — Uđimo unutra, na toplo, reče Kalder i okrenu se prema dvorani. — Ti si poznavatelj umijeća mačevanja, ovo će ti se svidjeti.

en: The boy darted around a lunge, flicked his sword out and nicked the big man’s hand. He gasped through clenched teeth, blade dropping to the straw. The lad stepped in, sword raised.
bs: Dječak je munjevito izmaknuo nasrtaju, trznuo mačem i zarezao krupnog čovjeka po ruci. Ovaj je uzdahnuo kroz stisnute zube, a oštrica mu je ispala u slamu. Mladić je zakoračio naprijed, podignutog mača.

en: Clover raised his brows even higher. That explained a few things. His being on intimate terms with long-dead heroes for one. The way Black Calder scraped around him for another. He hadn’t the look of a legendary wizard, truth be told. Thicker in the neck and quicker to smile. But there was something in Bayaz’s eyes as he took Clover’s measure. Something that made him think this would be a bad enemy to have.
bs: Klover je obrve podignuo još više. To je objasnilo nekoliko stvari. Njegovu bliskost s davno preminulim junacima, kao prvo. Način na koji se Black Kalder ulagivao oko njega, kao drugo. Istini za volju, nije izgledao kao legendarni čarobnjak. Imao je deblji vrat i bio je skloniji osmijehu. No, bilo je nečega u Bajazovim očima dok je odmjeravao Klovera. Nečega zbog čega je pomislio kako bi bilo pogubno imati takvog neprijatelja.

en: “You lacked somewhat of manners when you first came to visit me, as I recall.” Bayaz peered down his nose at Calder as if he was still a prideful pup. “But in all the years since the battle at the Heroes, my support for you has never wavered.”
bs: — Koliko se sjećam, manjkalo vam je manira kada ste me prvi put posjetili. Bajaz je odmjerio Kaldera s visoka, kao da je još uvijek nadobudan štenac. — No, svih ovih godina od bitke kod Heroes, moja podrška vama nikada nije jenjala.

en: “We have.” Clover glanced about at the hard faces. The hard hands near the hard weapons. He decided if Calder had wanted him dead he wouldn’t have wasted poison, and took a sup. “But then I turned on you and your son.” Might’ve seemed madness to bring it up, but he judged it better to face it now than find it stabbing him in the arse later.
bs: — Jesmo. Klover je pogledom prešao preko grubih lica. Grubih ruku blizu grubog oružja. Zaključio je da ga je Kalder htio ubiti, ne bi trošio otrov, pa je otpio gutljaj. — Ali onda sam se okrenuo protiv tebe i tvoga sina. Možda se činilo kao ludilo spominjati to, ali procijenio je da je bolje suočiti se s tim sada nego kasnije osjetiti ubod u leđa.

en: “Huh.” And Calder grinned at him, teeth shining in the light of the fire-pit. “I still like you, Clover. I never can bring myself to trust loyal men. Can’t understand the bastards.”
bs: — Hm. Kalder se nacerio prema njemu, a zubi su mu blistali na svjetlosti ognjišta. — I dalje te volim, Klover. Nikako se ne mogu natjerati vjerovati odanim ljudima. Ne mogu razumjeti te gadove.

en: Calder watched him, in silence calm as a mountain lake. There was some laughter and clapping down where the sword-work was happening. There was a crunch and a whirl of sparks as a glowing log shifted in the fire-pit. Clover glanced around. Still the hard faces, the hard weapons. Still the ever-present threat of a quick trip back to the mud.
bs: Kalder ga je promatrao, u tišini mirnoj poput gorskog jezera. Dolje gdje se odvijalo mačevanje čuli su se smijeh i pljesak. Začulo se krckanje i kovitlac iskri dok se užarena cjepanica pomaknula u ognjištu. Klover se osvrnuo. I dalje ona tvrda lica, tvrdo oružje. I dalje sveprisutna prijetnja brzog puta natrag u blato.

en: “As a man who’s been cast as both hero and villain, you should know better’n anyone, Jonas Steepfield—the hero’s whoever wins.” And Calder smiled out at all those fires, the deep lines spreading around the corners of his eyes. “Reckon I’ve a trick or two to teach Tricky Rikke yet. No doubt she’s crafty, but I heard she’s making mistakes. Heard she had a little falling out with the Nail.”
bs: — Kao čovjek koji je glumio i heroja i zlikovca, trebao bi znati bolje od ikoga, Jonas Stipfild — heroj je onaj tko pobijedi. Kalder se nasmiješio gledajući sve te vatre, dok su se duboke bore širile oko kutova njegovih očiju. — Računam da imam još pokoji trik kojim mogu podučiti Lukavu Rike. Nema sumnje da je prepredena, ali čuo sam da radi pogreške. Čuo sam da se malo posvađala s Najlom.

en: “Well, if I’m so damn reliable…” He looked out at the valley, and all those fires, right to the far hills. “You already know what side I’m on.”
bs: — Pa, ako sam toliko prokleto pouzdan… Pogleda dolinu i sve te vatre, sve do dalekih brda. — Već znaš na čijoj sam strani.

en: Glaward nodded sadly. “Solid, careful, caring, not much imagination.” He could’ve been describing himself.
bs: Glavard je tužno kimnuo. — Čvrst, oprezan, brižan, bez previše mašte." Mogao je opisivati samoga sebe.

en: Gasps of disgust from every side. Leo expected the truth was simpler. Bell had been promoted far beyond his ability and thrown against a dedicated enemy on ground of their choosing. His army was ill-provisioned, ill-equipped and stuffed with Purity Officers who bastardised every military decision with politics. The surprise was that disaster hadn’t struck sooner.
bs: Uzdisaji gnušanja sa svih strana. Leo je pretpostavljao da je istina jednostavnija. Bell je bio unaprijeđen daleko iznad svojih sposobnosti i bačen pred predanog neprijatelja na terenu koji su oni odabrali. Njegova je vojska bila loše opskrbljena, slabo opremljena i nakrcana časnicima čistoće koji su svaku vojnu odluku upropastili politikom. Iznenađenje je bilo to što katastrofa nije udarila i ranije.

en: “It’s true I hear some fine reports o’ your conduct, Bell. It’s how you got the job in the first place. Put yourself in danger to save wounded soldiers. Gave up meals so others could eat. Walked while sick men rode on your horse. Noble stuff. It’d make me weep in a storybook.” Judge stretched further, her black eyes fixed on the accused. “But I weep very easily. You told us you did everything you could to win.”
bs: — Istina je da čujem neka lijepa izvješća o tvom ponašanju, Bell. Tako si uopće i dobio posao. Izlagao si se opasnosti da spasiš ranjene vojnike. Odricao si se obroka da bi drugi mogli jesti. Hodao si dok su bolesni Folk jahali na tvom konju. Plemenite stvari. Zbog toga bih zaplakala u nekoj priči. Džadž se još više protegnula, njezine crne oči prikovane za optuženika. — Ali ja vrlo lako zaplačem. Rekao si nam da si učinio sve što si mogao pobijediti.

en: Leo glanced over at Kort and gave him the slightest nod. He rose to roar the piece they’d agreed on. “Only five days ago, a group of farmers on the coast near Keln, banding together against Gurkish invaders, were mistaken for Gurkish invaders themselves and attacked by a group of armed fishermen. Twelve men died!” It had actually been one, but nobody got excited over a single corpse any more.
bs: Leo baci Oko prema Kortu i dade mu jedva primjetan znak glavom. Ustao je kako bi zagrmio ono oko čega su se dogovorili. — Samo prije pet dana, skupinu farmera na obali blizu Kelna, koji su se udružili protiv Gurkish osvajača, zamijenili su za same Gurkish osvajače i napala ih je skupina naoružanih ribara. Dvanaest Folk je poginulo!" Zapravo je bila jedan, ali nitko se više nije uzbuđivao zbog jednog jedinog leša.

en: “Stoffenbeck was a battle he knew he couldn’t win!” lied Jurand smoothly, clapping Leo on the shoulder. “But one he chose to fight anyway, whatever it cost him. Against the odds. Against countless royalist forces. Every Citizen can see the sacrifices he made on their behalf!”
bs: — Štopenbek je bila bitka za koju je znao da je ne može dobiti! slagao je Džurand vješto, potapšavši Lea po ramenu. — Ali bitka koju je svejedno odlučio voditi, bez obzira na cijenu. Usprkos izgledima. Usprkos bezbrojnim rojalističkim snagama. Svaki građanin može vidjeti žrtve koje je podnio u njihovo ime!

en: “Better to turn it down before they refuse to offer it,” murmured Jurand, lips carefully pursed as he gauged the feeling in the galleries. “Then we can take it up later.”
bs: — Bolje odbiti prije nego što nam uskrate ponudu, promrmljao je Džurand, pažljivo stisnutih usana dok je procjenjivao raspoloženje na galerijama. — Tada ćemo je moći prihvatiti kasnije.

en: “I am alive, Citizeness Brock, and my wife is alive, which, after the events we endured in Valbeck, I consider to be remarkable good fortune.”
bs: — Živ sam, građanko Brok, a i moja je supruga živa, što nakon događaja koje smo pretrpjeli u Valbeku smatram iznimnom srećom.

en: “You know I have the highest regard for you as a woman of business.” Vallimir cleared his throat. His voice had an ill crackle to it. “But prominent connections are not the safest thing these days. Might I ask why you sent for me?”
bs: — Znate da vas iznimno cijenim kao poslovnu ženu. Valimir pročisti grlo. Glas mu je imao neugodan, hrapav prizvuk. — No, istaknute veze danas nisu najsigurnija stvar. Smijem li upitati zašto ste me pozvali?

en: She waved towards one of the braziers, a matching pair of Majir’s frowning thugs in attendance. “The people queue, hopefully without freezing. They receive a bag of coal, two loaves of bread, a blanket. There might be meat or milk for children, on a good day. Names and addresses are taken, marks and signatures given to discourage fraud. But sometimes examples have to be made even so.”
bs: Mahnula je prema jednom od žeravnika, uz koji su stajala dva Valimirova namrštena nasilnika. — Folk čekaju u redu, nadajmo se bez smrzavanja. Dobiju vreću ugljena, dvije štruce kruha, pokrivač. Ponekad bude mesa ili mlijeka za djecu, kad je dobar dan. Uzimaju se imena i adrese, daju se potpisi i oznake kako bi se spriječile prijevare. No, ponekad se ipak mora dati primjer drugima.

en: Vallimir took out a paper, creased and faded. The Darling of the Slums. And there was that etching of a radiantly smiling Savine dan Brock dispensing coins to the starving while orphans clutched at her skirts. The sight of it made Savine feel faintly nauseous.
bs: Valimir je izvadio zgužvan i izblijedjeli papir. Miljenica sirotinjskih četvrti. I bio je tu bakrorez nasmijane Savine dan Brok kako dijeli novčiće izgladnjelima dok se siročad hvata za njezine skute. Od samog pogleda na to Savine je osjetila laganu mučninu.

en: Why indeed? Savine took a deep breath, the cold of it almost painful, and gazed into the flames in the brazier. “It is, as you have no doubt guessed, entirely selfish. The truth is… the past seems to be a scab I cannot stop picking. I often think about Valbeck. About the uprising, and what I did there… and what I did before. About the children we used in our mill. The children… I made you use.” The fire, the queue, the snowy street, it had all become a sparkling blur, her eyes focused beyond. “I
bs: Zašto, doista? Savine duboko udahne, a hladnoća je gotovo zaboljela, te se zagleda u plamen u žeravniku."To je, kao što si nedvojbeno naslutio, posve sebično. Istina je… prošlost mi se čini kao krasta koju ne prestajem čačkati. Često mislim na Valbek. Na ustanak i na ono što sam ondje učinila… i na ono što sam učinila prije. Na djecu koju smo koristili u našoj tvornici. Djecu… koju sam ja natjerala tebe koristiti. Palioc, red, snježna ulica, sve se pretvorilo u svjetlucavu maglu, a njezine su oč

en: “They tossed General Bell from the Tower of Chains,” called Leo. A moment later, Savine heard the clonk of his leg tossed onto the floor as he dropped back against his pillows.
bs: — Bacili su generala Bella s Chainsa, pozvao je Leo. Trenutak kasnije, Savine je čula topot njegove noge kako udara o pod dok se zavalio natrag na jastuke.

en: If only. She looked at the floor, wondering how she could possibly put any gloss on what she had to say. “There is something… I need to share with you. Something I found out shortly before we were married.”
bs: Kad bi barem bilo tako. Pogledala je u pod, pitajući se kako bi uopće mogla uljepšati ono što mora reći. — Postoji nešto… što moram podijeliti s tobom. Nešto što sam saznala nedugo prije nego što smo se vjenčali.

en: “Not that.” Well, yes, that, but so much more than that. It still shocked her to say it. Still repelled her to think it. She squeezed her eyes shut, her ears full of the sound of blood surging, and blurted it in a rush. “We have the same father!”
bs: — Nije to. Pa, jest to, ali i mnogo više od toga. Još uvijek ju je šokiralo izgovoriti to. Još uvijek joj se gadilo i pomisliti na to. Čvrsto je zatvorila oči, ušiju punih zvuka krvi koja joj je pulsirala u glavi, i izlanula u dahu: — Imamo istog oca!

en: She sat in silence as he limped out, teeth gritted. Click, tap, grunt. Click, tap, grunt. That mixture of cunning, ruthlessness, burning ambition and constant pain was far from unfamiliar.
bs: Sjedila je u tišini dok je šepao van, stisnutih zuba. Klik, tap, hropac. Klik, tap, hropac. Ta mješavina lukavstva, nemilosrdnosti, goruće ambicije i stalne boli bila joj je itekako poznata.

en: Broad could hardly see the point of screaming at folk already good as dead. But he was what you’d have to call blind drunk. Spent most of his waking hours blind drunk, now. Like he had in Styria. The only way he could see to get through it.
bs: Brod nije vidio smisao u deranju na ljude koji su ionako već bili mrtvi. No, bio je, kako bi se reklo, mrtav pijan. Većinu budnih sati sada je provodio mrtav pijan. Baš kao što je činio u Stiriji. Bio je to jedini način na koji je mogao izdržati.

en: Sometimes felt like all Broad had was doubts. But they changed nothing. He took another nip. The more he drank, the harder it was to keep count. The more he drank, the less he cared about innocence or guilt. The more he drank, the less their crying bothered him. Their arguing. Their endless fucking reasoning. A cuff across the head would shut ’em up, when it got too much. It’d been the same with the prisoners in Styria. No food to spare for the enemy, so… get Gunnar Broad. He’ll do what needs do
bs: Ponekad se činilo da Brod ima samo dvojbe. Ali one nisu ništa mijenjale. Potegnuo je još jedan gutljaj. Što je više pio, to je teže bilo zadržati broj. Što je više pio, to ga je manje bilo briga za nevinost ili krivnju. Što je više pio, to ga je manje diralo njihovo zapomaganje, njihovo prepiranje, njihovo beskrajno jebeno opravdavanje. Šamar po glavi ušutkao bi ih kad bi postalo previše. Bilo je isto i sa zarobljenicima u Stiriji. Nije bilo hrane za neprijatelja, pa… dovedite Gunara Broda. On ć

en: They clung to each other with desperate strength, these two, trying somehow to put off that final parting. Broad had the pain of sentimental tears at the back of his nose as he prised them apart, hands numb from the cold, numb from the drink. But he still did it.
bs: Očajnički su se držali jedno za drugo, njih dvoje, pokušavajući nekako odgoditi taj konačni rastanak. Brod je osjećao bol sentimentalnih suza u korijenu nosa dok ih je razdvajao, ruku utrnulih od hladnoće, utrnulih od pića. Ipak, učinio je to.

en: They handed the prisoners over to the Burners at the foot of the tower. Herded them onto Curnsbick’s new lift. A wonder of the modern age. The signal was given, the machinery clattered into life and the platform lurched upwards. The climb had almost been kinder.
bs: Predali su zatvorenike Paliocima u podnožju tornja. Natjerali su ih na Kurnsbikovo novo dizalo. Čudo modernog doba. Znak je dan, mehanizam je zazvečao i platforma se trzavo vinula uvis. Uspon je gotovo bio milosrdniji.

en: Told himself he didn’t want to do it, but he was scared. A coward. That was better’n the alternative. That he did want to do it, ’cause there was a pit of rage in him there was never any filling. He’d rather tell himself he hated Judge than admit he was just like her.
bs: Govorio je sam sebi da to ne želi učiniti, ali bio je uplašen. Kukavica. To je bilo bolje od alternative. Od toga da to zapravo želi učiniti jer je u njemu zijevala provalija bijesa koju nikad nije mogao ispuniti. Radije bi sam sebi lagao da mrzi Džadž nego priznao da je baš poput nje.

en: “I should pop your fucking head off,” said Broad. Not some wild, hissing threat. Just a dull observation. Bored, almost.
bs: — Trebao bih ti otkinuti tu jebenu glavu, rekao je Brod. Ne kao divlju, prijeteću galamu. Već kao dosadnu opservaciju. Gotovo nezainteresirano.

en: Bannerman was standing guard in the anteroom, sneer on his face and red paint all up his sleeves. Wasn’t long ago he’d been beating labourers for Savine dan Brock. Now he’d joined the Burners and was beating aristocrats for Judge and taking equal pleasure in his work. Chances are that men who’ll hurt folk for one master won’t flinch at hurting folk for another. It’s a job. A potter doesn’t need a grand cause to shape his clay for, does he? Why hold a thug to a higher standard?
bs: Banerman je stajao na straži u predsoblju, s podrugljivim cerekavanjem na licu i crvenom bojom po cijelim rukavima. Nije prošlo mnogo vremena otkako je mlatio radnike za Savine dan Brok. Sada se pridružio Paliocima i mlatio aristokrate za Džadž, uživajući u svom poslu jednako kao i prije. Vjerojatno je da Folk koji će nauditi drugima za jednog Majstora neće ustuknuti ni pred nanošenjem boli za drugoga. To je samo posao. Lončaru ne treba uzvišen cilj da bi oblikovao glinu, zar ne? Zašto bi se od

en: When she said better, did she mean they’d kill fewer? He’d a horrible feeling she meant they’d kill more.
bs: Kad je rekla bolji, je li mislila da će ubiti manje Folk? Imao je užasan osjećaj da je mislila kako će ih ubiti više.

en: He could kill her now. Catch her thin, rash-speckled throat and choke the life from it. Smash her head against the table, spray her blood across the tiles, easy as crushing a beetle. He could put an end to this madness.
bs: Mogao ju je sada ubiti. Zgrabiti njezin tanki, osipom posut vrat i istisnuti život iz njega. Razbiti joj glavu o stol, poprskati njezinu krv po pločicama, lako kao da gnječi kornjaša. Mogao je stati na kraj tom ludilu.

en: She grabbed him. Or did he grab her? They were kissing, anyway, if you could even call it kissing. Too hard, too violent, too painful for that. Growling and biting. Like they were eating each other.
bs: Zgrabila ga je. Ili je on zgrabio nju? u svakom slučaju, ljubili su se, ako se to uopće moglo nazvati ljubljenjem. Pregrubo, prenasilno, prebolno za to. Režali su i grizli, kao da su proždirali jedno drugo.

en: The procession wended from the gloom of falling snow. The Burners walked ten abreast in their paint-spattered clothes, their red-speckled armour, each of them holding high a torch, light falling hard on their hollow faces. Everyone else had to scrape out of their way, press themselves to the buildings and the doorways. Even Vick and her Constables and their prisoners.
bs: Povorka je mileći izranjala iz sumornog, snježnog meteža. Palioci su koračali desetorica u vrsti, u odjećama poprskanima bojom i crveno točkastim oklopima, a svaki je visoko držao baklju čija je svjetlost oštro padala na njihova upala lica. Svi su se ostali morali micati s njihova puta, pribijati se uz zgrade i dovratnike. Čak i Vik, njezini stražari i njihovi zatvorenici.

en: the Great Change, not even half-built beside the Four Corners, where the heroes of the Breakers and Burners were being laid to rest. “Let’s move!” she called, trudging on through the slush and the crowds and the frosty cold, past a great heap of burning books, pages occasionally floating on fire into the night, and down the echoing entrance tunnel of the Agriont.
bs: Velikog Gorenja, koji nije bio ni upola sagrađen pokraj Četiriju kutova, gdje su se heroji Lomljača i Palitelja polagali u vječni počinak. — Pokret!, pozvala je, probijajući se kroz bljuzgavicu, gomilu i prodornu hladnoću, kraj goleme gomile zapaljenih knjiga, čije su stranice povremeno u plamenu lebdjele u noć, pa sve do odzvanjajućeg ulaznog tunela Agrionta.

en: “All right, Tallow, I get the picture.” It was coming to something when a child of the prison camps was finding life in the capital too dark for comfort.
bs: — Dobro, Talou, shvaćam poantu. Bilo je doista prešlo svaku mjeru kada je dijete iz zatvorskih logora nalazilo da je život u glavnoj prebivališnoj zoni pretaman za utjehu.

en: “Not even then, I daresay.” Tallow glanced towards another sorry set of the accused being driven hunched through the snow. “But you might want to keep your voice down.”
bs: — Ni tada, usuđujem se reći. Talou baci Oko prema još jednoj skupini jadnih optuženika koje su pogurene gonili kroz snijeg. — Ali možda bi bilo pametno da malo stišaš glas.

en: There was no poetry to it. Scrawled on a scrap of candle-wrapper with a stub of charcoal from a dead fire. Just love, and best wishes, and keep going, and don’t forget me. She realised she’d no idea who to take it to. No idea who the woman had been. Could’ve been anyone. Could almost have been Vick herself. Except she had no one to write a letter to.
bs: U tome nije bilo poezije. Naškrabano na komadiću omota od svijeće, ugljenom iz ugašene vatre. Samo ljubav, najbolje želje, poruka da nastavi dalje i da je ne zaboravi. Shvatila je da nema pojma kome bi to trebala odnijeti. Nije imala pojma tko je ta žena bila. Mogla je biti bilo tko. Mogla je to gotovo biti i sama Vik. Osim što ona nije imala nikoga kome bi napisala pismo.

en: “Sworfene, and sadly no. Supply of late, what with the weather, and the politics, is something of a nightmare. If you can get stale bread from the end of the road you’re doing well. To get liquor in from Jacra requires a magician.” His hand skimmed across the bottles, then plucked one out. “Why don’t you…” And he slipped a glass in front of her and poured a shot. “Try this instead?”
bs: — Sworfene, i nažalost nemam. Opskrba je u zadnje vrijeme, zbog vremena i politike, prava noćna mora. Ako uspiješ nabaviti ustajali Hardbred na kraju ulice, dobro si prošla. Za dopremiti alkohol iz Jacre potreban je mađioničar. Ruka mu je prešla preko boca, a zatim jednu izvukla. — Zašto ne… I gurnuo je čašu pred nju te natočio piće. — Pokušaš li s ovim?

en: “The weather alone would be worth the trip. The time comes…” And he swallowed his shot in one and slapped the empty glass down on the bar. “You have to get out.”
bs: — Samo vrijeme bilo bi vrijedno puta. Dođe trenutak… Iskapio je piće u jednom gutljaju i tresnuo praznu čašu o šank. — Moraš otići.

en: Bloody hell, it was cold down here. But then it was cold everywhere. He took perverse pleasure in tolerating the same conditions his least fortunate subjects must be enduring. He used to have such privilege and such guilt. He felt far lighter, carrying neither one.
bs: Kvragu, ovdje dolje bilo je hladno. No bila je hladnoća posvuda. Nalazio je perverzno zadovoljstvo u podnošenju istih uvjeta kakve su morali trpjeti i njegovi najnesretniji podanici. Nekad je imao takve povlastice i takvu krivnju. Osjećao se mnogo lakšim ne noseći ni jedno ni drugo.

en: “Oh, you’ll love it,” said Halder, with a glance over his shoulder that implied he wouldn’t. Not that Orso had liked anything for some weeks now. Before the Great Change, he’d often joked that being High King of the Union was the worst job in the world. After the Great Change, it wasn’t even a joke. He’d heard they were selling night pots with his face on the inside of the bowl. Once, the ladies of Adua had scrambled into his bed. Now they queued up to shit on him. He could hardly say he didn’t
bs: — Oh, svidjet će ti se, odvrati Halder bacivši Oko preko ramena koji je davao naslutiti suprotno. Ne kao da se Orsu u posljednjih nekoliko tjedana išta svidjelo. Prije Velike promjene često se šalio kako je položaj Velikog kralja Unije najgori posao na svijetu. Nakon Velike promjene to više nije bila šala. Čuo je da prodaju noćne posude s njegovim licem na dnu posude. Nekad su se dame iz Adua otimale tko će prije u njegov krevet. Sad su stajale u redu da se poseru po njemu. Jedva da je mogao reć

en: The room was a sparse white box, plaster speckled with mould in one corner. There was something that looked like a badly scrubbed bloodstain on one badly whitewashed wall.
bs: Soba je bila oskudna bijela kutija, s gipsom koji se u jednom kutu ljuštio od plijesni. Na jednom loše okrečenom zidu nalazilo se nešto što je nalikovalo na grubo ispranu mrlju od krvi.

en: “We’re all in desperate straits.” Teufel slid out a stained slip of paper, very like the ones Hildi had been bringing him since Tunny’s visit to his attic. “Royalist traitors are pressing the People’s Army hard, out there in the east of Midderland. And from what I read, it looks like you’re in contact with Lord Marshal Forest.”
bs: — Svi smo u očajnoj situaciji. Tojfel izvuče umrljan komadić papira, vrlo sličan onima koje mu je Hildi donosila još od Tunnyjeva posjeta njegovu potkrovlju. — Rojalistički izdajnici snažno pritišću Narodnu armiju tamo na istoku Miderlanda. A prema onome što čitam, izgleda da ste u kontaktu s lordom maršalom Forestom.

en: When she spoke, her voice had turned oddly soft. “Forest isn’t the only one who’d like to see the monarchy restored.”
bs: Progovorivši, glas joj je postao neobično blag. — Forest nije jedini koji bi volio vidjeti obnovu monarhije.

en: Orso patted his trousers. “I seem to be a little light at the moment. In fact, I’ve a hell of a debt to my valet, you’d never guess what a shirt costs these days—”
bs: Orso se potapšao po hlačama. — Trenutočno mi se čini da sam pomalo kratak s novcem. Zapravo, dugujem prokletu silu novca svom sobaru, ne bi vjerovala koliko košulja danas košta…

en: “Vick.” She pressed her fist on the tabletop, took a long breath through her nose, and let it sigh away. “If we’re going down in flames together, it might as well be on first-name terms.”
bs: — Vik. Pritisnula je šaku o ploču stola, duboko udahnula kroz nos i ispustila uzdah. — Ako ćemo već zajedno izgorjeti, red je da budemo na ti.

en: She lifted him from his cot, quivering he was crying so hard. She held him close, shushing and cooing desperately. She pulled the door to and went to sit in one of the chairs beside the fire, the one with the shawl over the back that still smelled like her mother—
bs: Podigla ga je iz kolijevke; drhtao je jer je plakao tako silovito. Privila ga je uz sebe, očajnički ga umirujući i šapućući mu. Zatvorila je vrata i sjela u jednu od stolica pored vatre, onu s ogrtačem preko naslona koji je još uvijek mirisao na njezinu majku —

en: Silence stretched while they carefully considered one another, as they had a long time ago, when they shared a carriage on the way to Valbeck. “I suppose you have me there,” Savine admitted. Her trouble with Teufel was not that she was a liar, after all, but that she had proved herself a better liar than Savine. “Do you know where my father is?” she found she had asked.
bs: Tišina se razvukla dok su pažljivo odmjeravali jedno drugo, kao što su to činili davno, dijeleći kočiju na putu za Valbek. — Pretpostavljam da si me uhvatila, priznala je Savine. Njezin Trobli s Tojfel nije bio u tome što je ona lažljivica, naposljetku, već u tome što se pokazala boljom lažljivicom od Savine. — Znaš li gdje mi je otac?" uhvatila se kako pita.

en: There was a pause one could only have called pregnant. Savine spent it thinking of the old Union, her old life, her old self, and trying not to let her desperate yearning show. “I somehow doubt… that Judge would simply give the power back.”
bs: Nastade stanka kakva se mogla nazvati jedino nabijenom iščekivanjem. Savine ju iskoristi misleći na staru Unija, na svoj stari život, na svoju staru sebe, i trudeći se ne pokazati očajničku čežnju. — Nekako sumnjam… da bi Džadž naprosto vratila moć.

en: It all sounded depressingly plausible. “What exactly do you expect us to contribute?” asked Savine. For four chairs, she imagined it would be quite a lot.
bs: Sve je to zvučalo porazno uvjerljivo. — Što točno očekuješ da mi priložimo?" upitala je Savine. Za četiri stolice, pomislila je, to bi bilo poprilično mnogo.

en: Leo took a breath and sighed noisily through flared nostrils. “Great tempests wash up strange companions, Farans said.”
bs: Leo je duboko udahnuo i bučno izdahnuo kroz raširene nosnice. — Velike oluje na obalu izbacuju čudne suputnike, govorio je Farans.

en: “The way things are going, the bigger gamble would be to do nothing. We are living on borrowed time. Anyone who used to be powerful. Anyone who is powerful. All of us.”
bs: "s obzirom na to kako stvari stoje, veća bi kocka bila ne učiniti ništa. Živimo na posuđenom vremenu. Svatko tko je nekad bio moćan. Svatko tko jest moćan. Svi mi."

en: She’d never thought so when it was happening, but Rikke had to admit that she quite liked being bullied. She’d heaps of practice, and it brought out the stubborn best in her. Plucky Rikke. Everyone loved that girl. Sharp thinking, sharp talking, with the odds against her but right on her side.
bs: Sadržaj joj nikada ne bi pao na pamet dok se to događalo, ali Rike je morala priznati da joj se zapravo sviđalo maltretiranje. Imala je pregršt prakse, a to je iz nje izvlačilo njezinu najtvrdoglaviju najbolju stranu. Hrabra Rike. Svi su voljeli tu djevojku. Oštroga uma, oštra jezika, s izgledima protiv sebe, ali opravdano na svojoj strani.

en: But the Long Eye refused to open, and the answer was more’n likely neither one anyway, but somewhere in between, as answers always are. Times were hard, and she could squeeze more out of him, but it’d hurt. It’d hurt him, and it’d hurt her. It’d hurt him more, of course, but he’d only get squeezed once today. There was a whole queue of hat-twisters outside Skarling’s Hall ready to fling themselves onto their knees at the least provocation. If she was soft on one, she’d have to be soft on ’em all
bs: No dugo se oko odbilo otvoriti, a odgovor je vjerojatno bio nijedan od toga, nego negdje između, kao što odgovori uvijek jesu. Vremena su bila teška i mogla je izvući više iz njega, ali to bi boljelo. Boljelo bi njega i boljelo bi nju. Boljelo bi njega više, ali danas bi bio stisnut samo jednom. Naprijed Skarlingove dvorane bio je cijeli red vrtitelja šešira koji su se bili spremni baciti na koljena na najmanju provokaciju. Ako bude blaga prema jednomu, morala bi biti blaga prema svima njima. A

en: From her father it would’ve sounded patient and level-headed. From her it sounded like a thin-beer compromise. She saw it on the faces. Hardbread scratching his wispy pate. The warriors about the hall sighing away like bellows. Now every farmer in the North would be trying every trick to tickle out her mercy.
bs: Od njezina oca to bi zvučalo strpljivo i razborito. Od nje je zvučalo poput kompromisa s razvodnjenim pivom. Vidjela je to na njihovim licima. Hardbred češka rijetku tjemenu kosu. Ratnici oko dvorane uzdišu poput mehova. Sada bi svaki seljak na Sjeveru pokušao svakojakim trikovima izmamiti njezinu Grace.

en: Hardbread looked even more worried than usual. “We send men to fight the Nail, we’ll scarcely have enough to keep Carleon, let alone to hold the walls if Calder comes.”
bs: Hardbred je izgledao još zabrinutije nego obično. — Pošaljemo li ljude da se bore protiv Najla, jedva ćemo imati dovoljno Folk da zadržimo Carleon, a kamoli da držimo Tell ako dođe Kalder.

en: Rikke drew him close, lowering her voice. “As we discussed, now, Hardbread. You remember what we discussed?”
bs: Rike ga privuče bliže, stišavši glas. — Kao što smo dogovorili, sad, Hardbred. Sjećaš li se o čemu smo razgovarali?

en: “I know it’s a weight, having responsibility dropped on you from a height, all unexpected, believe me I know, but you’ve got the shoulders for a burden, eh?” And Rikke hugged her tighter, walking her towards the doors. “It’s a funny thing, isn’t it, how chance throws the right people in your path? But I daresay you want to check in on your grandmother. Make sure her fire stays banked in this weather.” Though it wasn’t near as cold as it had been, thaw water dripping from the archway above.
bs: — Znam da je to teret kad ti odgovornost sruče s visine, onako neočekivano, vjeruj mi da znam, ali imaš ti leđa za taj teret, jelda? I Rike je zagrli čvršće, vodeći je prema vratima. — Baš je čudno, zar ne, kako nas slučajnost nanosi na prave ljude? No usudila bih se reći da želiš obići baku. Pripaziti da joj Palioc ne trune po ovom vremenu. Iako nije bilo ni približno hladno kao prije, otopljena je voda kapala s Utočište iznad njih.

en: “Don’t toy with me, you old fucker, you know what I mean. Am I doing the right thing with Isern, with the Nail, with Black bloody Calder.” She waved a floppy hand at Skarling’s Chair and took the cage with Stour Nightfall in, too. “With all of it.”
bs: — Nemoj se igrati sa mnom, stari gade, znaš na što mislim. Radim li pravu stvar s Izern, s Najlom, s prokletim Blackom Kalderom? Mahnu opuštenom rukom prema Skarlingovoj stolici, a uze u obzir i kavez sa Staurom Najtfolom. — Sa svim tim.

en: Drip, drip, drip. Cold water, onto Clover’s head, his shoulders, his back, working its way through every seam, trickling, tickling against his sore and clammy skin.
bs: Kap, kap, kap. Hladna voda curi Kloveru na glavu, na ramena, niz leđa, probijajući se kroz svaki šav, curkajući i golicajući njegovu bolnu i oznojenu kožu.

en: It’d been a cold winter, snow banked up man tall in the High Places. With the weather tilting warmer, seemed the world was melting. Water dripped from the trees. Dripped from the eaves of Currahome’s sodden houses. Seeped through the boggy grass and gathered in the streams and swole ’em to dirty rivers. Downside came squelching over, knocking melting snow from the brambles.
bs: Bila je to hladna zima, snijeg se nakupio visoko poput čovjeka u Visoravni. Kako se vrijeme zagrijavalo, činilo se da se cijeli svijet topi. Voda je kapala s drveća. Kapala je s krovova blatnjavih kuća u Currahomeu. Procjeđivala se kroz močvarnu travu, skupljala u potocima i pretvarala ih u prljave rijeke. Dausaid je tromo gazio uokolo, otresajući otopljeni snijeg s kupina.

en: “High time,” grunted Downside with an approving nod, and you know you’ve a reckless notion on your hands when you win Downside’s approval.
bs: — Krajnje vrijeme, dometnu Dausaid uz odobravajući kim, a znaš imati ludu ideju na pameti kad zadobiješ Dausaidovo odobravanje.

en: “Like lazy fucks whose first preference is sitting under a tree and whose second is betraying you? Don’t try my patience, Clover, I’ve none to spare these days. We march today.”
bs: — Poput lijenih pizda kojima je prvi izbor sjedenje pod stablom, a drugi izdaja? Nemoj mi testirati strpljenje, Clove, nemam ga za bacanje ovih dana. Marširamo danas.

en: “I’ve got plans like I’ve got boots.” Clover frowned down at his waterlogged footwear. “Honestly, I could always do with better ones.”
bs: — Imam planova koliko i čizama. Klover se smrknuto zagleda u svoju promočenu obuću. — Bogami, uvijek bi mi dobro došao par boljih.

en: Snow swirled in through a broken window, bang, bang, banging a shutter against the frame and leaving a chilly puddle in the hallway. Some of them even had their faces smeared with crimson lady’s blusher, stuck somewhere between war-daubed savages from beyond the Crinna and murderous clowns.

en: It was busy in the tavern. Noisy with idle chatter and hot with wasted breath, the windows misted so the street outside became a sparkling blur. One of those places where rich young men gather to pretend to be poor young men, and vomit up whatever point of view they last heard. One of those places where rich young men once brayed for a Great Change, and now drank hard and hoped desperately it would go away again.

Rike je u tome pronašla hrabrost, premda joj je srce toliko snažno udaralo da se bojala kako bi ga Black Kalder mogao čuti, premda je bio udaljen dan ili dva.

en: “Better sad and alive, though. Shivers’ll help you.” Rikke was already strolling over to Stour’s cage. “And we’ve still got a card or two left to play.” There sat the used-to-be terror of the North, his eyes gleaming in the shadows, one limp leg hanging through the bars so his toes near brushed the stone.
bs: — Bolje tužna nego mrtva, međutim. Šivers će ti pomoći. Rike se već uputila prema Staurovu kavezu. — A u rukavu još imamo pokoju kartu. Tamo je sjedio nekadašnji strah i trepet Sjevera, a oči su mu sijevale u sjeni dok mu je jedna mlohava noga visjela kroz rešetke tako da su mu prsti zamalo doticali kamen.

en: A couple of weeks of marching and Black Calder’s carefully stitched-together host was coming apart at the seams. Men sick. Men hungry. Men frozen and frostbitten. Men sleepless and exhausted. Men so filth-caked they looked like devils, white eyes staring haunted from dirt-grey faces. Plenty more chosen to turn their backs on this boggy nightmare and run, in spite of the deserters strung from trees by the road and carved with the bloody cross, flyblown guts dangling. Scouts stared into their fire
bs: Nakon tjedan-dvije marširanja, vojska koju je Black Kalder brižljivo skrpao počela se raspadati po šavovima. Folk bolesni. Folk gladni. Folk smrznuti i ozebli. Folk neispavani i iscrpljeni. Folk toliko prekriveni blatom da su nalikovali na demone, bijelih očiju koje su usplahireno zurile s prljavosivih lica. Mnogi su drugi izabrali okrenuti leđa toj močvarnoj moriji i pobjeći, usprkos dezerterima obješenima o stabla uz cestu i izrezbarenima krvavim križem, s čijih su iskapljenih utroba visjele m

en: Clover had expected some raven-haired, brooding giant, like Stranger-Come-Knocking had been. But the new Chief of a Hundred Tribes was a colourless man, with whirls of grey scar cut into his hollow cheeks, thick veins showing in the skull-like rings under his eyes in which you almost thought you could see the blood pulse.
bs: Klover je očekivao nekakvog crnokosog, sumornog diva, kakav je bio Stranac-Come-Knocking. No novi poglavar Sto plemena bio je bezbojan čovjek, s krugovima sivih ožiljaka urezanima u upijene obraze, s debelim žilama koje su se ocrtavale u lubanjastim krugovima pod očima u kojima bi čovjek gotovo pomislio da vidi kako krv pulsira.

en: or beyond the Crinna, which was about the same thing—with various expressions of grim hate, shock, fear, outrage and disgust.
bs: Ili nasuprot tome Crinne, što mu je dolazilo na isto — s raznim izrazima sumorne mržnje, šoka, straha, gnjeva i gađenja.

en: Stand-i’-the-Barrows caught her chain from the bunch and dragged her towards him so sharply, the corner of the cart dug into her shoulder and she was knocked down in the mud. He wound the chain around his fist, hauling her bruised face up towards his, her bare toes scraping at the ground. “Did you not hear me? I asked what’s for dinner.”
bs: Grobovi je istrgnuo njezin lanac iz snopa i odvukao je k sebi tako naglo da joj se rub kola zabio u rame te se srušila u blato. Namotao je lanac oko šake, privukavši njezino modro lice svojemu, dok su joj se bosi prsti strugali po tlu. — Zar me nisi čula? Pitao sam što je za večeru.

en: “I mean…” Flick was looking down at himself, patting his chest as if picturing a costume like Stand-i’-the-Barrows wore. “Why cover yourself with bones?”
bs: — Mislim… Flik je gledao u sebe, potapšavši se po prsima kao da zamišlja nošnju kakvu je Grobovi nosio. — Zašto bi se prekrivao kostima?

en: “The sad truth is, men love to follow a man other men fear,” said Clover. “Makes them feel fearsome, too. We tell the odd fond story of the good men. The straight edges. Your Rudd Threetrees, your Dogmen. But it’s the butchers men love to sing of. The burners and the blood-spillers. Your Cracknut Whirruns and your Black Dows. Your Bloody-Nines. Men don’t dream of doing the right thing, but of ripping what they want from the world with their strength and their will.”
bs: — Tužna je istina da Folk vole slijediti onoga kojega se drugi boje, reče Klover. — Zbog toga se i sami osjećaju opasnima. Ponekad ispričamo pokoju dragu priču o dobrim ljudima. O onima pravednima. O vašem Ruddu Tri Drveta, vašim Dogmanima. Ali o mesarima Folk rado pjevaju. O paljacima i prolijevačima krvi. O vašem Cracknutima Whirrunima i vašim Black Dowovima. O vašem Bloody-Nineu. Folk ne sanjaju o tome da čine ono što je ispravno, nego da svojom snagom i voljom otmu iz svijeta ono što žele.

en: “They found the manager, then?” Tallow gave a long sniff as he looked up at the bank. Before the Great Change, Valint and Balk had towered over every scrap of business done in the Union, an untouchable colossus. Now the marble skin had been stripped from the pillars of its headquarters to show the cheap bricks beneath, the word Usurers slopped in red paint a thousand thousand times, all over the ruined façade.
bs: — Znači, našli su upravitelja? Talou je duboko udahnuo kroz nos dok je dizao Oko prema banci. Prije Velike promjene, Valint i Balk nadvijali su se nad svakim poslom sklopljenim u Uniji, nedodirljiv kolos. Sada je mramorna obloga bila oguljena s njegovih stupova kako bi se ukazala jeftina cigla ispod nje, dok je na uništenom pročelju crvenom bojom tisuću i tisuću puta bila ispisana riječ Kamatari.

en: She looked up at the towering door, feeling the need for something more momentous than the turning of a little rod of metal. But that’s how locks open. She slid the key into one of the keyholes and looked across at Pike as he did the same.
bs: Pogledala je prema golemim vratima, osjećajući potrebu za nečim značajnijim od okretanja komadića metala. Ali brave se tako otvaraju. Gurnula je ključ u jednu ključanicu i pogledala Pajka dok je on učinio isto.

en: “The power of Valint and Balk comes down to an empty vault.” Pike sounded almost impressed. “Just promises, just lies, just…”
bs: — Moć Valinta i Balka svodi se na prazan trezor. Pajk je zvučao gotovo zadivljeno. — Samo obećanja, samo laži, samo…

en: For a giddy moment, it didn’t quite register. Vick stood there with the puzzled frown of someone who sees blood squirting but hasn’t yet realised it’s their own throat that’s slit.
bs: U omamljujućem trenutku to joj nije sasvim doprijelo do svijesti. Vik je stajala ondje sa zbunjenim izrazom lica osobe koja vidi krv kako šiklja, a još nije shvatila da joj je prerezan vlastiti vrat.

en: “I always was,” said Vick. She thought of Sibalt, then. That sad little smile, in the half-light of the foundry, before the end. “But the time comes…” She supposed she could allow herself a little flourish. “You have to stand up.”
bs: — uvijek sam bila, odvratila je Vik. Tada se sjetila se Sibalta. Onog tužnog, sitnog osmijeha u polusvjetlu ljevaonice, prije kraja. — No dođe vrijeme… Pretpostavila je da si može dopustiti malo patetike. — Moraš ustati.

en: Outside in the chilly street the snow was still melting. The queues still stretching. The crier still busy with his list of doomed names.
bs: Vani se u prohladnoj ulici snijeg još topio. Redovi su se još uvijek pružali. Glasnik je i dalje revno čitao svoj popis osuđenih.

en: The hallway was full of children. Crowded with them, down both sides. Ragged. Scabbed. Filthy. Five or six haggard nurses stood among them, looking hardly better. Savine’s mother had insisted on fresh flowers here, every day. There were no flowers now. Someone had taken away the chandelier, and the place smelled stale. Savine forced a queasy smile onto her face. Nodded a greeting at no one in particular. She heard Zuri take a sharp breath, as unsettling from her as a scream of horror might have
bs: Hodnik je bio pun djece. Nakrcan njima, s obje strane. U rascjepkanim krpama. Krastavi. Prljavi. Pet ili šest ispijenih bolničarki stajalo je među njima, izgledajući jedva nešto bolje. Savinina majka inzistirala je na svježem cvijeću na ovom mjestu, svakoga dana. Sada nije bilo cvijeća. Netko je skinuo luster, a prostor je zaudarao po ustajalom zraku. Savine je na lice natjerala mučan osmijeh. Kimnula je u znak pozdrava nikome određenom. Čula je kako Zuri oštro uzima zrak, što je od nje bilo jed

en: The children crowded into the bare room were like some other species. Twisted, stunted, wounded, strange. Shafts of dusty light fell on ugly details. A great bloom of scabs on a hollow ribcage. A hunched shape, endlessly rocking. Mouths gaped and dribbled. Flies buzzed about leaking eyes. Some of them slumped, insensible. Some of them crouched, baring blackened teeth. They were thin as stray cats. They were mad as mean dogs. One girl had puke in her hair. One boy’s face was a mass of sores. Anot
bs: Djeca natrpana u goloj prostoriji bila su poput neke druge vrste. Iskrivljena, zakržljala, ranjena, čudna. Snopovi prašnjave svjetlosti padali su na ružne detalje. Great cvat krasta na upalim rebrima. Pognut oblik koji se unedogled njihao. Usta su bila otvorena i iz njih je curila slina. Muhe su zujale oko krezubih, vodenastih očiju. Neki od njih klonuli su u polusvijesti. Neki su čučali, pokazujući pocrnjele zube. Bili su mršavi poput uličnih mačaka. Bili su ludi poput opakih pasa. Jedna je dje

en: Savine felt Zuri’s reassuring touch on her shoulder. “You have done good here. All the good you could. Never forget that.”
bs: Savine osjeti Zuri ruku na svom ramenu koja ju je tješila. — Ovdje si učinila dobro djelo. Sve dobro što si mogla. Nikad to nemoj zaboraviti.

en: So it seemed Judge would finally have a genuine conspiracy to expose before the Court of the People. Teufel had been caught, or Orso had talked, or Leo had failed. While Savine was thinking that all was lost, she was also thinking that pikes were an absurd weapon for a confined space, and she felt tears in her eyes and almost giggled at once.
bs: Tako bi Džadž konačno imao pravu-pravcatu urotu koju će raskrinkati pred Sudom Naroda. Tojfel je bio uhvaćen, ili je Orso progovorio, ili je Leo podbacio. Dok je Savine razmišljala kako je sve propalo, istodobno joj je kroz glavu prošlo kako su pikes apsurdno oružje za zatvoreni prostor, pa su joj suze navrle na oči i zamalo se glasno nasmijala.

en: Sarlby held up a smudged document. “Citizeness Brock, you’ve been denounced—quite fucking spectacularly, as it happens—and are summoned to the House o’ Purity to await trial.”
bs: Sarlbi podigne zamazani dokument. — Građanko Brok, prijavljeni ste — sasvim jbno spektakularno, štoviše — te ste pozvani u Dom čistoće da pričekate suđenje.

en: “Don’t worry,” said Sarlby, giving her shoulder a reassuring pat. “You won’t have to wait long. You’ve been bumped right up the schedule. Friends in high places, eh?”
bs: — Ne brinite, reče Sarlbi, ohrabrujuće joj potapšavši rame. — Nećete morati dugo čekati. Pomaknuti ste sasvim na Kruna rasporeda. Prijatelji na visokim položajima, jelda?

en: There was a clattering above, the Burners bundling someone down the stairs. “We’ve got her!” one shouted in triumph. Savine realised with a lurch of horror that their prisoner was Zuri, wrists and ankles shackled with great black fetters, links a finger thick. She could hardly move for their weight.
bs: Odozgo se začulo tutnjanje dok su Palioci nekoga gurali niz stepenice. — Ulovili smo je!, pobjedonosno viknu jedan. Savine uz trzaj užasa shvati da im je zarobljenica Zuri, čija su zapešća i gležnjevi bili okovani velikim crnim verigama, karika debelih poput prsta. Jedva se mogla pomaknuti od njihove težine.

en: Broad winced, as if the sound of his first name was painful. “Not up to me,” he grunted, and he lifted a flask and took a little sip. “Up to the court.”
bs: Brod se trznuo, kao da mu je spomenut vlastiti nadimak bio bolan. — Ne odlučujem ja, promrmlja, pa podigne plosku i otpije gutljaj. — Odlučuje Sud.

en: He clenched his jaw, worked the sleeve up his numb arm to his shoulder, then whipped his right hand around behind his head—collar sliding between finger and thumb—and into the other armhole with a snapping of cloth, smooth as a step in a dance.
bs: Stisnuo je čeljust, nagurao rukav uz obamrlu ruku do ramena, a onda hitnuo desnu ruku iza glave — ovratnik mu je klizio između prsta i palca — i u drugi rukav uz prasak tkanine, gladak poput plesnoga koraka.

en: Jurand frowned down as he did up the buttons of Leo’s jacket, quick and practised as any valet. “Their men look almost as much of a mess as ours. Almost. There were more desertions in the night.”
bs: Džurand se namrštio gledajući dolje dok je zakopčavao dugmad na Leovoj jakni, brzo i vješto poput kakvog sobara. — Njihovi Folk izgledaju gotovo jednako raspušteno kao i naši. Gotovo. Noćas je bilo još dezertiranja.

en: “I’ll always be there.” Did Jurand reach gently for Leo’s useless hand, as if to help him with that, too? Leo took it first and awkwardly stuffed it into the gap in his jacket, turning to the mirror with a forced smile. “How do I look?”
bs: — uvijek ću biti ondje. Je li Džurand nježno posegnuo za Leovom beskorisnom rukom, kao da mu i u tome želi pomoći? Leo ju je prvi dohvatio i nespretno gurnuo u prorez na jakni te se s iznuđenim osmijehom okrenuo ogledalu. — Kako izgledam?

en: “I’m hoping for a happier outcome this time around,” said Leo. “Between you and me, I’m running out of limbs at quite a rate.”
bs: — Nadam se sretnijem ishodu ovog puta, reče Leo. — Među nama rečeno, ponestaje mi udova zabrinjavajućom brzinom.

en: Forest’s shoulders sagged slightly. “Since we’re being honest, I’ll take all the help I can get. Your men look in pretty poor shape, though.”
bs: Forestova su se ramena lagano spustila. — Kad već govorimo posve iskreno, dobro će mi doći svaka pomoć. Ipak, vaši Folk izgledaju prilično jadno.

en: “Then let’s make it a good one,” said Leo, turning his horse. “Glaward, give the order! We’re marching for Adua!”
bs: — Onda se pobrinimo da bude vrijedna spomena, izusti Leo okrenuvši konja."Glavard, izdaj zapovijed! Krećemo na Aduu!

en: No doubt there were a lot of the bastards. As many as Black Calder had brought to the Battle of Red Hill, maybe. A lot more than Rikke had been hoping for. Her own men looked sparse on the walkways atop Carleon’s walls. Nervous and lonely. Carls of Uffrith who’d served her father, far from home and with a leader who looked shakier every day.
bs: Nije bilo sumnje da je tih gadova bilo mnogo. Možda onoliko koliko ih je Black Kalder dovio na bitku kod Reda. Puno više nego što se Rike nadala. Njezini su Folk djelovali malobrojno na stazama Kruna Carleonovih zidina. Nervozno i usamljeno. Carls iz Afrita koji su služili njezinu ocu, daleko od doma i s vođom koja je svakim danom izgledala sve nesigurnije.

en: “I’m excited!” called Rikke, stretching up on tiptoes and forcing out a grin, like she knew just what was coming even if she was bubbling over with doubts. She clapped Corleth on the shoulder. She liked doing it. Her shoulders had a meaty, reassuring feel. “You excited?”
bs: — Uzbuđena sam! povika Rike, propinjući se na prste i izvlačeći silom osmijeh, kao da točno zna što dolazi usprkos tome što je kipjela od sumnji. Potapša Corleth po ramenu. Sviđalo joj se to činiti. Ramena su joj imala mesnat, umirujući dodir. — Jesi li ti uzbuđena?

en: He’d owned a horse once, long time ago, but only ’cause it was the type o’ thing folk expect a famous warrior to own. Didn’t think he’d ever ridden it. Except once, when he bought it, pretending he wasn’t scared witless he’d fall off, and only ’cause it was the type o’ thing folk expect someone to do when buying a horse. Rest of the time it just stood in a stable, looking sad, eating his hay and costing him money. Strange, how much of his time he’d spent worrying about what people expect. You’d
bs: Imao je on jednom konja, davno, ali samo zato što je to bila ona vrsta stvari koju svijet očekuje od slavnog ratnika. Mislio je da ga nikad nije jahao. Osim jednom, kad ga je kupio praveći se da nasmrt ne strahuje kako će pasti, i to samo zato što je to bila ona vrsta stvari koju čovjek učini kad kupuje konja. Ostatak vremena samo je stajao u štali, izgledajući tužno, jedući njegovo sijeno i gutajući mu novac. Čudno je koliko je vremena proveo brinući se o tome što Folk očekuju. Čovjek bi pomisl

en: Black Calder was having his own troubles getting mounted. He had to bounce a couple of times before he could haul himself into the saddle. He looked weak when he got there, and grey, and grim. Not much left of the handsome joker who nicked the North from under everyone’s noses. A man who’d lasted past his time. A man dragged back for one fight too many.
bs: Black Kalder se mučio s jahanjem. Morao se poskočiti nekoliko puta prije nego što se uspio otkotrljati u sedlo. Kad je napokon uspio, djelovao je slabo, sivo i sumorno. Malo je toga ostalo od onog naočitog mangupa koji je oteo Sjever svima iza leđa. Čovjeka koji je potrajao dulje nego što je trebao. Čovjeka kojeg su odvukli natrag u još jednu borbu previše.
