Dok je pozornost bila usmjerena drugamo, Savine se izvuče iza svoje lepeze i uze maleni prstohvat bisernog praha, trepćući trepavicama na ono slasno, okrepljujuće Veliko Gorenje u licu. Hvala Sudbinama, trgovina svake vrste opet je cvjetala, barem za one s novcem. Voljela je misliti da se promijenila, ali kraljeva majka, kao i svaka majka, povremeno treba malo nečega.

en: For a moment, Savine felt a sucking of terror. As if they might see through her, to all the secrets, and the guilt, and the things she wished she had not done. As if they might denounce her on the spot and drag her to the Tower of Chains.
bs: Na trenutak je Savine osjetila nalet užasa. Kao da bi mogli prozreti njezine tajne, svu krivnju i ono što je željela učiniti ne učiniti. Kao da bi je mogli smjesta optužiti i odvucarati u Toranj Chains.

en: She swallowed that horrible, lovely pearl dust bitterness and swept down the steps into the foyer. Her foyer. Once she had fought battles here. Now she reigned over the place as the unquestioned victor. The dozen armoured Anglanders who followed her everywhere she went were something of a clattering nuisance, and more had been posted at the theatre’s every doorway. She did wonder, in her more suspicious moments, whether Leo sent them to watch her as much as to protect her, but she supposed great
bs: Progutala je onaj užasan, divan gorki okus praha bisernice i sjurila se niz stube u predvorje. Svoje predvorje. Nekada je ovdje vodila bitke. Sada je vladala tim mjestom kao neprikosnovena pobjednica. Tušta oklopljenih Anglanđana koji su je pratili u stopu bili su pomalo zveckava napast, a još ih je bilo raspoređeno na svakom ulazu u kazalište. U trenucima sumnje doista se pitadva je li ih Leo poslao da je motre koliko i da je štuju, no zaključila je da velike ličnosti naprosto moraju imati prat

en: “A new and improved patent office must be the priority, Your Highness, everything is in turmoil, new standards for the new age…”
bs: — Prioritet mora biti nov i poboljšan patentni ured, Uzvišenost, sve je u previranju, novi standardi za novo doba…

en: “One minute past never,” she said, quickly checking the golden watch that had replaced the silver one around her neck.
bs: — Jednu minutu poslije nikada, odvrati ona, hitro provjerivši zlatni Straža koji je zamijenio srebrni oko njezina vrata.

en: Savine would not have been surprised if it turned out one of the best in history, especially since she’d bought up half the Arches, too. “For the sake of the tenants, you understand. Most of them are paying less than half rent.” For the time being, at least…
bs: Savine se ne bi iznenadila da se pokaže jednom od najboljih u povijesti, pogotovo otkad je otkupila i pola Archesa. — Zbog stanara, razumiješ. Većina ih plaća manje od pola stanarine." Barem za sada…

en: “Are you sure? I hear the easy manners of the Young Lion are not very much in evidence lately. He is proving to be far from agreeable when it comes to sharing power, and as vengeful as Glustrod at any hint of a slight—”
bs: — Jeste li sigurni? Čujem da lagodni maniri Mlada Lava nisu odveć primjetni u posljednje vrijeme. Pokazuje se prilično neraspoloženim kada je riječ o dijeljenju moći, a osvetoljubiv poput Glustroda na svaku naznaku uvrede —

en: Savine smiled. Is there anything finer than seeing an enemy humbled? “I have my moments. But we are all offered a new beginning, now. A chance to make ourselves afresh. You may not have covered yourself in glory in the Court of the People, but you emerged alive. You are ruthless, ambitious, clever and persistent. Qualities I could make use of, if you were willing to serve His August Majesty.”
bs: Savine se nasmiješi. Postoji li išta slađe od prizora raskajana neprijatelja? — Imam ja svojih trenutaka. No svima nam se sada pruža novi početak. Prilika da se iznova stvorimo. Možda se niste ovjenčali slavom u Narodnom sudu, ali izvukli ste se živi. Bezobzirni ste, ambiciozni, mudri i ustrajni. Osobine koje bih mogla iskoristiti, ako ste voljni služiti Njegovu Veličanstvu Augustu.

en: “I was very careful over the language in the Grand Declaration. The gender of the Closed Council’s members was nowhere specified. We did not get where we are by having too much respect for tradition, did we? I mean to be there, I promise you.”
bs: "Bila sam vrlo oprezna s formulacijom u Velikoj deklaraciji. Spol članova Zatvorenog vijeća nigdje nije izričito naveden. Nismo dospjele ovdje gajeći pretjerano poštovanje prema tradiciji, zar ne? Ja namjeravam biti ondje, uvjeravam te."

en: “Who’s hiding?” asked Savine, lifting her chin. “The Breakers did their worst in Valbeck, and here I am. The cannons did their worst at Stoffenbeck, and here I am. Judge did her worst on the Tower of Chains, and even so, here I am. You tried your very best to destroy me, too, as I recall, blabbing my ugliest secrets around town, and it only made me more powerful.”
bs: — Tko se sakriva? upita Savine uzdignuvši bradu. — Lomljači su dali sve od sebe u Valbeku, pa eto me ovdje. Topovi su dali sve od sebe u Štopenbeku, pa eto me ovdje. Džadž je dala sve od sebe na Tornju Okova, pa ipak, eto me ovdje. I ti si Dow sve od sebe da me uništiš, koliko se sjećam, razglašujući moje najružnije tajne po gradu, a to me učinilo samo moćnijom.

en: The vast banners of Angland and the Union covered the fronts of the warehouses entirely, billowing faintly with the sea breeze. The ranks of dark-uniformed soldiers stood to stiff attention. The buglers blew an awkward fanfare. The threadbare crowd gave scattered cheers as Lady Finree stepped to the quay, a few dozen seasick worthies of Angland in her wake.
bs: Goleme zastave Englenda i Unije prekrivale su pročelja skladišta, lagano lepršajući na morskom povjetarcu. Poredci vojnika u tamnim odorama stajali su u stavu mirno. Trubači su odsvirali nespretnu fanfaru. Izlizana gomila slabo je navijala dok je Lady Finri kročila na kej, a u stopu ju je pratilo nekoliko desetaka dostojanstvenika Englenda kojima je pozlilo od mora.

en: “No need!” he snapped, finally heaving himself free and twisting back into his seat, teeth gritted against the pain.
bs: — Nema potrebe! kresnu on, napokon se trgnuvši i uskočivši natrag na svoje sjedište, stisnutih zuba od bola.

en: His mother looked even more dismayed at that. “I remember what your father used to say… about the founding principles of the Union.” She had always thought Leo’s father was a fool, and he was starting to think she had been right. “You can have too much order, Leo. People need liberty.”
bs: Njegova majka djelovala je još potresenije na te riječi. — Sjećam se što je tvoj otac znao govoriti… o temeljnim načelima Unije." Oduvijek je smatrala da je Leo otac budala, a on je polako počinjao misliti da je bila u pravu. — Možeš imati previše reda, Leo. Ljudima treba sloboda.

en: “By the Fates,” breathed his mother, eyes wide at the sight. Leo had got used to the city’s scars, perhaps, the way he had to his own, but now he saw those fresh, too.
bs: — Tako mi Sudbine, udahnu majka, širom otvorenih očiju pri tom prizoru. Leo se možda naviknuo na gradske ožiljke, baš kao i na vlastite, ali sada je i on vidio one svježe.

en: “Very popular,” he said, grudgingly. “Have you had the bloody pamphlets up in Angland? Savine, bare-breasted in the Court of the People, shielding her babies from the spears of the Burners. Savine, duelling with Judge on the roof of the Tower of Chains and throwing her down like your bloody friend Bayaz threw down the Master Maker. Savine, bringing shelter to the orphans, bread to the starving, hope to the hopeless. The Darling of the Slums! The Mother of the Nation!” He gave a snort. “Anyone wo
bs: — Vrlo popularna, odgovorio je zlovoljno. — Jesu li i gore u Englendu dijelili one proklete letke? Savine, gologruda u Trgu Naroda, štiti svoju djecu od koplja Palitelja. Savine, u dvoboju s Džadž na krovu Kule Lanca, baca je dolje baš kao što je vaš prokleti prijatelj Bajaz bacio Majstora Umijeća. Savine, koja donosi sklonište siročadima, Hardbred gladnima, nadu beznadnima. Miljenica sirotinjskih četvrti! Majka Nacije! Zanjäkao je. — Čovjek bi pomislio da je sama okončala Veliku Promjenu.

en: “Feels like there are, though.” He frowned out of the window at the lonely well-wishers. “And everyone’s on hers.”
bs: — Čini se kao da ih ima, međutim. Namrštio se gledajući kroz prozor usamljene simpatizere. — I svi su na njezinoj strani.

en: Leo’s mother put her wrinkled nose close to Harod’s blankets. “His August Majesty has soiled himself.”
bs: Leova majka primaknu svoj naborani nos blizu Harodovih dekica. — Njegovo August Vaša Uzvišenosti se pokakalo.

en: It was only then he realised how much he’d wanted her approval. A man who’d made himself one of the most powerful in the Circle of the World, still endlessly trying and failing to impress his mother. The Lord Regent of the Union, jealous of his own babies.
bs: Tek je tada shvatio koliko je silno želio njezino odobravanje. Čovjek koji se prometnuo u jednog od najmoćnijih Folk u Krugu Svijeta, a još se uvijek neprekidno trudi i ne uspijeva impresionirati svoju majku. Lord namjesnik Unije, ljubomoran na vlastitu djecu.

en: Every grate of cutlery, every grind of crockery, every retch of conversation felt like a nail hammered into him.
bs: Svaki zvuk pribora za jelo, svako struganje posuđa, svaki kreštavi uzvik iz razgovora doimao se poput čavla zabijenog u njega.

en: He’d always imagined absolute power meant doing whatever you pleased, but it was starting to look like one sordid compromise after another. He wished he was back in Uffrith, among the Northmen, where you could say what you meant and eat any way you fucking pleased and a missing limb or two won you admiration rather than pity.
bs: Uvijek je zamišljao da apsolutna moć znači činiti što god ti je volja, ali sve je više nalikovala na niz nečasnih kompromisa. Poželio se vratiti u Afrit, među Sjevernjake, gdje si mogao reći što misliš i jesti kako ti se jebeno prohtije, a nedostajući ud ili dva donosili bi ti divljenje umjesto sažaljenja.

en: “But…” And Shudra raised his brows towards the empty chairs on the opposite side of the table. “It is most regrettable that Lord Governor Skald and the other representatives of Starikland have not attended.”
bs: — Ali… Šudra uzdiže obrve prema praznim stolicama na suprotnoj strani stola. — Iznimno je žalosno što lord guverner Skald i drugi predstavnici Stariklanda nisu došli.

en: There was an utter silence in the room. For a long moment, it seemed no one even breathed. Shudra winced slightly. Filio peered down at his meal. Out of the corner of his eye, he saw the tendons stand from the back of Savine’s hand as she gripped her fork as tightly as a standard-bearer might his flagstaff.
bs: U prostoriji zavlada potpuna tišina. Dug trenutak činilo se kao da nitko čak ni ne diše. Šudra se lako trznuo. Filio baci Oko na svoj obrok. Krajičkom oka vidio je kako su se tetive napeti na poleđini Savininih ruku dok je stiskala vilicu čvrsto poput barjaktara koji drži stijeg.

en: It was more of a relief than Leo had expected to find the old Savine beside him again. He turned his hand over and gripped hers tight. He needed her guile. He needed her popularity with the masses. The dead knew, he couldn’t do bloody everything himself.
bs: Bilo mu je veće olakšanje nego što je očekivao ponovno vidjeti staru Savine pored sebe. Okrenu ruku i čvrsto joj stisnu prste. Trebala mu je njezina lukavost. Trebala mu je njezina popularnost u narodu. Mrtvi znaju, nije mogao sve jebeno sam obaviti.

en: Orso served up another sigh. In truth, he could hardly blame them. He was the son of a bastard himself, after all. And people were desperate, exhausted, sick of chaos, sick of fear. He would have happily voted for anything that brought the Great Change to an end himself. It was just a shame for him that this ending almost certainly meant his death.
bs: Orso je isporučio još jedan uzdah. Doista, jedva im je mogao zamjeriti. Uostalom, i sam je bio kopile. A Folk su bili očajni, iscrpljeni, siti kaosa, siti straha. I sam bi rado glasovao za bilo što bi okončalo Veliku promjenu. Jedino je po njega bilo porazno što je taj kraj gotovo Sejf značio njegovu smrt.

en: “Most becoming. I’m not sure how one refers to a deposed king. Am I deposed? Or retired? Or simply… unmentionable?”
bs: "Više nego prikladno. Nisam siguran kako se uopće obraća svrgnutom kralju. Jesam li svrgnut? Ili umirovljen? Ili naprosto… nespomenut?

en: “Tunny?” breathed Orso. He was followed by a girl in a soldier’s cap, a big man at her back, sliding heavy swords into his belt. “Hildi? Gorst, by the Fates!” Orso used to be thoroughly dismayed at the sight of his father’s bodyguard. Now he seized his hand and pumped it like an old friend’s, much missed.
bs: — Tani?, prosu Orso dah. Za njim uđe djevojka s vojničkom kapom, a krupni muškarac joj je bio za petama, umećući teške mačeve u remenje. — Hildi? Gorsta mi, tako im Sudbina! Orso bi se nekada nasmrt zaprepastio ugledavši tjelohranitelja svoga oca. Sada ga uhvati za ruku i prodorno je stisne poput staroga, silno željenoga prijatelja.

en: It was Jurand who appeared in the doorway first, staring into the cell with its bed, chair, table and instantly obvious lack of an imprisoned king.
bs: Džurand se prvi pojavio na vratima, zagledan u ćeliju s krevetom, stolicom, stolom i bjelodano očiglednim nedostatkom sužanj-kralja.

en: She had raised her fist to shake it in his face and Leo noticed the rolled-up paper she was gripping. “What’s this?”
bs: Podignula je stisnutu pesnicu da mu njome zaprijeti pred licem, a Leo je primijetio smotani papir koji je držala. — Što je ovo?

en: “You’d hand him to the Styrians?” Leo looked at her in shocked disappointment. “You’d make a weapon of him, for our enemies to use against us?”
bs: "Predao bi ga Styrijskim brodovima?" Leo ju je pogledao s prijekorom i šokiranim razočaranjem. — Napravio bi od njega oružje koje bi naši neprijatelji upotrijebili protiv nas?

en: They clattered towards the Duke Rogont’s gangplank, half-hidden among a mass of boxes and barrels. The leading man looked sideways, took a whooping breath, then flew from the wharf and tumbled flailing into the sea. Leo winced as he skittered to an ungainly halt.
bs: Strka ih ponese prema skeli Vojvode Rogonta, napola sakrivenoj među gomilom sanduka i bačava. Vodeći čovjek pogleda u stranu, udahnu zrak u kriku, a zatim skoči s doka i uz mlataranje rukama sune u more. Leo se zacrvenje dok se spretno zaustavi u mjestu.

en: He’d never seen Gorst smile before. He’d seemed a man incapable of expressions. But he smiled now as he raised his steels, metal flashing in the sun. Like a man who feels a wonderful relief. “In the name of King Orso,” he piped, his boots grinding into the weathered wood as he lowered himself into a ready crouch, “no.”
bs: Nikad prije nije vidio Gorsta da se smije. Djelovao je kao čovjek nesposoban za izraze lica. No sada se nasmiješio podižući čelike dok mu je metal bljeskao na suncu. Poput čovjeka koji osjeća predivno olakšanje. — U ime kralja Orsa, zacvrkutao je dok su mu se čizme urezivale u trošno drvo dok se spuštao u borbeni stav, ne.

en: Blood sprayed over Gorst, speckled his face, flooded across the wharf. Men stepped back in shock, opening a path. Flatbows clicked and rattled. One man cried out as he was nailed in the back by a stray bolt. Another sank into Gorst’s meaty shoulder. A third bounced from his breastplate. A fourth caught him in the right arm, dangling from his sleeve. He whipped out of the way, behind some crates, as a fifth buried itself in the wood.
bs: Krv je šiknula po Gorstu, poprskala mu lice, prolila se po rivi. Folk su šokirano odskočili, otvarajući prolaz. Samostreli su kliktali i zveckali. Jedan je čovjek zavrištao kad ga je zalutala strijela pogodila u leđa. Druga se zabila u Gorstovo mesnato rame. Treća se odbila od njegovog oklopa. Četvrta ga je pogodila u desnu ruku, viseći mu s rukava. Izmaknuo se u stranu, iza nekih sanduka, dok se peta zabila u drvo.

en: Planks rattled under Gorst’s boots. A flatbow bolt pinged off his breastplate. Another sank into the same shoulder he was already stuck in. He barely noticed, coming on faster and faster, twisted face speckled red, eyes fixed on Leo under his furiously wrinkled brows, short steel going up high.
bs: Dasčice su zveckale pod Gorstovim čizmama. Strijela iz samostrela odskočila mu je od oklopa. Druga se zabila u isto rame u koje mu je već bila zabodena. Jedva ju je primijetio, jurišajući sve brže, izobličena lica poprskana krvlju, očiju uprtih u Lea ispod bijesno naboranih obrva, podižući kratki mač visoko u zrak.

en: “Fucking pointless,” hissed Leo, kicking Gorst’s short steel skittering into the sea with a swing of his iron leg. There’d been a time when he’d admired that man more than anyone. When he’d wanted to be just like him. “Goes to show,” he grunted, “you have to be your own hero.” He limped on towards the gangplank, past the corpses and the sobbing man still trying to hold his guts in.
bs: "Jebeno besmisleno", prozbori Leo pa zamahom željezne noge šutnu Gorstov kratki mač da je zveckajući kliznuo u more. Bilo je vrijeme kad se tom čovjeku divio više nego ikome. Kad je želio biti baš poput njega. — Tako ispada, progunđa, moraš sam sebi biti heroj." Nastavio je šepati prema skeli, mimo leševa i onog muškarca koji je još uvijek jecajući pridržavao svoja crijeva.

en: “I gave the orders as soon as we found Orso wasn’t in his cell,” said Jurand. “There’s a company at every gate, Arnault’s Wall and Casamir’s. Others out combing the streets. A rat won’t leave Adua without us knowing.”
bs: — Dow sam zapovijedi čim smo otkrili da Orsa nema u ćeliji, reče Džurand. — Na svakim je vratima satnija, na Arnaultovim zidinama i Casamirovim. Drugi češljaju ulice. Nijedan štakor neće napustiti Aduu a da mi to ne saznamo.

en: “What would I do without you?” Orso watched the stained sheds of warehouses and manufactories slide by. “I hope Gorst got away.”
bs: — Što bih ja bez vas? Orso je promatrao kako pokraj njih klize zapuštene barake skladišta i manufaktura. — Nadam se da je Gorst uspio pobjeći.

en: Orso retreated into his tarp, working his back against the coal. He could not help wondering about a world in which he simply… let it go. Folded his hand and let the Young Lion have it all. Found some unregarded corner in which to live in harmless obscurity. No more fighting. No more deaths on his account. No more crushing responsibilities.
bs: Orso se povukao pod svoju ceradu, prislonivši leđa uz ugljen. Nije se mogao oteti pomisli o svijetu u kojem jednostavno… sve to pusti. Prizna poraz i prepusti sve Mlađem Lavu. Pronađe neki zabačeni kutak u kojem će živjeti u bezimenoj tami. Nema više borbe. Nema više smrti na njegovu dušu. Nema više pritiska golemih odgovornosti.

en: “And a lot more organised.” Tunny hopped from the barge onto the towpath, holding out his hand to help Orso across. “Time to go.”
bs: — I puno organiziraniji. Tani poskoči s barže na stazu za tegljenje, ispruživši ruku kako bi pomogao Orsu da prijeđe. — Vrijeme je za pokret.

en: Sun just up as Broad made his last preparations. Straightened the plates on the rack. Kind of plates Liddy had always admired. Shifted the flowers about in the vase. Only things he knew about flowers were that they show up in spring and May liked ’em. Then he took off his lenses, and wiped them, and put them back on, and stood there, frowning.
bs: Sunce se tek diglo dok je Brod obavljao posljednje pripreme. Poravnao je tanjure na stalku. Baš takve tanjure Lidi je uvijek obožavala. Premjestio je cvijeće u vazi. Jedino što je znao o cvijeću bilo je to da niče u proljeće i da ga Mej voli. Zatim je skinuo naočale, obrisao ih, vratio ih na lice i stajao ondje mršteći se.

en: But the path leading out was a coward’s path. He took a sharp breath and clenched his aching fists. If there was one good word said over his grave, it’d be that Gunnar Broad was no coward. It’d be a lie, but still.
bs: Ali staza koja vodi van bila je kukavička staza. Duboko je udahnuo i stisnuo bolne šake. Ako se nad njegovim grobom prozbori ijedna lijepa riječ, bit će to da Gunar Brod nije kukavica. Bila bi to laž, ali svejedno.

en: After a while, when his sobs started to calm, she put her hands on his cheeks and lifted his head so she was looking straight up at him, calm and serious. She wiped the tears from his face and traced the healing scratches with her thumbtip.
bs: Nakon nekog vremena, kad mu se jecaji počeše smirivati, spusti ruke na njegove obraze i podigne mu glavu tako da ga je gledala ravno u oči, smirena i ozbiljna. Obriše mu suze s lica i vrhom palca pređe preko ozljeda koje su zacjeljivale.

en: “Money’s where the money is, Da. Well… that and labour relations.” She said the words with this knowing twist to her grin that made Broad go cold.
bs: "Novac je tamo gdje je novac, Da. Pa… to i radni odnosi." Izgovorila je te riječi uz onaj pronicljivi grč u osmijehu od kojeg je Broadhu prostrujala hladnoća.

en: It came out all right. Broad’s mouth felt dry. Wanted a drink so bad. He’d been fixed on not saying anything, but now he felt he had to be honest, blurt it all out. Burn it down like the Lords’ Round so they could somehow start fresh.
bs: Dobro je ispalo. Brodu su usta bila suha. Toliko je želio piti. Bio je čvrsto odlučio šutjeti, ali sada je osjećao da mora biti iskren, sve izlanuti. Spaliti sve do temelja poput Vijećnice Lordsa kako bi nekako mogli početi iznova.

en: A thumping knock at the door made Broad jump. He wanted to tell Liddy not to answer it. To leave them as they were, for a little longer. But she was already on the way.
bs: Teško kucanje na vratima trgnulo je Broda. Htio je reći Lidi neka ne otvara, da ih ostavi onakvima kakvi jesu, još samo malo. Ali ona je već bila na putu.

en: “So.” Savine raised one brow at him as she lowered herself, gracefully as ever, into one of his new leather-covered chairs. “It must be lovely to have the family back together—”
bs: — Dakle. Savine je digla obrvu i spustila se, graciozno kao obično, u jednu od njegovih novih kožnih fotelja. — Mora da je divno ponovno imati obitelj na okupu –

en: Broad swallowed. “But… Liddy and May, they just got here.” A pathetic whine of an excuse. Like saying he couldn’t murder anyone today ’cause he had to trim his fingernails.
bs: Brod proguta knedlu. — Ali… Lidi i Mej, tek su stigle." Jadna isprika, poput žalopojke. Poput tvrdnje da danas ne može nikoga ubiti jer mora podrezati nokte.

en: “Jurand!” She ignored his hand and gave him a hug instead. “Still…” She waved a hand at him, trying to find the right words. “Juranding, then?”
bs: — Džurand! Zanemarila je njegovu ruku i umjesto toga ga zagrlila. — I dalje… Odmahnula je rukom prema njemu, tražeći prave riječi. — Juranduješ, dakle?

en: “Touched,” said Rikke. “I never feel so safe as when I’m surrounded by heavily armed strangers.” Took her a moment to mount up, as she wasn’t much happier on a horse than a ship. “Must confess I was a smidge worried Leo and Savine might not be all that pleased to see me.” Rikke nudged her mount close to Jurand and murmured out of the corner of her mouth. “I did betray ’em, after all. Just a bit.”
bs: — Dirnuta, odvrati Rike. — Nikad se ne osjećam sigurnije nego kad sam okružena do zuba naoružanim Strancima. Trebalo joj je malo vremena da uzjaše, budući da joj konji nisu bili ništa draži od brodova. — Moram priznati da me malo brinulo to što Leo i Savine možda neće biti odveć oduševljeni mojim dolaskom. Rike približi svog konja Džurandu i prošapta preko usta: — Uostalom, izdala sam ih. Samo malo.

en: Isern looked shocked to her roots. “Lies! I am all yielding fellowship and good humour! I like Shivers.”
bs: Izern je izgledala duboko potreseno. — Laži! Ja sam sama srdačnost i dobro raspoloženje! Sviđa mi se Šivers.

en: “And you’re shifting me in the right direction. Love easily given isn’t worth a thing, d’you see. Another few years and I might like you as much as my brothers.” She twisted in her saddle to look at Scofen and Scenn, gazing about at the great soot-streaked buildings in amazement.
bs: — I pomičeš me u pravom smjeru. Ljubav koja se lako poklanja ne vrijedi pišljiva boba, vidiš. Još koju godinu pa bi mi se mogla svidjeti koliko i moja braća. Okrenula se u sedlu kako bi pogledala Skofena i Skenna, koji su u čudu promatrali goleme zgrade umrljane čađom.

en: “I understand there is an urgent need for loans and investment. For new business and construction. The Lady Regent has plans… to build the world’s largest bank.”
bs: — Shvaćam da postoji hitna potreba za zajmovima i ulaganjima. Za novim poslom i gradnjom. Gospođa namjesnica ima planove… izgraditi najveću banku na svijetu.

en: The hall alone was big as a chieftan’s audience chamber and a lot finer furnished. Two well-turned-out women were waiting there, one older, one younger, with a dark-skinned fellow wide as a door. They looked a bit shocked at Rikke’s face, for which she hardly blamed them; she still jumped herself whenever she passed a mirror. They looked more shocked as Shivers loomed up behind her, then very shocked indeed as the fur- and mail-clad Named Men and the tattooed hillfolk and some great tall woman w
bs: Samo je predvorje bilo veliko poput poglavičine dvorane za prijeme i mnogo raskošnije uređeno. Tamo su čekale dvije dotjerane žene, jedna starija, jedna mlađa, s tamnoputim momkom širokim poput vrata. Djelovali su pomalo zatečeno Rikkeinim licem, što im nije mogla zamjeriti; i sama bi poskočila svaki put kad bi prošla pokraj ogledala. Djelovali su još šokiranije kad se Šivers nadvio iza nje, a onda posve šokirani kad su se Folk s imenom ogrnuti krznom i oklopom, tetovirani gorštaci i neka golema

en: “You help make Lady Savine look all…” And Rikke waved her hands around, searching for the word. “Savine-y?”
bs: — Pomažeš li lady Savine izgledati sva ono… I Rike mahnu rukama u zraku tražeći pravu riječ. — Savine-y?

en: Leo was in no mood to heal wounds. He stood grim and aloof, as usual, surrounded by armed Anglanders, as usual, refusing to sit down, as usual. He had taken Adua in a vice-like grip the day Judge fell, but since Orso’s escape, and with Jurand to help, he had instigated a crackdown far harsher than any the Burners had dreamed of.
bs: Leo nije bio raspoložen za zacjeljivanje rana. Stajao je smrknut i otuđen, kao obično, okružen naoružanim Anglanđanima, kao obično, odbijajući sjesti, kao obično. Čvrsto je zagospodario Aduom onog dana kad je Džadž pao, no nakon Orsova bijega, uz Džurandovu pomoć, pokrenuo je čistku oštru kakvu ni Palioci nisu mogli zamisliti.

en: “Savine!” And Rikke slipped between her outstretched hands and folded her in a hug. Savine could hardly remember the last time anyone held her that way, and she found herself squeezing Rikke back, as if they truly were old friends, with no jealousies or rivalries or backstabbings behind them.
bs: — Savine! I Rike se izvila između njezinih ispruženih ruku i privukla je u zagrljaj. Savine se jedva sjećala kad ju je netko posljednji put tako držao, pa se i sama uhvatila kako uzvraća stisak, kao da su doista stare prijateljice, bez ikakvih ljubomora, rivalstava ili zabadanja noževa u leđa.

en: “Chiselled into my memory.” Savine wondered how many people who had laughed, and drunk, and danced in the Hall of Mirrors that night were dead now. Half? More? A chilly gust swept across the gardens and it was the most she could do not to shiver.
bs: — Urezano u moje pamćenje. Savine se upitala koliko je Folk koji su se smijali, pili i plesali u Dvorani ogledala te večeri sada mrtvo. Polovica? Više? Prohladan je nalet vjetra prešao preko vrtova i jedva se uspjela suzdržati da ne zatreperi.

en: “Ha again! You were kind to me that night and you’re being kind now. You’re a lot kinder than folk make out.”
bs: — Ha, opet! Bila si dobra prema meni te noći, a dobra si i sada. Puno si ljubaznija nego što Folk priča.

en: Rikke held on to Savine’s arm as she stifled a sneeze, then pulled a little brown pellet from her glove and held it out. “We can swap gifts this time, too.”
bs: Rike se uhvati za Savininu ruku dok je gušila kihanje, a zatim izvuče malu smeđu kuglicu iz rukavice i pruži je. — I ovaj put možemo razmijeniti darove.

en: “Civilisation just finished a round of slaughter to make the Bloody-Nine blush. The North has some remarkable natural advantages—”
bs: — Civilizacija je upravo završila Round klanja zbog kojeg bi i Krvavi Nine pocrvenio. Sjever ima neke izuzetne prirodne prednosti…

en: “Oh, you didn’t come out of it too badly. Stour Nightfall did the same and he’s hosting no garden parties, I promise you.” From a few strides off one would have taken it all for good-natured blather. But there was an edge on Rikke’s every word. A conversation with her was a cake full of razors.
bs: — Oh, nisi prošla tako loše. Staur Najtfol prošao je isto, a ne priređuje nikakve vrtne zabave, uvjeravam te. S udaljenosti od nekoliko koraka sve bi zvučalo kao dobroćudno čavrljanje. No svaka je Rikina riječ nosila oštricu. Razgovor s njom bio je poput torte punjene britvama.

en: It should have been a palace function where he finally felt at home. It was his home now, after all. He’d earned it. He’d won it. And it was full of Northmen. The feel of the gardens was closer to the Dogman’s old hall in Uffrith than the stuffy receptions of King Jezal’s reign.
bs: Trebala je to biti palača u kojoj će se napokon osjećati kao kod kuće. Uostalom, to je bio njegov dom. Zaslužio ga je. Osvojio ga je. A bio je pun Sjevernjaka. Ugođaj u vrtovima više je podsjećao na staru dvoranu Psa Čovjeka u Afritu nego na zagušljive prijeme iz vladavine kralja Džezal.

en: He took a sour slurp of wine, watching Rikke plough through the throng. She didn’t work the crowd with Savine’s silky subtlety. She did it in a way all her own, with her big smile and her crazy eyes and that easy laughter and those wild gestures, wine sloshing from her glass as she threw up an arm.
bs: Gucnuo je oporog vina promatrajući Rike kako se probija kroz gomilu. Ona nije šarmirala svjetinu onom svilenkastom suptilnošću kakvu je imala Savine. Činila je to na svoj način, sa svojim širokim osmijehom i ludim očima, s onim lakim smijehom i divljim gestama, dok joj se vino prosipalo iz čaše kad god bi podigla ruku.

en: He felt himself blushing, the way his mother always made him blush when a conversation didn’t go her way. “Everyone had fun that night,” he said, stiff and unconvincing, “and everyone’s having fun now,” managing to sound bitter, too.
bs: Osjetio je kako crveni, onako kako bi ga majka uvijek zacrvenjela kad razgovor ne bi tekao po njezinu. — Te noći su se svi zabavljali, reče ukočeno i neuvjerljivo, a svi se zabavljaju i sada, uspjevši zvučati i prilično ogorčeno.

en: But those children were long gone. Leo hadn’t chosen to make himself fearsome, but that was what the times demanded. For the sake of the country, his family, his wife. Whether they thanked him or not. Softness now was weakness. Weakness now was death. He could see no way back.
bs: No ta su djeca odavno nestala. Leo nije izabrao postati strašan, ali vremena su to zahtijevala. Zbog zemlje, svoje obitelji, svoje žene. Bilo da mu zahvaljivali ili ne. Mekoća je sada bila slabost. Slabost je sada bila smrt. Nije vidio put natrag.

en: Rikke narrowed her eyes, the tattoos on her forehead twisting as she frowned. Somewhere in the distance there was a soft rumble of thunder. “Your wife stabbed me in the back the first chance she got. Bought the Great Wolf’s help with my home.” Here was a part of the story Savine had conveniently left out. Leo stared over at his wife, standing beside the Great Machinist in her usual dazzling white, and found her looking back. Studying them. Trying to gauge what they might be saying, and how to tu
bs: Rike je stisnula oči, a tetovaže na njezinu čelu iskrivile su se dok se namrštila. Negdje u daljini začula se prigušena grmljavina. — Tvoja mi je žena zabila nož u leđa čim joj se pružila prilika. Platila je pomoć Velikog Vuka mojim domom." Ovo je bio dio priče koji je Savine zgodno izostavila. Leo je pogledao svoju ženu, koja je stajala pored Velikog Mehaničara u svojoj uobičajenoj blistavoj bjelini, i primijetio da ona gleda njega. Proučava ih. Pokušava odgonetnuti o čemu razgovaraju i kako to

en: “So did I. But apparently I’ve been wrong about a great many things.” By the dead, what Leo really wanted was for her to put her arms around him and hold him the way she’d held Savine. But somehow, without meaning to, he’d made himself into a man no one wanted to touch. “It’s good to see you again, Rikke. Really it is. I miss what we had. Really I do.”
bs: — Tako sam i ja mislio. No očito sam bio u krivu o mnogim stvarima. Tako mi mrtvih, Leo je doista želio zagrliti ga i stisnuti onako kako je zagrlila Savine, ali htio je i pitati… No nekako je, i ne hoteći, od sebe stvorio čovjeka kojeg nitko nije želio dotaknuti. — Lijepo te opet vidjeti, Rike. Doista jest. Nedostaje mi ono što smo imali. Stvarno nedostaje.

en: And he turned on his heel and strode back into the palace. Or came as close to striding as he could, metal ankle squeaking with each lurching step.
bs: I okrenuo se na peti te se vratio krupnim koracima u palaču. Ili onoliko krupnim koliko je mogao, dok mu je metalni gležanj škripao sa svakim posrtajućim korakom.

en: “Tongues neatly extracted from my rear and slipped between the Young Lion’s scarred buttocks without so much as a blush, no doubt. They used to huddle around me at those bloody events like geese at the trough.”
bs: — Jezici uredno izvučeni iz moje stražnjice i uvučeni među ožiljkaste stražnjice Mlađeg Lava bez imalo rumenila, nesumnjivo. Okupljali bi se oko mene na tim krvavim događajima poput gusaka oko jasala.

en: “Two hundred and sixteen marks…” Hildi was pretending her eyes were wet from the rain and fooling no one. “And thirty bits.”
bs: — Dvjesto šesnaest maraka… Hildi se pretvarala da su joj oči vlažne od kiše i nije zavaravala nikoga. — I trideset novčića.

en: “Thank you very much,” she said, patting his arm. Quite an arm, far as she could tell. Then she teetered across the slick cobbles towards the steps. Bloody things wouldn’t stay still, wobbling about all over the place. Or was that her? She was drunk as shit and making no apologies.
bs: — Puno ti hvala—, reče tapšajući ga po ruci. Kakva ruka, koliko je mogla primijetiti. Zatim se zateturala preko skliskog kamenja prema stepenicama. Proklete stvari nisu mogle mirovati, lelujajući se na sve strane. Ili je to bila ona? Bila je pijana kao majka i nije se namjeravala ispričavati.

en: “Shit on that.” Isern turned the doorknob and they spilled into the hall together, leaving a crooked trail of wet footprints. “You’re the North now, and the North kneels to no one. Besides, a man who’s moved by grovelling will never get enough grovelling for his taste. Let him once set his foot on your back and you’ll have a fucking bootprint ’twixt your shoulder blades till the day you’re buried. What’re you doing still up?”
bs: — Ma idi u pičku materinu. Izern okrenu kvaku i njih dvije utrčase zajedno u hodnik ostavljajući za sobom krivudav trag mokrih stopa. — Ti si sada Sjever, a Sjever ne kleči ni pred kim. Osim toga, čovjeka kojeg dirne nečije puzanje nikada neće zasititi to silno puzanje. Daj mu samo jednom da ti stane nogom na leđa i imat ćeš jebeni otisak čizme između lopatica sve do dana kad te zakopaju. Što još radiš budna?

en: “You look…” She took a step or two into the room. Felt like she couldn’t help it. “A touch less prosperous than last time we met.”
bs: — Izgledaš… Zakorači korak-dva u prostoriju. Osjećala je kao da si ne može pomoći. — Nešto malo manje imućno nego kad smo se posljednji put vidjeli.

en: “Never mind that!” said Rikke, herding her towards the door. She was keenly aware of how dangerous it was. Maybe that was the appeal. Maybe she was a moth drawn to the flame and would very soon go up in a fireball.
bs: — Ma nemoj brinuti o tome! odvrati Rike, gurajući je prema vratima. Bila je i te kako svjesna koliko je to opasno. Možda je u tome i bio privlačan dio. Možda je bila poput moljca privučenog plamenom koji će se vrlo brzo pretvoriti u buktinju.

en: “I’ll confess I’m fucking astonished.” But the truth was Rikke was glad to see him, and not just because of the pearl dust and the drink. Though partly because of the pearl dust and the drink. And partly because he was handsome, and funny, and charming, and the certain knowledge that he was a very excellent lover was kissing constantly at the back of her pearl-dusted mind. She had to keep herself hidden, these days. Behind the tattoos and the knowing smiles and the stony heart. With him, she cou
bs: — Moram priznati da sam u pičku materinu zapanjen. No istina je bila da mu se Rike obradovala, i to ne samo zbog bisernog praha i pića. Mada dijelom i zbog bisernog praha i pića. A dijelom i zato što je bio zgodan, duhovit i šarmantan, dok joj se u prikrajku uma, zasutog bisernim prahom, neprestano motala misao kako je bio izvanredan ljubavnik. Ovih se dana morala skrivati. Iza tetovaža, proračunatih osmijeha i kamenog srca. S njime se mogla opustiti i pokazati kakva jest.

en: “No doubt. We’re all of us changed.” All the things seen since then. The things done. The people gone back to the mud. He’d lost his throne, she’d gained one. But as she came close and took the glass from his hand, he had that same look in his eyes he’d had that night. That look of unguarded desire. And being looked at that way felt just as good. Better’n ever, maybe.
bs: — Nema sumnje. Svi smo se promijenili. Sve ono što se vidjelo otada. Sve što se učinilo. Svi oni Folk koji su se vratili u blato. On je izgubio prijestolje, ona ga je dobila. No kad mu se primaknula i uzela čašu iz ruke, u očima mu je zabljesnuo onaj isti Oko koji je imala te noći. Onaj Oko nezaštićene žudnje. I osjećaj da te netko tako gleda bio je jednako dobar. Možda i bolji nego ikad.

en: “And if it is, it turns wrong soon enough.” She took two fistfuls of her damp dress and gathered it up. “It rots. It rusts. It dies.” Gathered it up all the way to her thighs, goosefleshed from the cold outside and the warm inside. “Life’s naught but a set of moments.” And she slipped one knee onto the cushions to either side of him, lowered herself gently into his lap. “You’ve got to live each one.”
bs: — A ako i jest, vrlo se brzo pokvari. Zgrabila je vlažnu haljinu objema šakama i podigla je. — Trune. Hrđa. Umire. Podigla ju je sve do bedara, naježenih od hladnoće vani i topline unutra. — Život nije ništa drugo nego skup trenutaka. Potom je spustila jedno koljeno s obje strane njegovih nogu i nježno mu sjela u krilo. — Čovjek mora proživjeti svaki.

en: He caught a glimpse of flags through the budding branches. The crossed hammers of Angland, maybe. He heard the familiar tramp of armoured feet and let the curtains fall. No doubt they were still searching for him. Plainly, he was far from free. But with Rikke on his side he had a chance. In Adua, self-styled zenith of civilisation, they liked to think of anything beyond the Circle Sea as primitive. But they could have learned a lot from the Northmen. About courage, about endurance, about loyalty
bs: Kroz pupajuće je grane primijetio djelić zastava. Možda prekrižene čekiće Englenda. Čuo je dobro poznat Trdak korak oklopljenih čizama i pustio zastore da padnu. Nema sumnje da su ga još tražili. Bilo je posve jasno da je daleko od slobode. No s Rike na svojoj strani imao je šansu. U Aduji, koja se samoprozvano smatrala vrhuncem civilizacije, voljeli su misliti da je sve s one strane Kružnog Mora primitivno. No mogli su mnogo naučiti od Sjevernjaka. O hrabrosti, o izdržljivosti, o odanosti. Što

en: “Barely,” said Isern as she stalked past him to the door, endlessly chewing. From the short patch of sunlight in front of the windows it could not have been far short of midday.
bs: — Jedva, odvrati Izern dok je prohujala pokraj njega prema vratima, neprestano žvačući. Sudeći po maloj krpi sunčeve svjetlosti pred prozorima, nije moglo biti daleko od podneva.

en: She looked up sharply. Looking into the gaping pupil of that Long Eye still scared him and excited him at once. As though she might see some secret truth in him that he had never guessed at. “Why d’you say that?”
bs: Ona oštro podigne Oko. Oko u golemu zjenicu tog Dugog Oka još ga je uvijek istovremeno plašio i uzbuđivao. Kao da bi u njemu mogla ugledati neku tajnu istinu koju on sam nikad nije naslutio. — Zašto to govoriš?

en: Orso puffed out his cheeks. “I’d never know you had doubts. You seem so sure of yourself.” He gave a snort of laughter. Perhaps he had a type, after all. “You remind me of Savine, in a way.”
bs: Orso je napuhnuo obraze. — Nikad ne bih rekao da sumnjaš. Djeluješ toliko sigurna u sebe." Tiho se nasmijao. Možda je ipak imao svoj tip žene. — Na neki me način podsjećaš na Savine.

en: Brock looked even more gaunt, pale and furious than the last time Orso saw him, the day the Lords Round burned and he stabbed Lord Marshal Forest in the chest. All those high qualities everyone had once so envied—the honesty, the bravery, the blunt good nature—seemed to have been crushed out of him like the pulp out of a lemon, leaving just the bitter seeds of pride, anger and an insatiable need to conquer. That and a truly unforgivable lack of any sense of humour.
bs: Brok je izgledao još mršavije, bljeđe i ljuće nego posljednji put kad ga je Orso vidio, onoga dana kad je gorio Lords Round i kad je zabio nož u prsa lordu maršalu Forestu. Sve ono plemenito čemu su se svi nekoć toliko divili — iskrenost, hrabrost, neposrednu dobrodušnost — činilo se kao da je iz njega istisnuto poput soka iz limuna, ostavljajući za sobom samo gorke sjemenke ponosa, gnjeva i nezasitne potrebe za osvajanjem. To, te uistinu neoprostiv manjak bilo kakva smisla za humor.

en: “In Adua, we like to think of anything beyond the Circle Sea as primitive.” Orso gave a sigh and placed his knife and fork neatly together with a final sounding clink. He was finished. And not just with breakfast. “But it turns out you Northmen can teach us a thing or two about treachery.”
bs: — U Adui volimo misliti da je sve izvan Kružnoga mora prilično primitivno. Orso uzdahnu te složi nož i vilicu uredno jedno uz drugo uz konačan, zvakav zvuk. Završio je. I to ne samo s doručkom. — Ali pokazalo se da nam vi Sjevernjaci možete održati lekciju-dvije o izdaji.

en: Rikke winced again, even harder, as Glaward walked over with a set of heavy manacles. “Believe it or not, so am I.”
bs: Rike se ponovno trznula, još jače, dok je Glavard prilazio s teškim okovima. — Vjerovao ili ne, i meni je.

en: The bracelets snapped shut around Orso’s wrists. One could almost hear the discomfort in Glaward’s voice. “Hope that’s not too tight, Your…”
bs: Okovi su škljocnuli oko Orsovih zapešća. Moglo se gotovo čuti nelagodu u Glavardovu glasu. — Nadam se da nisu preuski, Vaše…

en: “He was hiding in the Gloktas’ old house, of all places, with bloody Black Rikke.” She went to the lamp and blew it out, sinking the room into darkness. “She gave him up.”
bs: — Skrivao se ni manje ni više nego u staroj kući obitelji Glokta, zajedno s krvavom Black Rike. Prišla je svjetiljki i ugasila je, utopivši sobu u mrak. — Izdala ga je.

en: Tallow slipped out a key, unlocked the door with a trembling hand, turned the knob and pushed it creaking open. There was a musty-smelling little hall beyond, paper peeling from the mould-speckled plaster.
bs: Talou izvuče ključ, drhtavom rukom otključa vrata, okrenu kvaku i gurnu ih, a ona se otvoriše uz škripu. Pred njima se ukazao malen, zagušljiv hodnik s tapetama koje su se ljuštile s plijesni posute žbuke.

en: She didn’t know where they were taking her. She didn’t know who was behind this. She hardly knew what the sides were any more, let alone which one she was supposed to be on. She didn’t even know what betrayal, what deception, what secret she was paying for. Probably she’d never know. Body found floating by the docks. An unsatisfactory ending to her bitter little story.
bs: Nije znala kamo je vode. Nije znala tko stoji iza svega ovoga. Jedva je više znala i tko je na čijoj strani, a kamoli na kojoj bi ona sama trebala biti. Nije znala ni kakva izdaja, kakva obmana, kakva tajna je košta glave. Vjerojatno neće saznati nikad. Tijelo pronađeno kako pluta uz dokove. Nezadovoljavajući kraj njezine gorke male priče.

en: One pointed out the door like an usher showing a valued client to her seat in the theatre. “Just inside, Inquisitor, if you’d be so kind?”
bs: Jedan je pokazao na vrata poput redara koji uvaženog klijenta vodi do sjedala u kazalištu. — Samo unutra, Inkvizitorice, ako biste bili tako ljubazni?

en: Sand dan Glokta bared his ruined teeth as he sat back in his wheeled chair and considered her calmly. “Yes.”
bs: Sand dan Glokta ogoli svoje uništene zube dok se zavaljivao u svoja kolica i mirno je promatrao. — Jesam.

en: “Or you.” He waved towards the bench on the other side of the table. “Have a seat, Inquisitor. Towering over me like that, you’re making me nervous.”
bs: — Ili poput tebe. Mahnuo je prema klupi na drugoj strani stola. — Sjedni, Inkvizitor. Dok se tako nadvijaš nada mnom, činiš me nervoznim.

en: “Don’t be upset at him, Vick, it’s beneath you. I found him in the camps, like you. I offered him the same deal and he made the same choice. The only choice. To stand with the winners.”
bs: — Nemoj se ljutiti na njega, Vik, to je ispod tvoje časti. Našao sam ga u logorima, baš kao i tebe. Ponudio sam mu istu pogodbu i on je donio istu odluku. Jedinu moguću. Stati na stranu pobjednika.

en: Vick blinked down at the squares board, the anger already drained away to leave her hollow and helpless. Risinau, Judge, Orso, Leo dan Brock, they were all small pieces in the game Glokta had been playing. So small they never even guessed how vast the board truly was. Which made her what? A speck of dust between the squares, at best.
bs: Vik spusti Oko na šahovsku ploču; bijes je već iščeznuo, ostavivši je praznom i nemoćnom. Risinau, Džadž, Orso, Leo dan Brok bili su tek sitne figure u igri koju je Glokta vodio. Toliko sitne da nikad nisu ni naslutili koliko je ta ploča zapravo golema. Što je onda činilo nju? Tek zrnce prašine između polja, u najboljem slučaju.

en: Rubbish, most likely. A made-up drawing in a book full of lies. But there comes a time you have to say no to what you’re given and reach for what you want.
bs: Glupost, najvjerojatnije. Izmišljeni crtež u knjizi prepunoj laži. No dođe vrijeme kad moraš reći ne onome što ti se nudi i posegnuti za onim što želiš.

en: “Isn’t it.” Jurand was teetering on the edge of impatience as he stepped to his own mark, weighing his steels. “Then when I say begin—”
bs: — Zar ne. Džurand je balansirao na rubu nestrpljenja dok je koračao do svoje oznake, važući čelike."Onda, kad kažem počni —"

en: He bent to collect his steels. “So… not only have you fenced before, but you were trained by one of the best swordsmen the Union ever produced?”
bs: Sagnuo se da pokupi svoje čelike. — Znači… ne samo da si se mačevala prije, nego te obučavao jedan od najboljih mačevaoca koje je Unija ikada Dow?

en: “To you first of all.” She danced in, their blades rang together prettily enough but with no real fire, and they broke again. “The new Closed Council must represent the new Union, and you will be its heart. You should be confirmed as Lord Chamberlain.”
bs: — prije svega s tobom. Zakoračila je bliže, oštrice im se zveckajući dodirnuše posve umiljato, ali bez ikakve istinske vatre, pa se odmaknuše. — Novo Uže Vijeće mora predstavljati novu Unija, a ti ćeš joj biti srce. Treba te potvrditi za lorda komornika.

en: “I am of the firm opinion, however…” Cut, cut, jab. “That it would be a missed opportunity to return to the way things were in King Jezal’s reign.” Jab, jab, cut. “A regime that ensured its own downfall with its waste, and exploitation, and callous disregard for its subjects.” Steel rang with each word. “We need a new kind of person on the Closed Council. Engineers and architects. Investors and inventors.” Jurand came back at her and she parried once, twice, thrice. “People who understand the to
bs: — Međutim, čvrstog sam mišljenja… Udarac, udarac, ubod. — …da bi bila propuštena prilika vratiti se onome kako je bilo u vrijeme kralja Džezal. Ubod, ubod, udarac. — Režimu koji je svojim rasipništvom, iskorištavanjem i bezosjećajnim zanemarivanjem svojih podanika osigurao vlastitu propast. Čelik je zazvečao uz svaku riječ. — Trebamo novu vrstu Folk u Užem Vijeću. Inženjere i arhitekte. Ulagače i izumitelje. Džurand joj se ponovo približio, a ona je parirala jednom, dvaput, triput. — Ljude koji

en: “I cannot tell you what a comfort that is.” She rested a gentle hand on his forearm. A little human contact, carefully administered, can have such a powerful effect. “To know that even if I have made a mess of things with Leo, we will always have a good friend in common.”
bs: — Ne mogu ti opisati koliko mi to znači. Položila mu je nježnu ruku na podlakticu. Malo ljudskog dodira, pomno doziranog, može imati tako snažan učinak. — Znati da čak i ako sam sve uprskala s Leom, uvijek ćemo imati zajedničkoga dobrog prijatelja.

en: “I think we are alike, in many ways. I can be quite perceptive, too.” She eased even closer, squeezed his arm tighter, made her voice softer so he had to lean down towards her. “I have started to believe that Leo…” She fixed him with her eye and whispered the words. “Is in love with someone else. That he always has been. I have often thought about how he reacted… to what happened in Sipani.” Jurand’s cheek flushed. He tried to pull away but she gripped his arm. “I have come to believe it might n
bs: — Mislim da smo slični, na mnogo načina. I ja mogu biti prilično prodorna. Približila se još više, čvršće mu stisnula ruku, stišala glas kako bi se morao sagnuti k njoj. — Počela sam vjerovati da je Leo… Pogledala ga je prodorno i prošaptala riječi. "Zaljubljen u nekog drugog. Da je oduvijek bio. Često sam razmišljala o tome kako je reagirao… na ono što se dogodilo u Sipani." Džurandov se obraz zarumenio. Pokušao se izvući, ali ona mu je uhvatila ruku. "Uvjerila sam se da to možda uopće nije bil

en: Jurand cleared his throat with some difficulty. “Er… I… yes. Were there… any names in particular you—”
bs: Džurand je s određenim naporom pročistio grlo. — Ovaj… ja… da. Je li bilo… ikakvih određenih imena koja ti…

en: “I never doubted it.” She caught Savine’s eye, that brow creeping higher. “It only remains to be seen whether he can tickle your husband half so deftly.”
bs: — U to nisam ni sumnjala. Uhvatila je Savine Oko, a ona joj se obrva popela još više. — Ostaje samo vidjeti može li on tvoga muža bocnuti upola tako vješto.

en: Savine’s mother stood beside the cots, rocking her tiny namesake with practised carelessness, pulling faces while the baby gurgled happily.
bs: Savinina majka stajala je kraj kolijevki i s uvježbanom ležernošću ljuljala svoju malenu imenjakinju, praveći smiješne grimase dok je beba radosno gugutala.

en: She sank into a chair with a rustling of expensive skirts, sitting Harod on her knee so she could look deep into his eyes. “I still feel very much like the same sarcastic drunk I was at seventeen. But now I’m a grandmother, apparently. And to a king, would you believe?”
bs: Ona se uz šuškanje skupocjenih suknji sruši u naslonjač, posadivši Haroda na koljeno kako bi mu se zagledala u oči. — Još se uvijek osjećam kao ista ona sarkastična pijančura kakva sam bila sa sedamnaest. Ali sad sam, eto, baka. I to kralju, možeš li zamisliti?

en: “He isn’t my father,” grumbled Savine, but it sounded churlish. How the hell could she have come out of this as the unreasonable one?
bs: "On mi nije otac, prozbori Savine mrzovoljno, premda je zvučalo zajedljivo. Kako zaboga iz ovoga može ispasti ona nerazumna?

en: Savine walked to him, skirts hissing on stone in the heavy silence. All the way her mouth was open to speak, but when she got to the chair she still had not found the words. In the end, she simply put her hand on her father’s bony shoulder, the way she might have years ago. He laid his hand on top of hers. They looked up at the half-finished painting of Leo embodying the manly virtues, his iron leg hidden by horseflesh and his ruined arm by gold braid, pointing his sword towards a better tomorro
bs: Savine mu priđe, a suknje joj zafuštaše po kamenu u teškoj tišini. Usne su joj cijelim putem bile otvorene za govor, no kad je stigla do stolice, još nije pronašla riječi. Na kraju je jednostavno stavila ruku na očevo koštunjavo rame, onako kako bi to učinila prije mnogo godina. On položi svoju ruku na njezinu. Pogledom su pratili napola dovršenu sliku Lea koji utjelovljuje muževne vrline, čiju su željeznu nogu skrivali konjski trup, a uništenu ruku zlatne pletenice, dok je mačem pokazivao prema

en: best to help you, in my own way. Someone had to have an eye on the bigger picture. I was working with Superior Pike to bring this madness to an end.”
bs: Hladan komadić sumnje probio je toplu ušuškanost njihova ponovnog susreta i počeo bosti dublje. — Surađivao si s Pajkom? Zar nije on stajao iza svega ovoga?

en: “Don’t talk to me about fucking gardening!” she screamed, tearing her hand from his. “People died! Thousands of them!” She felt dizzy. She felt sick. “I nearly died, more than once!”
bs: "Nemoj mi govoriti o jebenom vrtlarstvu!" vrisnula je, istrgnuvši ruku iz njegove. — Folk su ginuli! Tisuće njih!" Osjetila je vrtoglavicu. Mučninu. "Ja sam umalo umrla, i to više puta!"

en: “To everyone’s advantage!” he barked, wheeling himself towards her. “Put aside your pique, Savine, this was war. In war one must make use of every weapon. Restraint is folly. Worse. Restraint is cowardice. You can give us a better Union. A better world! The horrors of the Great Change have left people pliable. Desperate for strong leadership. You are loved as much as I was hated, and the banks are torn up by the roots. We will finally have a free hand!”
bs: — U svačiju korist! odbrusio je, dovezavši se u kolicima bliže njoj. "Ostavi po strani svoju uvrijeđenost, Savine, ovo je bio rat. U ratu se čovjek mora poslužiti svakim oružjem. Uzdržanost je Ludilo. Još gore. Uzdržanost je kukavičluk. Možeš nam dati bolju Unija. Bolji svijet! Užasi Velike promjene učinili su ljude podatnima. Očajnički žudnima za čvrstim vodstvom. Tebe vole onoliko koliko su mene mrzili, a banke su iščupane iz korijena. Konačno ćemo imati slobodne ruke!"

en: “I should have denounced you, in the Court of the People,” whispered Savine. “I should have denounced you to hell.”
bs: — Trebala sam te raskrinkati pred Narodnim sudom, prošapta Savine. — Trebala sam te poslati k vragu.

en: Savine heard shouting in the corridor, then a long, thin scream. She took an unsteady step away. She had been on a battlefield and knew what genuine agony sounded like. It ended in a sickening metallic crash, and another, closer, then a crunching thud so near and so hard that Savine felt the floor vibrate. The painting rattled on its stand. Dust filtered gently down from the vaults above.
bs: Savine je čula viku u hodniku, a potom dug, tanak vrisak. Nesigurno je istupila korak unatrag. Bila je na bojnom polju i znala je kako zvuči istinska agonija. Završila je mučnim metalnim treskom, pa još jednim, bližim, a onda i krckavim udarcem toliko bliskim i snažnim da je Savine osjetila kako joj pod podrhtava pod nogama. Slika na stalku je zveckala. Prašina se polako sipala s visokih svodova.

en: Sulfur smiled at her father. The smile of a disappointed tutor, finally tracking down a wayward pupil. “Sand dan Glokta. You have become a difficult man to find.”
bs: Salfur se nasmiješio njezinu ocu. Osmijeh razočarana učitelja koji je napokon ušao u trag neposlušnu učeniku. — Sand dan Glokta. Postao si čovjek kojega je teško pronaći.

en: The shock on Sulfur’s face only lasted for an instant. Then the air above his shoulders shimmered and Rabik was flung across the room as if by a slap from a giant’s hand. Savine gasped as he crashed into the window in a spray of glass, bounced from the stone frame leaving a great crack. He should have been dead, every bone shattered. Instead he fell in a ready crouch like a cat dropped from a high place, dust showering from a great dry split in his cheek but his mouth still fixed in a smile.
bs: Zaprepaštenje na Salfurovu licu trajalo je samo tren. Zatim je zrak iznad njegovih ramena zatreperio i Rabik je odbačen preko prostorije kao da ga je ošamarila divovska ruka. Savine uzdahnu kad se on uz prasak razbijenog stakla zabio u prozor, odbivši se od kameni okvir i ostavivši za sobom veliku napuklinu. Prema svemu sudeći, trebao je biti mrtav, sa svakom slomljenom kosti. Umjesto toga pao je u spreman četveronožni položaj poput mačke bačene s velike visine, a s velike i suhe pukotine na obr

en: Little fires were scattered across the floor, blurred and sparkling through the tears stung from her eyes. Leo’s ruined painting was scorching, canvas curling, the room crazily lit by flickering flames, cast into dancing shadow. Sulfur reeled and thrashed while Rabik clawed at him, bit at him, his hair turned to a burning torch. Sulfur flung him away but Rabik tore a mouthful of meat from his face as he went, ripping one of his ears half off, tumbling across the floor, spinning, sliding, fingern
bs: Sitni su požari gorjeli posvuda po podu, zamućeni i svjetlucavi kroz suze što su joj pekle oči. Leo je uništeni slikarski rad gorio, platno se savijalo, a prostorija je bila nestvarno osvijetljena treperavim plamenom i uronjena u ples sjenki. Salfur se teturao i mlatarao rukama dok ga je Rabik grebao i grizao, a kosa mu se pretvorila u goruću buktinju. Salfur ga je odbacio, ali mu je Rabik u letu otkinuo komad mesa s lica, napola mu otkinuvši uho, te se otkotrljao preko poda, okrećući se i klize

en: Savine cowered behind her father’s chair, staring between her fingers. Zuri twisted Sulfur’s head back, one hand hooking his top jaw, one hooking the bottom. She snarled as she began to drag them apart, his eyes bulging, his mouth gaping wider and wider until with a snapping crunch she ripped his face wide open, blood showering, tearing his bottom jaw from his head until it hung on strings of gristle.
bs: Savine se sklupčala iza očeve stolice, gledajući kroz prste. Zuri mu je zavinula glavu unatrag, zakačivši jednu ruku za gornju čeljust, a drugu za donju. Zarežala je počevši ih razdvajati, oči su mu ispale iz duplji, usta su se širila sve više i više dok mu s krckajućim praskom nije raznijela lice širom otvoreno, prskajući krv i trgajući mu donju čeljust s glave sve dok nije visjela na nitima hrskavice.

en: “You had to be protected,” said Savine’s father, baring the teeth he still had as he wheeled his chair towards her. “I made an arrangement with the only ones who could do it.”
bs: — Morala si biti zaštićena, prozborio je Savinin otac pokazujući zube što su mu još preostali dok je gurao stolicu prema njoj. — Sklopio sam dogovor s jedinima koji su to mogli izvesti.

en: She slid the box from her sleeve and took a healthy pinch of pearl dust up each nostril. Then another. Just to stop her hands from shaking. She wiped her nose carefully, dabbed her eyes on her unburned sleeve, pushed her chin up and her shoulders back, and managed something like a smile.
bs: Izvukla je kutijicu iz rukava i udahnula poveću šaku bisernog praha u svaku nosnicu. Zatim još jednu. Tek toliko da joj ruke prestanu podrhtavati. Pažljivo je obrisala nos, potrala oči nezapaljenim rukavom, podignula bradu, zabacila ramena i uspjela izmamiti nešto poput osmijeha.

en: “True enough. But you’ve made the whole North your garden now.” Shivers shook his head like he could hardly believe it. “Reckon he’d be proud.”
bs: — Istina. Ali sada si cijeli Sjever pretvorila u svoj vrt. Šivers je odahnuo glavom kao da jedva u to vjeruje. — Vjerujem da bi bio ponosan.

en: “Surely, but you’ve no time to indulge yours. You’ve the whole North to lead from the darkness and into the moon’s silvery favour. Tell me this—what else could you have done?”
bs: —, ali nemaš vremena prepuštati se svojim sumnjama. Moraš voditi cijeli Sjever iz tame u mjesečevu srebrnu naklonost. Reci mi ovo — što si drugo mogla učiniti?

en: Rikke was shocked, almost, that she said it. But the moment she made the choice, she was sure of it. “The only place those great men’s footsteps lead is round and round in circles of blood,” she said. “The only history there is violence and betrayal. Send to Hardbread and the rest. Tell ’em I’m staying here.”
bs: Rike je bila gotovo šokirana što je to izgovorila. No čim je donijela odluku, u nju je bila sigurna. — Jedino mjesto kamo vode stope tih velikaša jest vrzmanje u Round po lokvama krvi, rekla je. — Jedina povijest koja ondje postoji jest nasilje i izdaja. Pošaljite glasnike Hardbredu i ostalima. Recite im da ostajem ovdje.

en: “Aye, a little bit.” Isern grinned as she offered out a chagga pellet. “With any luck the last you’ll need.”
bs: — Da, donekle. Izern se nasmiješila pružajući joj kuglicu čage. — Uz malo sreće, i posljednja koja će ti trebati.

en: Bolts clanked and the door creaked slowly open. An old man, bent under an old-fashioned suit of armour, frowned at him from the other side. He had a long sword far too heavy for him, point wobbling wildly as he strained to keep it level.
bs: Zasun zaškrguta i vrata se polako otvoriše uz škripu. Starac, pognut pod starinskim oklopom, namršti se na nj nasuprot tome. Nosio je dugačak mač koji mu je bio pretežak, a Kruna mu je divlje podrhtavao dok se naprezao održati ga u ravnini.

en: “None other.” The afternoon sun shone brightly off Bayaz’s tanned pate as he stepped forwards, took Clover’s right hand in both of his and pressed it warmly. “Welcome to the Great Northern Library, Jonas Steepfield. I understand there is no man alive who knows more about sword-work.”
bs: — Nitko drugi. Popodnevno je sunce sjajno bljesnulo o osunčanu lubanju Bajazovu dok je istupio naprijed, uzeo desnu Kloverovu ruku u obje svoje i toplo ju stisnuo. — Dobro došao u Veliku sjevernu knjižnicu, Jonas Stipfild. Vjerujem da nema živog čovjeka koji zna više o mačevanju.

en: “I reckon.” Honestly, Clover was somewhat troubled by the tone, along with the memory of Black Calder’s nervous hand-wringing around the man. But then he’d been serving dangerous bastards all his life. A master no one fears won’t take you far, and men who make the worst enemies, after all, can make the best friends. “I… er, have something for you.”
bs: — Vjerojatno. Iskreno govoreći, Klovera je donekle uznemirio taj ton, zajedno sa sjećanjem na nervozno kršenje ruku Black Kaldera u prisutnosti tog čovjeka. No ionako je čitavog života služio opasnim gadovima. Gospodar kojega se nitko ne boji neće te daleko dovesti, a Folk koji su najgori neprijatelji, naposljetku, mogu biti najbolji prijatelji. — Ja… ovaj, imam nešto za tebe.

en: “Magic and money are two things I know a little about,” Bayaz was saying as he slipped Bethod’s chain into a pocket. “Kings, also, are an area of some expertise. But I must confess that when it comes to sword-work, I have always relied on others.”
bs: — Umijeće i novac dvije su stvari o kojima ponešto znam, govorio je Bajaz uvlačeći Bethodov lanac u džep. — Kraljevi su također područje u kojem imam određene stručnosti. No moram priznati da se, kad je riječ o mačevanju, uvijek oslanjam na druge.
